new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: A hosting fleet running cPanel & WHM or WP2 must be driven to the fixed release on a KEV-tied clock measured in hours, and applied fleet-wide rather than server-by-server on a rolling window. The bypass needs no credentials and targets the login flow itself, while the panel is by design internet-reachable so tenants can log in — so an unpatched host is a fully exposed control-plane takeover for the entire time it waits, and a rolling schedule simply means the last host in the queue stays open longest. Because no live-patch primitive is registered for this entry, the fix is a vendor update requiring a service restart or reboot, so that restart has to be pre-authorized against the KEV clock instead of deferred to the next tenant-notified maintenance slot. Hosts that cannot be updated inside the SLA must have their panel and WHM listeners restricted to operator networks and be booked as unremediated.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Packet: CISA KEV-listed 2026-04-30 with active_exploitation=confirmed; RWEP 83, CVSS 9.1, poc_available=true. The vector states WebPros cPanel & WHM (WebHost Manager) and WP2 (WordPress Squared) contain an authentication bypass vulnerability in the login flow that allows unauthenticated remote attackers to gain unauthorized access to the control panel (CWE-306, missing authentication for a critical function). patch_available=true, live_patch_available=false, and live_patch_notes state the vendor patch typically requires service restart or system reboot per the KEV requiredAction.

new_control_requirements.name: PERIMETER-COMPROMISE-REBUILD-NOT-PATCH
new_control_requirements.description: A panel host that was internet-reachable while unpatched must go through compromise assessment and credential rotation rather than patch-and-continue. Because the bypass hands an unauthenticated caller the control panel itself, the attacker inherits the panel's own legitimate capabilities — creating accounts and API tokens, rewriting mail and DNS records, writing files into tenant document roots, installing cron persistence — and none of that is removed by the update. The default response is configuration export, rebuild or restore of the panel host from known-good state, rotation of every tenant, reseller and API credential the panel issued, and an audit of accounts, cron entries and tenant webroots created since the KEV listing date. Anti-malware scanning is not the test here: the artifacts left behind are ordinary panel objects and ordinary web content, not malware signatures.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Packet: CISA KEV-listed 2026-04-30 with active_exploitation=confirmed, poc_available=true and RWEP 83, so an exposed unpatched host is an exploitation opportunity rather than a hypothetical. The vector states the authentication bypass in the login flow allows unauthenticated remote attackers to gain unauthorized access to the control panel of WebPros cPanel & WHM and WP2 — the attacker operates as a panel principal rather than through a memory-corruption payload (CWE-306). patch_available=true with live_patch_available=false; the packet's remediation is a vendor patch requiring service restart or system reboot, which closes the entry path but makes no statement about actions already taken through it.

new_control_requirements.name: FLEET-CONTROL-PLANE-ADMIN-PRIVILEGE-TIER
new_control_requirements.description: WHM is the fleet control plane for every tenant site, mailbox, database and DNS zone on the host, and this flaw is the argument for making its administration a distinct privilege tier instead of the same login surface at a higher permission level. The WHM root and reseller surface should be reachable only from a PAM jumphost or operator network, behind FIDO2 step-up and just-in-time elevation with a separate identity from tenant accounts, so that a defect in the login flow does not present the whole hosting estate to an anonymous internet caller. Splitting the surfaces also bounds the damage where the tenant-facing cPanel login has to stay internet-exposed for customers: that side gets patched under the KEV clock, while the administrative plane is never an unauthenticated caller's first hop in the first place.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Packet: CWE-306, missing authentication for a critical function — the vector records an authentication bypass in the login flow of WebPros cPanel & WHM (WebHost Manager) and WP2 (WordPress Squared) allowing unauthenticated remote attackers to gain unauthorized access to the control panel. CISA KEV-listed 2026-04-30, active_exploitation=confirmed, CVSS 9.1, RWEP 83, poc_available=true. The citing gaps recorded for this entry include NIST-800-53-AC-6 (Least Privilege) and UK-CAF-B2 (Identity and access control), both of which the packet marks as insufficient here.

new_control_requirements.name: PERIMETER-COMPROMISE-REBUILD-NOT-PATCH
new_control_requirements.description: Upgrading the ScreenConnect server to the fixed build removes the traversal but not what the traversal already wrote. CVE-2024-1708 is an arbitrary file-write primitive: chained with the companion authentication bypass it plants a web shell in a ScreenConnect-served directory, and that file is application content rather than product code, so the vendor update leaves it in place and running. Any ScreenConnect instance that was reachable from an untrusted network on a vulnerable build must therefore be handled as compromised rather than as remediated: export the configuration, session history and extension inventory for forensics, rebuild the host from known-good media, reinstall at the fixed version, and rotate everything the server held or brokered — the relay/agent join material, the ScreenConnect administrative and integrated-identity accounts, and any credential a technician entered through a remote session during the exposure window. Deleting the one web shell that was found and then patching is not equivalent, because the same write primitive places files anywhere the service account can reach, and the read half of the traversal means configuration secrets on the host should be assumed disclosed.
new_control_requirements.evidence: ConnectWise ScreenConnect, CISA KEV-listed 2026-04-28 with confirmed in-the-wild exploitation and a public PoC available. The packet's attack-vector record states the path traversal (CWE-22) lets an attacker write or read files outside the intended directory and was used with the companion authentication bypass to drop a web shell — i.e. attacker-planted files persist independently of the vendor patch. RWEP 83 against CVSS 7.5: the gap between the two is exactly the post-exploitation persistence that a base score for an information-disclosure-shaped traversal does not carry.

new_control_requirements.name: FLEET-COMPROMISE-IR-PLAYBOOK
new_control_requirements.description: ScreenConnect is a fleet control plane, not an ordinary web application: its access agents run with service-level privilege on every managed endpoint and execute what the server tells them to. An incident-response plan scoped to 'the ScreenConnect host' therefore has the wrong blast radius, because a web shell reached through this traversal gives the attacker the same command channel into the managed estate that the legitimate operator has. The playbook must be written and rehearsed before the event and must cover: revocation and re-issue of the relay/agent trust material so existing agent installations cannot be driven by attacker-held server identity; an audit of session, command and file-transfer history plus any extension or extension directory added since the exposure window opened; quarantine criteria for endpoints that received a session or a queued command during that window; and rotation of every credential used through a remote session, including the customer-side administrative accounts a technician authenticated with. Recovery timing must assume the ScreenConnect server itself is unavailable during the response, since it is the system being rebuilt.
new_control_requirements.evidence: ConnectWise ScreenConnect path traversal, CISA KEV-listed 2026-04-28, active exploitation confirmed, public PoC available, RWEP 83. The packet records the traversal being used with the companion authentication bypass to drop a web shell on the server that brokers remote sessions to managed endpoints, which places every endpoint reachable from that server inside the incident scope rather than outside it.

new_control_requirements.description: For a DIR-823X the KEV clock has to terminate in a verified per-unit outcome, because the failure mode of consumer-router patching is not a missed deadline, it is an open-ended 'awaiting firmware' state that never resolves. The interface-isolation half of the tier is the right action under either reading, which is why it belongs alongside the patch clock rather than behind it.

new_control_requirements.name: ENDPOINT-MGMT-DEPLOYMENT-CHANNEL-INTEGRITY
new_control_requirements.description: The primitive in this CVE is an arbitrary write anywhere on the filesystem as the SimpleHelp server user — so the exposed asset is not just the web root but every file that remote-support server holds and hands out: session and client artifacts, technician-facing downloads, service configuration and any script the server executes. Treat that content as a privileged distribution channel rather than as application data: file-integrity-monitor the SimpleHelp installation and every directory it serves artifacts from, alert on writes that do not correspond to a sanctioned administrator action or a vendor update, and hold the support server to KEV-priority patching as a management-plane asset. This is the control that still has value after the patch lands, because the fix closes the zip-slip write path but removes nothing already written through it — an attacker file placed before remediation survives the upgrade, and neither signature-based anti-malware nor authentication logging will surface a bespoke artifact dropped through a legitimate upload endpoint.
new_control_requirements.evidence: The catalog vector states the flaw lets an actor 'upload arbitrary files anywhere on the file system by uploading a crafted zip file (i.e. zip slip)' and thereby 'execute arbitrary code on the host in the context of the SimpleHelp server user'; the attack_vector locates the flaw 'on the remote-support server'. KEV-listed 2026-04-24 with active_exploitation 'confirmed' and poc_available true, RWEP 83. The gaps this entry already cites include CIS Controls v8 10.1 (Deploy and Maintain Anti-Malware Software) and UK CAF C1 (Security monitoring) — neither detects an attacker-written artifact that carries no malware signature and arrives over an authenticated upload path.

attack_vector.description: a missing-authorization flaw (CWE-862) letting a low-privileged or unauthenticated attacker reach privileged functionality on the remote-support server. CISA KEV-listed 2026-04-24 with confirmed in-the-wild exploitation.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none (the flaw is reachable by an unauthenticated attacker on the platform's public interface)
attack_vector.complexity: low — KEV-listed, actively exploited; treat as weaponized
attack_vector.ai_factor: No AI involvement documented in discovery or weaponization.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Apply the SimpleHelp security update; hunt for web shells, rotate credentials and secrets, and review downstream managed/integrated systems — management platforms reach the whole estate, so treat compromise as fleet-wide.
prevention.adequacy: Patch is necessary but insufficient alone — web shells, stolen credentials, and pushed tasking survive the patch and require explicit cleanup across managed systems.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Monitoring on the SimpleHelp: exploit-shaped requests, new web-shell files, unexpected process execution, administrative actions without a matching session, and anomalous jobs/scripts pushed to managed endpoints.
detection.adequacy: Necessary to catch resident persistence and downstream tasking after patching.

response.what_would_have_worked: Patch immediately, hunt and remove web shells, rotate all platform and integration credentials, and audit every action the platform pushed to managed systems during the exposure window; assume downstream compromise.
response.adequacy: Mandatory; a management-platform compromise can re-establish itself through the very systems it administers, so downstream review is non-negotiable.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: The 30-day flaw-remediation SLA is far longer than the observed exploitation window for a KEV-listed, unauthenticated IT-management/enterprise platform RCE; these are mass-exploited within days, and RMM/ITSM/endpoint-management compromise reaches the entire managed estate.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: 'Appropriate timescales' is undefined; the standard 30-day reading is unsafe for an actively-exploited, internet-facing management platform whose compromise is fleet-wide.

NIS2-Art21-network-security.gap: Treats management platforms as essential-function infrastructure but lacks a CISA-KEV-style compressed remediation SLA, and does not require the web-shell-hunt / credential-rotation / downstream-review cleanup these RCEs need given their managed-estate reach.

PCI-DSS-4.0-6.3.3.gap: The 30-day critical-patch window is exploitation acceptance for an internet-facing management platform that can administer systems in or adjacent to the CDE.

compliance_exposure_score.basis: Internet-facing SimpleHelp is run by audited organizations on a standard patch SLA and is mass-exploited within days; the required web-shell hunt, credential rotation, and downstream-estate review are rarely part of the documented patch procedure, and the management reach amplifies the blast radius.

new_control_requirements.name: FLEET-CONTROL-PLANE-ADMIN-PRIVILEGE-TIER
new_control_requirements.description: SimpleHelp is a remote-support control plane, so its server admin role reaches every machine the technician population supports — the technician tier and the server-admin tier are not two shades of the same application user. This CVE collapses the distance between them: the entry records that low-privileged technicians can create API keys with excessive permissions and use those keys to escalate to the server admin role. Server administration of SimpleHelp needs to be classified as its own privilege tier — identity separate from every other admin role, jumphost-only access with hardware-key step-up, just-in-time elevation with approval — and the technician surface must not be able to mint or hold API keys at all. A framework that enumerates one admin role for this product attests accurately while the technician surface remains the real path into it.
new_control_requirements.evidence: SimpleHelp missing authorization (CWE-862), CVSS 8.8, RWEP 83. The entry states low-privileged technicians can create API keys with excessive permissions and that these keys can be used to escalate privileges to the server admin role, on a remote-support server. CISA KEV-listed 2026-04-24 with active_exploitation=confirmed and poc_available=true.

new_control_requirements.name: FLEET-COMPROMISE-IR-PLAYBOOK
new_control_requirements.description: The escalation product here is a durable credential rather than a session: an API key minted through the missing-authorization flaw still carries server-admin power after the vendor fix is installed. The playbook for this CVE therefore has to enumerate and revoke every API key issued on the SimpleHelp server across the exposure window, audit technician accounts and role assignments for keys they should never have been able to create, and treat every endpoint reached through the server during that window as requiring credential rotation and review — a remote-support server is a path into the machines it supports, so its compromise fans outward rather than stopping at the appliance. Patching closes the minting path and leaves already-minted keys valid, which is precisely the state an audit reading only installed version would score as clean.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Missing authorization (CWE-862) on a remote-support server; the entry records that the API keys created through the flaw can be used to escalate to the server admin role. active_exploitation=confirmed, poc_available=true, CISA KEV-listed 2026-04-24, RWEP 83, CVSS 8.8.

new_control_requirements.description: SimpleHelp entered CISA KEV on 2026-04-24 with confirmed exploitation and a public PoC and a vendor fix exists, so this runs on the KEV clock rather than a quarterly application-patch cycle. new_control_requirements.name: DEVICE-MANAGEMENT-GATEWAY-CONFIG-ENDPOINT-AUTH-INPUT-NEUTRALIZATION
new_control_requirements.description: Catalyst SD-WAN Manager is the management plane the packet names, and the defect sits on its API interface: improper file handling lets an uploaded file drive a privileged API into overwriting arbitrary files on the system, ending in vmanage user privileges. Bound to this product, the control means every file-accepting API endpoint on SD-WAN Manager authorizes its caller before the upload is processed at all, and normalizes and validates the destination path before the privileged write executes, so a caller-supplied name cannot select which file gets overwritten; and no SD-WAN Manager instance is left with that API interface reachable from a segment with no operational need to reach it. The packet's own summary describes the path as reachable by an unauthenticated attacker, which is why the endpoint's own authorization decision — not the surrounding account model — is the only thing standing between an untrusted caller and a privileged file write. This is also why the cited least-privilege gap does not close this path: the attacker never holds a vManage operator account, so per-account privilege scoping is never consulted and an AC-6 attestation passes cleanly while the path stays open. Distinguishing test: on a staging SD-WAN Manager, send each file-accepting API endpoint an unauthenticated upload whose destination path resolves outside the intended upload directory, and confirm it is refused before anything is written. Precondition: the endpoint-side authorization and path validation are properties the vendor update establishes — this control states what to verify, it does not implement it. Until that update and its restart land, restricting which segments can reach the API interface bounds who can send the upload but leaves the endpoint fully exploitable to anything inside the permitted segment, and it is unavailable where the API interface must stay reachable for normal operation.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Packet vector: 'Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager contains an incorrect use of privileged APIs vulnerability due to improper file handling on the API interface of an affected system. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by uploading a malicious file on the local file system. A successful exploit could allow the attacker to overwrite arbitrary files on the affected system and gain vmanage user privileges.' Packet attack_vector: 'an incorrect use of privileged APIs (CWE-648) reachable by an unauthenticated attacker, enabling privileged actions on the management plane.' Citing gaps record NIST-800-53-AC-6 (Least Privilege) against this entry. patch_available true; live_patch_available false.

Applied to this product, the control means treating the SD-WAN Manager installation as privileged content rather than as application data: file-integrity-monitor the installation and the directories its API writes into, and alert on any write that does not correspond to a sanctioned administrator action or a vendor update. This is the control that still has value after the update lands, because the fix closes the write path but removes nothing already written through it — a file overwritten or planted before remediation survives the upgrade and the restart. With exploitation confirmed and a public exploit recorded in the packet, an instance whose API interface was reachable before remediation needs forensic triage of what was written rather than being closed on the patch. Where no such baseline exists, the honest position is that the overwritten set is unknown and the instance is a rebuild candidate, not a patched-and-cleared one.

new_control_requirements.name: ENTERPRISE-ERP-MANAGEMENT-FUNCTION-AUTHENTICATION

Bound to this product, the control means each administrative function on the PaperCut server authorizes its caller itself rather than inheriting a verdict from the filter that fronts it, and the admin surface is segmented so an untrusted network caller cannot present a request to that filter in the first place. The least-privilege control cited as insufficient here does not touch this path — the attacker never authenticates as any PaperCut operator, so per-account privilege scoping is never consulted, and the account model that an identity-and-access attestation examines is bypassed rather than abused. Distinguishing test: from a segment with no operational need for the print-administration console, issue unauthenticated requests to each administrative endpoint on a staging PaperCut instance and confirm each is refused before the function runs — an attestation that every PaperCut administrator authenticates at login passes cleanly while this path stays open.

UK-CAF-B2 (Identity and access control) and NIST-800-53-AC-6 (Least Privilege) are both recorded among the citing gaps.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: This is the case where a severity-ranked patch queue and a KEV-driven SLA give opposite answers, and the KEV answer is the correct one. At CVSS 6.1 the ZCS cross-site scripting flaw falls below the high/critical cut most Zimbra operators use to schedule mail-service downtime, yet it is KEV-listed with confirmed in-the-wild exploitation, has a public PoC, and scores RWEP 77 — the same real-world priority as the 9.8-rated RCEs in the same catalog. The remediation is not free: the packet records no live-patch tool for this entry and states that the vendor patch typically requires a service restart or system reboot per the KEV requiredAction, so closing it means booking a mailbox-server outage. That cost is precisely why a CVSS-ranked queue keeps deferring it, and why the SLA has to be pinned to the KEV listing date instead. Until the restart is booked, the exposure is live on every ZCS web-client session.

new_control_requirements.name: FLEET-CONTROL-PLANE-ADMIN-PRIVILEGE-TIER
new_control_requirements.description: This flaw's entire precondition is a low-privileged local account on the SD-WAN Manager appliance: the packet has an authenticated, local attacker reading a credential file for the DCA user from the filesystem and thereby gaining DCA privileges. Bound here, privilege tiering means the appliance carries no general-purpose local accounts at all — every operator who can obtain shell or filesystem-level access on vManage sits in a distinct tier above application and network admins, reached only through a PAM jumphost with FIDO2 step-up, just-in-time elevation, an identity used for nothing else, and per-session attribution. State the precondition honestly rather than claiming the surface is removed: this shrinks the population that can reach the credential file, it does not make the stored password unrecoverable. Any principal that does obtain low-privileged local access on the appliance — through an operational account, a support process, or any other local-access defect on the same host — still recovers the DCA credential, and the control has no effect at all on a credential that was already read. The cited least-privilege and identity-and-access-control gaps are recorded here because the escalation runs from one local account to another via a file read, so an attestation that vManage roles are least-privileged passes cleanly while the recoverable credential file sits on disk. Distinguishing test: from a deliberately low-privileged local account on a staging appliance, attempt to read the DCA credential file and confirm the account cannot exist in the first place under the tiering policy.

new_control_requirements.name: FLEET-COMPROMISE-IR-PLAYBOOK
new_control_requirements.description: A recoverable-format password disclosure is not closed by the code fix: the update changes how the DCA credential is stored, but a password an attacker has already read stays valid until it is changed. With the packet recording confirmed in-the-wild exploitation from the 2026-04-20 KEV listing on a controller whose own filesystem held the credential, the response half of this control is the load-bearing half — rotate the DCA credential and any other credential recoverable from the appliance filesystem as part of the update rather than as a follow-up ticket, audit what that account was used for across the exposure window, and invalidate device-trust state established through the controller where the account's use cannot be accounted for. Two preconditions decide whether the rotation is worth anything. It has to happen after the fixed build is running: rotating first simply writes a fresh password back into the recoverable format, leaving the operator with a rotation record and an unchanged exposure. And it only covers credentials the operator knows the appliance stores, so an inventory of what the controller holds on disk has to precede the rotation. This is a response control — it does not reduce the likelihood of the initial low-privileged local foothold that the flaw requires.

There is no live-patch tool recorded for this entry, and the packet states the vendor patch typically requires a service restart or system reboot per the KEV required action — so the SLA is satisfied when each controller has restarted onto the fixed build, not when the package is staged or installed, and the restart outage has to be scheduled inside the clock rather than deferred to the next maintenance window. new_control_requirements.name: ENTERPRISE-ERP-MANAGEMENT-FUNCTION-AUTHENTICATION
new_control_requirements.description: KACE SMA takes an authentication decision in front of an endpoint-management console, and this CVE is that decision failing open: the packet has an attacker impersonating legitimate users without valid credentials, reaching functionality behind the gate without ever presenting an account. Bound to this appliance the control means each administrative and API function on the SMA authorizes its own caller instead of inheriting a verdict from the front-door authentication, and the appliance's management surface is segmented so a caller with no operational need cannot present a request to that front door at all. This is precisely why the packet's cited multi-factor, identity-and-access and least-privilege gaps do not help here: the attacker never authenticates, so no second factor is demanded and no role is consulted, and an attestation that every KACE operator uses MFA passes cleanly while the path stays open. The precondition on the segmentation half must be stated rather than implied — it bounds who can reach the bypass, not whether the bypass works. A request originating from a permitted management segment, from an already-compromised administrator workstation, or from access obtained before the restriction was applied still reaches it, so segmentation buys time until the appliance is restarted onto the fixed build and never substitutes for that restart. Distinguishing test: from a segment with no operational need for the SMA console, issue unauthenticated requests to each administrative endpoint on a staging appliance and confirm each is refused before the function runs.

The entry's citing gaps name AU-Essential-8-MFA (Multi-factor authentication), UK-CAF-B2 (Identity and access control) and NIST-800-53-AC-6 (Least Privilege) as the framework controls that do not cover it.

new_control_requirements.name: FLEET-COMPROMISE-IR-PLAYBOOK
new_control_requirements.description: The packet pairs confirmed in-the-wild exploitation and a public PoC with a fix that the vendor notes typically requires a restart or reboot, which means every affected appliance had an exposure window and the update closes the authentication path without touching anything already done through it. Because the compromised asset is an endpoint-management appliance, the playbook has to cover what that appliance can reach and not just the appliance itself: review what it was configured to distribute to managed endpoints across the window running from first plausible exposure to the restart onto the fixed build, rotate the credentials the appliance holds for reaching those endpoints along with any operator account used through it during that window, invalidate device-trust state, and set quarantine criteria for endpoints that received anything from it in that period. The precondition worth naming is that the playbook must already exist and be rehearsed before the next disclosure, because the detection an operator would reach for first will not fire: the packet's own words are that the attacker impersonates legitimate users without valid credentials, so the activity presents as a legitimate operator and authentication-failure monitoring has nothing to surface. Patching alone answers the vulnerability question and leaves the compromise question unasked.

Between the KEV listing and the restart that lands the fix, the only coverage is behavioural — alert on anomalous Common Log File System driver activity from processes that have no business touching it, on process token and integrity-level transitions that promote a user-context process to SYSTEM, and on the escalate-then-move-laterally sequence — with alerting fast enough to interrupt a ransomware operator's dwell time rather than surface in the next day's report.

new_control_requirements.name: DOWNLOAD-PROVENANCE-ENFORCEMENT
new_control_requirements.description: Exploitation of this CVE requires the victim to open an attacker-controlled PDF, so on the long-tail hosts the packet says are still unpatched the delivery path is the only control left that can be enforced. response.what_would_have_worked: Patch immediately under the KEV SLA, then investigate for post-exploitation persistence and rotate credentials reachable from the FortiClient EMS management server.
response.adequacy: Mandatory for a KEV-listed unauthenticated flaw; patch-in-place without compromise assessment can leave attacker persistence.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: The 30-day flaw-remediation SLA is far longer than the observed exploitation window for a KEV-listed unauthenticated flaw; CISA KEV due dates are days, not a month.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: 'Appropriate timescales' is undefined; the standard 30-day reading is unsafe for an unauthenticated, actively-exploited flaw on an internet-facing management/infrastructure system.

new_control_requirements.name: SECURITY-TOOL-INTEGRITY-VERIFICATION
new_control_requirements.description: Put the FortiClient EMS server itself inside vulnerability-management scope at the SLA of the most privileged software in the estate, instead of wherever 'endpoint security product' falls in the OS-versus-application patch split. The exploited surface is the management server operators deploy in order to secure endpoints, and the flaw is reachable by an unauthenticated caller sending crafted requests — so the EMS build level is itself a security control, not an operations detail. Audits must establish the deployed EMS build from the server rather than from the console's own status view, and must include the trust-anchor-inversion test: send an unauthenticated crafted request to the EMS request handlers on a staging instance and confirm it is refused before any code or command runs. Remediation is a scheduled EMS outage: the entry registers no live-patch path and the vendor patch requires a service restart or reboot, so the security console is offline during its own fix and that window must be planned on the KEV clock rather than deferred to the routine cycle.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Packet: 'Fortinet FortiClient EMS contains an improper access control vulnerability that may allow an unauthenticated attacker to execute unauthorized code or commands via crafted requests' (CWE-284). CISA KEV-listed 2026-04-06, active_exploitation: confirmed, CVSS 8.8, RWEP 77, poc_available: true. patch_available: true with live_patch_available: false; live_patch_notes records 'No live-patch tool registered for this entry at bulk-import time. Vendor patch typically requires service restart or system reboot per the KEV requiredAction.'

new_control_requirements.name: ENDPOINT-MGMT-DEPLOYMENT-CHANNEL-INTEGRITY
new_control_requirements.description: Treat the EMS-to-FortiClient agent channel as a privileged supply-chain control plane for the duration of this exposure. Unauthenticated code or command execution on the EMS server hands an attacker the system that distributes configuration and software to every managed endpoint, so the blast radius is the agent fleet rather than one server: integrity-monitor the deployment artifacts and any key material the server holds, and alert on agent pushes and policy changes that do not correspond to a sanctioned admin action. Because the fix requires taking EMS down for a service restart, that monitoring has to span the outage and continue after it — restarting the server applies the patch but does not by itself evict anything placed through the flaw beforehand, and with exploitation confirmed in the wild an internet-reachable EMS instance is a forensic question, not a hypothetical. The distinguishing test: replay the deployment-artifact and key-table integrity baseline after the patch restart and confirm it matches the pre-exposure baseline.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Packet: improper access control (CWE-284) 'allowing an unauthenticated attacker to access functions or data beyond authorization', with the KEV description recording that it 'may allow an unauthenticated attacker to execute unauthorized code or commands via crafted requests'. CISA KEV-listed 2026-04-06, active_exploitation: confirmed, CVSS 8.8, RWEP 77, poc_available: true. live_patch_available: false and the vendor patch requires a service restart or system reboot per the KEV requiredAction.

new_control_requirements.name: FLEET-CONTROL-PLANE-ADMIN-PRIVILEGE-TIER
new_control_requirements.description: Classify FortiClient EMS as a fleet control plane and confine its reachability on that basis: the EMS console and its request handlers should be reachable only through a privileged administrative path (PAM jumphost or a dedicated admin segment), with EMS administration held as an identity separate from general IT or application admin roles and elevated just-in-time. Against this CVE the tier's operative benefit is reachability rather than authentication strength — the flaw is exercised pre-authentication via crafted requests, so any deployment that leaves the EMS request surface reachable from general user networks or the internet gives the attacker the entire path no matter how the EMS credentials are governed. Frameworks that enumerate a single 'admin' tier do not distinguish the server that governs every endpoint agent from an application administrator, which is why this network-position requirement has to be stated as its own control. The distinguishing test: from a general user subnet, attempt to reach the EMS request handlers and confirm the connection is refused at the network boundary before authentication is ever reached.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Packet: FortiClient EMS is exploited by 'an unauthenticated attacker to execute unauthorized code or commands via crafted requests' (CWE-284, improper access control). CISA KEV-listed 2026-04-06, active_exploitation: confirmed, CVSS 8.8, RWEP 77, poc_available: true. No live-patch tool is registered for this entry and the vendor patch requires a service restart or system reboot per the KEV requiredAction, so the exposure persists until an EMS restart window can be taken.

CVE-2026-3502.name: TrueConf Client Download of Code Without Integrity Check Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: the TrueConf client downloads code/updates without verifying their integrity (CWE-494), letting an attacker who can influence the download channel (a hijacked update endpoint or machine-in-the-middle) substitute malicious code that runs on the client. CISA KEV-listed 2026-04-02 with confirmed in-the-wild exploitation.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none (the attacker influences the download/update channel or the shipped artifact; no authentication to the victim is required)
attack_vector.complexity: low — KEV-listed, actively exploited; treat as weaponized
attack_vector.ai_factor: No AI involvement documented in discovery or weaponization.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Enforce cryptographic integrity verification on all downloaded code and updates (code signing with signature verification, Sigstore/in-toto, TLS-pinned update channels); for the embedded-malicious-code case, verify build provenance (SLSA) and pin/verify the tool's release artifacts before use.
prevention.adequacy: Signature and provenance verification is the definitive control; the flaw exists precisely because it was absent or unenforced — patching the version does not retroactively restore trust in artifacts already installed.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Monitoring for unexpected code/DLLs loaded by the TrueConf client, updates fetched over unauthenticated channels, and anomalous outbound connections or process execution from the tool.
detection.adequacy: Necessary because supply-chain substitution is silent — the tool runs as expected while the embedded/substituted code executes alongside it.

response.what_would_have_worked: Pull the affected version, reinstall from a verified-signed release, rotate any credentials the compromised process could reach, and audit every host where the tool ran — a compromised updater or scanner has broad reach.
response.adequacy: Mandatory; supply-chain compromise propagates through every host that ran the tainted code, so response is environment-wide, not host-local.

NIST-800-53-SR-11.gap: Component authenticity / anti-counterfeit is named, but verification is not enforced at install/update time — these products fetched or shipped code without a verified signature, so the control is paper unless signed-artifact verification (Sigstore/in-toto) is mandated at the download step.

NIST-SSDF-800-218-PS.2.gap: The SSDF calls for protecting release integrity and providing provenance, but downstream consumers had no enforced way to verify it; without signed releases plus provenance a consumer cannot detect substitution or embedded malicious code.

SLSA-build-provenance.gap: SLSA build provenance and signed releases would let a consumer detect tampering or substitution; absent enforced verification at the download/update step the trust gap remains open.

EU-CRA-secure-update.gap: The EU Cyber Resilience Act requires secure update mechanisms and shipping without known exploitable defects; an unauthenticated download path or embedded malicious code violates the secure-update and integrity expectations.

compliance_exposure_score.basis: Software-distribution and update integrity is widely assumed rather than verified; audited organizations that install vendor updates or run security tooling without enforcing signature/provenance verification are exposed to substitution and embedded-malicious-code attacks — and a compromised updater or scanner reaches every host it touches.

new_control_requirements.name: INDEPENDENT-INTEGRITY-VERIFICATION-OF-SIGNED-VENDOR-INSTALLERS
new_control_requirements.description: TrueConf Client fetches update code without verifying its integrity, so nothing on the client side distinguishes the vendor's build from one substituted by an attacker who has gained influence over the delivery path. The operator response is to stop letting the in-app updater be the trust decision: pull TrueConf Client builds through managed software distribution, verify each build against an integrity source independent of the download itself — vendor-published per-release hashes obtained over a separate channel, or a behavioural baseline of the installed binaries — and only then push it to endpoints. This is the harder form of the control's premise: the original lesson was that a valid signature is not proof of integrity, whereas here the client performs no verification step at all, so an out-of-band check is the only thing standing between a tampered payload and execution in the updating process's context.
new_control_requirements.evidence: The packet records a "download of code without integrity check vulnerability" (CWE-494) in which "An attacker who is able to influence the update delivery path can substitute a tampered update payload. If the payload is executed or installed by the updater, this may result in arbitrary code execution in the context of the updating process or user," and identifies the delivery-path influence as "a hijacked update endpoint or machine-in-the-middle." CISA KEV-listed 2026-04-02 with active_exploitation confirmed, poc_available true, CVSS 8.8, RWEP 77.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: The KEV clock here governs a client fleet rather than a single server: every endpoint running TrueConf Client is independently exploitable by whoever can influence its update fetch, so the fixed client has to reach all of them on the KEV window rather than on the ordinary endpoint-software refresh cycle. Two facts make the rollout a scheduled fleet action rather than a background update — the packet registers no live-patch tool for this entry, and the vendor patch typically requires a service restart or system reboot per the KEV requiredAction. Until the fixed build is present on a given endpoint, the interim posture is to keep that endpoint's updater off networks where the delivery path can be influenced, because the vulnerable client will accept whatever the channel returns.
new_control_requirements.evidence: cisa_kev is true with kev_date 2026-04-02 and active_exploitation confirmed; poc_available is true; patch_available is true and live_patch_available is false, with the packet noting "No live-patch tool registered for this entry at bulk-import time. Vendor patch typically requires service restart or system reboot per the KEV requiredAction." The exploitation precondition per the packet is an attacker who "can influence the download channel (a hijacked update endpoint or machine-in-the-middle)." CVSS 8.8, RWEP 77, CWE-494.

attack_vector.description: a use-after-free in Dawn / WebGPU (CWE-416) usable by an attacker who has already compromised the renderer, as a sandbox-escape step in an exploit chain. CISA KEV-listed 2026-04-01 with confirmed in-the-wild exploitation.
attack_vector.privileges_required: low (a prior renderer compromise; this is a sandbox-escape step in a chain)
attack_vector.complexity: low — KEV-listed, actively exploited; treat as weaponized
attack_vector.ai_factor: No AI involvement documented in discovery or weaponization.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Update Chrome / Chromium-based browsers to the patched build via auto-update; the WebGPU surface can be disabled by policy on managed fleets pending the update.
prevention.adequacy: Browser/app auto-update is definitive and fast for unmanaged endpoints; the gap is managed fleets that gate updates behind a change window slower than the in-the-wild exploitation.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Endpoint monitoring for browser renderer / GPU process crashes on content render and for unexpected child processes spawned by the browser renderer / GPU process after rendering attacker-controlled web content after a renderer compromise.
detection.adequacy: Detection backstops endpoints not yet updated; client exploitation is fast and often single-interaction.

response.what_would_have_worked: Force the browser/application update across the fleet, then run an EDR sweep on endpoints that rendered untrusted attacker-controlled web content after a renderer compromise before the update.
response.adequacy: Mandatory for a KEV-listed client RCE; the exposure is every endpoint that opened attacker content pre-patch.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: The 30-day flaw-remediation SLA is far longer than the observed exploitation window for a KEV-listed, actively-exploited client RCE delivered by attacker-controlled content.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: 'Appropriate timescales' is undefined; the standard reading is unsafe for an actively-exploited browser/document-reader memory-corruption flaw reachable by drive-by content.

AU-ISM-1546.gap: Essential 8 patch-applications (48h at ML3) is closer to the operational reality for a client RCE than a 30-day cycle, but still trails same-day browser auto-update for an in-the-wild exploit.

compliance_exposure_score.basis: Google Chrome (Dawn / WebGPU) is ubiquitous on endpoints; audited organizations that gate client updates behind a managed change window (rather than allowing same-day auto-update) were exposed for this KEV-listed, actively-exploited flaw.

new_control_requirements.name: BROWSER-MANAGED-UPDATE-NO-DEFERRAL
new_control_requirements.description: The fix for this Dawn/WebGPU use-after-free reaches endpoints only as a browser security-channel release, so any managed update ring that pins a version or holds the security channel for staging leaves the sandbox-escape link of the chain live fleet-wide. Managed browser policy has to let the security channel land within 24h and force the relaunch that actually replaces the running GPU process — an updated binary on disk beside a browser session that has not been restarted is still executing the vulnerable Dawn code.
new_control_requirements.evidence: KEV-listed 2026-04-01 with confirmed in-the-wild exploitation, a public PoC, and a patch available; the flaw is the sandbox-escape step used after the renderer is already compromised, so it is the link that converts a contained renderer bug into host code execution.

new_control_requirements.name: SCANNER-PAPER-COMPLIANCE-TEST
new_control_requirements.description: A scan that reports the installed browser version as fixed does not prove this defect is gone. Dawn is Chromium's WebGPU implementation, so the same component ships inside Chromium-derived browsers and inside desktop applications that embed Chromium, each on its own update cadence and none of them moved by the browser's updater. The operational test: does the scan enumerate every Chromium-embedding runtime on the host as a separate versioned asset, record whether WebGPU is reachable in each, and read the version of the running process rather than the installed package?
new_control_requirements.evidence: Patch available and KEV-listed 2026-04-01 with confirmed exploitation; the packet locates the flaw in Dawn/WebGPU rather than in a single vendor application, and exploitation requires prior renderer compromise, so the escape path only matters where a vulnerable Dawn build is actually loaded.

attack_vector.description: an out-of-bounds read (CWE-125) on Citrix NetScaler, disclosing adjacent memory used to steal authenticated session material. CISA KEV-listed 2026-03-30 with confirmed in-the-wild exploitation.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none (the flaw is reachable by an unauthenticated attacker on the appliance's public interface)
attack_vector.complexity: low — KEV-listed, actively exploited; treat as weaponized
attack_vector.ai_factor: No AI involvement documented in discovery or weaponization.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Apply the Citrix NetScaler security update; invalidate active sessions and rotate session secrets — a patch alone does not revoke tokens already exfiltrated from memory.
prevention.adequacy: Patch is necessary but insufficient alone: tokens already disclosed from memory survive the patch and must be revoked via session termination + secret rotation.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Monitoring on the NetScaler: exploit-shaped requests, oversized/leaked response bodies (for the OOB-read class), appliance crashes (for the memory-corruption class), and session reuse with no matching login event.
detection.adequacy: Necessary to catch token-theft and post-exploit footholds that survive patching.

response.what_would_have_worked: Patch immediately; for the OOB-read class terminate sessions and rotate secrets, for the RCE class rebuild the appliance from a known-good image and rotate all credentials it held; review for lateral movement off the edge plane.
response.adequacy: Mandatory; a patch-in-place without session revocation or appliance rebuild leaves the attacker resident or with stolen session material.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: The 30-day flaw-remediation SLA is far longer than the observed exploitation window for a KEV-listed flaw on an internet-facing perimeter appliance; CitrixBleed-class disclosures were mass-exploited within days.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: 'Appropriate timescales' is undefined; the standard 30-day reading is unsafe for an actively-exploited perimeter-appliance flaw.

NIS2-Art21-network-security.gap: Treats perimeter appliances as essential-function infrastructure but lacks a CISA-KEV-style compressed remediation SLA, and does not mandate the session-revocation/credential-rotation cleanup these memory-disclosure flaws require.

PCI-DSS-4.0-6.3.3.gap: The 30-day critical-patch window is exploitation acceptance for an internet-facing edge appliance fronting the CDE.

compliance_exposure_score.basis: Citrix NetScaler is a load-bearing perimeter device run by audited organizations on standard change-controlled patch windows; the required session-revocation/rebuild cleanup is rarely part of the documented patch procedure.

new_control_requirements.name: PERIMETER-DEVICE-ZERODAY-SLA-TIER
new_control_requirements.description: When NetScaler is configured as a SAML IDP it is the authentication enforcement point for everything behind it, so its remediation tier cannot be derived from the CVE's severity band. This entry reads as a low-severity information disclosure by CVSS, yet the memory it overreads is authenticated session material and it is KEV-listed with confirmed in-the-wild exploitation — the RWEP score is 77 against a CVSS of 5.5. A vulnerability-management program that sorts by CVSS puts this appliance in the routine maintenance window. The tier requirement for this CVE: the update is due on the KEV clock, or the SAML IDP virtual server is taken out of service until the appliance is on a fixed build. Nothing upstream compensates, because the vulnerable device is the trust boundary the upstream controls delegate to.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Packet: out-of-bounds read (CWE-125) on NetScaler ADC, NetScaler Gateway and NetScaler ADC FIPS/NDcPP when configured as a SAML IDP, leading to memory overread; the attack vector is described as disclosing adjacent memory used to steal authenticated session material. cisa_kev true, kev_date 2026-03-30, active_exploitation confirmed, poc_available true; cvss 5.5 against rwep_score 77.

new_control_requirements.name: PERIMETER-COMPROMISE-REBUILD-NOT-PATCH
new_control_requirements.description: Updating this appliance stops the overread but does nothing about what has already left it. The exploited primitive hands an attacker authenticated session material read out of the SAML IDP's memory, and that material stays valid after the fix is applied — the vulnerability is closed while the access it produced is not. Remediation for this CVE must be run as compromise response rather than maintenance: once the appliance is on a fixed build, terminate every active session, rotate and reissue the session and signing secrets the IDP holds, rotate credentials that traversed it, and review the authentications it brokered during the exposure window (from KEV listing back through the earliest plausible exploitation). Patch-in-place with standing sessions is the failure mode this control exists to prevent.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Packet: out-of-bounds read (CWE-125) in the SAML IDP path of NetScaler, disclosing adjacent memory used to steal authenticated session material; active_exploitation confirmed, cisa_kev true with kev_date 2026-03-30, poc_available true. patch_available true, live_patch_available false, live_patch_notes recording no registered live-patch tool and a vendor patch that typically requires service restart or system reboot per the KEV requiredAction.

attack_vector.description: a stack-based buffer overflow (CWE-121) exploitable by an unauthenticated attacker for memory-corruption remote code execution on the appliance. CISA KEV-listed 2026-03-27 with confirmed in-the-wild exploitation.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none (the device/appliance is reachable by an unauthenticated attacker on its network interface)
attack_vector.complexity: low — KEV-listed, actively exploited; treat as weaponized
attack_vector.ai_factor: No AI involvement documented in discovery or weaponization.

detection.adequacy: Necessary because device/appliance compromise is often silent and persists across reboots in firmware/config.

PCI-DSS-4.0-6.3.3.gap: The 30-day critical-patch window is exploitation acceptance for an internet-facing network device or edge appliance fronting or bridging the CDE.

new_control_requirements.name: PERIMETER-DEVICE-ZERODAY-SLA-TIER
new_control_requirements.description: A BIG-IP APM appliance is the trust boundary for the remote-access path it fronts, so the routine 14/30-day windows generic vulnerability-management controls allow are the wrong clock for an unauthenticated stack-based overflow reaching code execution on its data path. This CVE belongs in a perimeter tier: vendor fix deployed within hours of the KEV listing, or the vulnerable virtual server and management interface taken out of untrusted reach until it can be. The packet records no live-patch path for this entry and a vendor fix that requires a service restart or system reboot per the KEV requiredAction, so the SLA has to pre-authorize a failover or downtime window on the appliance itself. Frameworks that grade patch timeliness on a single estate-wide average let a 9.8 pre-auth RCE on the device that terminates remote access sit inside an acceptable-looking metric.
new_control_requirements.evidence: F5 BIG-IP APM stack-based buffer overflow (CWE-121), CVSS 9.8, RWEP 77, exploitable by an unauthenticated attacker for memory-corruption remote code execution on the appliance. CISA KEV-listed 2026-03-27 with confirmed in-the-wild exploitation and poc_available=true. patch_available=true, live_patch_available=false; the entry states the vendor patch typically requires service restart or system reboot per the KEV requiredAction.

new_control_requirements.name: PERIMETER-COMPROMISE-REBUILD-NOT-PATCH
new_control_requirements.description: Confirmed in-the-wild exploitation plus a public PoC against an unauthenticated RCE on BIG-IP APM means any appliance that was network-reachable before the fix has to be treated as possibly already running attacker code, not merely as unpatched. The default IR path for this CVE is capture the running configuration off the box, rebuild the appliance from vendor media, and rotate the credentials and keys the appliance held or proxied before it returns to service. Installing the vendor fix removes the overflow; it does not remove anything an operator installed through the overflow beforehand, and the restart the fix requires is a convenient moment for an implant to reload. A compliance verdict of remediated based on the installed version alone is the failure this control exists to prevent.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Unauthenticated memory-corruption RCE on the appliance (CWE-121, CVSS 9.8, RWEP 77), active_exploitation=confirmed, poc_available=true, CISA KEV-listed 2026-03-27. patch_available=true with live_patch_available=false and a vendor patch that typically requires service restart or system reboot per the KEV requiredAction.

new_control_requirements.name: FIREWALL-EGRESS-TELEMETRY-SEPARATE-TRUST-ZONE
new_control_requirements.description: Code execution on BIG-IP APM is code execution on the device that writes the access and authentication records for the remote-access path it fronts, so the appliance's local log store cannot answer whether it was hit before the fix landed. Syslog, access-policy and authentication events must already be landing on a collector in a separate trust zone, with different credentials and a different management path, and retained far enough back to cover the window preceding the 2026-03-27 KEV listing. Without that, the rebuild-versus-patch decision this CVE forces is made with no evidence, and the exposure window can only be guessed at from the disclosure date rather than measured.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Confirmed in-the-wild exploitation of an unauthenticated RCE on the appliance (CWE-121, CVSS 9.8, RWEP 77) with poc_available=true, CISA KEV-listed 2026-03-27; remediation requires a service restart or system reboot per the KEV requiredAction with no live-patch path registered.

Remediation per the packet: patch_available is true but live_patch_available is false, and live_patch_notes record that the vendor patch typically requires a service restart or system reboot per the KEV requiredAction — so the fix is a pipeline-image/binary replacement with restart, not an in-place hot fix. Because the packet's vector states the attacker reaches every token, SSH key, cloud credential, database password and in-memory configuration in the CI/CD environment, every secret a Trivy step could read during the exposure window must be treated as disclosed.

Prompt injection must be modeled as a code-execution primitive, not a content-safety nuisance.

CVE-2026-24207.name: NVIDIA Triton Inference Server Authentication Bypass (Alternate Path) RCE

attack_vector.complexity: low (NVD AC:L)

CVE-2025-1550.name: Keras .keras Model Deserialization Arbitrary Code Execution

attack_vector.privileges_required: none beyond getting a victim to load an untrusted .keras model
attack_vector.complexity: low
attack_vector.ai_factor: The abused surface is the ML model file format itself — the canonical AI supply-chain risk: an untrusted model artifact is executable code at load time. The lesson, sharpened by the CVE-2025-1550 -> CVE-2025-8747 sequence, is that model artifacts must be treated as untrusted code (provenance, scanning, safe formats like safetensors), and a partial mitigation such as safe_mode is necessary-but-insufficient when it can be bypassed.

ALL-AI-PIPELINE-INTEGRITY.gap: No framework treats an ML model file as untrusted executable input; loading one from an untrusted source is RCE.

compliance_exposure_score.basis: ML pipelines pull models from hubs and user uploads and treat them as data; safe_mode is assumed sufficient despite the documented bypass.

new_control_requirements.description: Treat ML model artifacts as untrusted code: never load .keras / pickle-based models from untrusted sources, verify provenance, prefer safe formats (e.g. safetensors), and load untrusted models only in a sandboxed, network-isolated, least-privilege environment. CVE-2024-42479.name: llama.cpp RPC Backend SET_TENSOR Out-of-Bounds Write RCE

attack_vector.description: llama.cpp's RPC backend deserializes attacker-controlled tensor pointers without bounds validation (CWE-787/CWE-123 write-what-where via SET_TENSOR), so an unauthenticated TCP client to the RPC server (default port 50052) reads/writes arbitrary memory and achieves code execution.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none (NVD AV:N / PR:N) — unauthenticated TCP access to the RPC server
attack_vector.complexity: low (NVD AC:L)
attack_vector.ai_factor: The abused surface is the distributed-inference RPC backend of the most widely used local LLM runtime. The lesson: the inference RPC backend is an unauthenticated execution boundary that must validate all deserialized tensor bounds on every command path and never be network-exposed. The CVE-2024-42478/42479 -> CVE-2026-34159 sequence shows per-command patching (GET/SET) left GRAPH_COMPUTE exploitable — the fix belongs in deserialize_tensor itself.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: Does not track the local-LLM runtime's RPC backend as RCE-bearing, nor that the first fix left the GRAPH_COMPUTE path unpatched.

NIST-800-53-SC-7.gap: Does not flag the unauthenticated RPC server (port 50052) as a network-exposed execution surface.

ALL-AI-PIPELINE-INTEGRITY.gap: No framework requires the inference RPC backend to validate deserialized tensor bounds on every command path.

compliance_exposure_score.basis: Local-LLM RPC servers are run on trusted-network assumptions and rarely tracked; per-command patches are assumed complete despite the GRAPH_COMPUTE bypass.

new_control_requirements.name: AI-INFERENCE-RPC-BACKEND-HARDENING
new_control_requirements.description: The inference RPC backend (llama.cpp / ggml) must validate all deserialized tensor bounds inside deserialize_tensor itself — every command path (GET_TENSOR, SET_TENSOR, GRAPH_COMPUTE), not per-handler — and must never be exposed to untrusted networks (the RPC server on port 50052 has no authentication; bind to localhost or a trusted segment). Upgrade llama.cpp to b8492 or later — b3561 fixed only GET_TENSOR / SET_TENSOR (CVE-2024-42478 / CVE-2024-42479), and builds b3561 through b8491 remain exploitable via the GRAPH_COMPUTE buffer=0 path (CVE-2026-34159), which b8492 closes. The distinguishing test: send a crafted rpc_tensor with buffer=0 / out-of-range data pointer via GRAPH_COMPUTE to a staging RPC server and confirm it is rejected, not dereferenced.
new_control_requirements.evidence: https://github.com/ggerganov/llama.cpp/security/advisories/GHSA-wcr5-566p-9cwj

CVE-2023-43654.name: PyTorch TorchServe Management API SSRF to Remote Code Execution (ShellTorch)

CVE-2024-37032.name: Ollama Model Registry Path Traversal Arbitrary File Write RCE (Probllama)

attack_vector.description: Ollama CWE-22 path traversal via unvalidated model-blob digest: an attacker reaching the Ollama HTTP API (default port 11434) manipulates a path/digest the runtime then uses against the filesystem, writing attacker content to an arbitrary path and achieving RCE.
attack_vector.privileges_required: low / network (NVD PR:L) — reachable via the Ollama API + a rogue registry
attack_vector.complexity: low (NVD AC:L)
attack_vector.ai_factor: The abused surface is the model-pull / model API of the most widely used local LLM runtime. The lesson: the model-runtime API must validate digests and path parameters and must never be network-exposed to untrusted clients; pulling from untrusted registries is a supply-chain trust decision.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: Does not track the local-LLM runtime as managed, network-exposed software.

NIST-800-53-SI-10.gap: Input validation is not applied to model-blob digests / API path parameters in the runtime.

ALL-AI-PIPELINE-INTEGRITY.gap: No framework treats the model-runtime API's path/digest handling as untrusted input reaching the filesystem.

compliance_exposure_score.basis: Local-LLM runtimes are run on trusted-network assumptions and rarely tracked; model pulls from arbitrary registries are not gated.

new_control_requirements.name: AI-RUNTIME-API-PATH-TRAVERSAL-VALIDATION
new_control_requirements.description: The model-runtime API must validate path-bearing inputs (model-blob digests must be exactly 64-hex SHA256; API route parameters must reject traversal sequences) before touching the filesystem, must not be exposed to untrusted networks (Ollama default port 11434), and must only pull models from trusted registries. The AI-security lesson: an AI agent/workflow orchestration platform is itself an RCE-bearing web trust boundary — compromising it grants control over every model, tool, and credential it brokers. NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: 30-day flaw-remediation SLA inadequate for a KEV-listed, in-the-wild-exploited RCE; the CISA KEV due date is the binding clock.

compliance_exposure_score.basis: Self-hosted AI-platform deployments rarely audit CORS / session-cookie configuration; audit programs check patch SLA and TLS but not application-layer origin policy. Exposure widened by Langflow's 140k-star footprint and the drive-by trigger (victim need only visit a page).

The platform's session boundary is a remote-code-execution boundary and must be reviewed as one.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: 30-day SLA inadequate for a KEV-listed LPE; KEV due date (2026-06-03) is the binding clock, and engine-version currency is not a tracked remediation target.

new_control_requirements.description: The remediation unit here is not an OS package but a Composer-managed component living inside every Laravel application that uses Livewire, so the KEV clock has to be run against an inventory of applications rather than an inventory of hosts. The packet qualifies the flaw as reaching unauthenticated remote command execution in specific scenarios, which is the reason a host-level scan is not sufficient evidence of closure: an operator cannot tell from a server inventory which applications sit in the exposed configuration. With confirmed in-the-wild exploitation from the 2026-03-20 listing, the four-hour target starts at KEV listing / patch availability rather than at the next release train, and a Laravel estate whose deploys are gated on a weekly window has no way to meet it without an out-of-band path for a single dependency bump. The distinguishing test: on a production host, confirm the Livewire version actually loaded by the running PHP workers is the fixed one — not the version declared in the repository lockfile, which says what the next deploy will ship, not what is serving traffic now.

new_control_requirements.name: PERIMETER-COMPROMISE-REBUILD-NOT-PATCH
new_control_requirements.description: Livewire's defect runs attacker-supplied code inside the PHP process that serves the request, with no credential required, and the packet records confirmed in-the-wild exploitation from the 2026-03-20 listing. Any internet-reachable Laravel application that was serving traffic during that window therefore has to be triaged as possibly compromised rather than closed out when the dependency is bumped: updating the package removes the injection sink but removes nothing the injected code already did — a PHP file written under the application's public or storage tree, a poisoned compiled view or cached container file, a queued job, an added administrative user, or a read of the application's environment file that handed over its database, cache, mail and third-party API credentials in one request. The control for this deployment: redeploy the application from the build pipeline onto a clean host image rather than patching the running one, restore the code tree from version control rather than editing in place, and rotate every secret the application process could read, since the exploit path could read all of them. new_control_requirements.name: SCANNER-PAPER-COMPLIANCE-TEST
new_control_requirements.description: A nine-year-old unauthenticated-administrator flaw surviving to a 2026 KEV listing is what a vulnerability-management program looks like when its scanning coverage stops at servers and workstations. Bound to this entry, the test is whether the estate's scan actually reaches each Hikvision device and reads the firmware it is running, and whether the verdict is derived from a build known to contain the fix rather than from an asset record, a VMS inventory page, or the installer's handover document — all of which describe what was deployed at commissioning, not what is executing now. A camera subnet excluded from scanning, or scanned only for open ports without ever interrogating the device, returns a clean result that is indistinguishable from a compliant one, and that clean result is what an operator would otherwise present as evidence of managing technical vulnerabilities. Distinguishing test: produce, per Hikvision device, the firmware version the device itself reports and the date that scan ran, and confirm the version carries the vendor fix; any device for which the program can produce a compliance verdict but not a device-reported firmware string has been counted as compliant without being examined.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Packet: CVE published against Hikvision products in 2017 and CISA KEV-listed 2026-03-05 with active_exploitation confirmed and poc_available true; improper authentication (CWE-287) allowing an unauthenticated attacker to escalate to administrator; patch_available true; citing gaps include ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.8 management of technical vulnerabilities.

CVE-2021-22681.name: Rockwell Multiple Products Insufficient Protected Credentials Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: an insufficiently-protected-credentials flaw (CWE-522) in the Studio 5000 / Logix secret-key handling, letting an unauthenticated attacker bypass authentication and connect to the PLC to alter its configuration or control logic. CISA KEV-listed 2026-03-05 with confirmed in-the-wild exploitation.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none (the device is reachable by an unauthenticated attacker; exposure is amplified when the OT zone is not segmented)
attack_vector.complexity: low — KEV-listed, actively exploited; treat as weaponized
attack_vector.ai_factor: No AI involvement documented in discovery or weaponization.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Apply the vendor firmware/update where one exists; where the device cannot be patched, isolate it in a segmented OT zone (zones-and-conduits / Purdue model), block all IT and internet reachability, and restrict access to authenticated engineering workstations.
prevention.adequacy: Patching is often impossible on OT; segmentation and access restriction are the real controls, and a flat or internet-exposed OT network defeats them.

detection.what_would_have_worked: OT-network monitoring for unauthorized connections to the Rockwell Logix PLC, unexpected configuration/logic changes, and access from outside the device's intended zone.
detection.adequacy: Necessary because unpatched OT devices may stay exploitable indefinitely; behavioral detection is the backstop.

response.what_would_have_worked: Isolate the device, validate and restore its configuration/logic from a known-good baseline, rotate any credentials/keys it held, and investigate for safety-impacting manipulation; engage OT/safety engineering before any change.
response.adequacy: Mandatory; OT compromise can have physical/safety consequences, so response must include process-integrity validation, not just IT cleanup.

NIST-800-82r3-ICS.gap: OT/ICS devices often cannot be patched on an IT cadence (availability and safety constraints, vendor re-certification), so the exposure window for a KEV-listed flaw is months-to-years; the standard treats patching as primary but for OT the load-bearing control is network segmentation and access restriction.

IEC-62443-3-3-zones-conduits.gap: Zones-and-conduits segmentation is required, but it is frequently unimplemented or bypassed (flat OT networks, internet-exposed HMIs/cameras/PLCs); the device itself is exploitable whenever it is reachable, and the standard does not force a compromised-device response plan.

NIS2-Art21-OT.gap: Treats OT/ICS as essential-function infrastructure but lacks a device-level compressed remediation expectation and does not address the reality that many OT devices are end-of-life or unpatchable and must be isolated rather than fixed.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: 'Appropriate timescales' is undefined and ill-suited to OT, where patching may be impossible; compensating controls (segmentation, monitoring, restricted engineering-workstation access) carry the load and must be explicit.

compliance_exposure_score.basis: Rockwell Automation Logix controllers is OT/ICS equipment that frequently cannot be patched on an IT cadence and is often reachable on flat or internet-exposed networks; audited organizations that rely on a patch SLA rather than enforced segmentation remain exposed for this KEV-listed, actively-exploited flaw.

new_control_requirements.name: OT-DEFAULT-CREDENTIAL-ELIMINATION
new_control_requirements.description: The packet states this exploit's only access requirement outright: an unauthorized user would require network access to the controller. So on this entry the segmentation half of this control is the load-bearing half, and the credential-elimination half is not a lever the operator holds — the key that authenticates design software to Logix controllers is discoverable from Studio 5000 itself rather than set per site, so there is no vendor-default or blank administrative account for the operator to rotate away. Applied here, it means the Logix controllers' network interfaces answer only from a segmented engineering and management plane — the engineering workstations and servers with an operational need to program them — and not from a flat plant network, a general business VLAN, or any routable path from outside. Distinguishing test: from a segment with no programming role, attempt to open a connection to a Logix controller on a staging cell; anything that answers is within reach of the published exploit, because past that point the attacker supplies the key from the design software rather than obtaining anything from the target. Precondition: segmentation bounds the population that can reach the controller, it does not repair the key handling. The packet's stated requirement is only network access to the controller, so any compromised engineering workstation, contractor laptop or jump host already inside the permitted segment satisfies that precondition in full, and the segmentation does nothing against an unauthorized application running on a host that legitimately talks to the controller. It is a holding measure for the window before the vendor update, not a closure.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Packet vector: 'This key is used to verify Logix controllers are communicating with Rockwell Automation design software. If successfully exploited, this vulnerability could allow an unauthorized application to connect with Logix controllers. To leverage this vulnerability, an unauthorized user would require network access to the controller.' Packet: CISA KEV listed 2026-03-05, active_exploitation confirmed, poc_available true, RWEP 77, CVSS 8.8.

new_control_requirements.name: FRAMEWORK-DEFAULT-SECRET-DETECTION
new_control_requirements.description: The packet puts the secret inside the product: Studio 5000 Logix Designer 'may allow a key to be discovered', and that key is what verifies Logix controllers are communicating with Rockwell design software. Because the constant an attacker needs is obtainable from the design software rather than from the target site, no amount of operator-side credential hygiene reduces the exposure — which is exactly why the least-privilege and identity-and-access-control gaps are recorded against this entry: the attacker never authenticates as any engineer, so per-account privilege scoping is never consulted and the account model an identity attestation examines is bypassed rather than abused. The control's requirement here is to inventory every Studio 5000 installation and every Logix controller in the estate as depending on a product-shipped verification key, gate each of those deployments on the vendor update rather than on a password or account policy, and re-run that check after any engineering-workstation rebuild, image restore or controller replacement, since those are the operations that quietly reintroduce an unpatched pairing at a site that had been remediated. Distinguishing test: produce, per cell, the Studio 5000 version and the controller firmware actually in service and show each is at or above the vendor's fixed level — an attestation that every engineer holds a unique Studio 5000 account passes cleanly while this flaw stays fully exploitable. Precondition: the vendor update is what removes the dependence on the discoverable key; this control is the inventory and the gate that ensure every installation reaches it, and it gives nothing on its own to a site that has not yet taken the update. It also does not detect a controller an unauthorized application has already connected to, so a cell that was reachable during the exposure window needs its controller configuration and control logic compared against a known-good copy rather than being closed on the patch.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Packet vector: 'Studio 5000 Logix Designer software may allow a key to be discovered. This key is used to verify Logix controllers are communicating with Rockwell Automation design software.' CWE-522. Citing gaps record NIST-800-53-AC-6 (Least Privilege) and UK-CAF-B2 (Identity and access control) against this entry. patch_available true; active_exploitation confirmed; poc_available true.

new_control_requirements.name: MITIGATION-ACTIVE-PATCH-PENDING-VERDICT-CLASS
new_control_requirements.description: The packet records a vendor patch, no live-patch path, and a fix that per the KEV requiredAction typically requires a service restart or system reboot. On Logix controllers driving a live process, that restart is scheduled against the process rather than against the 2026-03-05 KEV clock, which produces a long interval in which the estate's real state is 'reachability restricted, patch pending' — not remediated. This control requires that state to be recorded distinctly for each affected cell: the compensating control actually in force (the controller-reachability restriction), the residual risk it leaves (any host already inside the permitted segment still meets the exploit's only stated precondition, network access to the controller), and a dated action item tied to the next outage window in which the restart can be taken. It must not be reported as 'patched per SLA' and the KEV row must not be closed on the basis of the update having been obtained. Precondition and limit: this is a reporting-integrity control, not a technical mitigation — it changes what the audit sees, not what the attacker can reach, and it is only honest if the compensating control it records has been tested against a staging cell rather than asserted from a network diagram.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Packet: patch_available true, live_patch_available false; live_patch_notes: 'No live-patch tool registered for this entry at bulk-import time. Vendor patch typically requires service restart or system reboot per the KEV requiredAction.' CISA KEV listed 2026-03-05, active_exploitation confirmed. Packet vector: 'To leverage this vulnerability, an unauthorized user would require network access to the controller.'
