new_control_requirements.description: The affected surface here is the general-purpose Apple estate — macOS, iOS, iPadOS and Safari — where Apple ships the fix but it only reaches a device when a user accepts a restart, and this class of flaw is reached simply by rendering a web page. Enforce the update through device management against a hard deadline measured from the 2026-03-05 KEV listing rather than a notification: push a declarative software-update deadline, remove the deferral option, and quarantine devices past the deadline from organisational data. A management console that reports how many devices are behind is not the control — the enforcement is. The citing patch controls are satisfied by an estate-wide policy existing; this entry is exploited on the individual handset that deferred.

new_control_requirements.name: MOBILE-ZERO-CLICK-HARDENING
new_control_requirements.description: Reachability is ordinary web-content rendering, so the exposure is live for anyone who opens a page or previews a link in the interval between disclosure and the device actually restarting — and the packet places this class in targeted-spyware chains, which means a named cohort (executives, legal, journalists, security staff) carries far more of the risk than the estate average. Put that cohort in the platform's reduced-attack-surface mode (Lockdown Mode) as standing configuration, not as an incident response, so the complex web-content processing paths this use-after-free is reached through are not exercised at all. This is compensating cover for the gap between disclosure and restart — the Apple update still has to land, and NEW-CTRL-056 is what makes it land.

new_control_requirements.evidence: The packet's vector states that Apple tvOS, macOS, Safari, iPadOS and watchOS contain an integer overflow or wraparound arising from the processing of maliciously crafted web content that may lead to arbitrary code execution (CWE-190). cisa_kev is true with kev_date 2026-03-05, active_exploitation is confirmed, poc_available is true, and rwep_score is 77 against a CVSS of 8.8. patch_available is true, live_patch_available is false, and live_patch_notes states the vendor patch typically requires a service restart or system reboot per the KEV requiredAction — so the fixed build plus a reboot is the entire remediation and the only variable an operator controls is how quickly both happen. new_control_requirements.name: MOBILE-ZERO-CLICK-HARDENING
new_control_requirements.description: Users at elevated targeting risk must run their Apple devices in a reduced-attack-surface mode rather than relying on the update clock alone for this flaw. The packet's vector puts the trigger in the processing of maliciously crafted web content, which means exposure begins the moment a device renders an attacker's page or a message that automatically previews one — before any operator decision is available. Since the packet records no live-patch option and states the fix requires a restart or reboot, there is a period between disclosure and rebooted-and-fixed during which nothing in the patch programme protects the device; a mode that suppresses automatic processing of untrusted content is the only prevention that operates inside it. The enrolment decision therefore has to be taken for the at-risk population ahead of the next disclosure, since enrolling in response to a KEV listing repeats the same lag the control exists to remove.

new_control_requirements.name: FLEET-CONTROL-PLANE-ADMIN-PRIVILEGE-TIER
new_control_requirements.description: Classify the Aria Operations administrators and the appliance's own integration/service identities as a management-plane privilege tier above ordinary application admins, instead of folding them into the generic admin scope that AC-6 is audited against. This does not prevent the vulnerability — no admin tiering gates an unauthenticated request, and the packet's attacker needs no credential — but it bounds what the attacker inherits the moment command execution lands on the appliance. Under the tier, the standing estate-integration credentials the appliance holds become just-in-time, approval-gated grants rather than always-live ones; the Aria console is reachable only from a PAM jumphost rather than from general internal networks; and the identities used to administer it are distinct from any other admin role, so credentials or sessions captured on a compromised appliance are not replayable against the rest of the estate. new_control_requirements.name: DEVICE-MANAGEMENT-GATEWAY-CONFIG-ENDPOINT-AUTH-INPUT-NEUTRALIZATION
new_control_requirements.description: Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Controller (formerly SD-WAN vSmart) and Catalyst SD-WAN Manager (formerly SD-WAN vManage) are the management plane the packet names, and the defect sits on the interface where they authenticate fabric peers: the packet states the peering authentication mechanism in an affected system is not working properly, so crafted requests let an unauthenticated remote attacker log in as an internal, high-privileged, non-root user account, access NETCONF from it, and manipulate network configuration for the SD-WAN fabric. Distinguishing test: from a segment carrying no SD-WAN fabric role, send unauthenticated peering requests to a staging Controller and Manager and confirm each is refused before any session is issued, then attempt a NETCONF session from that same origin and confirm it is refused too — an estate that audits vManage operator roles and passes remains fully exposed to the path the packet describes, because the path never touches those roles. Precondition: repairing the peering authentication mechanism is what the vendor update does; this control states the property to verify and does not implement it. Until that update and the restart the packet's live-patch note requires have landed, restricting which segments can present requests bounds who can attempt the bypass but leaves it fully available to anything inside the permitted segment — and because a fabric's peers are distributed by design, the peering interface must stay reachable to those peers for the overlay to work, so the restriction is partial by construction rather than a closure.

For any unit that untrusted callers could reach before its fix and restart landed — and the KEV listing dates confirmed exploitation to at least 2026-02-24 — the vendor update restores the code and nothing else: an added account, a scheduled job, an altered configuration, or any file written through the command sink survives the upgrade untouched, because the fix closes the path and does not undo what already traversed it. The default disposition for such a unit is therefore configuration capture, rebuild, and credential rotation rather than patch-in-place. Two preconditions are load-bearing. The rebuild only yields a clean appliance if it is built at or above the vendor's fixed level — rebuilding to the pre-fix level puts the identical vulnerable HTTP path straight back on the network — and the credentials the appliance held (its administrative accounts, any directory-integration or service accounts, any keys shared with transfer partners) must be rotated after the rebuild completes rather than before, or the clean unit is handed the same secrets. This control also does not establish what left the appliance: files that transited FileZen during the exposure window need their own disclosure assessment, which no amount of rebuilding performs. Distinguishing test: for each unit, ask what evidence excludes exploitation during the window rather than what evidence proves it — a flaw-remediation record showing the fixed version installed reads clean on an appliance that was executing attacker-supplied commands the week before.

new_control_requirements.name: CONTROL-PANEL-PLUGIN-USER-SURFACE-MUST-NOT-REACH-ROOT-OPERATIONS
new_control_requirements.description: The packet's vector conditions this exploit on a product login: FileZen 'contains an OS command injection vulnerability when an user logs-in to the affected product and sends a specially crafted HTTP request'. That is the shape this control forbids — a constrained user surface, here the web interface of a file-transfer product, wired through to an operating-system command interpreter on the appliance host, so that holding a FileZen account amounts to holding command execution on the box. Bound to this product, the requirement is that no FileZen request handler composes an OS command from request-supplied content, and that the transfer functions reach the operating system only through a constrained, validated interface. This is why the least-privilege gap cited on this entry stays open however carefully FileZen accounts are scoped: the request crosses out of the application into the OS regardless of which directories or transfer rights the account carries, so an access-control attestation passes cleanly while the path is fully reachable. new_control_requirements.description: The packet records this flaw as a later variant of the Roundcube XSS class, and that word is the finding. The sink is an animate tag inside an SVG document — markup the message renderer's sanitizer was already supposed to be filtering — so what the CVE demonstrates is not one missed tag but that the allowlist governing SVG and animation markup in the mail body renderer keeps admitting script, one element at a time. Per-CVE severity scoring cannot express that: each instance lands as another 6.1 reflected-script issue, the structural defect never surfaces, and the operator has no basis for predicting the next one. A vulnerability-management program covering webmail must therefore carry a multiplier for the Nth flaw on the same sanitizer primitive — escalating handling above what the base score alone would trigger, and treating the renderer's markup filter as a standing area of exposure that warrants defence at the rendering layer rather than a series of unrelated Medium tickets closed on the routine queue.

new_control_requirements.description: This is a 2021 identifier that CISA listed on 2026-02-18 — years after the vendor fix shipped and long after any normal patch window closed. Inside that window the work is inventory-led rather than patch-led: enumerate every self-managed GitLab instance including team-run and forgotten ones (the same lack of ownership that let a years-old flaw persist is what will hide instances from the sweep), confirm each running version against the fixed release, and apply the vendor update with the service restart the packet says it requires. new_control_requirements.name: PERIMETER-DEVICE-ZERODAY-SLA-TIER
new_control_requirements.description: The packet's path into BeyondTrust Remote Support and Privileged Remote Access needs no credential and no user interaction — an unauthenticated remote attacker reaches the product and executes operating system commands in the context of the site user — so these systems are not servers sitting behind an access boundary, they are the boundary the exploit crosses, which is what puts them in this control's distinct SLA tier rather than in the general server population. For these two products the control means the remediation clock runs from the 2026-02-13 KEV listing rather than from the next scheduled maintenance window, and that completion is measured per system by the version actually running against the vendor's fixed version, not by 'update approved', 'update downloaded' or a closed change ticket. The packet registers no live-patch path and records that the vendor patch typically requires a service restart or system reboot per the KEV requiredAction, so a system that has taken the update but not restarted still runs the vulnerable code and has to be counted as exposed for the whole interval until it restarts. The control's alternative branch — isolating the vulnerable interface instead of meeting the clock — carries a precondition that frequently does not hold for this product: Remote Support and Privileged Remote Access exist in order to be reachable, so isolation is only available where the operator can name a user and technician population whose access can be suspended for the duration, and where it cannot, the update plus its restart is the only lever and there is no compensating control to record in its place. Priority follows the packet rather than the CVSS band alone: confirmed in-the-wild exploitation plus a public PoC against a no-authentication path means the window is being actively worked. Distinguishing test: produce, per affected system, the running version and the timestamp of the restart that activated it, set against the vendor's fixed version — a patch-management attestation that reports an SLA-compliance percentage over a 14- or 30-day window passes cleanly while a system sits updated-but-unrestarted on a KEV-listed no-authentication remote command-execution flaw.

new_control_requirements.name: PERIMETER-COMPROMISE-REBUILD-NOT-PATCH
new_control_requirements.description: The packet records confirmed in-the-wild exploitation and a public PoC against a path that requires no authentication and no user interaction, which changes what the response has to cover: any Remote Support or Privileged Remote Access system that was reachable before it was updated is possibly already executed against, not merely possibly vulnerable. Bound to this product, the control means the answer to the 2026-02-13 KEV listing is not the vendor update alone — for each system reachable during the exposure window, export the configuration off the box, rebuild from vendor media rather than patching in place, and rotate the credentials and key material the system held. The packet's own outcome statement is the reason: command execution in the context of the site user, with the vendor stating exploitation may lead to system compromise including unauthorized access, data exfiltration and service disruption. An attacker who reached that before the update keeps everything they wrote after it. This is also precisely why the anti-malware control cited against this entry does not close the path: an anti-malware attestation covers the hosts the agent is installed on and the content it has signatures for, whereas an operating-system command-execution foothold on this product typically leaves an added account, an altered configuration entry, or a script the platform itself executes on schedule — content with nothing to match. Distinguishing test: take a system that was reachable before remediation and diff its accounts, automated tasks and on-disk content against a freshly built system at the same fixed version; a clean anti-malware scan and a version number at or above the fixed release are both fully consistent with a system that is still implanted. Preconditions: the vendor update is what closes the injection path and this control does not substitute for it; the control applies only to systems that were actually reachable during the window, not to every unit in the inventory; and where a rebuild genuinely cannot be scheduled, the honest record is an accepted exposure with a dated review, because the system continues to be trusted with no evidence it is clean — not a remediation entry.

new_control_requirements.name: FLEET-COMPROMISE-IR-PLAYBOOK
new_control_requirements.description: Remote Support and Privileged Remote Access are, by what the packet names them, the products through which support sessions into other systems are established, so command execution on them is not bounded by the systems themselves. Applied to this CVE, the control means the response includes an accounting of what passed through each affected system during the exposure window — the accounts that authenticated to or through it, the credential and session material it held for the systems it serves, and the trust those serviced systems extend to it — with each of those rotated or re-established rather than left standing because the system now reports a fixed version. Two preconditions must be stated rather than assumed. First, the scope list cannot be drawn solely from the affected system's own records: the packet gives an attacker executing operating system commands in the context of the site user, and records written on a system in that state are attacker-influenceable, so an off-system record of sessions is the authoritative source where one exists, and where it does not, the defensible scope is every account that used the service during the window. Second, this control assumes the deployment actually brokers access to other systems — the packet establishes the products and the exploitation outcome, not any particular site's session inventory, so the rotation list is a deployment fact the operator has to produce and it may be narrower or wider than the product name suggests. Rotation is also not containment on its own: it invalidates what the attacker took, it does not remove what the attacker left, which is the rebuild half of the response, and it gives nothing back to a system that was never reachable during the window. Distinguishing test: name the accounts whose sessions traversed each affected system between the earliest plausible compromise and completion of its rebuild, and show a rotation timestamp after that completion for each — an identity-and-access attestation showing that every technician holds a unique account with MFA passes cleanly here, because the packet's path never authenticates as any of them and no per-account privilege decision is ever consulted.

new_control_requirements.name: MOBILE-ENDPOINT-MDM-ENFORCED-KEV-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: The packet names iOS, macOS, tvOS, watchOS and visionOS as affected by the same memory-buffer flaw, which is broader than the device classes a typical Apple update policy actually enforces — most estates enforce phones and laptops through management and leave watches, TV devices and headsets to whatever the user gets around to, so a single KEV entry leaves enforced and unenforced device classes carrying the same defect. Enforcement must therefore cover the whole managed Apple estate, including personally-owned devices under BYOD enrollment, pushed through declarative device management with user deferral disabled and a hard enforcement deadline. 'Update deferred by user' has to be treated as a non-compliant state that loses access to organizational data, not a line on a compliance report. The vendor update is the remediation and it is available; the packet registers no live-patch path and notes the fix typically requires restart, so the enforced deadline must include the device restart, not merely the download.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Packet name and vector: 'Apple iOS, macOS, tvOS, watchOS, and visionOS contain an improper restriction of operations within the bounds of a memory buffer vulnerability that could allow an attacker with memory write the capability to execute arbitrary code' (CWE-119). CISA KEV-listed 2026-02-12 with active_exploitation 'confirmed', poc_available true, CVSS 8.8, RWEP 77. patch_available true; live_patch_available false, with live_patch_notes recording that the vendor patch typically requires service restart or system reboot per the KEV requiredAction.

new_control_requirements.name: MOBILE-ZERO-CLICK-HARDENING
new_control_requirements.description: The packet describes this overflow as reachable via attacker-controlled content and places the class in targeted-spyware chains, which means delivery happens when content arrives at the device rather than when a user takes an action an awareness policy could influence — the interval between in-the-wild use and an enforced estate-wide update is unprotected by any patch SLA, however short it is written. For users at elevated targeting risk (executives, legal, security staff, anyone handling sensitive negotiations), the reduced-attack-surface mode must be enabled as a standing configuration, so untrusted message attachments, fonts and link previews are not auto-processed, and it must stay on across Apple's platforms in the estate rather than being switched on reactively after a specific CVE is announced. This is the control that covers the next member of the class before its patch exists, which is the same position operators were in when this one was listed.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Packet attack_vector: 'a buffer overflow (CWE-119) reachable via attacker-controlled content. CISA KEV-listed 2026-02-12 with confirmed in-the-wild exploitation (Apple zero-days of this class are typically used in targeted-spyware chains).' The vector adds that an attacker with memory-write capability can execute arbitrary code. poc_available true, CVSS 8.8, RWEP 77; live_patch_available false, so there is no mid-window fix that avoids the update-and-restart cycle.

CVE-2024-43468.name: Microsoft Configuration Manager SQL Injection Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: SQL injection (CWE-89) on Microsoft Configuration Manager escalating to unauthenticated remote code execution. CISA KEV-listed 2026-02-12 with confirmed in-the-wild exploitation.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none (unauthenticated network reach to the server)
attack_vector.complexity: low — KEV-listed, actively exploited; treat as weaponized
attack_vector.ai_factor: No AI involvement documented in discovery or weaponization.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Apply the Microsoft Configuration Manager security update; ConfigMgr governs endpoint management, so treat compromise as fleet-level and review managed-client integrity.
prevention.adequacy: Patch is necessary but, for these deserialization RCEs, insufficient alone — stolen machine keys and dropped web shells survive the patch and require explicit cleanup.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Monitoring on the Configuration Manager: exploit-shaped requests, new .aspx/web-shell files under the server's web root, unexpected process execution, and anomalous use of stolen cryptographic keys.
detection.adequacy: Necessary to catch resident persistence after patching; the ToolShell-class chains specifically steal keys for durable access.

response.what_would_have_worked: Patch immediately, rotate machine keys, hunt and remove web shells, and review for lateral movement; assume credential compromise for any account reachable from the Configuration Manager.
response.adequacy: Mandatory; patch-in-place without key rotation and web-shell hunting leaves the attacker resident.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: The 30-day flaw-remediation SLA is far longer than the observed exploitation window for a KEV-listed unauthenticated server flaw; CISA KEV due dates are days. The ToolShell SharePoint chain was mass-exploited within days of disclosure.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: 'Appropriate timescales' is undefined; the standard 30-day reading is unsafe for an unauthenticated, actively-exploited flaw on an internet-facing enterprise server.

NIS2-Art21-network-security.gap: Treats the server class as essential-function infrastructure but lacks a CISA-KEV-style compressed remediation SLA, and does not require the key-rotation/web-shell-hunt cleanup these deserialization RCEs need.

PCI-DSS-4.0-6.3.3.gap: The 30-day critical-patch window is exploitation acceptance for an unauthenticated RCE on an internet-facing server in or adjacent to the CDE.

compliance_exposure_score.basis: Internet-facing Microsoft Configuration Manager is business-critical and change-controlled, so emergency patching loses to change windows; the required key-rotation and web-shell hunt is rarely part of the documented patch procedure.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: Configuration Manager is the system operators patch everything else with, which is exactly why it tends to sit outside its own SLA — the site server is treated as remediation infrastructure rather than as a remediation target. This CVE is KEV-listed 2026-02-12 with confirmed exploitation and a public PoC, and the packet describes an unauthenticated caller sending crafted requests that end in command execution on the server or its database, so the site server has to be enrolled in the same KEV clock it enforces on managed endpoints. A vendor fix exists; the packet records no live-patch path and notes the vendor patch typically requires a service restart or system reboot, so a maintenance window for the site server itself — not just for the fleet it patches — must be pre-authorised inside the SLA.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Packet fields for CVE-2024-43468 (Microsoft Configuration Manager SQL Injection Vulnerability): cwe_refs CWE-89; cisa_kev=true with kev_date 2026-02-12; active_exploitation=confirmed; poc_available=true; cvss 9.8; rwep_score 77; vector text states an unauthenticated attacker could exploit it by sending specially crafted requests to the target environment which are processed in an unsafe manner, enabling the attacker to execute commands on the server and/or underlying database; patch_available=true; live_patch_available=false with live_patch_notes stating no live-patch tool is registered and that the vendor patch typically requires service restart or system reboot per the KEV requiredAction.

new_control_requirements.name: DB-ABSTRACTION-LAYER-PARAMETERIZATION-VERIFICATION
new_control_requirements.description: The injectable path on Configuration Manager is reached without credentials — the packet describes crafted requests processed in an unsafe manner by the server — so the two assumptions operators normally lean on for this product ('the site server is on the internal network' and 'a WAF fronts the client-facing endpoints') are both untested inferences, and neither is evidence that a query is bound rather than concatenated. The control requires parameterization to be proven at the query layer for every request handler that accepts client-originated content, and re-proven after each site-server update, rather than inferred from upstream input validation. The distinguishing test: from an unauthenticated host that can reach the site server's request-handling endpoints on a staging hierarchy, submit request fields carrying SQL metacharacters and confirm the value is passed as a bound parameter rather than becoming part of the statement — a hierarchy that passes an application-firewall audit while a handler concatenates client-supplied content still yields command execution on the server and the database behind it.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Packet fields for CVE-2024-43468: cwe_refs CWE-89; attack_vector states SQL injection on Microsoft Configuration Manager escalating to unauthenticated remote code execution; vector text states an unauthenticated attacker sends specially crafted requests processed in an unsafe manner, enabling execution of commands on the server and/or underlying database; cvss 9.8; active_exploitation=confirmed; poc_available=true.

new_control_requirements.name: ENDPOINT-MGMT-DEPLOYMENT-CHANNEL-INTEGRITY
new_control_requirements.description: Configuration Manager is the fleet's software-deployment control plane, and this CVE hands an unauthenticated attacker command execution on that server and its database — the same authority the product legitimately uses to push packages, scripts and updates to every managed endpoint, which is why a single unauthenticated request here is a fleet-wide code-execution primitive rather than one compromised host. The control requires the deployment channel to be integrity-monitored independently of the site server itself: alert on deployment objects, scripts and task sequences that appear without a matching sanctioned admin action, and land that audit trail on a collector the site server cannot rewrite, so a foothold on the server cannot quietly launder itself into signed-looking fleet distribution. It also sets the post-remediation obligation the patch does not: any window in which a site server ran the vulnerable build while exposed must be treated as fleet-wide code-execution exposure and everything deployed during it reviewed — patching closes the entry point but says nothing about what the deployment channel did while it was open.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Packet fields for CVE-2024-43468: vector text states the unauthenticated attacker can execute commands on the server and/or underlying database of Microsoft Configuration Manager; active_exploitation=confirmed; cisa_kev=true with kev_date 2026-02-12; poc_available=true; rwep_score 77; cvss 9.8; patch_available=true with live_patch_available=false.

CVE-2025-15556.name: Notepad++ Download of Code Without Integrity Check Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: Notepad++ downloads code/components without an integrity check (CWE-494), enabling malicious-code substitution via a tampered download or planted binary for execution on the host. CISA KEV-listed 2026-02-12 with confirmed in-the-wild exploitation.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none (the attacker influences the download/update channel or the shipped artifact; no authentication to the victim is required)
attack_vector.complexity: low — KEV-listed, actively exploited; treat as weaponized
attack_vector.ai_factor: No AI involvement documented in discovery or weaponization.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Enforce cryptographic integrity verification on all downloaded code and updates (code signing with signature verification, Sigstore/in-toto, TLS-pinned update channels); for the embedded-malicious-code case, verify build provenance (SLSA) and pin/verify the tool's release artifacts before use.
prevention.adequacy: Signature and provenance verification is the definitive control; the flaw exists precisely because it was absent or unenforced — patching the version does not retroactively restore trust in artifacts already installed.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Monitoring for unexpected code/DLLs loaded by the Notepad++, updates fetched over unauthenticated channels, and anomalous outbound connections or process execution from the tool.
detection.adequacy: Necessary because supply-chain substitution is silent — the tool runs as expected while the embedded/substituted code executes alongside it.

response.what_would_have_worked: Pull the affected version, reinstall from a verified-signed release, rotate any credentials the compromised process could reach, and audit every host where the tool ran — a compromised updater or scanner has broad reach.
response.adequacy: Mandatory; supply-chain compromise propagates through every host that ran the tainted code, so response is environment-wide, not host-local.

NIST-800-53-SR-11.gap: Component authenticity / anti-counterfeit is named, but verification is not enforced at install/update time — these products fetched or shipped code without a verified signature, so the control is paper unless signed-artifact verification (Sigstore/in-toto) is mandated at the download step.

NIST-SSDF-800-218-PS.2.gap: The SSDF calls for protecting release integrity and providing provenance, but downstream consumers had no enforced way to verify it; without signed releases plus provenance a consumer cannot detect substitution or embedded malicious code.

SLSA-build-provenance.gap: SLSA build provenance and signed releases would let a consumer detect tampering or substitution; absent enforced verification at the download/update step the trust gap remains open.

EU-CRA-secure-update.gap: The EU Cyber Resilience Act requires secure update mechanisms and shipping without known exploitable defects; an unauthenticated download path or embedded malicious code violates the secure-update and integrity expectations.

compliance_exposure_score.basis: Software-distribution and update integrity is widely assumed rather than verified; audited organizations that install vendor updates or run security tooling without enforcing signature/provenance verification are exposed to substitution and embedded-malicious-code attacks — and a compromised updater or scanner reaches every host it touches.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: Notepad++ is fleet-wide desktop software that updates itself through WinGUp, so the KEV clock lands on every workstation carrying the vulnerable build rather than on a small set of managed servers. The mitigation that satisfies the SLA must be a managed software-deployment push of the fixed build, not a prompt to run the in-application update check — that check is the exact channel the flaw lets an attacker redirect, so using it as the remediation mechanism runs the attack. No live-patch path is registered for this entry and the packet records that a patch of this class typically requires a restart, so the SLA has to be met with the vendor update plus that restart, or with a documented compensating control (blocking or disabling the in-app update check) until the fleet is on the fixed build.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CISA KEV-listed 2026-02-12 with active_exploitation 'confirmed', RWEP 77, CVSS 9.8, and poc_available true. patch_available is true; live_patch_available is false, and live_patch_notes states no live-patch tool is registered and that the vendor patch typically requires service restart or system reboot per the KEV requiredAction. The packet's vector states that Notepad++, when using the WinGUp updater, downloads code without an integrity check, allowing an attacker to intercept or redirect update traffic to download and execute an attacker-controlled installer with the privileges of the user.

new_control_requirements.name: INDEPENDENT-INTEGRITY-VERIFICATION-OF-SIGNED-VENDOR-INSTALLERS
new_control_requirements.description: The Notepad++ update path makes the delivery channel the trust anchor: whatever WinGUp retrieves is executed. The organization must therefore verify the Notepad++ installer against an integrity source independent of the channel that delivered it — a published per-release hash fetched over a separate path — and deploy only the verified artifact, instead of allowing endpoints to accept whatever the updater fetches. The distinguishing test for this CVE: on a staging workstation, serve a substituted installer from an operator-controlled endpoint in place of the real update host and confirm the deployment tooling refuses the artifact on hash mismatch before it runs. A software-supply-chain policy that only asserts 'we install vendor software from the vendor' passes while this exact substitution succeeds.
new_control_requirements.evidence: The packet's CWE is CWE-494 (download of code without integrity check), and the vector states the WinGUp updater downloads code without an integrity check so that intercepted or redirected update traffic results in an attacker-controlled installer being downloaded and executed. KEV-listed 2026-02-12 with confirmed active exploitation and poc_available true.

new_control_requirements.name: DOWNLOAD-PROVENANCE-ENFORCEMENT
new_control_requirements.description: Application-control and provenance policy on the endpoint must refuse to execute an installer image that an application fetched from the network unless it carries verified publisher provenance, so that a redirected Notepad++ update cannot run on a host that has not yet reached the fixed build. Reputation-service verdicts are worthless against this specific path: the defect is the absence of any integrity check on the fetched payload, so the payload never has to defeat a reputation check to be executed by the updater. The distinguishing test: on a staging endpoint, have a non-vendor-signed installer be launched by the updater process and confirm execution is blocked by policy rather than allowed on the basis of the parent application's own trust.
new_control_requirements.evidence: The vector states the attacker-controlled installer is downloaded and executed, yielding arbitrary code execution with the privileges of the user. patch_available is true and live_patch_available is false, so the only in-window alternative to deploying the fixed build is blocking the execution step.

CVE-2025-40536.name: SolarWinds Web Help Desk Security Control Bypass Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: a security-control-bypass flaw (CWE-693) on SolarWinds Web Help Desk, letting an unauthenticated attacker bypass an intended security control to reach protected functionality. CISA KEV-listed 2026-02-12 with confirmed in-the-wild exploitation.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none (the flaw is reachable by an unauthenticated attacker and defeats the access-control mechanism)
attack_vector.complexity: low — KEV-listed, actively exploited; treat as weaponized
attack_vector.ai_factor: No AI involvement documented in discovery or weaponization.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Apply the SolarWinds Web Help Desk update; review privileged-function access during the exposure window and rotate service credentials — Web Help Desk has been a repeated exploitation target.
prevention.adequacy: Patch is necessary; restricting the management plane to a trusted network is the compensating control when the access-control enforcement is itself bypassed.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Monitoring on the Web Help Desk: requests exercising the bypass, administrative actions without a matching authentication event.
detection.adequacy: Necessary because a bypass produces access that looks authorized; the anomaly is the absence of a legitimate authentication event.

response.what_would_have_worked: Patch immediately, restrict the management plane, rotate credentials and keys, review configuration/account changes during the exposure window, and audit privileged actions and (for file-transfer/secure-access) data exposure.
response.adequacy: Mandatory; an access-control bypass typically leaves administrative persistence or a code-execution foothold that a patch alone does not remove.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: The 30-day flaw-remediation SLA is far longer than the observed exploitation window for a KEV-listed access-control/security-control bypass on an internet-facing system; these grant unauthorized access to protected functionality and are mass-exploited within days.

NIST-800-53-AC-3-enforcement.gap: Access-enforcement is required, but these flaws defeat the enforcement mechanism itself (alternate channel, missing authorization check, security-control bypass, assumed-immutable parameter); restricting the management plane to a trusted network is the load-bearing compensating control when enforcement fails.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: 'Appropriate timescales' is undefined; the standard 30-day reading is unsafe for an actively-exploited, internet-facing application or appliance whose access control is bypassed.

PCI-DSS-4.0-6.3.3.gap: The 30-day critical-patch window is exploitation acceptance for an internet-facing application or appliance (file-transfer / secure-access / help-desk) in or adjacent to the CDE.

compliance_exposure_score.basis: Internet-facing SolarWinds Web Help Desk is run by audited organizations whose access-control posture is irrelevant when the enforcement mechanism is bypassed; without management-plane restriction and prompt patching the system is exposed, and the required privileged-action review / web-shell hunt is rarely documented.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: A help-desk portal is normally reachable by the people it serves, including from outside the corporate network, so an unauthenticated bypass on Web Help Desk is exploitable from the same anonymous position the deployment is designed to accept — there is no 'internal only' fallback posture to hold while a routine change window is scheduled. Start the clock at the KEV listing rather than at the next patch cycle: inventory every Web Help Desk instance including staging, disaster-recovery and departmental copies that share the same exposure, apply the vendor update, and book the service restart the packet's requiredAction implies inside that same window. An instance that has the fix staged but has not been restarted must not be recorded as remediated.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Packet: CWE-693 security-control bypass on SolarWinds Web Help Desk that 'could allow an unauthenticated attacker to gain access to certain restricted functionality'; cisa_kev true, kev_date 2026-02-12, active_exploitation 'confirmed', poc_available true, cvss 8.8, rwep_score 77. patch_available true; live_patch_available false, with live_patch_notes 'No live-patch tool registered for this entry at bulk-import time. Vendor patch typically requires service restart or system reboot per the KEV requiredAction.'

new_control_requirements.name: SCANNER-PAPER-COMPLIANCE-TEST
new_control_requirements.description: A protection-mechanism failure means the product's security control was present and did answer — it simply did not stop the request — so an access-control attestation and a version-based scanner verdict can both be truthful while the restricted functionality is reachable by anyone. Verification has to be behavioural rather than declarative: from an unauthenticated client against a staging Web Help Desk instance, request each restricted function the bypass reached and confirm it is refused before the function executes, then re-run the same probe after the update instead of accepting the build number as proof. An audit that records 'Web Help Desk authenticates its users' or 'Web Help Desk is on the fixed build' without that probe cannot tell an enforced control from a bypassed one, which is the exact state this CVE describes.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Packet: CWE-693 protection-mechanism failure letting an unauthenticated attacker bypass an intended security control to reach protected functionality; active_exploitation 'confirmed' with CISA KEV listing 2026-02-12 and poc_available true. The framework gaps already citing this CVE include UK-CAF-B2 (identity and access control) and ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8 (management of technical vulnerabilities) — the two controls an operator can satisfy on paper while the bypass works.

CVE-2026-21513.name: Microsoft MSHTML Framework Protection Mechanism Failure Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: a protection-mechanism failure (CWE-693) in the MSHTML framework that bypasses the Mark-of-the-Web / trust protection, letting attacker-controlled content run without the expected security warning. CISA KEV-listed 2026-02-10 with confirmed in-the-wild exploitation.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none (the victim opens the attacker's document or visits the attacker's content)
attack_vector.complexity: low — KEV-listed, actively exploited; treat as weaponized
attack_vector.ai_factor: No AI involvement documented in discovery or weaponization.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Apply the Microsoft security update; because this flaw defeats a protection mechanism, do not rely on that single control — enforce defence-in-depth (ASR rules, application control, mail/web content filtering, and macro restrictions) so a bypass of SmartScreen / Mark-of-the-Web / Protected View is not a single point of failure.
prevention.adequacy: Patch is required; the lasting lesson is that a single protection mechanism (the one bypassed) cannot be the only barrier — layered controls are mandatory.

detection.what_would_have_worked: EDR / endpoint telemetry for execution of content lacking Mark-of-the-Web provenance and security-prompt bypass.
detection.adequacy: Backstops endpoints not yet patched and catches the post-bypass execution stage.

response.what_would_have_worked: Force the patch across the estate, isolate exploited endpoints, hunt for follow-on payloads, and review for credential theft.
response.adequacy: Mandatory; client-side exploitation typically leads to credential harvest and lateral movement that a bare patch does not remediate.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: The 30-day flaw-remediation SLA is far longer than the observed exploitation window for a KEV-listed, actively-exploited client-side flaw; the protection-bypass variants specifically defeat the warning that would otherwise slow the user, so the patch is the only barrier left.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: 'Appropriate timescales' is undefined; the standard reading is unsafe for an actively-exploited client flaw, and security-feature-bypass flaws mean a single layered control (Protected View, SmartScreen, Mark-of-the-Web) cannot be relied on alone.

AU-ISM-1546.gap: Essential 8 names application patching, application hardening, and macro/Office controls separately, but does not require defence-in-depth for the case where the protection mechanism itself is bypassed — ASR rules, application control, and mail/web content filtering are the load-bearing layers when SmartScreen/Protected View fail.

compliance_exposure_score.basis: Microsoft MSHTML is ubiquitous on endpoints; audited organizations that lean on a single protection (SmartScreen, Protected View, Mark-of-the-Web) without layered controls are exposed when that mechanism is bypassed, and long-tail patch hygiene leaves a window for the memory-corruption variants.

new_control_requirements.name: PROTECTION-MECHANISM-FAILURE-CLASS-REGRESSION
new_control_requirements.description: The flaw here is in the protection mechanism itself — MSHTML fails to apply the Mark-of-the-Web / trust check, so attacker-controlled content renders without the warning the rest of the endpoint hardening posture assumes is present. Verifying this fix therefore means re-running the whole MOTW/trust battery against MSHTML-rendered content after the update lands (mark propagation, zone-of-origin handling, prompt-on-execute for internet-sourced content), not confirming that the single reported bypass path is closed. An application-hardening attestation is only as strong as the last end-to-end test of the primitive it depends on, and this CVE is the demonstration that the primitive can silently stop working while every hardening setting still reads as enabled. Make the class battery a standing step of patch deployment on the affected estate.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Packet: protection-mechanism failure (CWE-693) in the Microsoft MSHTML framework that bypasses the Mark-of-the-Web / trust protection, letting attacker-controlled content run without the expected security warning; the KEV vector describes an unauthorized attacker bypassing a security feature over a network. cisa_kev true, kev_date 2026-02-10, active_exploitation confirmed, poc_available true, RWEP 77, CVSS 8.8.

new_control_requirements.name: DOWNLOAD-PROVENANCE-ENFORCEMENT
new_control_requirements.description: Because this bug suppresses the warning rather than corrupting memory, any posture that leans on the user seeing a prompt — or on a reputation verdict rendered at the same moment — is leaning on exactly what the flaw disables. Provenance has to be enforced by policy on the affected estate instead: block execution of internet-sourced shortcuts, installers and script hosts by rule, independent of whether the Mark-of-the-Web marking survived and independent of any reputation service outcome, so content delivered through the MSHTML path is refused even when it is never evaluated. This is also what closes the least-privilege gap for this CVE: the bypassed content runs in the user's own context, so removing administrative rights does not stop it — the enforcement point has to be what the user's own process is permitted to execute.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Packet: protection-mechanism failure (CWE-693) in Microsoft MSHTML bypassing Mark-of-the-Web / trust protection so attacker-controlled content runs without the expected security warning, reachable over a network by an unauthorized attacker. cisa_kev true, kev_date 2026-02-10, active_exploitation confirmed, poc_available true, RWEP 77.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For most endpoint CVEs the interval between disclosure and deployment is implicitly covered by the platform's trust prompts and user caution. This entry removes that cover — the entire defect is that the warning does not fire — so the unpatched window carries no residual endpoint-side compensating control, and the deployment clock has to run from the KEV listing rather than the next scheduled update ring. The packet records no live-patch path, so remediation is the vendor update plus the restart the KEV requiredAction implies; hosts that cannot take it inside the SLA need the provenance-enforcement block recorded as an explicit, time-bound compensating control, not counted as patched-per-policy.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Packet: cisa_kev true, kev_date 2026-02-10, active_exploitation confirmed, poc_available true; patch_available true with live_patch_available false, and live_patch_notes stating no live-patch tool is registered and that the vendor patch typically requires service restart or system reboot per the KEV requiredAction. RWEP 77, CVSS 8.8; protection-mechanism failure (CWE-693) bypassing Mark-of-the-Web / trust protection.

CVE-2026-21525.name: Microsoft Windows NULL Pointer Dereference Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: a NULL pointer dereference (CWE-476) in a network-reachable Windows component, exploitable by an unauthenticated attacker; described conservatively as a network-reachable memory-safety flaw pending Microsoft's component detail. CISA KEV-listed 2026-02-10 with confirmed in-the-wild exploitation.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none (the flaw is reachable by an unauthenticated attacker over the network)
attack_vector.complexity: low — KEV-listed, actively exploited; treat as weaponized
attack_vector.ai_factor: No AI involvement documented in discovery or weaponization.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Apply the Microsoft update; restrict and segment the affected network service from untrusted networks until patched.
prevention.adequacy: Patch is necessary but the named compensating controls are what hold when the patch lags or the trust mechanism itself is defeated.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Monitoring for crafted network input that crashes or restarts the affected Windows component, and for unauthenticated requests that trigger the fault.
detection.adequacy: Backstops the window before patching and catches the post-exploitation stage.

response.what_would_have_worked: Patch immediately, segment the service, and review the affected hosts for follow-on activity given confirmed in-the-wild exploitation.
response.adequacy: Mandatory; exploitation of this class leaves persistence or a foothold that a bare patch does not remediate.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: The 30-day flaw-remediation SLA is far longer than the observed exploitation window for a KEV-listed, unauthenticated network-reachable Windows flaw; these are mass-exploited within days.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: 'Appropriate timescales' is undefined; unsafe for an actively-exploited network-reachable Windows flaw.

NIS2-Art21-network-security.gap: Treats Windows infrastructure as essential-function but lacks a CISA-KEV-style compressed remediation SLA; network segmentation of the affected service is the compensating control pending patch.

compliance_exposure_score.basis: The affected Windows service is reachable on audited-organization networks; without prompt patching and segmentation the unauthenticated flaw remains exploitable past the KEV due date.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For this entry the KEV clock opens 2026-02-10 and the unit of completion is a restarted host, not an approved update. The packet records a vendor patch with no live-patch tool registered and a fix that typically requires a service restart or system reboot per the KEV requiredAction, so a Windows host that has installed the update but has not taken the restart is still running the pre-patch Remote Access Connection Manager image and has to be counted as exposed rather than as remediated. Scope the rollout to every host carrying the component rather than to a subset chosen from an assumed reachability model: the packet's vector describes an unauthorized attacker denying service locally, while the packet's own summary line describes the flaw conservatively as network-reachable pending Microsoft's component detail — the two framings do not agree, and narrowing the rollout to whichever one is cheaper is how a KEV-listed defect with confirmed exploitation survives the SLA on paper. The packet registers no live-patch path and states the vendor patch typically requires a service restart or system reboot, so a Metro process still running from a pre-fix load remains exposed until it is stopped and restarted on the fixed release — a host where the package was updated while a dev server kept running is not remediated, and this is the specific way the completion count goes wrong on a machine a developer leaves running for days. Compensating control for the window before that completes, with its precondition stated: the packet's stated access requirement is a network attacker reaching the exposed dev server, so binding Metro to loopback and denying inbound connections to its port at the host firewall bounds who can send the POST. That lever exists only where the workflow does not need off-host reach — a physical test device, an emulator or simulator on another machine, or a teammate or CI runner loading the bundle all require the server to answer from the network, and on those hosts the restriction is simply unavailable. It also does not repair the endpoint: anything still permitted to reach the dev server reaches the command-injection path unchanged, and the packet records that on Windows the attacker additionally controls shell arguments in full. new_control_requirements.name: SCANNER-PAPER-COMPLIANCE-TEST
new_control_requirements.description: The verdict that goes wrong on this CVE is a developer-fleet scan reporting no vulnerable software present. What is vulnerable is a command-line development tool a developer runs inside a project, and the exposure exists only while that tool's Metro dev server is live and answering from the network — neither fact is visible to a scanner that enumerates installed products and OS patch level, so an estate can hold a clean report while a fully exploitable dev server is listening on the same LAN as the attacker. The operational test has two halves and both are required. First, enumerate every developer host and every CI/build image capable of starting Metro and show the React Native Community CLI each one resolves is at or above the fixed release, rather than showing that the workstation's operating system and registered applications are current. Second, with a project running on a representative developer host, send a POST to that host's Metro dev server port from a different host on the same network segment and confirm it is refused before any executable is invoked. The second half is the one the patch dashboard structurally cannot answer, and it is the half that corresponds to the packet's actual access requirement. Scope discipline matters here: the packet ties this CWE-78 sink to the React Native Community CLI's Metro development server and gives no basis for treating other frameworks' development servers as instances of this CVE, so the test population is hosts that run this CLI — widen it only where a verified source identifies another product carrying the same endpoint, because instructing operators to hunt every development server in the estate manufactures findings against tooling no evidence implicates. new_control_requirements.name: ENTERPRISE-ERP-MANAGEMENT-FUNCTION-AUTHENTICATION

new_control_requirements.description: A help-desk server is where an IT organization's operational secrets accumulate: the service accounts wired into directory and asset-discovery integrations, the database and mail-integration credentials, and the ticket bodies in which staff paste passwords and access instructions. Applying the update to a running instance closes the deserialization path but removes nothing already placed through it: a web shell in the application's served tree, a scheduled task, an added administrative account, or a modified application file all survive the upgrade and none of them are visible to a version check. The distinguishing test: after remediation, reconcile the instance's file tree, service accounts and administrative user list against a known-good baseline; if the only evidence of closure is that the version now reports fixed, the compromise question has not been asked.

new_control_requirements.name: SERVICE-INTERNAL-PROTOCOL-DESERIALIZATION-HARDENING
new_control_requirements.description: For Web Help Desk this control means treating the service's own request listener as a trust boundary instead of an internal convenience: the defect is untrusted deserialization reaching command execution for a peer that never authenticates, and the deployment assumption that normally protects it — "the help desk is an internal ticketing system" — is not a control, it is a statement about where the box sits. The requirement for this product is that the Web Help Desk listener accepts connections only from the segments that legitimately raise and service tickets (staff networks, the management/jump network), enforced by network ACL or host firewall rather than inherited from network topology, and that no instance is published to the internet for remote-staff convenience without an authenticating gateway in front of it, since an unauthenticated request body is all the packet's path requires to reach the deserializer. Content arriving on that listener must not be permitted to construct arbitrary objects, rather than being trusted because of where it appears to come from. The distinguishing test: from a general user or guest VLAN, and from an external address, attempt to reach the Web Help Desk service port on a staging deployment and confirm the connection is refused before the application processes the request body — an instance that passes a patch-level audit while answering unauthenticated requests from any segment is exposed again the moment the next deserialization defect in this product lands.

new_control_requirements.name: DEVICE-MANAGEMENT-GATEWAY-CONFIG-ENDPOINT-AUTH-INPUT-NEUTRALIZATION
new_control_requirements.description: EPMM is the device-management gateway this control governs, and the packet places the defect squarely on its management surface: a code injection that 'could allow attackers to achieve unauthenticated remote code execution' (CWE-94). Bound to this product, the control means every request handler on the EPMM management surface makes its own authorization decision before any request content is interpreted, and never turns request-supplied content into executable code — the endpoint's own decision, not the surrounding operator account model, is what stands between an untrusted caller and code execution on the appliance. This is why the least-privilege gap cited here cannot be closed by tightening EPMM roles: the attacker holds no EPMM account, so per-account privilege scoping is never consulted and the account model an access-control attestation examines is bypassed rather than abused. Preconditions: endpoint-side authorization and input neutralization are properties the vendor update establishes — this control states what to verify, not how to build it. Until that update and the restart the packet says it typically requires have both landed, restricting which segments can reach the EPMM management surface bounds who can send the request but leaves the injection sink fully exploitable to any caller inside the permitted segment, and that lever is unavailable wherever the surface must stay reachable for normal operation. Distinguishing test: on a staging EPMM, send unauthenticated requests to each management endpoint carrying content shaped to be interpreted rather than stored, and confirm each is refused before interpretation — an estate that evidences unique, role-scoped accounts for every EPMM administrator passes its access-control review while this path stays wide open.

new_control_requirements.name: FLEET-COMPROMISE-IR-PLAYBOOK
new_control_requirements.description: Unauthenticated RCE on EPMM is not an appliance incident: EPMM is the control plane the managed fleet derives its configuration and trust state from, so code execution on that box is authority over everything downstream of it — and the packet records that exploitation as confirmed in the wild with a public PoC. The playbook this CVE demands, rehearsed before the next disclosure rather than drafted during one, covers the half no patch-shaped control reaches: certificate revocation issued from a control plane whose integrity has been re-established, device-trust-state invalidation, an audit of every configuration profile pushed since the earliest point at which exploitation cannot be excluded, quarantine criteria for downstream devices, and rotation of every credential the EPMM instance held or that authenticated through it during that window. The vendor update stops further exploitation of the code path; it removes nothing an attacker already pushed to the fleet or read out of the appliance, which is precisely the residue a flaw-remediation control records as closed. Precondition: the fleet-side steps sequence after the EPMM instance itself has been rebuilt or otherwise established as trustworthy — running them from the instance that was exploited re-signs the fleet from a box of unknown integrity, so the appliance work gates the fleet work and the fleet stays in its pre-incident trust state until that completes. Distinguishing test: for one managed device chosen at random, name the certificate that would be revoked, the profile history that would be audited, and the credential set that would be rotated, and time how long producing that answer takes — an incident-response policy that cannot produce it for a single device will not produce it for the fleet under an active compromise.

NIST-800-53-SI-2 (Flaw Remediation) is recorded as insufficient for this entry.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: The KEV clock for EPMM opened 2026-01-29, and the packet pairs that with confirmed in-the-wild exploitation, a public PoC and unauthenticated remote code execution at CVSS 9.8 — the profile a routine infrastructure-patch cadence is least able to absorb, on a management appliance whose compromise is the fleet's compromise rather than one host's. Applied here, the control means the Ivanti fix is driven across every EPMM instance on that clock, with completion measured per instance by the version actually running and the restart having been taken, not by an approval sitting in a change queue. Precondition: the packet records no live-patch path and a fix that typically requires a service restart or system reboot per the KEV requiredAction, so an instance that has taken the update but not restarted is still running the vulnerable code and must be counted as exposed — on a management appliance that restart is deferred because taking it interrupts device management, which is exactly how an instance ends up recorded as patched while it is not. Where the restart cannot be taken inside the window, restricting reachability of the EPMM management surface is the only remaining lever; it bounds who can send the request and does not remove the injection path, so it carries a dated end rather than closing the item. Distinguishing test: for each EPMM instance produce the running version and the restart timestamp that activated it — a vulnerability-management report showing the update deployed without the restart cannot distinguish a remediated instance from an exposed one.

new_control_requirements.name: ARCHIVE-CONTENT-TYPE-PROVENANCE
new_control_requirements.description: CWE-807 on this entry is Office deciding whether content is trusted from input the attacker supplies, so the durable operator-side control is to move the origin determination off the document and onto a boundary the organization operates: the mail gateway, the managed file share and the web download path apply and preserve the untrusted-origin marking themselves, and that marking survives archives, disk-image containers and renames, so the Office host is told the file is externally sourced instead of deriving it from metadata travelling with the file. This matters more than usual here because the packet does not name which Office security feature the bypass defeats — no in-product setting can be assumed to be the intact one, which is exactly why the control that is worth attaching is the one whose input is established outside the vulnerable decision. The precondition has to be written down rather than assumed: boundary-applied marking only covers files that cross a boundary you run. A document arriving on removable media, through a personal cloud-sync client, or on any unmanaged path never passes a marking point and reaches Office unmarked, so those ingress paths must be blocked or brought under the same marking; where that is not done, this control does not cover them and the vulnerable decision is still reached with attacker-supplied input. The distinguishing test: send an externally-sourced document through each ingress path in turn and confirm it arrives at the Office host already marked untrusted, rather than confirming that a hardening policy shows as enabled in the management console.

The packet does not name the specific Office security feature that is bypassed. Citing gaps on this entry include ASD Essential Eight 'User application hardening' and UK NCSC CAF B4 'System security'.

new_control_requirements.name: PROTECTION-MECHANISM-FAILURE-CLASS-REGRESSION
new_control_requirements.description: This entry is the case that makes a configured-and-enabled attestation worthless: the packet's flaw is the bypass of an Office security feature, so the setting is on and the check returns the wrong answer. Treat Office document handling as a protection-mechanism class and hold a regression battery of the known bypass primitives for that class, re-run on every Office patch deployment rather than once against this CVE, with the fixed build validated by detonating the battery on a representative managed image instead of by reading a version number off an inventory. The packet's own note that some impacted products may be end-of-life or end-of-service makes the recurring form of the test the load-bearing half: those installs will not receive the next fix, so the battery is the only mechanism that tells an operator whether the posture built around them still blocks. State the limit plainly instead of recording the battery as coverage — it exercises only the primitives already known to it and says nothing about the next bypass in the class, so it establishes that this fix landed and that the surrounding controls still hold, not that Office is immune to the class.

new_control_requirements.name: PERIMETER-DEVICE-ZERODAY-SLA-TIER
new_control_requirements.description: Versa Concerto orchestrates the SD-WAN fabric, so an unauthenticated route to its administrative endpoints is a trust-boundary failure rather than an application bug, and it belongs in the perimeter SLA tier alongside firewalls and VPN concentrators. The packet places the defect in the Traefik reverse-proxy configuration in front of the orchestrator — which is also the layer an operator can constrain immediately: the vendor fix goes on within hours of the 2026-01-22 KEV listing, or the administrative and internal Actuator routes are removed from every untrusted-network path until it does. A routine appliance-patch window does not apply to the device that defines the fabric's policy plane, and 'orchestrator, not edge device' is exactly the classification error that keeps this system on the slow tier.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Packet: CWE-288 improper authentication; vector states the flaw is in the Traefik reverse proxy configuration and allows an attacker to access administrative endpoints, with the internal Actuator endpoint leveraged for access to heap dumps and trace logs; attack_vector describes an unauthenticated attacker reaching administrative functionality on the Versa Concerto SD-WAN orchestrator; CISA KEV-listed 2026-01-22 with active_exploitation=confirmed; poc_available=true; CVSS 9.1, RWEP 77; patch_available=true, live_patch_available=false.

new_control_requirements.name: PERIMETER-COMPROMISE-REBUILD-NOT-PATCH
new_control_requirements.description: The packet states the internal Actuator endpoint can be leveraged for heap dumps and trace logs — process memory and log content from the system that holds credentials, session material and policy for the whole SD-WAN fabric. Applying the vendor fix to a Concerto instance that was reachable during the confirmed-exploitation window closes the entry path but leaves everything already dumped valid, and it destroys nothing the attacker planted. Response for this CVE must therefore default to treating an exposed orchestrator as compromised: capture and review its configuration, rebuild the instance from a known-good image, and rotate every credential, token and key the orchestrator held or distributed to managed devices — patch-in-place is not a remediation verdict for a device whose exploitation primitive is memory disclosure.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Packet: vector states the internal Actuator endpoint can be leveraged for access to heap dumps and trace logs, and that the improper authentication allows an attacker to access administrative endpoints; attack_vector confirms an unauthenticated attacker reaching administrative functionality on the SD-WAN orchestrator; cisa_kev=true, kev_date 2026-01-22, active_exploitation=confirmed, poc_available=true; patch_available=true (vendor fix exists, so this control governs what must accompany it, not a substitute for it).

new_control_requirements.name: FLEET-CONTROL-PLANE-ADMIN-PRIVILEGE-TIER
new_control_requirements.description: An SD-WAN orchestrator is a fleet control plane in the same sense as an MDM or a configuration-management server: whoever reaches its administrative surface reaches every managed device's policy. The requirement that bites for this CVE is the access-path half of the tier — the Concerto management surface, including the internal Actuator endpoint, must be reachable only from a dedicated privileged-access segment and never from a general or untrusted network. Because the flaw is an unauthenticated bypass, admin identity hardening alone does not stop it; what does is that an anonymous caller has no network route to the bypassed endpoints in the first place. Frameworks that file an SD-WAN orchestrator as an ordinary application-admin surface leave it directly reachable and let a proxy-configuration defect become fabric-wide administrative access.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Packet: attack_vector states an unauthenticated attacker reaches administrative functionality on the Versa Concerto SD-WAN orchestrator via an authentication bypass using an alternate path or channel (CWE-288); vector attributes the exposure to the Traefik reverse proxy configuration fronting administrative and internal Actuator endpoints; citing gaps include NIST-800-53-AC-6 (Least Privilege), UK-CAF-B2 (Identity and access control) and NIS2-Art21-network-security; CVSS 9.1 with active_exploitation=confirmed.

CVE-2025-31125.name: Vite Vitejs Improper Access Control Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: an improper-access-control flaw (CWE-200/CWE-284) in the Vite dev server, letting a remote attacker read files including source and environment secrets outside the served root. CISA KEV-listed 2026-01-22 with confirmed in-the-wild exploitation.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none (the flaw is reachable by an unauthenticated attacker on the application's public interface)
attack_vector.complexity: low — KEV-listed, actively exploited; treat as weaponized

prevention.adequacy: Patch is necessary but insufficient alone — any secret the file read disclosed survives the patch and must be rotated.

detection.adequacy: Necessary to catch resident persistence or credential abuse after patching.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: Vite is build-time developer tooling, and vulnerability-management programs routinely hold devDependencies outside the KEV clock entirely — yet this entry is KEV-listed with confirmed exploitation, so the same mitigation deadline that applies to a production server applies to the front-end toolchain. What makes the SLA achievable here is that the packet names a precondition, not just a version: only instances explicitly bound to the network via --host or the server.host config option are affected, so removing that binding is a documented compensating control that lands immediately across every project, while the Vite update is what actually closes the ?inline&import / ?raw?import read path. Sequence the response accordingly — unbind first, upgrade second — and treat the SLA as covering every repository, CI job, and container entrypoint that starts the dev server with --host, not only the instance that surfaced the finding. Because no live-patch tool is registered, the dev-server restart the update requires belongs inside the window.
