CVE-2025-12480.name: Gladinet Triofox Improper Access Control Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: an improper-access-control flaw (CWE-284) letting an unauthenticated attacker reach functionality reserved for authorized users. CISA KEV-listed 2025-11-12 with confirmed in-the-wild exploitation.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none (the flaw is reachable by an unauthenticated attacker on the application's public interface)
attack_vector.complexity: low — KEV-listed, actively exploited; treat as weaponized
attack_vector.ai_factor: No AI involvement documented in discovery or weaponization.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Apply the Gladinet Triofox update and review for unauthorized access to shared files during the exposure window.
prevention.adequacy: Patch is necessary but, for these RCE/auth-bypass flaws, insufficient alone — web shells and stolen credentials survive the patch and require explicit cleanup.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Monitoring on the Triofox: exploit-shaped requests, new web-shell files, unexpected process execution, and authentication/authorization events with no matching legitimate session or with forged key material.
detection.adequacy: Necessary to catch resident persistence and key abuse after patching.

response.what_would_have_worked: Patch immediately, hunt and remove web shells, rotate application secrets and credentials, and review data and downstream systems reachable from the Triofox; assume compromise of accounts and managed endpoints in its reach.
response.adequacy: Mandatory; patch-in-place without key rotation / web-shell hunting leaves the attacker resident or able to re-authenticate.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: The 30-day flaw-remediation SLA is far longer than the observed exploitation window for a KEV-listed, unauthenticated server-side application RCE/auth-bypass; these are mass-exploited within days, and RMM/file-sharing compromise reaches downstream systems.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: 'Appropriate timescales' is undefined; the standard 30-day reading is unsafe for an actively-exploited, internet-facing enterprise application.

NIS2-Art21-network-security.gap: Treats internet-facing enterprise applications as essential-function infrastructure but lacks a CISA-KEV-style compressed remediation SLA, and does not require the web-shell-hunt / key-rotation cleanup these RCEs and key-disclosure flaws need.

PCI-DSS-4.0-6.3.3.gap: The 30-day critical-patch window is exploitation acceptance for an internet-facing enterprise application in or adjacent to the CDE; WAF coverage is partial mitigation, not remediation.

compliance_exposure_score.basis: Internet-facing Gladinet Triofox is run by audited organizations on a standard patch SLA and is mass-exploited within days; the required web-shell hunt and key rotation are rarely part of the documented patch procedure, and RMM/file-sharing/MES reach amplifies the blast radius.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: The exposure here is a provisioning-state defect, not an install-window one: the packet's vector text records that Triofox's initial setup pages stay reachable after setup is complete, so every already-provisioned server is affected for its whole service life and an unauthenticated caller reaches functionality reserved for authorized users. That places the KEV clock (listed 2025-11-12, exploitation confirmed) on production instances operators consider finished and therefore out of the active change queue — the SLA has to reach 'completed' deployments, not just ones under build. A vendor fix exists; the packet records no live-patch path and notes the vendor patch typically requires a service restart or system reboot, so restart authority must be pre-approved inside the window rather than negotiated after it. Because the flaw grants access rather than degrading the service, meeting this SLA means verifying the remediated state of each server — confirming the setup surface is no longer reachable unauthenticated — not recording a build number and closing the ticket.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Packet fields for CVE-2025-12480 (Gladinet Triofox Improper Access Control Vulnerability): cwe_refs CWE-284; cisa_kev=true with kev_date 2025-11-12; active_exploitation=confirmed; poc_available=true; cvss 8.8; rwep_score 77; vector text states the product allows access to initial setup pages even after setup is complete; attack_vector states an unauthenticated attacker can reach functionality reserved for authorized users; patch_available=true; live_patch_available=false with live_patch_notes stating no live-patch tool is registered and that the vendor patch typically requires service restart or system reboot per the KEV requiredAction.

attack_vector.description: a race condition (CWE-362) in a Windows kernel-mode component, exploited by a local foothold to escalate privileges to SYSTEM. CISA KEV-listed 2025-11-12 with confirmed in-the-wild exploitation; LPEs of this class are routinely paired with an initial-access flaw by ransomware operators.
attack_vector.privileges_required: low (any local foothold — an unprivileged process, RDP session, or commodity malware on the endpoint)
attack_vector.complexity: low — KEV-listed, actively exploited; treat as weaponized
attack_vector.ai_factor: No AI involvement documented in discovery or weaponization.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Apply the Microsoft security update; enforce hypervisor-protected code integrity (HVCI) / Virtualization-Based Security (VBS), and enable the Microsoft Vulnerable Driver Blocklist to shrink kernel-LPE attack surface on the long tail.
prevention.adequacy: Patch is definitive; the gap is the chain (initial access → unpatched LPE → SYSTEM) which a patched endpoint shuts down. HVCI/Blocklist backstops unpatched estates.

detection.what_would_have_worked: EDR signatures for the LPE primitive (token swap, process-impersonation, kernel-driver crashes) and for unprivileged-to-SYSTEM transitions without an admin trigger.
detection.adequacy: Backstops endpoints not yet patched; LPE is typically silent without EDR coverage.

response.what_would_have_worked: Force the patch across the estate; for a confirmed exploitation, treat the host as compromised (ransomware kits typically follow within hours), isolate, preserve forensic state, and review for credential theft.
response.adequacy: Mandatory; SYSTEM-level exploitation makes the host an unreliable platform for further work and requires rebuild.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: The 30-day flaw-remediation SLA is far longer than the observed exploitation window for a KEV-listed Windows kernel/driver LPE; ransomware operators typically pair these with an initial-access flaw and elevate to SYSTEM within hours of a foothold.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: 'Appropriate timescales' is undefined; the standard reading is unsafe for an actively-exploited kernel/driver LPE that is part of every modern ransomware kit.

AU-ISM-1546.gap: Essential 8 patch-applications (48h at ML3) is the right tier for a Windows LPE, but the load-bearing endpoint controls are hypervisor-protected code integrity (HVCI/VBS) and the Microsoft Vulnerable Driver Blocklist — neither of which the framework demands explicitly.

compliance_exposure_score.basis: Windows endpoints are universal; audited organizations gate kernel patches behind change windows or rely on cumulative monthly updates that leave the LPE chain open for ~30 days at a stretch. HVCI/VBS and the Vulnerable Driver Blocklist remain off-by-default in many estates.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: Windows hosts must reach the fixed kernel build on a KEV clock rather than the routine monthly workstation/server patch cycle, and for this CVE the SLA end-state has to be defined as the host running the patched kernel, not as the update being approved or staged. The packet records no live-patch path, so the clock only stops after the restart. Scope the SLA to the entire Windows estate rather than just internet-facing systems, because the flaw is reached from an existing local foothold, not from the network edge.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CISA KEV-listed 2025-11-12 with active_exploitation recorded as confirmed, RWEP 77 against a CVSS of 7.8, and poc_available true. patch_available is true while live_patch_available is false; live_patch_notes states that no live-patch tool is registered for this entry and that the vendor patch typically requires service restart or system reboot per the KEV requiredAction.

new_control_requirements.name: MITIGATION-ACTIVE-PATCH-PENDING-VERDICT-CLASS
new_control_requirements.description: For this kernel race condition the compliance verdict must separate 'update installed, restart pending' from 'vulnerability eliminated'. What is vulnerable is the kernel currently executing, so on any fleet that defers restarts — servers under change control, laptops that sleep instead of rebooting — deployment dashboards will report the host as remediated while the escalation to SYSTEM is still live. Audit evidence for this CVE must be the post-restart running build per host, and the installed-but-not-restarted population must be carried as its own time-bound exposure state with a named owner, not folded into the patched count.
new_control_requirements.evidence: The packet records patch_available true and live_patch_available false, with live_patch_notes stating that no live-patch tool is registered and that the vendor patch typically requires service restart or system reboot per the KEV requiredAction — so a host can hold the fix and remain exploitable. Exploitation is confirmed in the wild per the 2025-11-12 KEV listing, and poc_available is true.

new_control_requirements.name: KERNEL-EXPLOITATION-DETECTION
new_control_requirements.description: Because the fix only takes effect after a restart, the exposure window on this CWE-362 kernel race is measured in reboot cycles, and runtime detection is the only coverage inside it. Instrument Windows endpoints for kernel privilege-escalation indicators — a low-privilege process acquiring a SYSTEM token, token or process-handle duplication from an unprivileged parent, and SYSTEM-context children under a user-context parent — and treat a hit on a host that has not yet restarted onto the fixed build as an active-intrusion trigger rather than a routine alert, since this class arrives after an initial-access foothold is already established.
new_control_requirements.evidence: The packet describes a Windows Kernel race condition (CWE-362) that lets a local attacker with low-level privileges escalate to SYSTEM-level access, records poc_available true, and states that LPEs of this class are routinely paired with an initial-access flaw by ransomware operators. Exploitation is confirmed in the wild per the 2025-11-12 KEV listing.

attack_vector.description: an out-of-bounds write (CWE-787) in the Firebox IKE/VPN handling, exploitable by an unauthenticated attacker for memory-corruption remote code execution on the firewall. CISA KEV-listed 2025-11-12 with confirmed in-the-wild exploitation.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none (the flaw is reachable by an unauthenticated attacker on the device's network interface)
attack_vector.complexity: low — KEV-listed, actively exploited; treat as weaponized
attack_vector.ai_factor: No AI involvement documented in discovery or weaponization.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Apply the WatchGuard Fireware update; treat an exploited firewall as fully compromised — rebuild it and rotate every credential and VPN/IKE secret it held, since the firewall terminates trust for the network behind it.
prevention.adequacy: Patch is necessary but, given the device's trust position, an exploited unit must be rebuilt and its secrets rotated — a patch in place does not evict a resident attacker.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Monitoring of the Firebox firewall: exploit-shaped requests, device crashes, new processes, and credential/config changes.
detection.adequacy: Necessary because device compromise is often silent and persists across reboots in firmware/config.

response.what_would_have_worked: Rebuild the device from a known-good image, rotate all credentials and secrets it held, and review the network behind it for lateral movement; assume the device's trust is fully compromised.
response.adequacy: Mandatory; network-device compromise gives an attacker a durable, trusted position that patching alone does not remove.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: The 30-day flaw-remediation SLA is far longer than the observed exploitation window for a KEV-listed unauthenticated flaw on an internet-facing network device; SOHO routers and edge appliances are mass-exploited into botnets and operational-relay (ORB) networks within days, and many run end-of-life firmware with no available fix.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: 'Appropriate timescales' is undefined; the standard reading is unsafe for an actively-exploited internet-facing device, and unmanaged/EOL devices fall outside most patch programs entirely.

NIS2-Art21-network-security.gap: Treats network devices/appliances as essential-function infrastructure but lacks a CISA-KEV-style compressed remediation SLA and does not address end-of-life devices that can only be replaced, not patched.

PCI-DSS-4.0-6.3.3.gap: The 30-day critical-patch window is exploitation acceptance for an internet-facing network device fronting or bridging the CDE.

compliance_exposure_score.basis: Internet-facing WatchGuard Firebox is frequently unmanaged or end-of-life; audited organizations rarely track SOHO/edge-device firmware on a KEV SLA, and the required re-flash/replace and secret rotation are almost never part of a routine patch procedure.

new_control_requirements.name: PERIMETER-DEVICE-ZERODAY-SLA-TIER
new_control_requirements.description: A WatchGuard Firebox is itself the network trust boundary, and the vulnerable code is the iked process that terminates IKE/VPN negotiation — reachable before authentication by anyone who can send IKE traffic to the gateway. Firebox firmware therefore cannot share a patch tier with server or workstation operating systems: the requirement is vendor firmware deployed within hours of the KEV listing, or the IKE/VPN listener restricted to known peer addresses until the firmware window can be taken. The packet records no live-patch path for this entry, so the update carries a device restart that drops the organization's VPN — which is exactly why routine change control pushes it into a maintenance window weeks out, and exactly why this tier has to name that outage as in-scope rather than as grounds to defer a pre-authentication code-execution flaw on the perimeter.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Packet: out-of-bounds write (CWE-787) in the Firebox OS iked process that may allow a remote unauthenticated attacker to execute arbitrary code; characterized as memory-corruption remote code execution on the firewall via the Firebox IKE/VPN handling. CVSS 9.8, RWEP 77, poc_available true. CISA KEV-listed 2025-11-12 with active_exploitation confirmed. patch_available true; live_patch_available false, with live_patch_notes stating the vendor patch typically requires service restart or system reboot per the KEV requiredAction.

new_control_requirements.name: PERIMETER-COMPROMISE-REBUILD-NOT-PATCH
new_control_requirements.description: Fireboxes that were reachable while this CVE was under active exploitation must be treated as compromised until proven otherwise, not simply firmware-updated. Unauthenticated code execution in iked runs inside the appliance that holds its own configuration, its VPN key material and certificates, and its administrative credentials — and a firmware update that preserves the running configuration also preserves anything an attacker added to it (accounts, tunnels, policy entries, management access). The default response is to export and review the configuration off the device, rebuild the appliance from a known-good configuration rather than updating in place, and rotate every credential the gateway held — VPN pre-shared keys, local user and administrator passwords, any directory or RADIUS service account bound to the gateway, and certificates — before the tunnels are returned to service.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Packet: the flaw is an out-of-bounds write in the Firebox OS iked process allowing a remote unauthenticated attacker to execute arbitrary code on the firewall (CWE-787, CVSS 9.8, RWEP 77), with poc_available true, CISA KEV-listed 2025-11-12 and active_exploitation confirmed. Confirmed in-the-wild pre-authentication code execution on the device that enforces the perimeter is what makes update-in-place insufficient; the citing gaps stop at flaw remediation (NIST SP 800-53 SI-2) and management of technical vulnerabilities (ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.8), neither of which requires post-exploitation rebuild or credential rotation.

new_control_requirements.name: FIREWALL-EGRESS-TELEMETRY-SEPARATE-TRUST-ZONE
new_control_requirements.description: Because this exploit executes attacker code inside the Firebox itself, the device's local log store and its logging configuration are within the attacker's control from the moment of compromise; the only records that can establish whether a given appliance was hit before its firmware was updated are records already off the box. Fireboxes must forward IKE/VPN negotiation and tunnel-establishment logs, management-plane authentication, and configuration-change events to a collector in a separate trust zone — different management plane, different credentials, different authentication path — with retention long enough to look backward past the KEV listing date. Without that, an operator asked after the fact whether the gateway was exploited can only answer using evidence produced by the device that was executing the attacker's code.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Packet: out-of-bounds write in the Firebox OS iked process allowing a remote unauthenticated attacker to execute arbitrary code on the appliance (CWE-787, CVSS 9.8), poc_available true, CISA KEV-listed 2025-11-12 with active_exploitation confirmed. Attacker code execution on the appliance is the packet fact that places the device's own telemetry inside the blast radius.

CVE-2025-21042.name: Samsung Mobile Devices Out-of-Bounds Write Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: an out-of-bounds write (CWE-787) in the Samsung image-parsing library, exploitable by a malicious image (zero-click, e.g. delivered through a messaging app) for code execution on the device — used in the wild in mobile spyware. CISA KEV-listed 2025-11-10 with confirmed in-the-wild exploitation; this class forms the initial-access half of a mobile-spyware chain.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none (the device renders an attacker-supplied image, often zero-click)
attack_vector.complexity: low — KEV-listed, actively exploited; treat as weaponized
attack_vector.ai_factor: No AI involvement documented in discovery or weaponization.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Apply the Samsung SMR OTA update promptly; enforce update SLAs via MDM on managed fleets, deploy mobile-threat-defense, and enable hardened/locked-down configurations for high-risk users.
prevention.adequacy: The OTA fix is definitive; the gap is OEM/carrier patch reach and managed fleets that defer mobile updates.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Mobile-threat-defense telemetry for image-parser crashes after inbound media and post-exploit beaconing; vendor threat notifications for targeted users.
detection.adequacy: Backstops unpatched devices; mobile-spyware chains are stealthy and frequently zero-click.

response.what_would_have_worked: Force the OTA update; for a confirmed targeted device, preserve forensic state, rotate credentials and tokens stored on the device, and consider device replacement — spyware can persist across reboots.
response.adequacy: Mandatory for a KEV-listed mobile RCE/LPE; the exposure is every device that processed attacker content pre-patch.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: The 30-day flaw-remediation SLA is far longer than the observed exploitation window for a KEV-listed, actively-exploited mobile flaw; commercial-surveillance and spyware chains weaponize these within days, and patch reach depends on OEM/carrier OTA cadence well beyond the vendor's release date.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: 'Appropriate timescales' is undefined; the standard reading is unsafe for an actively-exploited mobile OS flaw, and the OEM/carrier OTA chain means many devices receive the fix weeks-to-never after disclosure.

AU-ISM-1546.gap: Essential 8 patch-applications (operating systems) is the right tier, but the load-bearing controls for mobile are vendor OTA cadence (Android Security Bulletin / Samsung SMR), MDM-enforced update SLAs on managed fleets, mobile-threat-defense, and hardened/locked-down configurations for high-risk users — none of which the framework names explicitly.

compliance_exposure_score.basis: Samsung mobile devices update reach depends on OEM/carrier OTA cadence; audited organizations that do not enforce mobile update SLAs via MDM remain exposed for this KEV-listed, actively-exploited flaw long after the fix is published.

new_control_requirements.name: MOBILE-OS-MINIMUM-PATCH-LEVEL-ENFORCEMENT
new_control_requirements.description: Samsung handsets in the estate must be denied access to organizational data until their security-patch level carries the fixed libimagecodec.quram.so, not merely flagged as stale on an MDM dashboard. Because the delivery path is a malicious image processed without any user interaction, there is no user-behavior control to fall back on and no defensible 'the user will update eventually' allowance -- a handset sitting below the fixed patch level is exploitable for exactly as long as it is reported rather than quarantined. No live-patch path exists for this entry, so remediation is the vendor firmware update and its reboot; the MDM/EMM must therefore quarantine handsets that defer that update instead of counting deferral as compliance.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Packet: 'Samsung mobile devices contain an out-of-bounds write vulnerability in libimagecodec.quram.so. This vulnerability could allow remote attackers to execute arbitrary code.' cwe_refs CWE-787. CISA KEV-listed 2025-11-10 with active_exploitation 'confirmed'; CVSS 9.8, RWEP 77, poc_available true. patch_available true, live_patch_available false, live_patch_notes: 'No live-patch tool registered for this entry at bulk-import time. Vendor patch typically requires service restart or system reboot per the KEV requiredAction.'

new_control_requirements.name: MOBILE-ZERO-CLICK-HARDENING
new_control_requirements.description: High-risk Samsung users -- the population this exploit class actually targets -- must run in a reduced-attack-surface mode that stops untrusted inbound images being decoded automatically, because the vulnerable code is an image parser reached by a message the user never opens. A patch SLA, however tight, cannot cover the interval between a spyware operator's use of the bug and the firmware update reaching the handset; suppressing automatic processing of untrusted message attachments and previews removes the delivery path itself across that interval. This is an explicit per-role posture decision an enterprise mobility policy has to make for exposed users, not a fleet-wide default, and it is the half of the response that survives the device being unpatched.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Packet attack_vector: 'an out-of-bounds write (CWE-787) in the Samsung image-parsing library, exploitable by a malicious image (zero-click, e.g. delivered through a messaging app) for code execution on the device -- used in the wild in mobile spyware. CISA KEV-listed 2025-11-10 with confirmed in-the-wild exploitation; this class forms the initial-access half of a mobile-spyware chain.' poc_available true; CVSS 9.8 / RWEP 77.

CVE-2025-48703.name: CWP Control Web Panel OS Command Injection Vulnerability (CVE-2025-48703)

attack_vector.description: an OS command-injection flaw (CWE-78) enabling unauthenticated remote command execution on the hosting-control server. CISA KEV-listed 2025-11-04 with confirmed in-the-wild exploitation.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none (the flaw is reachable by an unauthenticated attacker; bundled-library flaws are reachable wherever the library processes attacker input)
attack_vector.complexity: low — KEV-listed, actively exploited; treat as weaponized
attack_vector.ai_factor: No AI involvement documented in discovery or weaponization.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Apply the CWP update; hunt for web shells across hosted sites and rotate panel/hosting credentials — a control-panel compromise reaches every site it manages.
prevention.adequacy: Patch is necessary but insufficient alone — web shells and stolen credentials survive the patch, bundled-library flaws require updating every consumer, and CI/MFT/EDR-console compromise has downstream reach.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Monitoring on the Control Web Panel: exploit-shaped requests, new web-shell files, and unexpected child-process execution by the service (a shell or interpreter spawned from a web/daemon process is a strong injection signal).
detection.adequacy: Necessary to catch exploitation and resident persistence after patching.

response.what_would_have_worked: Patch immediately (every consumer for a bundled library), hunt and remove web shells, rotate credentials and secrets, and review downstream/supply-chain impact (CI build artifacts, MFT data, EDR-managed endpoints).
response.adequacy: Mandatory; injection-to-RCE typically yields persistence and a pivot, which a bare patch does not remediate.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: The 30-day flaw-remediation SLA is far longer than the observed exploitation window for a KEV-listed, unauthenticated injection-to-RCE flaw; these are mass-exploited within days, and bundled-library flaws (PHPMailer/Bash) persist for years across the long tail.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: 'Appropriate timescales' is undefined; the standard 30-day reading is unsafe for an actively-exploited, internet-facing service or a widely-bundled vulnerable library.

NIS2-Art21-network-security.gap: Treats internet-facing services as essential-function infrastructure but lacks a CISA-KEV-style compressed remediation SLA, and does not require the web-shell-hunt / credential-rotation / supply-chain-review cleanup these RCEs need.

PCI-DSS-4.0-6.3.3.gap: The 30-day critical-patch window is exploitation acceptance for an internet-facing service in or adjacent to the CDE; WAF coverage is partial mitigation, not remediation.

compliance_exposure_score.basis: Internet-facing CWP Control Web Panel is run by audited organizations on a standard patch SLA and is mass-exploited within days; the required web-shell hunt, credential rotation, and (for bundled libraries) updating every consumer are rarely fully done, leaving long-tail exposure.

new_control_requirements.name: CONTROL-PANEL-PLUGIN-USER-SURFACE-MUST-NOT-REACH-ROOT-OPERATIONS
new_control_requirements.description: CWP Control Web Panel is the constrained user surface this control governs, and the packet places the defect exactly where the control forbids it: shell metacharacters supplied in the t_total parameter of a filemanager changePerm request reach a shell, so a request-supplied string on the panel's file-manager surface is what selects the command the server runs. Bound to this product the control means the panel's privileged filesystem operations — changing permissions on a hosted account's files is one of them — sit behind their own authorization boundary and are invoked through an argv-array interface, so no parameter of a file-manager request can extend the command line, and the panel authorizes the caller before the operation runs rather than relying on a check the request path reaches afterwards. This is also why the least-privilege gap recorded on this entry does not close the path: the packet's stated access requirement is knowing a valid non-root username, not holding that user's session, so the attacker never authenticates as any panel account, per-account privilege scoping is never consulted, and an AC-6 attestation passes cleanly while an unauthenticated caller reaches the shell. Distinguishing test: from an unauthenticated client against a staging CWP instance, send a filemanager changePerm request whose t_total value carries shell metacharacters and confirm it is refused before any command runs. Precondition: the vendor update is what repairs the endpoint — this control states the property to verify, it does not implement it. Until that update and its restart land, restricting which networks may reach the panel's web surface bounds who can send the request but leaves the endpoint fully exploitable to anything inside the permitted range, and it is unavailable where the panel must stay reachable for hosted-account administration.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Packet vector: 'CWP Control Web Panel (formerly CentOS Web Panel) contains an OS command Injection vulnerability that allows unauthenticated remote code execution via shell metacharacters in the t_total parameter in a filemanager changePerm request. A valid non-root username must be known.' CWE-78. CISA KEV listed 2025-11-04; active_exploitation confirmed; poc_available true; CVSS 9.8; RWEP 77. NIST SP 800-53 AC-6 (Least Privilege) is recorded among this entry's citing framework gaps. patch_available true, live_patch_available false, live_patch_notes: 'No live-patch tool registered for this entry at bulk-import time. Vendor patch typically requires service restart or system reboot per the KEV requiredAction.'

new_control_requirements.name: PERIMETER-COMPROMISE-REBUILD-NOT-PATCH
new_control_requirements.description: A CWP server answers unauthenticated callers by design and the packet's path ends in command execution on it, so the control's premise holds here without any appliance framing: the exploit needs no credential, only a known non-root username, and the packet records a public PoC with confirmed in-the-wild exploitation. Any instance that was reachable by untrusted callers before the update landed therefore has to be treated as one that may already have run attacker commands. For this product the runbook is to capture the panel and server configuration and the hosted-account inventory, rebuild the host from a known-good image, and rotate everything the panel held or could reach — panel administrator credentials, hosted-account and database passwords, and any API keys stored on it — rather than applying the update in place. Patch-in-place closes the changePerm injection and removes nothing written through it: a web shell under a hosted document root, an added cron entry, or an attacker-created account survives the upgrade intact, and none of those are what a build-version check inspects. Precondition: this is the response for an instance whose reachable window overlapped the exploitation the packet records; an instance that can be shown to have been unreachable by untrusted callers throughout is a straightforward patch item. Either way the packet registers no live-patch path, so the vendor fix carries the service restart or system reboot, and a server updated but not restarted is not yet remediated.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Packet attack vector: 'an OS command-injection flaw (CWE-78) enabling unauthenticated remote command execution on the hosting-control server. CISA KEV-listed 2025-11-04 with confirmed in-the-wild exploitation.' Vector states exploitation requires only that 'A valid non-root username must be known.' active_exploitation confirmed; poc_available true; CVSS 9.8; RWEP 77. patch_available true, live_patch_available false, live_patch_notes: 'No live-patch tool registered for this entry at bulk-import time. Vendor patch typically requires service restart or system reboot per the KEV requiredAction.'

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: CWP ships and updates on its own vendor channel, so a remediation programme whose patch obligation is written as operating-system patching never schedules this update at all — the host's OS package inventory stays current on every report while the panel that answers unauthenticated requests stays on the vulnerable build. For this CVE the clock runs from the KEV listing of 2025-11-04, with a public PoC and confirmed exploitation already in hand at that date, and completion has to be measured per host by the CWP build actually running rather than by an approved change record. The packet registers no live-patch tool and states the vendor patch typically requires a service restart or system reboot per the KEV requiredAction, so a server that took the update without restarting still runs the vulnerable code and must be counted as exposed until it does — on a shared hosting box that restart is also the step most likely to be deferred, because taking it interrupts every hosted site, and a deferral recorded as 'patched' is the specific way this remediation goes wrong.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CISA KEV listed 2025-11-04; active_exploitation confirmed; poc_available true; CVSS 9.8; RWEP 77; CWE-78. patch_available true, live_patch_available false, live_patch_notes: 'No live-patch tool registered for this entry at bulk-import time. Vendor patch typically requires service restart or system reboot per the KEV requiredAction.' attack_vector.description: an improper-input-validation flaw (CWE-20) in the Commerce/Magento REST API (the 'SessionReaper' flaw), letting an unauthenticated attacker take over customer/admin sessions and reach code execution. CISA KEV-listed 2025-10-24 with confirmed in-the-wild exploitation.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none (the flaw is reachable by an unauthenticated attacker on the application's public interface)
attack_vector.complexity: low — KEV-listed, actively exploited; treat as weaponized
attack_vector.ai_factor: No AI involvement documented in discovery or weaponization.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Apply the Adobe Commerce/Magento patch and the isolated hotfix; rotate the encryption key, invalidate sessions, and hunt for web shells — Magento RCE chains drop persistent backdoors.
prevention.adequacy: Patch is necessary but insufficient alone — web shells, stolen sessions, and forged keys survive the patch and require explicit cleanup and key rotation.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Monitoring on the Adobe Commerce / Magento: exploit-shaped requests, new web-shell files, unexpected process execution, and session/admin takeover without a matching login.
detection.adequacy: Necessary to catch exploitation and resident persistence after patching.

response.what_would_have_worked: Patch immediately, hunt and remove web shells, rotate application secrets/machine keys, and invalidate sessions, and review for lateral movement and data exfiltration.
response.adequacy: Mandatory; patch-in-place without cleanup leaves the attacker resident or able to re-authenticate.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: The 30-day flaw-remediation SLA is far longer than the observed exploitation window for a KEV-listed, unauthenticated web-application flaw; these are mass-exploited within days, and SSRF/deserialization/auth-bypass chains lead to data theft or RCE.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: 'Appropriate timescales' is undefined; the standard 30-day reading is unsafe for an actively-exploited, internet-facing web application.

NIS2-Art21-network-security.gap: Treats internet-facing applications as essential-function infrastructure but lacks a CISA-KEV-style compressed remediation SLA, and does not require the web-shell-hunt / key-rotation / egress-restriction cleanup these flaws need.

PCI-DSS-4.0-6.3.3.gap: The 30-day critical-patch window is exploitation acceptance for an internet-facing web application (e-commerce platforms like Magento sit squarely in PCI scope); WAF coverage is partial mitigation, not remediation.

compliance_exposure_score.basis: Internet-facing Adobe Commerce and Magento is run by audited organizations on a standard patch SLA and is mass-exploited within days; the required web-shell hunt, key rotation, and egress restriction are rarely part of the documented patch procedure.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: An Adobe Commerce or Magento Open Source storefront is on the public internet as a condition of doing its job, and the packet's path through the Commerce REST API requires no authentication, so there is no interior network step between a published exploit and the store — the exposure window is exactly the interval between the 2025-10-24 KEV listing and the fix being live. That makes this a KEV-clock item rather than a release-train item, which matters for this product class specifically: storefront deployments are commonly scheduled around retail change-freeze windows, and a freeze is precisely the period when the store is busiest, most reluctant to deploy, and most valuable to an attacker holding an unauthenticated session-takeover primitive. The packet records a vendor patch with no live-patch path and a service restart or reboot requirement, so remediation is applying the vendor fix and taking that restart inside the KEV window, with the freeze treated as something the KEV listing overrides rather than something that defers it. Distinguishing test: read the applied patch level from the running store and confirm the restart completed, rather than accepting the deployment ticket or the change-management record as evidence — a store whose pipeline shows the patch merged but not released is unremediated in the only place that counts.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Packet: CWE-20 improper input validation in Adobe Commerce and Magento Open Source, in the Commerce REST API (the 'SessionReaper' flaw), allowing an unauthenticated attacker to take over customer/admin sessions and reach code execution; the vector text records account takeover through the Commerce REST API. cisa_kev true with kev_date 2025-10-24; active_exploitation confirmed; poc_available true; cvss 9.8; rwep_score 77. patch_available true; live_patch_available false, with live_patch_notes recording no registered live-patch tool and that the vendor patch typically requires service restart or system reboot per the KEV requiredAction.

new_control_requirements.name: PERIMETER-COMPROMISE-REBUILD-NOT-PATCH
new_control_requirements.description: The storefront occupies the position this control governs even though it is an application tier rather than an appliance: an unauthenticated, internet-reachable path — the Commerce REST API — that ends in code execution, under exploitation confirmed in the wild as of the 2025-10-24 KEV listing. Applied to a store, the requirement is that remediation is not 'apply the patch and close the ticket'. Any store that was reachable and unpatched during the exploitation window has to be handled as possibly holding attacker-written code and attacker-held sessions, because the packet's primitive is session takeover: the fix closes the path that produced those sessions and does nothing to sessions already issued through it. That makes forced invalidation of every session predating the fix, plus rotation of administrator credentials and integration/API keys, part of remediation rather than a follow-up, and it makes the integrity question a comparison of deployed storefront code against the release artifact rather than an inference from the absence of an alert. Distinguishing test: on a patched store, confirm a session token minted before the fix is now refused, and diff the deployed code tree against the build artifact — a store that reports the vendor patch applied while pre-fix sessions still authenticate has closed the entry path and left the access it produced in place.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Packet: the flaw lets an unauthenticated attacker take over customer/admin sessions and reach code execution through the Commerce REST API; cisa_kev true with kev_date 2025-10-24 and active_exploitation confirmed, so the exploitation window predates any operator's remediation. poc_available true; cvss 9.8; rwep_score 77. The packet's citing framework gaps include UK-CAF-B2 (Identity and access control). patch_available true; live_patch_available false, with the vendor patch requiring service restart or reboot per the KEV requiredAction.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: The 30-day flaw-remediation SLA is far longer than the observed exploitation window for a KEV-listed unauthenticated server flaw; CISA KEV due dates are days. The ToolShell SharePoint chain was mass-exploited within days of disclosure.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: 'Appropriate timescales' is undefined; the standard 30-day reading is unsafe for an unauthenticated, actively-exploited flaw on an internet-facing enterprise server.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: WSUS is the host the rest of the estate takes its updates from, so this entry inverts the usual remediation ordering: the clock that opened with the 2025-10-24 KEV listing has to be run on the update server itself ahead of the endpoints it serves, because an unauthenticated deserialization path to remote code execution on WSUS sits upstream of every patch decision those endpoints make. The packet records no live-patch path and a vendor patch that typically requires a service restart or system reboot per the KEV requiredAction, so completion is measured by the WSUS host's state after that restart — a server that has installed the update and not restarted is still running the vulnerable service and must be counted as exposed, not as remediated. Because active exploitation is confirmed and a public PoC exists, an instance that stayed reachable through the window before that restart needs triage rather than a 'patched per SLA' verdict.

new_control_requirements.name: SERVICE-INTERNAL-PROTOCOL-DESERIALIZATION-HARDENING
new_control_requirements.description: The WSUS listener accepts content from a peer that never authenticates and hands it to a deserializer — the packet puts remote code execution ahead of any authentication decision — so that listener has to be treated as a trust boundary rather than as an internal convenience. For this deployment the requirement is that the WSUS service endpoints accept connections only from the managed clients and administrative hosts that legitimately speak to them, enforced by host firewall or network ACL rather than inherited from the assumption that WSUS sits on a trusted network, and that content arriving there is constrained to what the update protocol legitimately conveys instead of being permitted to construct arbitrary objects. The precondition has to be stated rather than implied: WSUS must remain reachable by every endpoint it services, so this narrows the caller set and cannot close the path for anything inside it — a compromised managed client, or any host that can place itself in that set, still reaches the deserializer. It bounds exposure during the remediation window and is not a substitute for taking the server through the update and its restart. This is also why the cited least-privilege gap is recorded here: the attacker never authenticates, so no account-privilege scoping is consulted on this path and an access-control attestation passes cleanly while it stays open.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Packet records CWE-502, vector 'Microsoft Windows Server Update Service (WSUS) contains a deserialization of untrusted data vulnerability that allows for remote code execution', and an attack_vector stating the flaw is 'reachable by an unauthenticated attacker for remote code execution'. CVSS 9.8, RWEP 77, active_exploitation confirmed, poc_available true. Citing gaps include NIST-800-53-AC-6 (Least Privilege) and UK-CAF-B4 (System security).

new_control_requirements.name: ENDPOINT-MGMT-DEPLOYMENT-CHANNEL-INTEGRITY
new_control_requirements.description: Code execution on WSUS lands inside the software-distribution channel every managed endpoint already trusts, so the WSUS installation and the content it serves have to be governed as a privileged distribution channel rather than as application data: file-integrity-monitor the installation and the directories it serves artifacts from, alert on writes that do not correspond to a sanctioned administrator action or a vendor synchronization, and hold the server to KEV-priority patching as a management-plane asset in its own right rather than as one more Windows server in the general fleet. This is the half of the response that still has value after the vendor update lands, because the fix closes the deserialization sink but removes nothing an attacker wrote through it — and with exploitation confirmed from the 2025-10-24 listing, an instance that was reachable before remediation needs forensic triage rather than patch-and-close. The precondition: integrity monitoring detects, it does not prevent, and it is only meaningful where the baseline predates the exposure window. Where no pre-exposure baseline exists, the content the server distributes has to be re-established from vendor-sourced material instead of being trusted from the server's present state.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Packet records active_exploitation confirmed with cisa_kev true and kev_date 2025-10-24, poc_available true, and an unauthenticated deserialization path (CWE-502) to remote code execution on the WSUS server. patch_available is true with live_patch_available false, so the deserialization sink is closed only once the vendor update and its restart are taken. new_control_requirements.name: DEVICE-MANAGEMENT-GATEWAY-CONFIG-ENDPOINT-AUTH-INPUT-NEUTRALIZATION
new_control_requirements.description: LANSCOPE Endpoint Manager is the device-management platform itself, and CWE-940 places the defect precisely at the trust decision: the receiving component decides whether to act on a packet by judging where it appears to have come from rather than by verifying who sent it, so an unauthenticated attacker's crafted packets are processed as trusted commands and reach arbitrary code execution. Applied to this product, the control means every service on the LANSCOPE management agent and server that accepts commands authenticates its caller cryptographically before the command is parsed or executed — a verdict that cannot be satisfied by source address, network position, or any other property the sender controls — and that those listening services are not reachable from networks with no managed endpoints on them. The precondition on the network half has to be stated rather than left implied: managed endpoints must be able to reach the management server for the product to function, so restricting reachability shrinks the population that can send crafted packets to hosts inside the managed network but does not close the path — any compromised workstation in that population still has it, and for a deployment where agents span the whole estate the reduction is small. Closure is the vendor update, and the packet records no live-patch tool with a vendor patch that typically requires a service restart or system reboot per the KEV requiredAction, so a server or agent that has taken the update without restarting is not remediated. Distinguishing test: on a staging LANSCOPE instance, send crafted command packets from an unauthenticated host and confirm refusal before execution — then repeat from a host inside the managed address range and confirm the command is still refused. If the second attempt succeeds, the product is still authenticating the channel rather than the caller, which is the defect itself; the least-privilege control cited against this entry is never consulted on this path because the attacker holds no LANSCOPE account to scope.

new_control_requirements.name: ENDPOINT-MGMT-DEPLOYMENT-CHANNEL-INTEGRITY
new_control_requirements.description: The packet puts arbitrary code execution on the LANSCOPE management agent and server — the component that holds the management relationship with the endpoints it administers — and records active_exploitation as confirmed with a public PoC. That makes the installation and, wherever the deployment uses it to distribute software or run commands on managed endpoints, the content it hands to its agents a privileged distribution channel rather than ordinary application data. Bound to this product, the control means file-integrity monitoring across the LANSCOPE installation and the directories it serves content from, with alerts on any write that does not correspond to a sanctioned administrator action or a vendor update, and holding the LANSCOPE server to KEV-priority patching as a management-plane asset in its own right. This is the control that retains value after the vendor update lands, which is why the update-shaped framework controls cited on this entry are insufficient on their own: the fix closes the path by which crafted packets became trusted commands, but it removes nothing that was already written or already executed through that path, and an artifact placed on the server before remediation survives the upgrade and keeps whatever reach the server has. Preconditions: monitoring neither prevents exploitation nor reconstructs the period before it was enabled — a monitor stood up after the exposure window has no baseline for what changed during it, so the comparison must be made against a record captured before that window or against vendor-shipped file state, and where neither exists the honest verdict is that server integrity is unestablished rather than clean. Distinguishing test: enumerate the content the LANSCOPE server would currently distribute or execute and reconcile it item by item against the change record of sanctioned administrator actions since before the exposure window; unreconciled items are the finding. An attestation that the LANSCOPE server is running the fixed build passes cleanly while a payload placed pre-update continues to reach managed endpoints.

new_control_requirements.name: EOL-ASSET-DECOMMISSION
new_control_requirements.description: This entry is the case the control exists for, and the packet states both halves. patch_available is true — a fixed build carrying this JavaScriptCore fix exists — and the vector itself states that the impacted product could be end-of-life and/or end-of-service and that users should discontinue product utilization. Those facts together define the requirement: on a unit whose hardware can still take an Apple security update, reaching the fixed build is an interim state; on a unit that can no longer take one, the terminal state is removal or replacement, because that device is exposed not only to this code-execution flaw but to everything found in that engine since its last build. Scope to what the packet names — macOS, iOS, tvOS, Safari and watchOS — and inventory those. The packet ties the CWE-94 sink to JavaScriptCore in those products and gives no mapping into other vendors' browsers or other software that embeds a web engine, so treating every renderer in the estate as an instance of this CVE manufactures findings and replacement work against software no evidence implicates. In operational terms: enumerate every macOS, iOS, tvOS, watchOS and Safari install that renders untrusted web content, record for each whether its hardware can still receive a build carrying the fix, put those on the interim clock against the 2025-10-20 KEV listing, and put the rest on a dated replacement schedule — a risk acceptance with no removal date leaves a KEV-listed flaw with a public PoC and confirmed exploitation in service indefinitely. Precondition on the interim half: live_patch_available is false and the packet records that the vendor patch typically requires a service restart or system reboot per the KEV requiredAction, so a device that downloaded the update but has not restarted still runs the vulnerable code and is not remediated. And because exploitation is confirmed and delivery is attacker-controlled web content, a device that rendered untrusted content while exposed belongs on the incident path rather than being closed on the patch record.

Vendor patch typically requires service restart or system reboot per the KEV requiredAction.' AU-Essential-8-Patch (Patch operating systems), ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8 (Management of technical vulnerabilities), NIST-800-53-SI-2 (Flaw Remediation) and NIS2-Art21-patch-management (Vulnerability handling and disclosure) are recorded as citing gaps against this entry — every one of them measures whether a fix was applied within a timescale, and none of them has a terminal state for a device on which no future fix will ever be installable.

new_control_requirements.name: MOBILE-OS-MINIMUM-PATCH-LEVEL-ENFORCEMENT
new_control_requirements.description: The population this control has to bite on for this entry is the one the decommission requirement produces: macOS, iOS, tvOS, watchOS and Safari installs that cannot reach a build carrying the JavaScriptCore fix. For those there is no future build that clears them, so the fixed build has to function as an access condition — organizational mail, VPN, document stores and identity access denied to a device below it — rather than as a stale row on a patch-compliance dashboard that ages indefinitely. The same condition covers the shorter window on devices that can take the fix: the packet records that the vendor patch typically requires a restart, so a device between download and restart is still in the exposed population and needs an access-side answer, not a patch-side one. The distinguishing test is to enrol a device pinned below the fixed build and confirm the policy actually denies it access to protected resources; an estate that surfaces the stale build on a report while the device keeps its mail and VPN has recorded the exposure rather than removed it. Precondition, and it is the reason this cannot be logged as the mitigation: an access condition bounds what an attacker gains from a compromised device, it does nothing to the device itself. It does not remove the JavaScriptCore defect, does not evict an implant on a device already compromised — and the packet's note that Apple flaws of this class are typically used in targeted-spyware chains makes that the case to plan for — and it reaches only devices the management channel enrols. Personally-owned or unenrolled Macs, iPhones, Apple TVs and Watches touching organizational data are not covered by it, and the only lever against those is removing the access path they use.

new_control_requirements.name: MOBILE-ZERO-CLICK-HARDENING
new_control_requirements.description: The delivery path the packet records is attacker-controlled web content processed by JavaScriptCore, and its attack_vector notes that Apple flaws of this class are typically used in targeted-spyware chains. For the cohort plausibly inside that targeting set — executives, journalists, legal and security staff — the reboot-gated update is not fast enough on its own, so place their macOS and iOS devices in Apple's reduced-attack-surface mode, where untrusted web content, message attachments, link previews and fonts are not processed automatically. That narrows the path into the CWE-94 sink during the window that opened before anyone in the estate learned of the flaw: the packet records confirmed exploitation and a public PoC, so the exposure predates the 2025-10-20 KEV listing and the assignment cannot be a reaction to it. The mode only helps if it was already on when the content arrived, which makes it a standing posture assigned to the high-risk cohort ahead of the next disclosure rather than a response to this one. new_control_requirements.evidence: Packet names the affected product as 'Adobe Experience Manager Forms in JEE' with 'an unspecified vulnerability that allows for arbitrary code execution' (CWE-94), reachable per the attack vector as 'unauthenticated remote code execution on the AEM Forms server'. CISA KEV listed 2025-10-15; active_exploitation confirmed; poc_available true; CVSS 8.8; RWEP 77. patch_available true, live_patch_available false, live_patch_notes: 'No live-patch tool registered for this entry at bulk-import time. CVE-2025-47827.name: IGEL OS Use of a Key Past its Expiration Date Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: use of a key past its expiration date (CWE-324) in IGEL OS Secure Boot verification, letting an attacker bypass signature verification and boot a modified or unverified OS image (a Secure Boot / boot-trust bypass). CISA KEV-listed 2025-10-14 with confirmed in-the-wild exploitation.
attack_vector.privileges_required: low-to-physical (an attacker who can place a modified image or influence boot, exploiting the bypassed signature check)
attack_vector.complexity: low — KEV-listed, actively exploited; treat as weaponized
attack_vector.ai_factor: No AI involvement documented in discovery or weaponization.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Apply the IGEL OS update so Secure Boot verification uses a valid, unexpired key; re-provision affected thin clients and verify the boot chain integrity against a hardware root of trust.
prevention.adequacy: Patch is necessary but the named compensating controls are what hold when the patch lags or the trust mechanism itself is defeated.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Monitoring for boot of unsigned/modified IGEL images, Secure Boot verification against an expired key, and persistence that survives re-imaging on thin clients.
detection.adequacy: Backstops the window before patching and catches the post-exploitation stage.

response.what_would_have_worked: Patch, re-provision affected devices with corrected trust anchors, and verify boot-chain integrity — a boot-trust bypass can leave persistence beneath the OS that a reinstall does not remove.
response.adequacy: Mandatory; exploitation of this class leaves persistence or a foothold that a bare patch does not remediate.

NIST-800-53-SI-7-integrity.gap: Software/firmware integrity verification is required, but the verification used an expired key, so the Secure Boot trust anchor itself failed; integrity verification must use valid, unexpired keys and reject expired ones, which the control does not explicitly enforce.

NIST-800-53-SC-7-boundary.gap: A boot-trust bypass lets unverified code run beneath the OS, defeating boundary and endpoint controls layered above it; the defense requires hardware root-of-trust enforcement that rejects images signed with an expired key.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: 'Appropriate timescales' is undefined and ill-suited to a boot-integrity flaw, where a tampered boot chain can persist across reinstalls until the device is re-provisioned with corrected trust anchors.

compliance_exposure_score.basis: IGEL thin clients are deployed at scale in VDI estates; audited organizations rarely verify boot-chain integrity against a hardware root of trust, so a Secure Boot bypass via an expired key leaves below-OS persistence that endpoint controls cannot see.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: The packet's chain runs entirely below the operating system: igel-flash-driver mis-verifies the image signature, so a crafted root filesystem mounts from an unverified SquashFS image and the device runs an attacker's OS. Nothing inside the booted session can detect or contain that, so the vendor update is the only closure, driven across every IGEL OS endpoint on the clock that opened with the 2025-10-14 KEV listing rather than folded into the next scheduled image-refresh cycle. Completion must be measured by the build each device actually booted, not by 'update assigned' or 'update downloaded' in the management console: the packet records a vendor patch with no live-patch path and a fix that requires a service restart or system reboot, so a device that has taken the update but not rebooted is still running an image the unfixed verification path admitted and has to be counted as exposed, not remediated. Scope this to IGEL OS, which is the product the packet names; it gives no mapping from igel-flash-driver into any other boot chain.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Packet: cisa_kev true, kev_date 2025-10-14, active_exploitation confirmed, poc_available true, RWEP 77 against CVSS 8.8. patch_available true, live_patch_available false, live_patch_notes 'No live-patch tool registered for this entry at bulk-import time. Vendor patch typically requires service restart or system reboot per the KEV requiredAction.' Vector: 'IGEL OS contains a use of a key past its expiration date vulnerability that allows for Secure Boot bypass. The igel-flash-driver module improperly verifies a cryptographic signature. Ultimately, a crafted root filesystem can be mounted from an unverified SquashFS image.' (CWE-324).

new_control_requirements.name: PROTECTION-MECHANISM-FAILURE-CLASS-REGRESSION
new_control_requirements.description: The mechanism that failed on this entry is boot-image signature verification itself: per the packet igel-flash-driver accepts a signature made with a key past its expiration date, so Secure Boot reports enforcement while an unverified SquashFS root filesystem mounts. A version-number attestation cannot separate 'verification restored' from 'verification still failing open', because the version string is exactly what the mechanism was already reporting while it admitted the image. For this CVE the control means the boot-verification path is re-tested as a class on every IGEL OS image deployment, keyed on the behaviour the packet documents: on a staging device, present the boot chain with a modified or unverified SquashFS root filesystem image and confirm it refuses to mount it — and keep that test in the battery for subsequent images instead of retiring it once this CVE is closed, since the defect is in the check rather than in one image. Precondition: the test needs a staging device the operator can attempt an unverified boot on and a way to observe the refusal. Where that does not exist the mechanism's state is unverified, and the device must be treated as exposed until it boots a build the vendor names as fixed rather than passing because a scanner read the version.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Packet vector: 'The igel-flash-driver module improperly verifies a cryptographic signature. Ultimately, a crafted root filesystem can be mounted from an unverified SquashFS image', classed CWE-324 (use of a key past its expiration date) and described in the attack vector as a Secure Boot / boot-trust bypass letting an attacker boot a modified or unverified OS image. cisa_kev true with kev_date 2025-10-14, active_exploitation confirmed and poc_available true, so the failing check is being exercised rather than theoretical. patch_available true, live_patch_available false.

CVE-2025-24990.name: Microsoft Windows Untrusted Pointer Dereference Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: an untrusted-pointer-dereference flaw (CWE-822) in a Windows kernel-mode component, exploited by a local foothold to gain kernel privilege. CISA KEV-listed 2025-10-14 with confirmed in-the-wild exploitation; LPEs of this class are routinely paired with an initial-access flaw by ransomware operators.
attack_vector.privileges_required: low (any local foothold — an unprivileged process, RDP session, or commodity malware on the endpoint)
attack_vector.complexity: low — KEV-listed, actively exploited; treat as weaponized
attack_vector.ai_factor: No AI involvement documented in discovery or weaponization.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Apply the Microsoft security update; enforce hypervisor-protected code integrity (HVCI) / Virtualization-Based Security (VBS), and enable the Microsoft Vulnerable Driver Blocklist to shrink kernel-LPE attack surface on the long tail.
prevention.adequacy: Patch is definitive; the gap is the chain (initial access → unpatched LPE → SYSTEM) which a patched endpoint shuts down. HVCI/Blocklist backstops unpatched estates.

detection.what_would_have_worked: EDR signatures for the LPE primitive (token swap, process-impersonation, kernel-driver crashes) and for unprivileged-to-SYSTEM transitions without an admin trigger.
detection.adequacy: Backstops endpoints not yet patched; LPE is typically silent without EDR coverage.

response.what_would_have_worked: Force the patch across the estate; for a confirmed exploitation, treat the host as compromised (ransomware kits typically follow within hours), isolate, preserve forensic state, and review for credential theft.
response.adequacy: Mandatory; SYSTEM-level exploitation makes the host an unreliable platform for further work and requires rebuild.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: The 30-day flaw-remediation SLA is far longer than the observed exploitation window for a KEV-listed Windows kernel/driver LPE; ransomware operators typically pair these with an initial-access flaw and elevate to SYSTEM within hours of a foothold.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: 'Appropriate timescales' is undefined; the standard reading is unsafe for an actively-exploited kernel/driver LPE that is part of every modern ransomware kit.

AU-ISM-1546.gap: Essential 8 patch-applications (48h at ML3) is the right tier for a Windows LPE, but the load-bearing endpoint controls are hypervisor-protected code integrity (HVCI/VBS) and the Microsoft Vulnerable Driver Blocklist — neither of which the framework demands explicitly.

compliance_exposure_score.basis: Windows endpoints are universal; audited organizations gate kernel patches behind change windows or rely on cumulative monthly updates that leave the LPE chain open for ~30 days at a stretch. HVCI/VBS and the Vulnerable Driver Blocklist remain off-by-default in many estates.

new_control_requirements.name: KERNEL-MODULE-INVENTORY-AND-DISABLE
new_control_requirements.description: The vulnerable component here is a modem driver that ships with Windows itself, so it is present and loadable on hosts whose owners never installed it and have no modem hardware. Operators need a per-host inventory of kernel-mode drivers that enumerates OS-supplied drivers, not only vendor-installed ones, with a business justification recorded per driver and a standing action to keep the Agere modem driver unloadable on machines with no modem function. Nothing in the citing frameworks obliges anyone to enumerate a privileged driver they never chose to deploy, which is exactly why this attack surface survived on fleets that pass driver-hygiene and asset-inventory audits.
new_control_requirements.evidence: The packet identifies the affected component as the Microsoft Windows Agere Modem Driver, with an untrusted pointer dereference (CWE-822) that allows privilege escalation such that a successful attacker could gain administrator privileges, exploited from a local foothold. CISA KEV-listed 2025-10-14 with active_exploitation confirmed and poc_available true.

new_control_requirements.name: VULNERABLE-DRIVER-BLOCKLIST-ENFORCEMENT
new_control_requirements.description: This is a signed kernel-mode driver whose untrusted-pointer-dereference primitive hands an unprivileged local process administrator-level kernel execution, so the enforcement question is whether the driver can be loaded at all rather than only whether the host took the latest update. Enable HVCI together with the vendor recommended-driver blocklist so the vulnerable Agere modem driver cannot load, and verify the enforcement on hosts rebuilt from older images or restored from backup — that is where a vulnerable driver binary reappears on a fleet that has otherwise been updated.
new_control_requirements.evidence: The packet records an untrusted pointer dereference (CWE-822) in the Microsoft Windows Agere Modem Driver yielding privilege escalation to administrator privileges from a local foothold, with poc_available true, RWEP 77 against a CVSS of 7.8, and confirmed in-the-wild exploitation per the 2025-10-14 KEV listing.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: Put the driver fix on a KEV clock and scope the affected population to every Windows install that carries the in-box Agere modem driver, not to the small set of machines with modem hardware attached — the driver's presence, not its use, is what makes the host exploitable. As with other kernel-mode fixes in this packet the SLA can only be closed out on the restarted host, since no live-patch path is recorded, so exception tracking has to name the hosts still awaiting a restart.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CISA KEV-listed 2025-10-14 with active_exploitation confirmed, RWEP 77 against a CVSS of 7.8, and poc_available true. patch_available is true while live_patch_available is false; live_patch_notes states no live-patch tool is registered for this entry and that the vendor patch typically requires service restart or system reboot per the KEV requiredAction.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: Windows Remote Access Connection Manager is present on the whole Windows estate, so this improper-access-control flaw turns any commodity local foothold - a phished payload, a low-privilege service account - into SYSTEM on the same host, and the packet records it as confirmed in-the-wild exploitation of a class routinely paired with an initial-access flaw by ransomware operators.
