attack_vector.description: An attacker already holding arbitrary kernel read/write uses this RTKit memory-corruption flaw to bypass kernel memory protections, a late stage of a targeted exploit chain.
attack_vector.privileges_required: low (local; presumes an earlier chain stage supplying kernel r/w)
attack_vector.complexity: high — requires a pre-existing kernel primitive and reliable RTKit mitigation-bypass
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered — reported to Apple via coordinated disclosure. No AI involvement documented.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Apply the iOS/iPadOS/macOS update; enable Lockdown Mode for high-risk users
prevention.adequacy: The update removes the primitive, but targeted users may already be compromised before the patch is applied.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Mobile-threat-defense telemetry and sysdiagnose/crash-log forensics
detection.adequacy: Kernel-chain exploitation is low-artifact; detection typically lags.

response.what_would_have_worked: Force fleet OS update, re-image suspected-targeted devices, rotate accessed credentials
response.adequacy: Kernel-level compromise warrants treating the device as untrusted.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: Scheduled OS-patch SLAs cannot beat a zero-day RTKit memory-corruption bypass that is exploited in the wild at disclosure time.

NIST-800-53-CM-7.gap: Hardening/least-functionality guidance does not extend to the RTKit real-time coprocessor firmware where this flaw lives; MDM policy cannot mitigate it.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: Patch-management obligations lack the rapid mobile-fleet enforcement mandate needed when the flaw is an actively-exploited kernel-protection bypass.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: The control assumes device mitigations hold; this bug defeats them, invalidating the assumed protection baseline until the update lands.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Essential-Eight patch maturity is workstation/server-scoped and does not compel same-day mobile OS updates for an active mobile zero-day.

new_control_requirements.name: MOBILE-ENDPOINT-MDM-ENFORCED-KEV-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: The packet names the fixed releases across the iOS, iPadOS, macOS, tvOS, visionOS and watchOS families — iOS 16.7.8 and iPadOS 16.7.8, iOS 17.4 and iPadOS 17.4, macOS Monterey 12.7.6, macOS Sonoma 14.4, macOS Ventura 13.6.7, tvOS 17.4, visionOS 1.1, watchOS 10.4 — and that list is this control's scope statement: an estate that drives the KEV clock opened 2024-03-06 across managed iPhones and Macs alone still leaves the tvOS, visionOS and watchOS builds the packet names running the vulnerable code, and those device classes typically sit outside the management channel that enforces the phone and Mac deadline. For this CVE the control means the update is pushed on that clock with user deferral disallowed, and completion is measured per device against the specific build the packet names for that device's OS family and track — not against an 'available' or 'downloaded' state in the management console. The packet records no live-patch mechanism and states that remediation requires applying the fixed release and rebooting, so a device that has staged the update but not restarted is still running the vulnerable code and must be counted as exposed; on a phone or a watch the restart is precisely the step a user defers, which is how this remediation gets recorded as complete while the exposure stands. Distinguishing test: enumerate the estate's Apple devices by OS family and installed build and confirm each is at or above the build the packet names for it, including the device classes the standard patch report does not cover. Precondition: this reaches only devices the management channel can see and compel — a personally owned or unenrolled device carrying organizational data is remediated by removing that access or that data, not by a deadline it never receives.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Packet vector: 'A memory corruption issue was addressed with improved validation. This issue is fixed in iOS 16.7.8 and iPadOS 16.7.8, iOS 17.4 and iPadOS 17.4, macOS Monterey 12.7.6, macOS Sonoma 14.4, macOS Ventura 13.6.7, tvOS 17.4, visionOS 1.1, watchOS 10.4. An attacker with arbitrary kernel read and write capability may be able to bypass kernel memory protections. Apple is aware of a report that this issue may have been exploited.' CWE-787, CISA KEV-listed 2024-03-06, active_exploitation confirmed, poc_available false, CVSS 7.8, RWEP 60. patch_available true, live_patch_available false, live_patch_notes: 'No vendor live-patch mechanism; remediation requires applying the fixed release and rebooting.'

new_control_requirements.name: MOBILE-OS-MINIMUM-PATCH-LEVEL-ENFORCEMENT
new_control_requirements.description: The packet fixes this on two parallel iOS/iPadOS tracks — 16.7.8 and 17.4 — and on three separate macOS releases, Monterey 12.7.6, Sonoma 14.4 and Ventura 13.6.7. That is the condition a single minimum-version threshold cannot express, and it fails in the dangerous direction: a policy admitting anything at or above 16.7.8 admits a device running 17.0, which is numerically higher and still carries the flaw, while a policy pinned at 17.4 marks every device that correctly took 16.7.8 as non-compliant. For this CVE the control therefore means the minimum build is stated per OS family and per track, and enforced as an access condition — mail, VPN and document access withheld from a device below the build named for its own track — rather than surfaced as a row on a patch-compliance report. The distinguishing test is to enrol a device sitting above one track's fix but below its own, a 17.x device on a build under 17.4, and confirm the policy denies it access to protected resources; an estate whose compliance rule is a single version comparison passes that device while it stays exposed. Precondition: withholding access bounds what the device can reach while it is exposed, it does not remediate the device, and the packet's attack description is of a device whose attacker already holds arbitrary kernel read and write — so a device suspected of having been in that state belongs on the incident path and is not returned to service by clearing a build check. This is a holding measure for the window before the fixed release and its required reboot land, not a substitute for them.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Packet vector names the fixed builds on parallel tracks: 'iOS 16.7.8 and iPadOS 16.7.8, iOS 17.4 and iPadOS 17.4, macOS Monterey 12.7.6, macOS Sonoma 14.4, macOS Ventura 13.6.7, tvOS 17.4, visionOS 1.1, watchOS 10.4', and states 'An attacker with arbitrary kernel read and write capability may be able to bypass kernel memory protections.' attack_vector: the attacker already holds arbitrary kernel read/write and uses this RTKit memory-corruption flaw to bypass kernel memory protections, a late stage of a targeted exploit chain. CWE-787, KEV 2024-03-06, active_exploitation confirmed. patch_available true with live_patch_available false; remediation requires applying the fixed release and rebooting.

new_control_requirements.name: MOBILE-ZERO-CLICK-HARDENING
new_control_requirements.description: The packet places this flaw at a late stage of a targeted exploit chain: the attacker already holds arbitrary kernel read and write, and uses this RTKit memory-corruption bug to bypass kernel memory protections. Nothing an operator configures reduces that primitive once the chain has reached this point, and the control must not be recorded as if it did. What it means for this CVE is the earlier stage — for the cohort plausibly inside the targeting set chains of this class serve, place the device in a reduced-attack-surface posture so untrusted web content, message attachments, fonts and link previews are not processed automatically, narrowing the delivery of the stages that produce the kernel read/write this bug consumes. Two conditions have to be stated or this becomes a mitigation on paper only. First, the posture has to already be in force: assigned in response to a disclosure it gives nothing for the window that mattered, and the packet's own record is Apple aware of a report that the issue may have been exploited — that is after the fact by construction. Second, it does not evict an attacker already resident; a device believed to have carried the chain goes to the incident path rather than into a hardening rollout, and the packet's description of an attacker with arbitrary kernel read and write is the state in which no device-side setting is trustworthy. Distinguishing test: name the high-risk cohort and show the reduced-attack-surface posture was applied to each of those devices before the disclosure date, not after — a policy that exists but was assigned reactively passes an attestation while providing nothing during the exposure.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Packet attack_vector: 'An attacker already holding arbitrary kernel read/write uses this RTKit memory-corruption flaw to bypass kernel memory protections, a late stage of a targeted exploit chain.' Packet vector: 'An attacker with arbitrary kernel read and write capability may be able to bypass kernel memory protections. Apple is aware of a report that this issue may have been exploited.' CWE-787, CISA KEV-listed 2024-03-06, active_exploitation confirmed, poc_available false, CVSS 7.8, RWEP 60. patch_available true, live_patch_available false — remediation requires applying the fixed release and rebooting. The entry cites NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 CM-7 (Least Functionality) among its insufficient framework controls.

attack_vector.description: A malicious app abuses a Framework UI flaw to hide the foreground-service notification Android normally forces, so background sensor/data access runs without the persistent status-bar indicator that would alert the user.
attack_vector.privileges_required: low (local; a malicious app already installed, no additional privileges)
attack_vector.complexity: low — no user interaction required once the app is installed
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered — reported via Android's security bulletin process. No AI involvement documented.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Apply the June 2023 Pixel patch level and restrict app installs to vetted sources
prevention.adequacy: The patch restores the notification guarantee, but a device that ran a malicious app pre-patch may already have leaked data.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Mobile-threat-defense checks for apps holding sensitive runtime permissions with suppressed foreground-service notifications
detection.adequacy: Most MDM/MTD tooling does not inspect notification integrity, so this is rarely caught.

response.what_would_have_worked: Remove the offending app, review sensor/data-access grants, rotate credentials entered on the device
response.adequacy: Because the abuse is covert, response depends on independent discovery of the malicious app.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: OS-patch SLAs for mobile fleets rarely enforce the specific Pixel/Android June-2023 patch level fast enough to close a flaw already exploited in the wild.

NIST-800-53-SI-4.gap: Endpoint monitoring rarely inspects Android foreground-service/notification integrity, so the very signal that would reveal a hidden malicious service is not collected.

NIS2-Art21-incident-handling.gap: Incident-handling obligations do not account for suppressed on-device indicators; a hidden foreground service defeats the user-facing signal responders would rely on.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: Device-security expectations assume the OS surfaces ongoing-activity notifications; this flaw removes that assurance, so the control's assumed transparency baseline fails.

AU-Essential-8-App-Hardening.gap: Application-hardening guidance is desktop-browser-centric and does not address Android app-permission/foreground-service abuse that this notification-hiding flaw enables.

new_control_requirements.name: MOBILE-OS-MINIMUM-PATCH-LEVEL-ENFORCEMENT
new_control_requirements.description: The packet pins this to Android-13 and to a Framework rendering path, and the trigger is an application already running on the device, so both halves of this control bind. First: the Android build carrying the fix is an access condition for organizational data — a device below it is quarantined from mail, VPN and document access rather than surfaced as a row on a patch-compliance dashboard — and because the packet says remediation requires applying the fixed release and rebooting with no vendor live-patch mechanism, a device that has downloaded the update but not restarted sits below the line and must be treated as exposed. Second, and load-bearing for the interval where a device is waiting on an OEM or carrier build it cannot obtain, the exploit needs a malicious app to be running at all, so the remaining lever is constraining what code gets installed: restrict installation to vetted sources and disallow unknown-source and side-loaded installs on any device holding organizational data. The precondition to state is that neither half is retroactive. Enforcing the build stops future suppression of the notification; it does not evict an app already present, does not revoke the background access that app already holds, and does not reconstruct what ran while the indicator was hidden — so a device suspected of carrying such an app needs an installed-app and permission review, not a build check alone. The distinguishing test: enrol a device pinned below the fixed build and confirm the policy actually denies it protected resources; an estate that lists the stale build on a report while the device keeps its mail and VPN access has recorded the exposure rather than removed it.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Packet vector: 'In applyRemoteView of NotificationContentInflater.java, there is a possible way to hide foreground service notification due to misleading or insufficient UI. This could lead to local information disclosure with no additional execution privileges needed. User interaction is not needed for exploitation. Product: Android Versions: Android-13 Android ID: A-251586912.' attack_vector: a malicious app hides the foreground-service notification Android normally forces, so background sensor/data access runs without the persistent status-bar indicator. CWE-200, CVSS 5.5, RWEP 47, poc_available false, CISA KEV-listed 2024-03-05 with active_exploitation confirmed. patch_available true, live_patch_available false, live_patch_notes: 'No vendor live-patch mechanism; remediation requires applying the fixed release and rebooting.'

new_control_requirements.name: PROTECTION-MECHANISM-FAILURE-CLASS-REGRESSION
new_control_requirements.description: Android's forced foreground-service notification is a protection mechanism in the sense this control governs: the platform mandates a persistent visible indicator precisely so background service execution cannot be silent, and the packet describes a Framework path that defeats it through misleading or insufficient UI. That makes the mechanism, not the individual CVE, the thing that needs testing — any detection or user-transparency posture that keys off the presence of the status-bar indicator is only as good as the mechanism producing it, and this entry is proof the mechanism can fail without the monitoring above it noticing anything at all. Applied to a managed mobile estate, the requirement is that every accepted OS build be validated against the known indicator-suppression primitives for this class before it is treated as the fixed build, and that mobile-threat-defense detections which infer background activity from the visible notification be regression-tested on the same schedule rather than assumed to carry forward. State the limits: class regression only covers primitives already known, so it does not detect a novel way of hiding the notification, and passing the battery on a build is not evidence that no app already on the estate used this one — it validates the mechanism going forward, it does not produce history. Because of that, this control complements an app-inventory and permission review rather than substituting for it, and where an operator cannot run the battery at all, the honest position is that indicator-derived monitoring on that build is unvalidated rather than sound.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Packet vector: the flaw is 'a possible way to hide foreground service notification due to misleading or insufficient UI', with 'no additional execution privileges needed' and 'User interaction is not needed for exploitation'. attack_vector: the malicious app's background sensor/data access runs 'without the persistent status-bar indicator that would alert the user'. CISA KEV-listed 2024-03-05, active_exploitation confirmed, poc_available false. The entry cites NIST-800-53-SI-4 (System Monitoring) among the framework controls that were insufficient.

CVE-2021-36380.name: Sunhillo SureLine OS Command Injection Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: An unauthenticated attacker submits shell metacharacters in the ipAddr/dnsAddr fields of /cgi/networkDiag.cgi; SureLine passes them into a system command run as root, yielding arbitrary command execution and an interactive shell.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none (unauthenticated, network-reachable web CGI)
attack_vector.complexity: low — single crafted HTTP request, publicly documented
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered — discovered by NCC Group. No AI involvement documented.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Upgrade to 8.7.0.1.1 and remove the appliance's management interface from internet exposure
prevention.adequacy: Patching fixes input handling, but exposed appliances should be assumed compromised given years of public exploitability and root-level impact.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Monitor for requests to /cgi/networkDiag.cgi containing shell metacharacters and for the CGI process spawning shells or outbound connections
detection.adequacy: Embedded appliances rarely emit logs to a SIEM, limiting detection.

response.what_would_have_worked: Rebuild/reflash the appliance, rotate any credentials it stored, and segment it off the internet
response.adequacy: Root-level command execution means only a full rebuild reliably evicts an attacker.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: The flaw was patched in 2021 yet remains actively exploited in 2024, showing that long-lived niche OT/network appliances routinely fall outside routine flaw-remediation cadences.

NIST-800-53-SC-7.gap: Boundary-protection guidance does not force these surveillance/telemetry appliances off the public internet, which is the only thing that stops unauthenticated reach to the vulnerable CGI.

NIS2-Art21-network-security.gap: Network-security obligations rarely enumerate embedded/OT appliances like SureLine, so the exposed management CGI goes unsegmented and unmonitored.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: System-security expectations assume input validation on management interfaces; an unauthenticated root command-injection means the assumed control simply is not present on the device.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Essential-Eight patching is scoped to mainstream OS/applications and does not compel firmware updates for niche network appliances, leaving a 3-year-old fix unapplied.

CVE-2024-21338.name: Microsoft Windows Kernel Exposed IOCTL with Insufficient Access Control Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: A local process opens the appid.sys device and sends a crafted IOCTL whose weak access control allows an untrusted-pointer dereference, yielding kernel read/write; Lazarus used this to install the FudModule rootkit and disable EDR.
attack_vector.privileges_required: low (local; the exploit elevates an admin/medium-integrity process to kernel)
attack_vector.complexity: low — reliable public exploit once weaponized
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered — reported by Avast (Jan Vojtesek). No AI involvement documented.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Apply the February 2024 update; enable HVCI/memory-integrity and Microsoft's vulnerable-driver blocklist
prevention.adequacy: The patch fixes the IOCTL, but until applied the exploit blinds EDR, so a patched host may still bear an installed rootkit — kernel-integrity controls are the durable mitigation.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alert on non-System handles to appid.sys and IOCTL 0x0022A018; hunt for FudModule/EDR-tampering artifacts
detection.adequacy: Because the goal is to disable EDR, detection must run before the rootkit loads.

response.what_would_have_worked: Isolate and re-image affected hosts, restore EDR integrity, and hunt laterally given Lazarus tradecraft
response.adequacy: A kernel rootkit warrants full rebuild rather than in-place cleaning.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: Monthly patch cadence (Patch Tuesday) leaves a multi-day window during which a public admin-to-kernel exploit disables endpoint defenses; SLA-based remediation is slower than the observed weaponization.

NIST-800-53-AC-6.gap: Least-privilege alone does not stop this: the exploit takes an already-admin process to kernel, so restricting standard users is insufficient — kernel-integrity controls (HVCI) are needed.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: Patch-management requirements do not compel the driver-blocklist/HVCI hardening that would blunt a vulnerable-driver-style kernel escalation between patch cycles.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: System-security expectations assume EDR remains authoritative, but this flaw is used specifically to blind EDR via a kernel rootkit, defeating the control's monitoring assumption.

AU-Essential-8-App-Hardening.gap: Application-hardening/driver-control guidance does not enumerate appid.sys, so the exposed-IOCTL path is not blocked by standard hardening baselines.

new_control_requirements.name: VULNERABLE-DRIVER-BLOCKLIST-ENFORCEMENT
new_control_requirements.description: Enforce a kernel vulnerable/malicious-driver blocklist (HVCI plus the vendor recommended-driver blocklist) so a signed-but-vulnerable driver cannot be loaded for bring-your-own-vulnerable-driver privilege escalation.
new_control_requirements.evidence: https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2024-21338

CVE-2023-29360.name: Microsoft Streaming Service Untrusted Pointer Dereference Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: A local process drives the mskssrv.sys streaming driver to dereference an attacker-controlled pointer, converting a user-mode foothold into a kernel write primitive and SYSTEM privileges.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none-to-low (local user; no admin required)
attack_vector.complexity: low — reliable public exploit code exists
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered — coordinated disclosure to Microsoft. No AI involvement documented.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Apply the June 2023 update; restrict/disable the Microsoft Streaming Service where unused
prevention.adequacy: The patch fixes the dereference, but as a post-compromise LPE it only matters after initial access — defense-in-depth against initial footholds remains necessary.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alert on standard users opening mskssrv/KS device handles and on SYSTEM processes spawned from medium-integrity parents
detection.adequacy: Driver-level LPE telemetry is uncommon, so detection depends on generic escalation heuristics.

response.what_would_have_worked: Isolate the host, determine the initial-access vector, and re-image if SYSTEM was obtained
response.adequacy: SYSTEM-level compromise justifies rebuild and credential rotation.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: Monthly patch cadence leaves the window a public LPE needs; SLA-based remediation is slower than the exploit's post-compromise use to reach SYSTEM.

NIST-800-53-AC-6.gap: Least-privilege limits initial access but does not prevent a low-priv process from abusing an exposed kernel driver to reach SYSTEM; driver-attack-surface reduction is required.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: Patch-management obligations do not mandate reducing exposure of optional media/streaming kernel components that provide this escalation path.

UK-CAF-C1.gap: Security-monitoring expectations rarely include driver-level LPE telemetry, so the escalation to SYSTEM proceeds without an alerting baseline.

AU-Essential-8-App-Hardening.gap: Application-hardening baselines do not disable or restrict the Microsoft Streaming Service driver, leaving the vulnerable IOCTL/KS path reachable by any local user.

new_control_requirements.name: ACTIVELY-EXPLOITED-OS-LPE-REMEDIATION-WINDOW-ENFORCEMENT
new_control_requirements.description: The packet's path for this flaw starts from an ordinary local process and ends at SYSTEM: a user-mode caller drives the mskssrv.sys streaming driver into dereferencing an attacker-controlled pointer, which yields a kernel write primitive. That makes the account-privilege posture most estates are audited on — standard users, no local administrators, least privilege attested — a boundary this flaw does not have to cross, so it cannot be the containment story while the fix is outstanding. The second half matters more for scheduling: the packet states there is no vendor live-patch mechanism and that remediation requires applying the fixed release and rebooting, which means exposure does not end when the update is pushed, it ends when each host restarts. A fleet reporting successful deployment while machines sit unrestarted is still exploitable on every one of them. Run the clock from the KEV listing date to completed reboot per host rather than to deployment-tool success, enumerate the fleet's actual installed builds against the fixed build for each SKU, and treat any host that has taken the update but not the restart as unremediated in the compliance record rather than as compliant-pending-reboot.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Packet: attack_vector "A local process drives the mskssrv.sys streaming driver to dereference an attacker-controlled pointer, converting a user-mode foothold into a kernel write primitive and SYSTEM privileges."; vector "Microsoft Streaming Service Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability"; CWE-822. patch_available true; live_patch_available false; live_patch_notes "No vendor live-patch mechanism; remediation requires applying the fixed release and rebooting." CISA KEV 2024-02-29, active_exploitation confirmed, CVSS 8.4, RWEP 77, poc_available true.

new_control_requirements.name: KERNEL-EXPLOITATION-DETECTION
new_control_requirements.description: Because the packet ties remediation to a reboot of every affected endpoint and records confirmed in-the-wild exploitation with a PoC available, this estate has a detection-only window whose length is set by its restart schedule rather than by how fast the update is pushed — and monitoring is the citing gap the packet names. On a Windows fleet the telemetry source is the EDR/ETW equivalent of the auditd or eBPF rules this control is usually expressed in: alert on a local, unprivileged process obtaining a handle to the Microsoft Streaming Service device, and on a subsequent token or integrity-level change to SYSTEM within the same process lineage. That pairing is what the packet's path actually produces — the user-mode foothold reaching the driver, then the kernel write cashing out as SYSTEM — and detecting only the second half means detecting the escalation after it has already succeeded, at whatever point the follow-on payload becomes noisy enough for signature-based tooling to notice. The rule has to be live for the whole reboot window and its coverage checked against the same host list used for the build enumeration, so unrestarted hosts are the ones being watched most closely rather than the ones nobody has instrumented.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Packet: attack_vector "A local process drives the mskssrv.sys streaming driver to dereference an attacker-controlled pointer, converting a user-mode foothold into a kernel write primitive and SYSTEM privileges."; live_patch_notes "No vendor live-patch mechanism; remediation requires applying the fixed release and rebooting."; live_patch_available false. CISA KEV 2024-02-29 with active_exploitation confirmed and poc_available true; RWEP 77, CVSS 8.4. Citing gap in the packet: UK-CAF-C1 "Security monitoring" (UK NCSC Cyber Assessment Framework v3.2).

CVE-2020-3259.name: Cisco ASA and FTD Information Disclosure Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: An unauthenticated attacker sends a crafted GET request with an invalid URL to the ASA/FTD web services interface; a buffer-tracking flaw returns device memory contents, which can include cleartext VPN credentials later used for ransomware entry.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none (unauthenticated, internet-facing web services interface)
attack_vector.complexity: low — a single crafted HTTP request, though only specific AnyConnect/WebVPN configs are vulnerable
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered — reported via Cisco PSIRT. No AI involvement documented.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Apply the fixed ASA/FTD release and rotate all VPN credentials that could have been resident in memory; enforce MFA on VPN
prevention.adequacy: Patching stops the leak, but any credentials exposed before patching remain usable unless rotated and protected by MFA — patch alone does not undo the disclosure.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Monitor for malformed GET requests to the WebVPN endpoint and correlate with new VPN logins from unusual sources
detection.adequacy: Memory-disclosure requests can look benign, so detection relies on downstream anomalous-login correlation.

response.what_would_have_worked: Force VPN credential rotation, enable MFA, and hunt for Akira precursors given the ransomware association
response.adequacy: Because leaked credentials seed later intrusion, response must assume credential compromise.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: The fix shipped in 2020 yet the flaw was still enabling ransomware entry in 2024, showing edge-VPN appliances routinely miss flaw-remediation cadences long after patches exist.

NIST-800-53-SC-7.gap: Boundary-protection controls treat the ASA/FTD as the boundary itself; they do not address the appliance leaking its own memory (and stored credentials) to unauthenticated requests.

NIS2-Art21-vulnerability-management.gap: Vulnerability-management obligations do not force credential rotation after a memory-disclosure exposure, so leaked VPN credentials remain valid and enable later ransomware access.

UK-CAF-B2.gap: Identity/access controls assume VPN credentials stay secret; a memory-disclosure that exposes them undermines the control unless MFA and post-exposure rotation are enforced.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Essential-Eight patching targets do not specifically drive perimeter-appliance firmware updates, leaving a years-old ASA/FTD fix unapplied on exposed devices.

new_control_requirements.name: PERIMETER-DEVICE-ZERODAY-SLA-TIER
new_control_requirements.description: The affected asset is a Cisco ASA / FTD unit terminating AnyConnect and WebVPN — a VPN concentrator sitting on the trust boundary — and the packet's primitive is reached with no credential: a crafted GET request carrying an invalid URL to the web services interface returns device memory contents through a buffer-tracking flaw. The isolation alternative this tier normally offers is largely unavailable here, and that is the precondition to state rather than skip: the web services interface carrying AnyConnect and WebVPN is reachable by remote users by design, so "restrict the vulnerable interface" means withdrawing remote access, not hardening it, and it is an option only for units whose remote-access population is small enough to source-restrict. What is left is the clock. The packet records a vendor fix and states there is no vendor live-patch mechanism — remediation requires applying the fixed release and rebooting — so the tier's requirement is that the fixed release and the reload are driven from the 2024-02-15 KEV listing rather than folded into the next maintenance window, and a unit that has taken the image but not reloaded is still running the vulnerable parser and counts as exposed, not as remediated. The packet also scopes the population for the operator: only specific AnyConnect and WebVPN configurations are affected, so the enumeration step is which units run those configurations — an asset inventory that lists ASA/FTD units without that configuration detail cannot say which are in scope. Distinguishing test: for each unit in the affected configuration set, compare the running image against the fixed release and confirm the reload has occurred; an "update deployed" entry in the management console is not evidence that the running device stopped serving the vulnerable web services parser.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Packet: a vulnerability in the web services interface of Cisco ASA and FTD Software allows an unauthenticated, remote attacker to retrieve memory contents; the flaw is a buffer-tracking issue when the software parses invalid URLs requested from the web services interface, exploited by sending a crafted GET request. The packet states the vulnerability affects only specific AnyConnect and WebVPN configurations. CWE-200; CISA KEV-listed 2024-02-15; active_exploitation confirmed; CVSS 7.5; RWEP 60; poc_available false. patch_available true; live_patch_available false; live_patch_notes: "No vendor live-patch mechanism; remediation requires applying the fixed release and rebooting."

new_control_requirements.name: PERIMETER-COMPROMISE-REBUILD-NOT-PATCH
new_control_requirements.description: The packet's outcome is a read primitive, not code execution: an unauthenticated crafted GET request returns ASA/FTD memory contents, which the packet says can include cleartext VPN credentials later used for ransomware entry. That makes one half of this control load-bearing here and the other inapplicable, and saying which is which matters. The packet documents no implant and no write to the device, so a rebuild is not what this CVE demands; credential rotation is — and it is exactly the step the fixed release does not perform. Applied to these units: every credential that could have been resident in the memory of an affected AnyConnect/WebVPN unit during the exposure window is treated as disclosed and rotated — remote-access VPN user credentials, the upstream directory or RADIUS accounts those users authenticate against, administrator credentials used on the device, and any shared secret the device holds — and the remote-access session and account history is reviewed for logins that used credentials valid before the rotation. Precondition: rotation reaches only credentials the operator can enumerate and change. A credential held by a third party, or embedded in a partner or appliance configuration outside the operator's control, keeps working after the fixed release lands, and that residual belongs in the record rather than assumed closed. The distinguishing test is not on the device: after the fixed release and reload, confirm that remote-access authentication for the affected units rejects the pre-remediation credential set — an identity-and-access attestation showing every VPN user authenticating correctly passes cleanly while an attacker holds a credential that also authenticates correctly.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Packet: "An unauthenticated attacker sends a crafted GET request with an invalid URL to the ASA/FTD web services interface; a buffer-tracking flaw returns device memory contents, which can include cleartext VPN credentials later used for ransomware entry." active_exploitation confirmed; CISA KEV-listed 2024-02-15. patch_available true; live_patch_available false; live_patch_notes: "No vendor live-patch mechanism; remediation requires applying the fixed release and rebooting." The packet describes retrieval of memory contents only — no code execution, implant, or device write.

CVE-2024-21410.name: Microsoft Exchange Server Privilege Escalation Vulnerability (CVE-2024-21410)

attack_vector.description: An attacker coerces a privileged account to authenticate (e.g. PetitPotam), then relays the NTLM credential to the Exchange EWS endpoint; without Extended Protection the relay succeeds and the attacker gains the victim's Exchange privileges.
attack_vector.privileges_required: low (network position to coerce/relay authentication; no valid Exchange credentials needed)
attack_vector.complexity: low — built from public relay/coercion tooling
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered — addressed by Microsoft via Extended Protection by default. No AI involvement documented.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Install the Feb 2024 Exchange update AND enable Extended Protection; disable NTLM where possible and require MFA
prevention.adequacy: The patch enables Extended Protection but administrators must confirm it is actually on for every vdir — a server that was patched without EP verification remains exploitable.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Detect NTLM relays to EWS and authentication-coercion RPC (MS-EFSR/MS-RPRN) preceding Exchange access
detection.adequacy: Relay traffic can blend with legitimate NTLM; detection needs source/behavior correlation.

response.what_would_have_worked: Verify Extended Protection everywhere, rotate exposed credentials, and hunt for unauthorized Exchange/AD changes
response.adequacy: Because the escalation grants a victim identity, response must audit actions taken under relayed accounts.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: Applying the Exchange update is not enough on its own — Extended Protection must be actively enabled — so a standard patch-and-reboot SLA leaves the relay path open even on 'patched' servers.

NIST-800-53-IA-2.gap: Identity/authentication controls that permit NTLM allow credential relay; without channel-binding/Extended Protection and MFA, the authentication assurance the control assumes does not hold.

NIS2-Art21-network-security.gap: Network-security obligations do not by default require disabling/segmenting NTLM or blocking authentication-coercion RPC, which is what stops the relay chain.

UK-CAF-B2.gap: Identity-and-access-control expectations assume authentication cannot be replayed; NTLM relay defeats that, so the control fails absent Extended Protection.

ISO-27001-2022-A.5.16-Federated.gap: Identity-management control does not, by itself, mandate channel binding / EPA for legacy NTLM, leaving relayed authentication to Exchange viable.

new_control_requirements.name: CONFIGURATION-SIDE-LIVE-PATCH-INVENTORY
new_control_requirements.description: For Microsoft Exchange Server the configuration-side path this control names is Extended Protection, and the packet makes it the load-bearing half rather than an optional extra: the affected condition is stated as Exchange Server where Extended Protection is not enforced, and the flaw-remediation gap records that applying the Exchange update is not enough on its own because Extended Protection must be actively enabled. Bound to this deployment that means every Exchange Server 2016 and 2019 host is inventoried by whether Extended Protection is enforced on the web endpoints that terminate authentication — Exchange Web Services first, because EWS is the endpoint the packet names as the relay target — and that this state is tracked, tested and driven as its own item rather than riding along with the CU14 upgrade project, since the packet describes CU14 as enabling Extended Protection by default rather than as the only route to it. Extended Protection is also exactly what the identity controls cited on this entry are missing: the packet's federated identity-management gap says the control does not by itself mandate channel binding for legacy NTLM, and channel binding at the EWS endpoint is what makes a relayed NetNTLM authentication fail instead of succeeding as the victim. Read the control's name carefully against this packet: live_patch_available is false, so enabling Extended Protection is a configuration change, not a vendor live-patch primitive, and it does not substitute for the remediation the packet records — applying the fixed release and rebooting. That is the precondition on treating this as closure: patch_required_reboot is true, so a server that took the February 2024 update but has not restarted is still running the vulnerable code. A second precondition is that Extended Protection bounds the relay into Exchange and does nothing about the step the attack begins with; the packet's network-security gap names disabling or segmenting NTLM and blocking authentication-coercion RPC as separate measures this control does not supply. And because active exploitation against internet-facing Exchange is confirmed, a server that was reachable while Extended Protection was off belongs on the incident path rather than being closed on the configuration change.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Packet affected: 'Microsoft Exchange Server; when Extended Protection is not enforced, an attacker can relay a coerced NTLM authentication to Exchange Web Services and act as the victim (privilege escalation). Fixed by CU14 enabling Extended Protection by default.' affected_versions: 'Exchange Server 2016 and 2019 without Extended Protection (prior to Feb 2024 update / CU14)'. NIST-800-53-SI-2 gap: 'Applying the Exchange update is not enough on its own — Extended Protection must be actively enabled — so a standard patch-and-reboot SLA leaves the relay path open even on "patched" servers.' ISO-27001-2022-A.5.16-Federated gap: 'Identity-management control does not, by itself, mandate channel binding / EPA for legacy NTLM, leaving relayed authentication to Exchange viable.' NIS2-Art21-network-security gap names disabling/segmenting NTLM and blocking authentication-coercion RPC as what stops the relay chain. attack_vector: an attacker coerces a privileged account to authenticate (e.g. PetitPotam) then relays the NTLM credential to the Exchange EWS endpoint. Remediation state: patch_available true, patch_required_reboot true, live_patch_available false, live_patch_notes 'No vendor live-patch mechanism; remediation requires applying the fixed release and rebooting.' CWE-287, CISA KEV listed 2024-02-15, active_exploitation confirmed, poc_available true, CVSS 9.8, RWEP 80.

new_control_requirements.name: SCANNER-PAPER-COMPLIANCE-TEST
new_control_requirements.description: The paper-compliance shape this control exists to catch is precisely the failure the packet records for this CVE. A scanner that reads the Exchange build, sees the February 2024 update present and reports the server remediated has measured the one thing that does not settle the question: the condition the packet ties exploitation to is Extended Protection not being enforced, and that is a configuration state the build number does not carry. The operational test for this product is therefore per-server and per-endpoint — for every Exchange Server 2016 and 2019 host, produce the enforced/not-enforced state of Extended Protection on the web endpoints that accept authenticated traffic, Exchange Web Services first because the packet names EWS as the relay target, and treat a host that cannot produce that state as unverified rather than as compliant. The distinguishing test keys on the behaviour the packet documents rather than on a version string or a tool signature: on a staging Exchange server, coerce an account to authenticate and relay that NetNTLM authentication to the EWS endpoint — the exact sequence in the packet's attack vector, using the publicly available coercion and relay tooling its application-hardening gap names — and confirm the relayed authentication is refused rather than accepted as the victim. An estate whose patch report is green and whose user-application-hardening attestation covers Exchange passes both checks while that relay still succeeds, which is what makes the version-only scan and the hardening attestation paper compliance here. The same inventory must carry restart state alongside configuration state: the packet gives patch_required_reboot true with no live-patch path and states remediation requires applying the fixed release and rebooting, so a host that has installed the update and not restarted onto it is not remediated no matter what either check reports.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Packet NIST-800-53-SI-2 gap: 'Applying the Exchange update is not enough on its own — Extended Protection must be actively enabled — so a standard patch-and-reboot SLA leaves the relay path open even on "patched" servers.' AU-Essential-8-App-Hardening gap: 'Application-hardening maturity does not enumerate Exchange Extended Protection or NTLM channel-binding, so a "hardened" server still relays a coerced NetNTLM authentication to EWS via public impacket/PetitPotam tooling; patching without enabling EPA leaves the relay path open.' affected_versions: 'Exchange Server 2016 and 2019 without Extended Protection (prior to Feb 2024 update / CU14)'. attack_vector: coerce a privileged account to authenticate (e.g. PetitPotam), relay the NTLM credential to the Exchange EWS endpoint; without Extended Protection the relay succeeds. patch_available true, patch_required_reboot true, live_patch_available false, live_patch_notes 'No vendor live-patch mechanism; remediation requires applying the fixed release and rebooting.' CISA KEV 2024-02-15, active_exploitation confirmed, poc_available true, CVSS 9.8, RWEP 80.

CVE-2024-21412.name: Microsoft Windows Internet Shortcut Files Security Feature Bypass Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: A victim opens a crafted .url internet shortcut that redirects to a second .url on a WebDAV/SMB share; the indirection strips Mark-of-the-Web, so SmartScreen does not warn and the referenced payload executes.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none (attacker-side); requires user interaction to open the shortcut
attack_vector.complexity: low — public exploit/Metasploit module, but depends on luring the user to open the file
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered — reported by Trend Micro ZDI (Water Hydra tracking). No AI involvement documented.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Apply the February 2024 SmartScreen update; block/limit outbound WebDAV and treat .url attachments as high-risk at the mail gateway
prevention.adequacy: The patch restores the MOTW check, but because delivery relies on user interaction, mail/web filtering and user awareness remain necessary layers.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alert on .url files referencing remote .url/network paths and on WebDAV (davclnt) fetches spawning executables
detection.adequacy: The bypass suppresses the usual SmartScreen signal, so detection must rely on the shortcut-chain and network-fetch behavior.

response.what_would_have_worked: Isolate hosts that opened the lure, hunt for DarkGate loaders, and reset credentials that could have been harvested
response.adequacy: Because the bypass delivers a loader, response must chase the follow-on payload rather than just the shortcut.

NIST-800-53-SI-3.gap: Malicious-code protection leans on SmartScreen/Mark-of-the-Web reputation, which this flaw bypasses outright, so signature/reputation defenses do not fire on the delivered payload.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: Monthly patch cadence lags the same-week weaponization by Water Hydra/DarkGate; SLA-based patching leaves the SmartScreen bypass open during active campaigns.

NIS2-Art21-incident-handling.gap: Incident-handling requirements assume defensive prompts surface risky files; a MOTW/SmartScreen bypass removes that signal, so the assumed detection point is absent.

UK-CAF-C1.gap: Security-monitoring expectations do not specifically cover WebDAV-fetched shortcut chains, so the bypass's network-share fetch is not routinely alerted.

AU-Essential-8-App-Hardening.gap: Application-hardening measures (block/limit WebDAV, disable script hosts, restrict .url handling) are not mandated, leaving the shortcut-chain delivery path open.

new_control_requirements.name: DOWNLOAD-PROVENANCE-ENFORCEMENT
new_control_requirements.description: Enforce Mark-of-the-Web / content-provenance on all internet-sourced files and block execution of provenance-stripped shortcuts, installers, and script hosts regardless of a reputation service verdict, which attackers bypass by design.
new_control_requirements.evidence: https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2024-21412

CVE-2024-21351.name: Microsoft Windows SmartScreen Security Feature Bypass Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: A user is lured to open a crafted internet-shortcut file; the shortcut chains to a second remote shortcut that never receives the Mark-of-the-Web tag, so SmartScreen skips its reputation warning and the payload runs.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none (attacker-supplied file; requires the victim to open it — UI:R)
attack_vector.complexity: low — the crafted-shortcut chain reliably suppresses the MotW/SmartScreen prompt
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered — reported by security researchers to Microsoft. No AI involvement documented.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Apply the February 2024 Windows cumulative update; block .url/.lnk and WebDAV/SMB egress at the mail/web gateway; strip incoming shortcut attachments.
prevention.adequacy: Patch closes the specific bypass, but shortcut-chain delivery and WebDAV abuse remain a class of technique that reputation controls alone will not stop.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alert on downloaded files lacking a Zone.Identifier stream and on .url/.lnk files resolving to remote WebDAV/SMB shares.
detection.adequacy: Effective post-delivery but presumes EDR visibility into MotW state and shortcut internals.

response.what_would_have_worked: Isolate hosts that executed shortcut-delivered payloads, hunt for follow-on loaders, rotate exposed credentials.
response.adequacy: Response is reactive; the bypass had already delivered code by the time host telemetry fired.

NIST-800-53-SI-3.gap: SmartScreen IS the malicious-code-protection control being bypassed; SI-3's reputation/reputation-check expectation gives false assurance when Mark-of-the-Web is not applied to the delivered file.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: Monthly patch cadence leaves a bypass window: this was a live zero-day when KEV-listed, so remediation had to outrun active exploitation, not the normal SI-2 SLA.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: A calendar-based patch program does not address a client-side defense-evasion bug already weaponized in phishing lures before the fix ships.

AU-Essential-8-App-Hardening.gap: Application-hardening guidance assumes SmartScreen/MotW warnings fire; this flaw silences them, so the hardening baseline over-credits the reputation prompt.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.7.gap: Anti-malware control effectiveness is undermined when the OS reputation gate can be skipped, so A.8.7 coverage is present-but-inadequate for MotW-bypass delivery.

CVE-2023-43770.name: Roundcube Webmail Persistent Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: The attacker emails a plain-text message containing a crafted link; Roundcube's link-replacer converts it into HTML with attacker-controlled attributes/script, so JavaScript runs in the victim's authenticated webmail session when the message is viewed.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none (unauthenticated — attacker only needs to send an email; victim must open it)
attack_vector.complexity: low — a single crafted email triggers the stored XSS on view
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered — fixed by the Roundcube project, exploitation reported by ESET. No AI involvement documented.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Upgrade to Roundcube 1.6.3 / 1.5.4 / 1.4.14; enforce a strict Content-Security-Policy on the webmail origin; sanitize/encode link rendering.
prevention.adequacy: Patch removes the specific sink, but webmail remains a high-value XSS target absent a defense-in-depth CSP.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Monitor for outbound requests from the webmail origin to unknown collectors and for messages whose plain-text links contain markup.
detection.adequacy: Detects exfiltration after script execution rather than preventing it.

response.what_would_have_worked: Invalidate webmail sessions, rotate credentials of targeted accounts, review sent-mail and forwarding rules for tampering.
response.adequacy: Reactive; credential theft may already have occurred by the time sessions are invalidated.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: The fix shipped in September 2023 but the flaw was already an operational zero-day against targeted governments; a routine SI-2 timeline is slower than the observed espionage exploitation.

PCI-DSS-4.0-6.2.4.gap: Injection-flaw handling in 6.2.4 targets first-party code review; it does not force timely upgrade of a third-party webmail component whose parser is the injection sink.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: Technical-vulnerability management is present but under-weights an internet-facing webmail XSS as a targeted-intrusion vector rather than a low-severity nuisance.

NIS2-Art21-vulnerability-management.gap: Vulnerability-management obligations do not by themselves prioritize a CVSS-medium XSS that is, in practice, a nation-state credential-theft primitive.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: System-security expectations assume webmail rendering is trustworthy; they do not mandate a content-security-policy / output-encoding control that would neutralize the stored-XSS payload.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: The CVSS 6.1 on this entry is precisely what makes it go wrong in practice. Read as a medium-severity webmail XSS it sorts into a routine queue, while the packet records it as a zero-day used by the Winter Vivern (TA473) espionage group against European governmental webmail from at least October 2023 to steal mail and credentials, with a public proof of concept available. For Roundcube the requirement is that the KEV listing rather than the severity band sets the clock, and that the clock runs against the Roundcube install itself — a self-hosted third-party webmail server that typically sits outside the operating-system patch pipeline that Essential Eight maturity and most flaw-remediation programmes actually measure, which is why an organisation can be fully compliant on OS patching while the vulnerable rcube_string_replacer.php parser keeps rendering crafted links. The fixed levels are the ones the packet's own vector gives: 1.4.14, 1.5.4 on the 1.5.x line, and 1.6.3 on the 1.6.x line; anything below those on any line is in scope regardless of how current the host operating system is. Precondition on remediation and measurement: live_patch_available is false and the packet records no vendor live-patch mechanism, so the vendor fixed release is the only remediation available — there is no configuration setting or filter in the packet to reach for in the interim. patch_required_reboot is false, which means no host reboot to schedule and not that the fix is live on deployment; count an instance remediated on the version the running Roundcube reports, not on the package version staged on disk. And because exploitation against this exact parser path is confirmed, an instance that was serving mail below the fixed version during the exposure window is an incident item as well as a patch item — the upgrade removes the sink but returns nothing about what was already read out of the mailboxes.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Packet vector: 'Roundcube before 1.4.14, 1.5.x before 1.5.4, and 1.6.x before 1.6.3 allows XSS via text/plain e-mail messages with crafted links because of program/lib/Roundcube/rcube_string_replacer.php behavior.' active_exploitation_notes: 'Exploited as a zero-day by the Winter Vivern (TA473) espionage group against European governmental webmail from at least October 2023; a crafted plain-text email link executed script in the victim's Roundcube session to steal mail and credentials.' NIST-800-53-SI-2 gap: 'The fix shipped in September 2023 but the flaw was already an operational zero-day against targeted governments; a routine SI-2 timeline is slower than the observed espionage exploitation.' AU-Essential-8-Patch gap: 'Essential-Eight patch maturity is oriented to OS and Office endpoints, not to timely upgrade of a third-party webmail server whose rcube_string_replacer.php parser is the stored-XSS sink.' PCI-DSS-4.0-6.2.4 gap: 'Injection-flaw handling in 6.2.4 targets first-party code review; it does not force timely upgrade of a third-party webmail component whose parser is the injection sink.' CISA KEV 2024-02-12; active_exploitation confirmed; poc_available true; CVSS 6.1; RWEP 67; patch_available true, patch_required_reboot false, live_patch_available false, live_patch_notes 'No vendor live-patch mechanism; remediation requires applying the vendor fixed release.'

new_control_requirements.name: NATION-STATE-INITIAL-ACCESS-IR-ESCALATION
new_control_requirements.description: The packet attributes exploitation of this Roundcube flaw to the Winter Vivern (TA473) espionage group operating against European governmental webmail, which is exactly the attribution trigger this control exists to act on and exactly the case where commodity handling gets it wrong: a CVSS 6.1 cross-site scripting finding routed through standard malware-infection response is treated as a browser-session nuisance, when the packet describes it as a nation-state credential-theft primitive. For this CVE the trigger condition is concrete — a Roundcube instance below 1.4.14, 1.5.4 or 1.6.3 together with any evidence of the crafted plain-text link arriving or being rendered — and the escalated response has to be scoped to what the packet says the actor actually took: mail and credentials out of the victim's authenticated webmail session. That makes mailbox-content exposure assessment and credential rotation for every account whose session rendered a message during the window the substance of the response, rather than the endpoint reimaging a commodity playbook would reach for; the payload runs in the webmail session, so the user's workstation is not where the compromise lives. Preconditions: attribution of this kind arrives after the fact, so the escalation only changes an outcome if the mail-server and webmail telemetry it needs was already being retained across a window the packet dates to at least October 2023, months before the 2024-02-12 KEV listing. And escalation is a response posture — it does not remove the parser defect, which only the vendor fixed release does, and it does not invalidate credentials that were taken; those stay usable until they are rotated.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Packet active_exploitation_notes: 'Exploited as a zero-day by the Winter Vivern (TA473) espionage group against European governmental webmail from at least October 2023; a crafted plain-text email link executed script in the victim's Roundcube session to steal mail and credentials. KEV ransomware use unconfirmed.' NIS2-Art21-vulnerability-management gap: 'Vulnerability-management obligations do not by themselves prioritize a CVSS-medium XSS that is, in practice, a nation-state credential-theft primitive.' ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8 gap: 'Technical-vulnerability management is present but under-weights an internet-facing webmail XSS as a targeted-intrusion vector rather than a low-severity nuisance.' Fixed levels per vector: 1.4.14, 1.5.x before 1.5.4, 1.6.x before 1.6.3. CVSS 6.1; RWEP 67; CISA KEV 2024-02-12; active_exploitation confirmed; patch_available true, live_patch_available false.

new_control_requirements.name: OWA-PER-REQUEST-SIEM-INGESTION
new_control_requirements.description: Applied to Roundcube, this control addresses why the Winter Vivern activity the packet describes leaves no authentication-layer trace. The script executes inside the victim's already-authenticated webmail session at the moment the crafted plain-text message is viewed, so there is no failed login, no new session establishment and no client-side artifact to match — an authentication-event log is complete and silent while the mailbox is being read. Detection therefore has to key on the behaviour the packet actually documents: a message view followed, within the same authenticated session, by message-fetch and search activity whose volume and ordering no human reading pattern produces, and by outbound requests carrying session or credential material to a destination outside the deployment. The requirement is that Roundcube per-request access logs — message view, search, message fetch, and requests the application issues on the session's behalf — are forwarded to a SIEM off the webmail host and retained long enough to answer a question that arrives late, which for this CVE means spanning from at least October 2023, when the packet dates exploitation, to the 2024-02-12 KEV listing and beyond. Preconditions, and the second one is the limit that must not be glossed. This is detection, not neutralization: it does not stop the payload, and it supplies only the monitoring half of the system-security expectation — the CAF B4 gap on this entry names a content-security-policy or output-encoding control as what would neutralize the stored payload, and this control does not provide that; the vendor upgrade to 1.4.14, 1.5.4 or 1.6.3 is what removes the sink in rcube_string_replacer.php. And a rule written after the attribution lands, against per-request logs nobody was shipping off the host, returns nothing at all.

UK-CAF-B4 gap: 'System-security expectations assume webmail rendering is trustworthy; they do not mandate a content-security-policy / output-encoding control that would neutralize the stored-XSS payload.' Fixed levels per vector: 1.4.14, 1.5.4, 1.6.3. CISA KEV 2024-02-12; active_exploitation confirmed; patch_available true, live_patch_available false, live_patch_notes 'No vendor live-patch mechanism; remediation requires applying the vendor fixed release.'

CVE-2023-4762.name: Google Chromium V8 Type Confusion Vulnerability (CVE-2023-4762)

attack_vector.description: A victim visits an attacker-controlled web page; malicious JavaScript drives a V8 type confusion that lets the attacker treat a memory object as the wrong type, yielding code execution inside the renderer as a stage toward full compromise.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none (unauthenticated; requires the victim to load a crafted page — UI:R)
attack_vector.complexity: low — a single crafted HTML page triggers the type confusion, though a reliable full chain needs a sandbox escape
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered — reported through Google's vulnerability process. No AI involvement documented.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Update Chrome/Chromium to 116.0.5845.179 or later and force-relaunch; enforce automatic browser updates fleet-wide.
prevention.adequacy: Patch is decisive, but only if relaunch is enforced; a running unpatched browser stays vulnerable until restart.

detection.what_would_have_worked: EDR alerting on renderer crashes and on child processes spawned by the browser after browsing untrusted sites.
detection.adequacy: Renderer exploitation is largely in-process and low-signal until a sandbox escape spawns activity.

response.what_would_have_worked: Isolate affected hosts, force browser update + relaunch, hunt for post-exploitation implants.
response.adequacy: Reactive; targeted-surveillance payloads may already have staged persistence.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: Browser flaw-remediation must be same-day for a live zero-day; a standard SI-2 cadence leaves users exploitable during the window commercial-surveillance actors were already using.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Essential-8 patch timelines (48 hours for internet-facing / extreme-risk) can still trail a browser zero-day already weaponized before the CVE is public.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: Endpoint-browser patch management is rarely enforced as tightly as server patching, yet this bug's exploitation vector is everyday web browsing.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: Technical-vulnerability management under-prioritizes client browsers relative to servers, leaving the actual exploited surface under-governed.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: System-security assurance assumes the browser sandbox holds; a renderer type-confusion with sandbox escape defeats that assumption without additional exploit-mitigation controls.

new_control_requirements.name: BROWSER-MANAGED-UPDATE-NO-DEFERRAL
new_control_requirements.description: The packet's exploitation path is a victim loading an attacker-controlled page, so every hour a managed endpoint keeps browsing on a Chrome build below 116.0.5845.179 is an hour that path stays open, and the packet records no live-patch mechanism — applying the vendor fixed release is the only thing that closes it. Bound to this deployment, the control means the browser's security channel is exempt from the pilot/broad ring staging that enterprise update policy applies to feature updates, and that completion is measured by the version the browser itself reports on each endpoint rather than by an 'approved' or 'downloaded' state in the management console. Distinguishing test: enumerate the Chrome version actually running across managed endpoints and confirm none report below 116.0.5845.179 — a ring policy that reports the update as deployed while endpoints still report a pre-fix build leaves the vulnerable V8 in the renderer that parses attacker-supplied HTML, with a clean patch-compliance row. Precondition: the ring reaches only Chrome installs the management channel can see and update. A user-installed copy outside that channel takes no ring policy at all, so it is remediated by bringing it under management or removing it, not by recording the fleet as patched.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Packet vector: 'Type Confusion in V8 in Google Chrome prior to 116.0.5845.179 allowed a remote attacker to execute arbitrary code via a crafted HTML page.' attack_vector: a victim visits an attacker-controlled web page and malicious JavaScript drives the V8 type confusion, yielding code execution inside the renderer. cwe_refs CWE-843; cisa_kev true with kev_date 2024-02-06; active_exploitation confirmed. patch_available true, live_patch_available false, live_patch_notes: 'No vendor live-patch mechanism; remediation requires applying the vendor fixed release.'

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For this entry the clock is the load-bearing half. The packet records no public PoC alongside confirmed in-the-wild exploitation, so an estate that prioritises by CVSS band alone files an 8.8 browser bug into the routine desktop-software cycle while it is actually being exploited — and the packet's RWEP of 55 sitting below the CVSS band is exactly the reading that invites the deferral. Bound to this product, the control means Chrome carries the same KEV-driven remediation clock an internet-facing server would: the vendor fixed release is available per the packet, so the deadline runs from the 2024-02-06 KEV listing rather than from the next scheduled application-update window. Because the packet registers no live-patch mechanism and no vendor mitigation rule, there is no intermediate state an operator can claim against that clock — an endpoint is either running the fixed release or fully exposed to the crafted-HTML path, and the clock has to be measured against the former.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Packet: cisa_kev true, kev_date 2024-02-06, active_exploitation confirmed, poc_available false, CVSS 8.8, RWEP 55, ai_discovered false. patch_available true, live_patch_available false, live_patch_notes: 'No vendor live-patch mechanism; remediation requires applying the vendor fixed release.'

CVE-2022-48618.name: Apple Multiple Products Memory Corruption Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: Within an exploit chain, code that already holds arbitrary kernel read/write wins a time-of-check/time-of-use race to defeat Pointer Authentication, removing a key mitigation and enabling reliable kernel-level control on the device.
attack_vector.privileges_required: low (requires a pre-existing arbitrary read/write primitive from an earlier chain stage)
attack_vector.complexity: high — winning the TOCTOU race and holding prior R/W is non-trivial, consistent with targeted implant use
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered — credited to Apple. No AI involvement documented.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Force iOS/iPadOS 16.2, macOS Ventura 13.1, watchOS 9.2, tvOS 16.2 (or later) via MDM; retire devices that cannot reach a patched OS.
prevention.adequacy: Patch closes the race, but the bug matters only in a chain; the earlier R/W bugs must also be patched to break the full path.

detection.what_would_have_worked: MDM posture checks flagging out-of-date OS builds; mobile threat defense detecting jailbreak/implant indicators.
detection.adequacy: Kernel-level compromise is low-signal; detection largely depends on device-integrity attestation.

response.what_would_have_worked: Re-image / factory-reset compromised devices, rotate any credentials handled on them, force OS update before re-enrollment.
response.adequacy: Reactive; a kernel implant may survive until a full wipe.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: OS flaw-remediation cadence must be immediate on managed mobile fleets; the exploited pre-15.7.1 window shows a lagging patch program is exploitable even for a chained secondary bug.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Essential-8 patching centers OS/application timelines but rarely enforces same-week mobile-OS updates, leaving the PAC-bypass stage available longer.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: Patch-management obligations seldom mandate MDM-forced iOS/macOS updates fast enough to close a mitigation-bypass used in targeted implants.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: Technical-vulnerability management under-weights an exploit-mitigation-bypass because in isolation it needs a prior R/W primitive, understating its role in a full chain.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: System-security assurance credits hardware mitigations like PAC; this flaw defeats that mitigation, so control coverage over-relies on the bypassed protection.

new_control_requirements.name: MOBILE-ENDPOINT-MDM-ENFORCED-KEV-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: Apple shipped this fix as an OS release across five product families at once — macOS Ventura 13.1, watchOS 9.2, iOS 16.2, iPadOS 16.2 and tvOS 16.2 — and the packet records no live-patch mechanism, so every affected device has to be carried through the update and rebooted before the defect is gone. Enforce the fixed build from the device-management channel with user deferral disallowed rather than by prompting the user, and make the enrolment scope cover the watchOS and tvOS members of the estate, which patch-compliance programs built around laptops and phones routinely leave out while the same defect sits on them. The clock runs from the KEV listing, not from the next device-refresh window, because the remediation the packet describes is a reboot the operator has to schedule rather than a silent background fix.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Packet vector: "This issue is fixed in macOS Ventura 13.1, watchOS 9.2, iOS 16.2 and iPadOS 16.2, tvOS 16.2." patch_available true; live_patch_available false with live_patch_notes "No vendor live-patch mechanism; remediation requires applying the fixed release and rebooting." cisa_kev true, kev_date 2024-01-31, active_exploitation confirmed.

new_control_requirements.name: MOBILE-OS-MINIMUM-PATCH-LEVEL-ENFORCEMENT
new_control_requirements.description: Treat the fixed build as an access condition for organizational data rather than a reporting metric: a Mac, iPhone, iPad, Watch or Apple TV still below macOS Ventura 13.1 / watchOS 9.2 / iOS 16.2 / iPadOS 16.2 / tvOS 16.2 is denied or quarantined from mail, VPN and document access until it takes the update. The distinction matters more than usual for this defect because what it removes is Pointer Authentication — a mitigation whose entire job is to stop an attacker who already holds arbitrary kernel read/write from converting that into reliable control. A device left below the fixed build is therefore not simply unpatched; it has lost the mitigation that would otherwise blunt the rest of the chain, and no downstream detection replaces it. Distinguishing test: enrol a device pinned below the fixed build and confirm the policy actually refuses it protected resources, rather than listing the stale build on a dashboard while the device keeps its access.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Packet vector: "An attacker with arbitrary read and write capability may be able to bypass Pointer Authentication." attack_vector: "Within an exploit chain, code that already holds arbitrary kernel read/write wins a time-of-check/time-of-use race to defeat Pointer Authentication, removing a key mitigation and enabling reliable kernel-level control on the device." CWE-367; RWEP 57 with CVSS 7.0; active_exploitation confirmed; fixed releases named in the packet vector.

new_control_requirements.name: MOBILE-ZERO-CLICK-HARDENING
new_control_requirements.description: The packet does not describe a standalone bug reachable on its own — it is a step inside a chain whose precondition is arbitrary kernel read/write already held, and the exploitation signal is Apple's own report against iOS releases predating iOS 15.7.1 with no public PoC, which is the targeted-implant profile rather than commodity malware. For the population plausibly inside that targeting set — executives, journalists, legal and security staff — place devices in the platform's reduced-attack-surface mode where the OS version supports it, so untrusted web content, message attachments, fonts and link previews are not processed automatically. That narrows the delivery path for the earlier chain stages that must land before this PAC bypass is reachable at all, which is the only lever available while devices wait on a reboot-gated update. It has to be a standing assignment made before the next disclosure, not a reaction to this CVE — the mode only helps if it was already on when the chain arrived.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Packet vector: "Apple is aware of a report that this issue may have been exploited against versions of iOS released before iOS 15.7.1." attack_vector places the flaw "[w]ithin an exploit chain". poc_available false while active_exploitation is confirmed. live_patch_available false; remediation per live_patch_notes requires applying the fixed release and rebooting.

CVE-2024-21893.name: Ivanti Connect Secure, Policy Secure, and Neurons Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: An unauthenticated attacker sends a crafted request to the SAML component that forces the appliance to make a server-side request to its own loopback backend on 127.0.0.1:8090, then chains the reachable command-injection flaw (CVE-2024-21887) to run OS commands and drop webshells.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none (unauthenticated, internet-facing gateway)
attack_vector.complexity: low — public tooling automates the SSRF-plus-command-injection chain and bypasses the first mitigation
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered — disclosed by Ivanti, weaponized by public researchers. No AI involvement documented.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Apply the Feb 1 2024 patch set (not just the interim mitigation.release.20240107 XML, which was bypassed), then run the external integrity checker and factory-reset before re-patching if compromise is suspected.
prevention.adequacy: Patching alone is insufficient because appliances compromised before patching retain implants; CISA directed disconnect-and-rebuild.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Run Ivanti's Integrity Checker Tool, alert on loopback-targeting SAML requests and new webshell files, and monitor outbound C2 from the appliance.
detection.adequacy: The ICT missed some tampering; on-box detection from a compromised appliance is not fully trustworthy.

response.what_would_have_worked: Disconnect the appliance, factory-reset, rebuild on a patched image, and rotate all secrets/certificates handled by the gateway.
response.adequacy: Full rebuild plus credential rotation is required because in-place patching cannot evict a pre-existing implant.

NIST-800-53-SC-7.gap: Boundary protection assumes the VPN gateway is a trust anchor; an SSRF that pivots to a loopback backend turns the boundary device itself into the attack surface, which SC-7 does not address.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: The observed exploitation window (days from disclosure to mass scanning) is far shorter than typical flaw-remediation SLAs, and the first mitigation was itself bypassed.

NIS2-Art21-network-security.gap: Network-security measures do not compensate for a preauth RCE on the perimeter appliance that terminates the network; the control that should protect the network is the vulnerable asset.

DORA-Art-9.gap: ICT protection requirements for financial entities do not force the rapid factory-reset-and-rebuild that a compromised, ransomware-targeted VPN appliance actually requires.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: System-security assurance for a remote-access gateway is undermined when a mitigation ships and is then bypassed; point-in-time hardening does not survive an evolving exploit chain.

new_control_requirements.name: PERIMETER-DEVICE-ZERODAY-SLA-TIER
new_control_requirements.description: Ivanti Connect Secure (9.x, 22.x), Ivanti Policy Secure (9.x, 22.x) and Ivanti Neurons for ZTA are the remote-access trust boundary, and the packet has an unauthenticated attacker reaching the SAML component, coercing the appliance into a server-side request to its own loopback backend on 127.0.0.1:8090, and chaining CVE-2024-21887 from there to run OS commands and drop webshells. For these products the control means the remediation clock starts at the 2024-01-31 KEV listing and is measured in hours, not folded into the next appliance maintenance window, because the device being remediated is the thing that decides who gets inside. The packet is specific about what completion means: there is no vendor live-patch mechanism and remediation requires applying the fixed release and rebooting, so a unit that has taken the fixed release but not rebooted still runs the vulnerable code and must be counted as exposed — and on a VPN concentrator that reboot is the step most likely to slip, because taking it drops every active remote-access session, which is exactly how a deferral gets recorded as 'patched'. Precondition, and this is where the control is usually over-claimed: its alternative to the compressed clock is isolating the vulnerable interface, and here that lever is largely unavailable, because the SSRF is reached through the SAML component of the appliance's public-facing web interface — the service itself. Restricting reachability of that interface means denying remote access to the workforce, so it is a time-boxed business decision to be taken explicitly, not an assumed compensating control. Nor does network boundary filtering substitute: the coerced request originates on the appliance and terminates on its own loopback address, so no ACL between the appliance and any other host is on that path.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Packet vector: SSRF (CWE-918) in the SAML component of Ivanti Connect Secure (9.x, 22.x), Ivanti Policy Secure (9.x, 22.x) and Ivanti Neurons for ZTA, allowing access to restricted resources without authentication. Attack vector: forces a server-side request to the appliance's own loopback backend on 127.0.0.1:8090, then chains CVE-2024-21887 to run OS commands and drop webshells.
