The playbook for this product hunts what the packet documents rather than a generic malware signature sweep: requests to the MICS Admin Portal on TCP/8443 with no preceding authentication event, command execution in root context originating from the System Manager API, and content written into the paths the appliance serves (the webshell). The window opens at the earliest date the portal was reachable, and inside it the playbook's actions are the identity ones frameworks do not prescribe post-compromise: rotate every credential the MDM handled, invalidate device-trust state, and review configuration profiles pushed to managed devices during the window. Precondition: these actions must be issued from a control plane the attacker does not hold. Pushing revocations or profiles from a Sentry that is still compromised routes them through the attacker's foothold, so the appliance rebuild precedes them. And this is a response capability, not a fix — it repairs nothing in the authorization path, and it only helps if it was rehearsed before the 2023-08-22 listing rather than drafted during the incident.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Packet: live_patch_notes states remediation includes 'rotating any credentials handled by a potentially compromised MDM'; the product is Ivanti MobileIron Sentry. Attack path reaches 'execute commands as root and drop a webshell' from an unauthenticated request to the MICS admin portal on TCP/8443. active_exploitation confirmed; CISA KEV 2023-08-22; CVSS 9.8; RWEP 76. Cited gaps include NIS2-Art21-identity-management (Identity and access management) and ISO-27001-2022-A.5.15 (Access control).

CVE-2023-27532.name: Veeam Backup & Replication Cloud Connect Missing Authentication for Critical Function Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: An unauthenticated caller connects to the Veeam.Backup.Service .NET remoting endpoint on TCP/9401 and invokes an internal method that returns stored credentials from the configuration database, then reuses them to access backup infrastructure hosts.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none (unauthenticated, network access to TCP/9401)
attack_vector.complexity: low — a single request to an exposed, unauthenticated method; PoC is public and cross-platform
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered — reported by a human researcher and analyzed by Horizon3.ai/Rapid7. No AI involvement documented.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Upgrade to the fixed builds (11a 11.0.1.1261 / 12 12.0.0.1420) and restrict TCP/9401 to the Veeam console via host firewalling/segmentation.
prevention.adequacy: The patch fully closes the missing-auth call; segmentation is the necessary interim control because the port is otherwise reachable by any host on the backup network.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alert on unauthenticated connections to TCP/9401 from any host other than the Veeam console and on credential-retrieval calls followed by lateral SMB/RDP.
detection.adequacy: Detection catches exploitation attempts and the lateral-movement follow-on but does not prevent the initial credential disclosure.

response.what_would_have_worked: Rotate every credential stored in the Veeam configuration database (hypervisor, storage, service accounts) after patching, since exposure must be assumed if the service was reachable.
response.adequacy: Credential rotation is essential post-incident because patching does not invalidate credentials already exfiltrated.

NIST-800-53-IA-2.gap: IA-2 assumes the backup service authenticates callers, but CVE-2023-27532 exposes a critical function on TCP/9401 with no authentication at all, so an IA-2 control set that only governs console/user login never sees the unauthenticated remoting call that dumps credentials.

NIS2-Art21-identity-management.gap: NIS2 Art.21 identity-management measures focus on operator identities; they do not compel segmenting the Veeam backup service port, so an attacker inside the backup network perimeter reaches the missing-auth endpoint without any identity check, exactly the pre-2023-08-22 KEV exposure.

UK-CAF-B2.gap: CAF B2 identity-and-access assurance is scoped to user authentication and does not require locking down machine-to-machine backup-service interfaces, leaving the unauthenticated credential-retrieval method reachable from the backup LAN.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Essential Eight patch timelines allow up to a month for internet-facing/critical fixes, but a public PoC existed within eleven days of disclosure, so a compliant 30-day patch cadence still leaves the ransomware-linked credential-dump exploitable for weeks.

ISO-27001-2022-A.5.15.gap: A.5.15 access control presumes credentials are protected behind an access-control decision; here the stored credentials are returned to any unauthenticated caller of the backup service, so an access-control policy that never gates the remoting endpoint provides no protection.

CVE-2023-26359.name: Adobe ColdFusion Deserialization of Untrusted Data Vulnerability (CVE-2023-26359)

attack_vector.description: An unauthenticated attacker sends a crafted WDDX packet to a ColdFusion endpoint; ColdFusion deserializes it without validating the incoming class contents, allowing a gadget chain to execute arbitrary code as the ColdFusion service account.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none (unauthenticated, network)
attack_vector.complexity: low — no user interaction, and a public Metasploit module plus GitHub PoCs automate the WDDX payload delivery
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered — resolved in Adobe APSB23-25 from conventional security research. No AI involvement documented.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Applying ColdFusion 2018 Update 16 / 2021 Update 6 (which adds a serialization filter/validation) and removing external exposure of ColdFusion admin/component endpoints.
prevention.adequacy: The patch is sufficient once applied, but the sub-week gap between the fix and a working Metasploit module made patch speed, not patch availability, the deciding factor.

detection.what_would_have_worked: WAF/IDS inspection for WDDX serialized markup in unauthenticated POSTs and monitoring for the ColdFusion JVM spawning shell processes.
detection.adequacy: Detection catches post-exploitation web-shell drops but does not prevent the initial deserialization RCE.

response.what_would_have_worked: Isolating the ColdFusion host, hunting for web shells under the webroot, and rotating any credentials the service account could reach.
response.adequacy: Response limits blast radius after compromise but cannot recover data already exposed to the service-account context.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: SI-2 flaw remediation assumes a monthly-to-quarterly patch cycle, but a public Metasploit module for this unauthenticated WDDX deserialization appeared within weeks of the APSB23-25 fix and before the 2023-08-21 KEV due date, so any ColdFusion instance not patched inside days of release was reachable for preauth RCE.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: NIS2 Art.21 patch-management expects timely remediation of known flaws, yet ColdFusion is often an externally exposed application server that operators patch on slow release trains; the preauth, no-user-interaction nature of CVE-2023-26359 means the window between disclosure and exploitation was too short for a routine change-management cadence.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: CAF B4 (system security) is undercut because ColdFusion accepts and deserializes attacker-supplied WDDX packets by design on a network-facing port; hardening guides rarely remove that endpoint, leaving the deserialization sink live until the Update 16 / Update 6 patch is applied.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Essential Eight 'patch applications' allows up to 48 hours for critical internet-facing application flaws, but exploitation of this CVSS 9.8 preauth ColdFusion RCE was observed at KEV-listing time, so even compliant 48-hour SLAs left a live exploitation window on exposed servers.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: A.8.8 technical-vulnerability management typically drives a risk-rated patch schedule; the CVSS 9.8, EPSS ~0.18 preauth deserialization vector plus a shipped Metasploit module means anything short of emergency out-of-band patching left the ColdFusion server exploitable.

CVE-2023-24489.name: Citrix Content Collaboration ShareFile Improper Access Control Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: Unauthenticated attacker exploits an unauthenticated-AES-CBC padding oracle in the StorageZones Controller, forges valid-padding encrypted parameters, and chains a path traversal to upload an .aspx web shell to the IIS webroot via /documentum/upload.aspx, achieving remote code execution.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none (unauthenticated, network-reachable)
attack_vector.complexity: low — public advisory and PoC describe the exact endpoint and crypto flaw; padding-oracle forging is mechanical once the endpoint is reachable
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered — reverse-engineered by Assetnote researchers. No AI involvement documented.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Upgrading to StorageZones Controller 5.11.24+ removes the padding oracle and traversal; alternatively restricting the controller behind authenticated access / a WAF blocking /documentum/upload.aspx.
prevention.adequacy: Patch is fully sufficient — the fix authenticates the ciphertext; the only gap was the months-long window between the quiet May release and August weaponization.

detection.what_would_have_worked: IIS log alerting on POST /documentum/upload.aspx from unauthenticated sources and file-integrity monitoring for new .aspx files in the webroot.
detection.adequacy: Detection catches successful uploads but only after the web shell is written; prevention via patch is the primary control.

response.what_would_have_worked: Removing planted web shells, rotating credentials reachable from the controller, and rebuilding compromised StorageZones hosts.
response.adequacy: Response is remediation-of-compromise; it does not prevent the initial preauth RCE.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: SI-2 flaw remediation assumes a scheduled patch cadence, but the fixed 5.11.24 build predated public disclosure by months; organizations that treated the quiet May release as low-priority were still exposed when weaponization arrived in late July 2023, missing the KEV due date of 2023-09-06.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: NIS2 Art. 21 patch-management expects timely remediation of known flaws, yet this crypto bug shipped a fix with no advisory urgency until CISA KEV listing on 2023-08-16; a monthly patch window leaves a customer-managed StorageZones controller reachable to unauthenticated RCE across the exploitation window.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: CAF B4 (system security) presumes hardened, patched network services, but a padding-oracle in the appliance's own AES implementation is exploitable regardless of network-service hardening; nothing short of the vendor fixed build stops the forged-ciphertext upload to /documentum/upload.aspx.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Essential Eight patch-applications targets a two-week SLA for internet-facing apps, but the 5.11.24 fix lacked exploitation signals until late July 2023, so a compliant two-week clock started from the wrong date and left the preauth RCE open when scanning began.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: A.8.8 technical-vulnerability management would flag CVE-2023-24489 only once tracked as KEV; the low-key May release meant many asset owners had no ticket until August, so the padding-oracle-to-web-shell chain stayed live on unpatched controllers.

new_control_requirements.name: PERIMETER-COMPROMISE-REBUILD-NOT-PATCH
new_control_requirements.description: The packet's exploitation path does not end at code execution, it ends at a file on disk: an unauthenticated attacker exploits the AES-CBC padding oracle in the StorageZones Controller, forges valid-padding encrypted parameters, chains a path traversal, and uploads an .aspx web shell into the IIS webroot via /documentum/upload.aspx. The remediation the packet records — upgrading the ShareFile StorageZones Controller to 5.11.24 or later and recycling the IIS application pool — replaces product code and restarts the worker process. Neither step deletes an .aspx file an attacker already wrote into the webroot, and neither invalidates any credential the application-pool identity holds, so the upgraded controller keeps serving the shell through the patched application. Applied to this product the requirement is that any customer-managed StorageZones Controller reachable during the exposure window is handled as compromised rather than as patched: export and preserve its configuration, rebuild the host at the fixed build from a known-good image instead of upgrading in place, rotate the credentials the controller's service identity holds, and enumerate the IIS webroot and the directories it serves against a known-good installation for .aspx files that are not part of the product. Distinguishing test: on a controller that has already been upgraded, list the webroot's .aspx files and account for each one — an attestation that every StorageZones Controller reports 5.11.24 or later passes cleanly with a web shell dropped before the upgrade still present. Precondition, and this is where the control gets over-claimed: it is an incident-response default, not a preventive measure. It does nothing for a controller still running a vulnerable build, since only the upgrade closes the padding oracle, and a rebuild helps only if the restore point predates the exposure window — where the stored content forces a later restore point, the artifact hunt above is the remaining lever, not the rebuild.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Packet attack_vector: 'Unauthenticated attacker exploits an unauthenticated-AES-CBC padding oracle in the StorageZones Controller, forges valid-padding encrypted parameters, and chains a path traversal to upload an .aspx web shell to the IIS webroot via /documentum/upload.aspx, achieving remote code execution.' Packet live_patch_notes: 'No live-patch mechanism; remediation is upgrading the ShareFile StorageZones Controller to version 5.11.24 or later and recycling the IIS application pool.' patch_available true, live_patch_available false. Vector: 'A vulnerability has been discovered in the customer-managed ShareFile storage zones controller which, if exploited, could allow an unauthenticated attacker to remotely compromise the customer-managed ShareFile storage zones controller.' cisa_kev true, kev_date 2023-08-16, active_exploitation 'confirmed', poc_available true, cvss 9.8, rwep_score 74, cwe_refs CWE-284. Citing gaps include AU-Essential-8-Patch, ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8 Management of technical vulnerabilities, NIST-800-53-SI-2 Flaw Remediation and NIS2-Art21-patch-management.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: The packet's vector names the customer-managed ShareFile storage zones controller, which is the fact that decides who owns the clock: none of this fix arrives through the vendor's cloud service, so the operator takes the upgrade to 5.11.24 or later and the IIS application-pool recycle themselves, on every controller they run, and the packet records no live-patch path that would let them defer the restart. Applied to this CVE the control means that clock runs from the 2023-08-16 KEV listing rather than from the next scheduled application-patch window: the flaw needs no credential, the PoC is public, exploitation is confirmed, and /documentum/upload.aspx answers an unauthenticated request, so a controller left on a vulnerable build across even a standard two-week application SLA is exposed for the whole window with no authentication step in front of it. The control's 'whichever is later' clause is the part that matters on this entry — the vendor's fixed build and the KEV listing are separate events, and an SLA keyed only to a vendor release starts counting from a build an operator may never have registered as security-relevant, whereas the KEV date is an unambiguous trigger. Distinguishing test: produce, per controller, the installed StorageZones Controller version and the timestamp of the application-pool recycle that followed it, measured against 2023-08-16. A patch report showing the fixed build with no recorded recycle does not demonstrate that the patched code is the code running, because the packet makes the recycle part of the remediation and offers no live-patch alternative. Precondition: meeting this SLA closes the exploit path forward only. It says nothing about a controller that was already reached during the window, which is the separate incident-response requirement recorded against this entry.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Packet: cisa_kev true, kev_date 2023-08-16, active_exploitation 'confirmed', poc_available true, cvss 9.8, rwep_score 74. patch_available true, live_patch_available false, live_patch_notes 'No live-patch mechanism; remediation is upgrading the ShareFile StorageZones Controller to version 5.11.24 or later and recycling the IIS application pool.' Vector: 'A vulnerability has been discovered in the customer-managed ShareFile storage zones controller which, if exploited, could allow an unauthenticated attacker to remotely compromise the customer-managed ShareFile storage zones controller.' attack_vector places the unauthenticated upload at '/documentum/upload.aspx'. Citing gaps include AU-Essential-8-Patch (ASD Essential Eight), NIS2-Art21-patch-management, NIST-800-53-SI-2 Flaw Remediation and UK-CAF-B4 System security.

CVE-2023-38180.name: Microsoft .NET Core and Visual Studio Denial-of-Service Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: An unauthenticated remote attacker sends crafted traffic to an ASP.NET Core / Kestrel or .NET application that triggers uncontrolled resource consumption (CWE-400), exhausting CPU/memory and denying service.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none (unauthenticated, network-reachable)
attack_vector.complexity: low — AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N; a single remote request path drives the availability impact
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered — fixed by Microsoft in the August 2023 update cycle. No AI involvement documented.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Applying the August 2023 .NET 6.0/7.0 runtime and Visual Studio updates and rebuilding affected container images.
prevention.adequacy: The patch fully closes the resource-exhaustion path; because it is availability-only it is often deprioritised, so the patch is necessary and the real gap is triage that ignores DoS.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Monitoring for sudden CPU/memory exhaustion and abnormal request patterns against exposed .NET/Kestrel endpoints.
detection.adequacy: Detection surfaces the DoS in progress but cannot prevent the outage; only patching removes the exploitable condition.

response.what_would_have_worked: Rate-limiting / WAF throttling and failover to healthy instances while the runtime update is deployed.
response.adequacy: Mitigations reduce blast radius but do not remove the vulnerable code path.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: SI-2 flaw remediation assumes a scheduled patch window, but this preauth network DoS was already exploited when it hit KEV on 2023-08-09 (one day after the fix); a monthly .NET servicing cadence leaves internet-facing Kestrel apps exposed through the exploitation window.

NIS2-Art21-availability.gap: The availability-of-service obligation is exactly what this CWE-400 resource-exhaustion bug defeats: an unauthenticated request can knock over an in-scope essential service, and generic capacity/HA planning does not stop a targeted protocol-level exhaustion against the vulnerable .NET runtime.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: CAF B4 (system security) presumes timely maintenance of supporting software, yet an unpatched .NET 6/7 runtime remains remotely DoS-able (AV:N, PR:N) until the August 2023 update is applied across every host and container image.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Essential Eight 'Patch applications' allows up to 48 hours only for internet-facing critical flaws; because exploitation was live at KEV listing, any org on a slower application-patch SLA served DoS-vulnerable .NET endpoints in the interim.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: A.8.8 technical-vulnerability management typically triages by CVSS confidentiality/integrity impact, but this is availability-only (C:N/I:N/A:H) and can be de-prioritised, leaving the exploitable .NET runtime unpatched despite confirmed in-the-wild DoS.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: This entry is KEV-listed 2023-08-09 with confirmed exploitation and an available vendor fix, and none of the frameworks cited against it carries a KEV-tied clock — so the control supplies the missing deadline: verified mitigation within 4 hours of the KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later. What 'verified' has to mean here is fixed by the packet's own remediation note — installing the August 2023 .NET 6.0/7.0 runtime and Visual Studio updates and restarting the affected applications, with no live-patch mechanism available — so a long-running Kestrel worker that has taken the runtime package but has not restarted is still executing the vulnerable code and the clock runs to process restart, not to package installation. Package-inventory evidence on its own will report this remediated while the unauthenticated crafted-traffic path still exhausts CPU and memory. The clock also has to span two estates normally on separate patch programs, both named by the packet's remediation: internet-reachable ASP.NET Core services and the Visual Studio installs on developer workstations. The 'documented compensating controls' branch of this SLA is usable only where the service has an enumerable client population whose reachability can be restricted for the window; a publicly reachable endpoint has no such population, and for those the restart is the only lever — restricting reachability narrows who can send the crafted traffic, it does not remove the resource-consumption defect, and it must be recorded as a bounded interim state with the restart still owed. This matters more than the RWEP of 38 suggests, because an availability-only impact is exactly the shape that slips a patch queue despite confirmed in-the-wild exploitation. Distinguishing test: on a staging service, apply the runtime update without restarting the worker and confirm the compliance record does not read remediated until the process itself reports the fixed runtime.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Packet: CISA KEV-listed 2023-08-09, active_exploitation 'confirmed', RWEP 38, CVSS 7.5, poc_available false, CWE-400. patch_available true, live_patch_available false, live_patch_notes 'No vendor live-patch mechanism exists; remediation is installing the August 2023 .NET 6.0/7.0 runtime and Visual Studio updates and restarting the affected applications.' Attack vector: 'An unauthenticated remote attacker sends crafted traffic to an ASP.NET Core / Kestrel or .NET application that triggers uncontrolled resource consumption (CWE-400), exhausting CPU/memory and denying service.'

CVE-2017-18368.name: Zyxel P660HN-T1A Routers Command Injection Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: An unauthenticated attacker sends a crafted request to /ViewLog.asp; the remote_host parameter of the Remote System Log function is passed into an OS command unsanitized, yielding remote command execution on the router.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none (unauthenticated)
attack_vector.complexity: low - single crafted HTTP request, no auth, publicly weaponized by botnet toolkits
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered - reported by an independent researcher. No AI involvement documented.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Vendor firmware that sanitizes remote_host (allowlist / no shell invocation), plus removing WAN exposure of the web-management interface.
prevention.adequacy: Patching is the fix, but it is only adequate where an update channel reaches the device; ISP-distributed and EOL units cannot receive it, so network-level WAN filtering is the compensating control.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Monitoring for ViewLog.asp requests containing shell metacharacters and for routers initiating outbound payload fetches / scanning.
detection.adequacy: Detection catches recruitment traffic but does not stop the initial single-request compromise.

response.what_would_have_worked: Isolating and reflashing (or replacing) affected gateways and blocking outbound botnet C2.
response.adequacy: Effective per-device but does not scale across an unmanaged subscriber fleet.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: SI-2 flaw remediation assumes a managed patch pipeline, but the vulnerable P660HN-T1A units are ISP-provisioned (TrueOnline) home gateways with no vendor auto-update, so the unauthenticated CWE-78 remote_host sink stayed exploitable for years past the 2023-08-07 KEV listing and kept feeding botnet recruitment.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: NIS2 patch-management obligations do not reach ISP-owned customer-premises equipment that the reporting entity does not administer; the WAN-reachable ViewLog.asp command injection remains unpatched across the deployed fleet regardless of any internal SLA.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: CAF B4 assumes hardened, maintained network devices, but the router ships the Remote System Log forwarding function reachable pre-authentication and internet-exposed, so the routine B4 hardening baseline never touches this legacy edge device.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: The Essential 8 48-hour internet-facing patch window is unenforceable when the device has no update channel; the popen-style injection in remote_host stays live because no patched firmware is deliverable to the fielded units.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: A.8.8 technical vulnerability management cannot enumerate or remediate CPE outside the organization's asset inventory, so the 9.8-rated CWE-78 sink on these subscriber routers is invisible to the vulnerability-management process.

CVE-2023-35081.name: Ivanti Endpoint Manager Mobile (EPMM) Path Traversal Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: An arbitrary file write reachable via path traversal in the EPMM admin interface; chained behind the CVE-2023-35078 auth bypass it lets an unauthenticated attacker plant a JSP web shell and execute code on the MDM appliance.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none when chained with CVE-2023-35078 (nominally authenticated administrator for the file write alone)
attack_vector.complexity: low — the traversal payload is deterministic and the auth-bypass chain is publicly documented
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered — found by Ivanti during incident investigation. No AI involvement documented.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Emergency upgrade to the fixed EPMM builds plus restricting the appliance admin interface to a management network rather than the public internet.
prevention.adequacy: Patch is necessary but was unavailable during the zero-day window; network exposure reduction was the only pre-patch mitigation.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alerting on new .jsp files in the appliance web root and on traversal sequences in admin requests.
detection.adequacy: Effective post-compromise but does not prevent the initial write; appliances rarely ship file-integrity monitoring by default.

response.what_would_have_worked: Rebuild the appliance from a known-good image and rotate MDM credentials/certs after any confirmed write.
response.adequacy: Necessary because a web shell on the MDM grants control of the managed mobile fleet; patching a live-compromised host is insufficient.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: SI-2 flaw remediation ran on a monthly patch cadence, but CVE-2023-35081 was a chained zero-day exploited before the 2023-07-28 fix existed; a monthly SLA leaves an internet-facing MDM writable-by-traversal for weeks after the KEV 2023-07-31 listing.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: NIS2 Art.21 patch management does not mandate emergency out-of-band patching of exposed MDM appliances; the CVE-2023-35078+35081 chain was live before any patch shipped, so a routine maintenance-window process would not have closed the arbitrary file write in time.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: CAF B4 secure-configuration assurance assumes the admin file-write path is reachable only by authenticated admins; because CVE-2023-35078 bypasses that gate, B4's trust in the appliance's own auth boundary is misplaced for this traversal.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Essential Eight patch-applications targets a 48-hour window for exploited internet-facing services, but that clock only starts once a fix exists; for this zero-day the appliance was exploitable from before disclosure, so patching alone left the file-write window open.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: A.8.8 technical-vulnerability management would have flagged EPMM for patching only after the 2023-07-28 advisory, whereas the arbitrary file write was already being chained in the wild; the control's disclosure-driven cadence trails the actual exploitation window.

CVE-2023-37580.name: Synacor Zimbra Collaboration Suite (ZCS) Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) Vulnerability (CVE-2023-37580)

attack_vector.description: A reflected XSS in the Zimbra Classic Web Client runs attacker JavaScript in the webmail origin when an authenticated victim clicks a crafted link, allowing theft of mailbox data, cookies, and auth tokens.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none for the attacker; the victim must be an authenticated Zimbra user who clicks the link (UI:R)
attack_vector.complexity: low — the payload is a single crafted URL parameter, and the un-released GitHub fix made the exact sink public
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered — found in the wild by Google TAG. No AI involvement documented.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Applying Zimbra 8.8.15 Patch 41 and, pre-patch, monitoring the vendor's public repository so the leaked fix did not become a free exploit primer.
prevention.adequacy: Patch is the durable fix but was unavailable during the zero-day window; the pre-release GitHub commit meant even fast patchers had an exposure gap.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Web-proxy/WAF alerting on reflected script markers in Classic Web Client URL parameters and on same-origin token exfiltration after a link click.
detection.adequacy: Useful for spotting campaigns but does not prevent the initial script execution in the victim's session.

response.what_would_have_worked: Invalidate all Zimbra auth tokens/sessions and force credential resets for any user who clicked a suspect link.
response.adequacy: Necessary because stolen tokens outlive the patch; rotating sessions is the only way to evict an attacker already holding a token.

NIST-800-53-SI-10.gap: SI-10 input-validation assurance was absent at exactly the sink that mattered: the Classic Web Client reflected an unescaped URL parameter into HTML, and because the fix landed in public source on 2023-07-05 before the advisory, an SI-10 review keyed to vendor bulletins had no signal until attackers were already stealing tokens.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: NIS2 Art.21 patch management assumes a fix is available to deploy, but CVE-2023-37580 was exploited from 2023-06-29 as a zero-day and then via the un-released GitHub commit; a bulletin-driven patch process left webmail exploitable through the KEV 2023-07-27 window and until 8.8.15 Patch 41.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: CAF B4 secure-configuration assurance treats the webmail front end as trusted once patched, but the injection point was reachable pre-patch by any authenticated user who clicked a link; B4's configuration baseline does not compensate for a reflected-XSS sink shipped in the running Classic Web Client.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Essential Eight patch-applications targets a two-week window for internet-facing apps, but that clock starts at fix availability; the Zimbra flaw was exploited as a zero-day and via the leaked commit before 8.8.15 Patch 41, so an on-time patcher was still exposed during the active campaign.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.28.gap: A.8.28 secure-coding controls should have caught the unescaped reflection of user-controlled URL parameters into the Classic Web Client; because the sink shipped to production and was exploited before the patch, the control failed at the code level rather than the deployment level.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For this entry the clock has two starts and the estate has to be driven against the earlier one. Zimbra Collaboration 8 installs below 8.8.15 Patch 41 carry the Classic Web Client sink the packet describes — an unescaped URL parameter reflected into rendered HTML inside the authenticated webmail origin — and the packet places exploitation at 2023-06-29, roughly four weeks before the 2023-07-27 KEV listing and ahead of the vendor advisory. A KEV-tied SLA measured from 2023-07-27 alone therefore produces a remediation record for the tail of the campaign, not for the campaign. Applied to this product: enumerate every Zimbra Collaboration 8 mail server in service, drive each to 8.8.15 Patch 41, and measure completion on the version the running Zimbra services report after they restart. The packet records no live-patch path and states that applying Patch 41 restarts the Zimbra services though not the host, so an instance where the package landed but the webmail service was never restarted is still serving the vulnerable Classic Web Client and counts as exposed — patch_required_reboot being false says only that the machine stays up. Distinguishing test: request the Classic Web Client from each server and confirm the build it actually serves is at or above 8.8.15 Patch 41; an inventory row reading 'Patch 41 applied' beside a running service still answering on the prior build is precisely how this remediation gets recorded complete while the sink is live. Precondition, and the one most often missed here: the packet states the exploit steals mailbox data, cookies and auth tokens from the victim's session, and Patch 41 does nothing to a token already taken — a server reachable during the exposure window needs its webmail sessions invalidated and the credentials of users who could have clicked a crafted link rotated, rather than being closed on the patch record. Steering users toward a different client is not a substitute either: the Classic Web Client endpoint stays served by the same instance until the build carries the fix.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Packet: cisa_kev true, kev_date 2023-07-27, active_exploitation confirmed, poc_available true, rwep_score 62 against cvss 6.1. active_exploitation_notes: 'Google TAG observed four distinct groups — including the Russia-aligned Winter Vivern — exploiting the flaw against government targets in Moldova and Tunisia starting 2023-06-29, at least two weeks before Zimbra's advisory.' affected: the ZCS Classic Web Client 'which reflects an unescaped URL parameter into rendered HTML, enabling cross-site scripting in the authenticated webmail origin'; affected_versions: 'Zimbra Collaboration 8 before 8.8.15 Patch 41'. patch_available true, patch_required_reboot false, live_patch_available false, live_patch_notes: 'No vendor live-patch mechanism; remediation requires applying Zimbra 8.8.15 Patch 41, which restarts Zimbra services but not the host.' attack_vector: attacker JavaScript runs in the webmail origin when an authenticated victim clicks a crafted link, 'allowing theft of mailbox data, cookies, and auth tokens'.

new_control_requirements.name: PRIMARY-SOURCE-INTAKE-VENDOR-BLOG-COVERAGE
new_control_requirements.description: This entry extends the control's premise past vendor blogs to the vendor's own public source repository. The packet records that Zimbra's fix landed in public source on 2023-07-05 and that a later wave of attackers harvested it from there and exploited the flaw before 8.8.15 Patch 41 shipped — so for the interval between that push and the released patch, the authoritative signal that Zimbra 8 webmail was exploitable existed in a primary source while every advisory-driven feed the estate subscribes to was still silent. For an operator running Zimbra Collaboration 8 the requirement is concrete: treat the vendor's public commit stream for that product as a monitored intake source alongside the advisory page; make a security-relevant commit touching the webmail rendering path, with no accompanying advisory, open a case rather than wait for the bulletin; and start the internal remediation clock at the earlier of the two signals rather than at the advisory. Distinguishing test: take a fix the vendor published in source ahead of its own advisory and check whether the intake pipeline raised anything on the commit date — a pipeline whose Zimbra coverage is the advisory page alone produces nothing, which is exactly the result it produced in July 2023 while a second wave was already exploiting the harvested fix. Precondition, stated because this control is easy to over-credit: it shortens the interval between a public fix and the operator knowing, and it gives nothing at all for the first window the packet describes — 2023-06-29 through the 2023-07-05 push — during which the flaw was a zero-day with no fix in any source. That window is bounded by response and by session/credential invalidation after the fact, not by intake coverage.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Packet active_exploitation_notes: 'A later wave harvested the fix from Zimbra's public GitHub (pushed 2023-07-05) and exploited it before the official 8.8.15 Patch 41 shipped', with initial exploitation from 2023-06-29 'at least two weeks before Zimbra's advisory'. The NIST-800-53-SI-10 gap in framework_control_gaps states that 'because the fix landed in public source on 2023-07-05 before the advisory, an SI-10 review keyed to vendor bulletins had no signal until attackers were already stealing tokens'. The NIS2-Art21-patch-management gap states 'a bulletin-driven patch process left webmail exploitable through the KEV 2023-07-27 window and until 8.8.15 Patch 41'. The AU-Essential-8-Patch gap states the two-week clock 'starts at fix availability' and that the flaw was exploited 'via the leaked commit before 8.8.15 Patch 41, so an on-time patcher was still exposed during the active campaign'.

CVE-2023-38606.name: Apple Multiple Products Kernel Unspecified Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: A malicious or sandboxed app, delivered via the Operation Triangulation zero-click iMessage chain, abuses undocumented hardware MMIO registers to bypass the memory-protection controller and write to sensitive kernel state, escalating within the device-compromise chain.
attack_vector.privileges_required: local user (code running as a sandboxed app, delivered without user interaction via the zero-click chain)
attack_vector.complexity: high — requires knowledge of undocumented hardware MMIO registers and chaining with other Triangulation-chain flaws
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered — found by Kaspersky GReAT via forensic analysis of infected devices. No AI involvement documented.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Installing the fixed OS build and rebooting closes the kernel-write primitive.
prevention.adequacy: The patch is fully remediating but arrived after in-the-wild use, and the low CVSS 5.5 risked deprioritization despite the flaw being chain-critical.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Mobile forensic triage (Kaspersky triangle_check / MVT) detecting Triangulation artifacts and anomalous kernel behavior.
detection.adequacy: Detection is post-compromise; the zero-click delivery leaves no user-visible signal and on-device EDR is largely blind on iOS.

response.what_would_have_worked: Device wipe/re-provision and credential rotation after a confirmed Triangulation infection.
response.adequacy: Response limits persistence but cannot recover data already exfiltrated during the zero-click window.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: The exploited primitive was an undocumented hardware feature, so no SI-2 flaw-remediation cadence could act until Apple shipped iOS 15.7.8/16.6 on 2023-07-24; devices patched only by the KEV due date (2023-08-16) stayed exposed across the entire zero-click in-the-wild window.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: Mobile-fleet patch SLAs keyed to the CVSS 5.5 (medium) score would deprioritize this, yet it was a live component of a zero-click APT chain; severity-driven patching misses low-CVSS kernel primitives that are chain-critical in real attacks.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: A hardware-level memory-protection bypass defeats the platform's secure-by-design assumption; B4 system-security assurance cannot be verified against an undocumented silicon MMIO register the vendor itself never documented.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: The Essential Eight 48-hour patch window for critical/internet-facing apps does not extend to managed mobile OS images on the same clock, and MDM update lag left devices exposed after the 2023-07-24 fix while the chain was actively deployed.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: An organization's technical-vulnerability register scored this 5.5 and would not flag it as chain-critical; A.8.8 as normally run does not correlate a low-CVSS kernel item with an active APT zero-click chain.

new_control_requirements.name: MOBILE-ZERO-CLICK-HARDENING
new_control_requirements.description: This Apple kernel flaw is not a standalone bug an operator can triage as an endpoint item — the packet places it as the kernel-primitive stage of the Operation Triangulation zero-click iMessage chain against iOS devices released before iOS 15.7.1, with Kaspersky documenting the abuse of undocumented hardware MMIO registers to defeat the memory-protection controller. Zero-click is the whole difficulty: there is no attachment for a user to decline and no link to leave untapped, so awareness training contributes nothing and the only pre-fix lever is refusing to process the content on arrival. For the cohort plausibly inside the targeting set this chain served, the requirement is a standing reduced-attack-surface posture on their iPhones, iPads and Macs in which message attachments, link previews, fonts and untrusted web content are not parsed automatically — assigned before the next disclosure rather than configured in response to this one, because the posture only helps if it was already on when the chain arrived. That timing is the point of the control on this entry: the packet's own flaw-remediation gap notes the exploited primitive was an undocumented hardware feature, so no remediation cadence could act until Apple shipped the fixed builds on 2023-07-24, which means the entire in-the-wild window was covered by whatever posture each device already carried. Preconditions: this narrows the delivery path into the kernel primitive, it does not remove it, and it is not available as a retroactive fix — a device compromised during the confirmed exploitation window is not remediated by enabling the posture afterwards and belongs on the incident path with its build and message history examined. It is a holding measure for the window before the fixed build and its required restart land, not a substitute for them.
new_control_requirements.evidence: active_exploitation_notes: 'Exploited in the wild as a kernel-primitive stage of the Operation Triangulation zero-click iMessage chain against iOS devices released before iOS 15.7.1. Apple confirmed awareness of active exploitation; Kaspersky documented the abuse of undocumented hardware MMIO registers to defeat memory protection.' affected records that 'a malicious app can modify sensitive kernel state by abusing undocumented memory-mapped I/O (MMIO) registers to bypass the hardware page-protection controller'. The packet's NIST-800-53-SI-2 gap: 'The exploited primitive was an undocumented hardware feature, so no SI-2 flaw-remediation cadence could act until Apple shipped iOS 15.7.8/16.6 on 2023-07-24; devices patched only by the KEV due date (2023-08-16) stayed exposed across the entire zero-click in-the-wild window.' Its UK-CAF-B4 gap adds that 'B4 system-security assurance cannot be verified against an undocumented silicon MMIO register the vendor itself never documented.' active_exploitation is confirmed; kev_date 2023-07-26.

new_control_requirements.name: MOBILE-ENDPOINT-MDM-ENFORCED-KEV-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: The scope trap on this entry sits in affected_versions, not in the vector's wording. Five Apple OS families are named — iOS/iPadOS below 15.7.8, iOS/iPadOS 16.x below 16.6, macOS Ventura below 13.5, macOS Monterey below 12.6.8, macOS Big Sur below 11.7.9, tvOS below 16.6 and watchOS below 9.6 — so an estate that enforces update policy on iPhones, iPads and Macs while never enumerating its Apple TV and Watch devices reports full compliance with two affected platforms untouched. For this CVE the control means the fixed build for each of those lines is pushed on the clock that opened with the 2023-07-26 KEV listing, with user deferral disallowed, rather than left to the device holder or to the next image refresh — the packet's Essential Eight gap records exactly this failing, that MDM update lag left devices exposed after the 2023-07-24 fix while the chain was actively deployed. Completion is measured on the build the device is running after its restart: live_patch_available is false and the packet states Apple ships no live-kernel-patch mechanism and that remediation requires installing the fixed OS build and rebooting the device, so an update downloaded and staged is not remediation and must not close the item. The trigger has to be the KEV listing rather than the score, because at CVSS 5.5 with poc_available false this ranks below routine work on a severity-sorted queue while being a live stage of a zero-click chain. Distinguishing test: report the running OS build for every enrolled iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple TV and Watch and show each against the fixed build for its own line — a console that reports 'update policy applied', or that covers only the families the management platform was set up for, is the paper form of this control.
new_control_requirements.evidence: affected_versions lists 'iOS/iPadOS < 15.7.8', 'iOS/iPadOS 16.x < 16.6', 'macOS Ventura < 13.5', 'macOS Monterey < 12.6.8', 'macOS Big Sur < 11.7.9', 'tvOS < 16.6', 'watchOS < 9.6'. live_patch_available is false and live_patch_notes states 'Apple ships no live-kernel-patch mechanism; remediation requires installing the fixed OS build (iOS/iPadOS 15.7.8 or 16.6, macOS Ventura 13.5, macOS Monterey 12.6.8, macOS Big Sur 11.7.9, tvOS 16.6, watchOS 9.6) and rebooting the device'; patch_required_reboot is true. cisa_kev is true with kev_date 2023-07-26 and active_exploitation confirmed; cvss is 5.5 and poc_available is false. The packet's AU-Essential-8-Patch gap: 'MDM update lag left devices exposed after the 2023-07-24 fix while the chain was actively deployed.' Its NIS2-Art21-patch-management gap: 'severity-driven patching misses low-CVSS kernel primitives that are chain-critical in real attacks.'

new_control_requirements.name: MOBILE-OS-MINIMUM-PATCH-LEVEL-ENFORCEMENT
new_control_requirements.description: Half of this control applies to this Apple flaw and half does not, and the half that does not is worth stating so it is never recorded as a mitigation. The packet's trigger is an app modifying sensitive kernel state, which would ordinarily make application-install restriction the operator's lever — but the delivery it documents is a zero-click iMessage chain, so the malicious code arrives without any installation an install policy could refuse, and restricting untrusted or side-loaded applications does nothing against this path. What remains is making the fixed build a condition of access rather than a row on a report: an enrolled iPhone, iPad or Mac running below its own line's fixed build — 15.7.8 or 16.6 for iOS/iPadOS, 13.5 for Ventura, 12.6.8 for Monterey, 11.7.9 for Big Sur — is denied mail, VPN and document access until it is at or above it, instead of keeping every entitlement it had while showing as non-compliant. The distinguishing test is to enrol a device pinned below the fixed build and confirm the policy actually withholds access to protected resources; an estate that surfaces the stale build and leaves the access in place has recorded the exposure rather than removed it. Where a device family holds no organisational resource for the gate to withhold, the access condition has no grip and those devices — the tvOS and watchOS units affected_versions names at fixed builds 16.6 and 9.6 — must be held to the fixed build by enumeration instead, not dropped from scope because the gate cannot reach them. Precondition: because the packet requires the fixed build to be installed and the device rebooted, the condition must evaluate the build the device is running rather than the update it has downloaded, or it re-admits a device still executing the vulnerable kernel. This is a holding measure for the window before the build lands, and it does nothing for a device already compromised during the confirmed exploitation window.
new_control_requirements.evidence: vector: 'An app may be able to modify sensitive kernel state. Apple is aware of a report that this issue may have been actively exploited against versions of iOS released before iOS 15.7.1', with the fix list 'macOS Monterey 12.6.8, iOS 15.7.8 and iPadOS 15.7.8, iOS 16.6 and iPadOS 16.6, tvOS 16.6, macOS Big Sur 11.7.9, macOS Ventura 13.5, watchOS 9.6'. active_exploitation_notes place delivery in 'the Operation Triangulation zero-click iMessage chain', not in a user-initiated installation. patch_required_reboot is true and live_patch_notes states remediation 'requires installing the fixed OS build ... and rebooting the device'. The packet's ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8 gap: 'An organization's technical-vulnerability register scored this 5.5 and would not flag it as chain-critical', and its AU-Essential-8-Patch gap records MDM update lag leaving devices exposed after the 2023-07-24 fix.

CVE-2023-35078.name: Ivanti Endpoint Manager Mobile Authentication Bypass Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: A remote unauthenticated attacker requests specific EPMM API paths that fail to enforce authentication, gaining access to device/user PII and the ability to change configuration, install software, and alter security profiles on managed devices; chaining CVE-2023-35081 turns this into web-shell RCE.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none (unauthenticated)
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L, a single crafted request to an unauthenticated API path
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered — coordinated disclosure by human researchers, patched by Ivanti. No AI involvement documented.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Upgrade EPMM to 11.8.1.1 / 11.9.1.1 / 11.10.0.2, restrict management-plane exposure to the public internet, and place the admin API behind a VPN or allowlist.
prevention.adequacy: Patching removes the bypass, but because it was exploited as a 0-day, network exposure reduction was the only mitigation available before the fix shipped.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alerting on unauthenticated 200-responses to /mifs/aad/api/v2/ paths and on anomalous external admin-API activity.
detection.adequacy: Detection surfaces active abuse but did not prevent the pre-disclosure ministry breaches.

response.what_would_have_worked: Assume compromise for internet-exposed EPMM, hunt for the chained CVE-2023-35081 web shell, and rotate device-management credentials/profiles.
response.adequacy: Response is essential given confirmed pre-patch exploitation and web-shell chaining.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: SI-2's fix-on-disclosure model lost the race here: CVE-2023-35078 was a 0-day used against Norwegian ministries before a patch existed, so flaw-remediation timelines gave no protection during the exploitation window that started before 2023-07-25.

NIS2-Art21-vulnerability-management.gap: NIS2 vulnerability-management assumes an authenticated, monitored management plane, but this preauth bypass reaches EPMM device-management APIs with no credentials, letting an attacker read fleet PII and alter security profiles without ever touching an access-control checkpoint.

UK-CAF-B2.gap: CAF B2 identity-and-access-control presumes API endpoints enforce authentication; CVE-2023-35078 defeats that assumption at the MDM tier, so B2's account-management controls never engage against an actor who bypasses auth entirely on /mifs/aad/api paths.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Essential 8 patch cadence could not help defenders during the 0-day window before Ivanti's 2023-07 fix, and because EPMM is an internet-facing identity/MDM server, even a fast patch left exposure for organisations already breached in the pre-disclosure period.

ISO-27001-2022-A.5.15.gap: A.5.15 access-control policy is bypassed at the application layer: the flaw grants unauthenticated access to restricted device-management functions, so documented role/authentication rules provide no barrier to the API paths CVE-2023-35078 exposes.

CVE-2023-29298.name: Adobe ColdFusion Improper Access Control Vulnerability (CVE-2023-29298)

attack_vector.description: A crafted request path with an unexpected extra segment defeats ColdFusion's access-control check, exposing administrator CFM/CFC endpoints to unauthenticated callers; attackers then chain the WDDX deserialization flaw (CVE-2023-29300) for remote code execution.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none (unauthenticated)
attack_vector.complexity: low — a single crafted HTTP path reaches the administrator endpoints; no user interaction
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered — reported to Adobe and analyzed by Rapid7. No AI involvement documented.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Applying the complete Adobe update (including the follow-up that fixed the incomplete first patch) and restricting administrator endpoints by network ACL / reverse-proxy allowlist
prevention.adequacy: Patch is sufficient only once the complete fix is applied; the incomplete first patch meant remediation had to be re-verified against the follow-up update.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Web-log monitoring for unauthenticated requests reaching administrator CFC/CFM endpoints and for the deserialization follow-on
detection.adequacy: Access to admin endpoints from unauthenticated sessions is a clear signal but is only visible with request-level logging on the ColdFusion instance.

response.what_would_have_worked: Assuming server compromise where the bypass was chained to RCE, rebuilding the host and rotating datasource/admin credentials
response.adequacy: Because the bypass fed an RCE chain, containment requires treating a hit as full server compromise.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: Adobe's APSB23-40 fix was initially incomplete, so SI-2 flaw remediation applied on the first patch still left the access-control bypass exploitable until the follow-up update; mass exploitation began within days of the 2023-07-20 KEV listing, faster than a single-pass SI-2 remediation could verify.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: The bypass exposed administrator CFM/CFC endpoints preauth; NIS2 patch-management on a monthly cadence leaves internet-facing ColdFusion exposed during the days-long window between the July 2023 disclosure and the emergency patching that active exploitation demanded.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: CAF B4 assumes the admin console is authentication-gated; this improper-access-control flaw let unauthenticated requests reach administrator endpoints, so system-security controls relying on the application's own auth were bypassed outright.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Essential Eight's two-week patch SLA for internet-facing applications was too slow — this preauth bypass was chained to RCE and exploited within days of the 2023-07-20 KEV date.

ISO-27001-2022-A.5.15.gap: A.5.15 access control is enforced by ColdFusion's own administrator authentication; CVE-2023-29298 bypasses that check via an unexpected path segment, so the documented access-control policy did not actually restrict the administrator endpoints.

new_control_requirements.name: ENTERPRISE-ERP-MANAGEMENT-FUNCTION-AUTHENTICATION
new_control_requirements.description: ColdFusion decides which requests may reach its administrator CFM and CFC endpoints, and this CVE is that decision failing open: the packet's attack vector is a crafted request path carrying an unexpected extra segment that defeats the access-control check, exposing administrator endpoints to unauthenticated callers with no user interaction required. Bound to this product the control means each administrator CFM/CFC endpoint authorizes its own caller rather than inheriting a verdict from the path-matching layer in front of it, and the ColdFusion administrator surface is segmented so an untrusted network caller cannot present a request to that layer at all — an internet-facing ColdFusion server should not answer administrator endpoints from the public internet whatever application content it serves. Apply this across all three product tracks the packet names, not just the one an inventory happens to list: ColdFusion 2018, 2021 and 2023 installations each carry the same administrator surface. This is also why an access-control-policy attestation passes while the flaw is live — the documented policy is enforced by ColdFusion's own administrator authentication, and the attacker never authenticates as any ColdFusion administrator, so no account model is ever consulted. Priority follows the chain rather than the 7.5 CVSS band: the packet records attackers chaining this with CVE-2023-29300 (WDDX deserialization) to reach unauthenticated RCE on internet-facing ColdFusion, so this is a code-execution precondition, not an information-exposure item. Distinguishing test: from a segment with no operational need to administer ColdFusion, request each administrator CFM/CFC endpoint on a staging instance — including with extra path segments appended — and confirm each is refused before the endpoint runs. Precondition: the endpoint-side check is what Adobe's update repairs; segmentation is the operator-side lever until that update and its follow-up land, and it bounds who can send the crafted request without repairing the check, so any caller inside a permitted segment still reaches it.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Packet vector: ColdFusion 2018u16 and earlier, 2021u6 and earlier and 2023.0.0.330468 and earlier are affected by an Improper Access Control vulnerability resulting in a security feature bypass; an attacker could leverage it to access the administration CFM and CFC endpoints, and exploitation does not require user interaction. attack_vector: a crafted request path with an unexpected extra segment defeats ColdFusion's access-control check, exposing administrator CFM/CFC endpoints to unauthenticated callers, after which attackers chain the WDDX deserialization flaw CVE-2023-29300 for remote code execution. CWE-284; CVSS 7.5; RWEP 68; poc_available true; CISA KEV 2023-07-20 with confirmed active exploitation. affected_versions: ColdFusion 2018 <= Update 16, 2021 <= Update 6, 2023 <= 2023.0.0.330468. The packet's UK-CAF-B4 gap states CAF B4 assumes the admin console is authentication-gated and that this flaw let unauthenticated requests reach administrator endpoints; its ISO-27001-2022-A.5.15 gap states access control is enforced by ColdFusion's own administrator authentication, which the CVE bypasses via an unexpected path segment, so the documented policy did not actually restrict the administrator endpoints.

new_control_requirements.name: INCOMPLETE-PATCH-SEQUENCE-SEVERITY-MULTIPLIER
new_control_requirements.description: This entry is the case the control names. The packet records that Adobe's initial fix was incomplete and required a follow-up update, and that first-pass remediation left the access-control bypass exploitable until that follow-up landed. For ColdFusion that means the vulnerability-management record cannot treat 'the July update was applied' as closure: the closing evidence is the build each running ColdFusion instance reports, measured against both the initial update the packet names for its track — 2018 Update 17, 2021 Update 7, 2023.0.0.1 — and the follow-up fix that completed it, with every server re-verified after the follow-up rather than only after the first pass. It also sets what the operator should expect next on this surface. A bypass reachable by appending an unexpected segment to the request path, whose first vendor fix did not fully close it, points at the path-handling layer itself rather than one endpoint, so further bypasses against the same primitive are a live expectation: the administrator-endpoint segmentation should be retained past the update rather than removed once the patch record reads clean. Distinguishing test: after applying the update, re-issue the crafted extra-path-segment request against an administrator CFM/CFC endpoint on a staging ColdFusion instance instead of reading the installed update level — an estate that verified only the first patch carried a clean flaw-remediation record while the bypass still worked, which is exactly the failure this control exists to catch.
new_control_requirements.evidence: live_patch_notes: 'No live-patch mechanism; remediation requires Adobe's ColdFusion update (2018 Update 17, 2021 Update 7, 2023.0.0.1) plus the follow-up fix that completed the incomplete initial patch.' active_exploitation_notes: Adobe's initial fix was incomplete and required a follow-up update, and attackers chained the flaw with CVE-2023-29300 to achieve unauthenticated RCE on internet-facing ColdFusion within days of Adobe's July 2023 patch. The packet's NIST-800-53-SI-2 gap states that Adobe's APSB23-40 fix was initially incomplete, so flaw remediation applied on the first patch still left the access-control bypass exploitable until the follow-up update, and that mass exploitation began within days of the 2023-07-20 KEV listing — faster than a single-pass remediation could verify. attack_vector identifies the primitive as a crafted request path with an unexpected extra segment defeating the access-control check. patch_available true; poc_available true; active_exploitation 'confirmed'.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: ColdFusion 2018 up to Update 16, 2021 up to Update 6 and 2023 up to 2023.0.0.330468 must be driven to their fixed updates on the clock that opened with the 2023-07-20 KEV listing, not on a monthly or fortnightly application cadence — the packet records mass exploitation beginning within days of that listing, a public PoC, and a chain to unauthenticated remote code execution via CVE-2023-29300. Enumerate all three tracks: an estate that updates its inventoried ColdFusion 2021 servers while a 2018 or 2023 install sits on an affected build still answers the crafted request. The clock does not stop at the first update — live_patch_available is false and the packet states remediation is Adobe's ColdFusion update (2018 Update 17, 2021 Update 7, 2023.0.0.1) plus the follow-up fix that completed the incomplete initial patch, so the SLA has to carry through the follow-up on every server rather than closing when the first pass is recorded. patch_required_reboot is false, which means there is no host reboot to schedule; it does not mean the fixed code is executing when the installer exits, so completion is measured on the build each running ColdFusion instance reports. And because active exploitation is confirmed and the chained outcome is code execution in the ColdFusion context, an internet-facing server that ran an affected build during the window belongs on the incident path — reviewing what was placed or executed through the administrator endpoints — rather than being closed on the update record.
new_control_requirements.evidence: cisa_kev true with kev_date 2023-07-20; active_exploitation 'confirmed'; CVSS 7.5; RWEP 68; poc_available true; ai_discovered false; patch_available true; patch_required_reboot false; live_patch_available false. live_patch_notes: 'No live-patch mechanism; remediation requires Adobe's ColdFusion update (2018 Update 17, 2021 Update 7, 2023.0.0.1) plus the follow-up fix that completed the incomplete initial patch.' affected_versions: Adobe ColdFusion 2018 <= Update 16, Adobe ColdFusion 2021 <= Update 6, Adobe ColdFusion 2023 <= 2023.0.0.330468. active_exploitation_notes: added to KEV 2023-07-20 amid active exploitation; attackers chained it with CVE-2023-29300 to achieve unauthenticated RCE on internet-facing ColdFusion within days of Adobe's July 2023 patch. The packet's AU-Essential-8-Patch gap states the two-week patch SLA for internet-facing applications was too slow because the preauth bypass was chained to RCE and exploited within days of the 2023-07-20 KEV date; its NIS2-Art21-patch-management gap states a monthly cadence leaves internet-facing ColdFusion exposed during the days-long window between the July 2023 disclosure and the emergency patching active exploitation demanded.

CVE-2023-38205.name: Adobe ColdFusion Improper Access Control Vulnerability (CVE-2023-38205)

attack_vector.description: A crafted request bypasses the ColdFusion administrator access-control check, letting an unauthenticated attacker reach admin CFM/CFC endpoints; combined with deserialization primitives this yields remote code execution on internet-facing servers.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none (unauthenticated) — direct HTTP access to the ColdFusion administrator surface
attack_vector.complexity: low — the bypass is a single crafted request requiring no user interaction; RCE chaining uses known ColdFusion deserialization sinks
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered — reported by security researchers and fixed by Adobe. No AI involvement documented.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Applying APSB23-47 (not just the earlier incomplete CVE-2023-29298 fix), applying the ColdFusion lockdown guide, and removing the administrator interface from internet exposure.
prevention.adequacy: The correct patch is required and sufficient to close the bypass; network isolation of the admin interface is a strong compensating control given the near-immediate exploitation.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Monitoring for unauthenticated access to /CFIDE/administrator and CFC endpoints, and for post-access file writes or scheduled-task creation on ColdFusion hosts.
detection.adequacy: Detection surfaces exploitation attempts and RCE follow-on but does not prevent the initial access-control bypass.

response.what_would_have_worked: Isolating the server, hunting for web shells and unauthorized scheduled tasks, rotating any credentials or secrets stored in ColdFusion, and rebuilding compromised hosts.
response.adequacy: Response is necessary once RCE is achieved but cannot undo data access or secrets exposure that already occurred.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: SI-2 flaw remediation was already exercised for the predecessor CVE-2023-29298, yet CVE-2023-38205 bypasses that patch; an organization that dutifully applied the prior fix remained exploitable, so a one-shot remediation posture failed against mass exploitation that began before the KEV 2023-08-10 due date.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: NIS2 Art.21 patch-management timelines assume a vendor fix closes the exposure, but here the first ColdFusion patch was incomplete and this CVE reopened admin-endpoint access; essential entities that patched CVE-2023-29298 still needed the APSB23-47 update, and any lag left an internet-facing RCE path open.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: CAF B4 system-security hardening of the ColdFusion administrator surface is undermined because the access-control filter itself is bypassable; restricting admin functionality does not stop unauthenticated reach to CFM/CFC endpoints until APSB23-47 is applied.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Essential Eight patch cadence for internet-facing applications was defeated by an incomplete-fix bypass: applying the earlier ColdFusion update did not remediate CVE-2023-38205, so the standard 48-hour critical-patch window only helped once the correct APSB23-47 build shipped.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: A.8.8 technical-vulnerability management presumes tracking and applying vendor fixes closes exposure, but the superseded fix left the admin endpoints reachable; the control needed to recognize the patch-bypass relationship to CVE-2023-29298 and re-remediate before near-immediate exploitation.

new_control_requirements.name: INCOMPLETE-PATCH-SEQUENCE-SEVERITY-MULTIPLIER
new_control_requirements.description: This Adobe ColdFusion flaw is the second CVE on one primitive and the packet states the relation outright: CVE-2023-38205 is recorded as a bypass of the CVE-2023-29298 fix, reinstating unauthenticated reach to the ColdFusion administrator's CFM and CFC endpoints. For this product the control means a ColdFusion server that already took the earlier update is not carried forward as remediated — the earlier ticket's evidence proves nothing about this CVE — and that a second bypass of the same access-control check is ranked on the expectation that a third is likely, rather than as a discrete 7.5-rated item. Scope the sweep from the packet's affected list, not from the headline product name: three separate release trains are named (ColdFusion 2018 Update 18 and earlier, 2021 Update 8 and earlier, 2023 Update 2 and earlier), each with its own fixed update recorded in the packet as 2018u19, 2021u9 and 2023u3 or later in APSB23-47, so an estate that updates only its ColdFusion 2023 servers leaves the 2018 and 2021 installs fully exposed behind a remediation report that reads clean. Measure completion on the build the running service is executing: the packet records no live-patch mechanism and requires a restart of the ColdFusion service after the upgrade, so a server whose files were replaced but whose service was never restarted is still running the pre-fix code — patch_required_reboot being false means no host reboot is needed, not that the fix is live. The clock is the KEV listing of 2023-07-20 against a 2023-08-10 due date, and the packet records exploitation within days of disclosure against internet-facing servers, so the re-remediation runs ahead of that due date rather than to it. Finally, keep the second half of the chain in scope: the packet's exploitation path reaches code execution by combining admin-endpoint reach with deserialization primitives, and the packet records Adobe recommending the associated lockdown and serial-filter guidance alongside the update — the update closes the access-control bypass, that guidance constrains what the bypass was being chained into.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Packet facts only: CWE-284; cisa_kev true with kev_date 2023-07-20 and a 2023-08-10 due date; active_exploitation confirmed; poc_available true; RWEP 68 / CVSS 7.5; active_exploitation_notes 'Actively exploited within days of disclosure in July 2023 as the access-control bypass that reinstated attacker reach to admin endpoints after the incomplete CVE-2023-29298 fix; EPSS sits at ~0.998'; affected_versions 'ColdFusion 2018 Update 18 and earlier', 'ColdFusion 2021 Update 8 and earlier', 'ColdFusion 2023 Update 2 and earlier'; patch_available true, patch_required_reboot false, live_patch_available false, live_patch_notes 'No live-patch mechanism; remediation requires upgrading to the fixed ColdFusion builds in APSB23-47 (2018u19, 2021u9, 2023u3 or later) and restarting the ColdFusion service. Adobe also recommends applying the associated lockdown/serial-filter guidance.'; attack_vector 'combined with deserialization primitives this yields remote code execution on internet-facing servers'; the SI-2, ISO A.8.8, NIS2 patch-management and Essential Eight gap statements, each of which names the incomplete-fix relationship to CVE-2023-29298.

new_control_requirements.name: ENTERPRISE-ERP-MANAGEMENT-FUNCTION-AUTHENTICATION
new_control_requirements.description: The ColdFusion administrator access-control check is where the product decides whether a caller may reach administrative functionality, and this CVE is that check failing open: the packet places the defect in the ColdFusion administrator interface as an improper access control (CWE-284) and has an unauthenticated caller reaching administrative CFM and CFC endpoints through a crafted request, with the vector stating that exploitation does not require user interaction. Bound to this product the control means each administrative CFM and CFC endpoint makes its own authorization decision rather than inheriting a verdict from the check that fronts it, and the ColdFusion Administrator surface is segmented so a caller on an untrusted network cannot present a request to that check at all — the packet records exploitation against internet-facing ColdFusion servers, which is precisely the deployment where the front check is the only thing in the path. Distinguishing test: from an external address and from an internal segment with no operational need for the ColdFusion Administrator, issue unauthenticated requests to administrative CFM and CFC endpoints on a staging server and confirm each is refused before the endpoint runs; a system-security attestation recording that 'administrator access is restricted' passes cleanly while this path stays open, because the restriction being attested to is the check the CVE bypasses. Precondition, stated rather than assumed: the endpoint-side authorization is a property the APSB23-47 update establishes — this control says what to verify, it does not implement it. Until that update and the ColdFusion service restart the packet requires have both landed, restricting which networks can reach the Administrator bounds who can send the crafted request but leaves the bypass fully usable from inside any permitted segment, and it is not available at all where the Administrator has to stay reachable for operations. And because exploitation is confirmed and a public PoC exists, a server that was internet-reachable during the window is a triage item rather than a patch item: the packet's path continues from admin-endpoint reach into code execution via deserialization primitives, so the update removes the reach without removing anything an attacker already placed.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Packet facts only: CWE-284; affected 'Adobe ColdFusion administrator interface, where an improper access-control check allows unauthenticated reach to administrative CFM and CFC endpoints (a bypass of the CVE-2023-29298 fix)'; vector 'An attacker could leverage this vulnerability to access the administration CFM and CFC endpoints. Exploitation of this issue does not require user interaction.'; attack_vector 'A crafted request bypasses the ColdFusion administrator access-control check, letting an unauthenticated attacker reach admin CFM/CFC endpoints; combined with deserialization primitives this yields remote code execution on internet-facing servers.'; active_exploitation confirmed, poc_available true, cisa_kev true (2023-07-20); the UK-CAF-B4 gap statement 'hardening of the ColdFusion administrator surface is undermined because the access-control filter itself is bypassable; restricting admin functionality does not stop unauthenticated reach to CFM/CFC endpoints until APSB23-47 is applied'; live_patch_notes recording the APSB23-47 builds and the required ColdFusion service restart.

CVE-2023-36884.name: Microsoft Windows Search Remote Code Execution Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: A spearphished Office document loads a remote payload that abuses the Windows Search (search-ms) handler to bypass Mark-of-the-Web, causing internet-origin content to execute without the protected-view warning and dropping a RomCom/Underground backdoor.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none for authentication, but requires the victim to open the malicious document (user interaction)
attack_vector.complexity: high — a multi-stage MOTW-bypass and exploit chain requiring social engineering, but Storm-0978 operationalized it reliably against high-value targets
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered — found by Microsoft Threat Intelligence during the Storm-0978 investigation. No AI involvement documented.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Apply the Microsoft update once available; in the interim set FEATURE_BLOCK_CROSS_PROTOCOL_FILE_NAVIGATION and enforce Office ASR rules blocking child-process creation and untrusted web content.
prevention.adequacy: Patch was the durable fix but did not exist at disclosure; only application hardening bridged the exploited-in-the-wild window.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Flag Office processes making outbound connections and loading search-ms/HTML resources, plus backdoor beaconing after document open.
detection.adequacy: Detection surfaces the intrusion but only after the MOTW bypass and code execution.

response.what_would_have_worked: Isolate affected hosts, remove the RomCom/Underground implant, and reset credentials on compromised endpoints.
response.adequacy: Response contains the espionage/ransomware follow-on but cannot undo the initial execution.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: SI-2 flaw remediation offered no protection during the zero-day window: Microsoft disclosed CVE-2023-36884 on 2023-07-11 with active Storm-0978 exploitation already underway and initially shipped only mitigation guidance, so there was no patch to apply until later.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: NIS2 Art.21 patch management could not remediate a bug Microsoft left unpatched at disclosure; essential entities had to rely on Office attack-surface-reduction rules, not a fix, during the exploited-in-the-wild period.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: CAF B4 system security assumes MOTW enforces the trust boundary on downloaded files, but this race-condition bypass makes internet-origin Office content execute without the protected-view warning, defeating the control by design.

AU-Essential-8-App-Hardening.gap: Essential Eight application hardening (block macros, disable child-process spawning, restrict Office web content) is the control that actually blunted this chain during the patch gap, yet organizations without those ASR rules had no MOTW fallback once the bypass fired.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: A.8.8 technical-vulnerability management had nothing to action at disclosure because no CVE fix existed; the exposure persisted until Microsoft's later cumulative update despite the vulnerability being tracked and exploited.

new_control_requirements.name: DOWNLOAD-PROVENANCE-ENFORCEMENT
new_control_requirements.description: Provenance enforcement is the control that actually breaks this specific exploit path: the spearphished Office document pulls a remote payload through the Windows Search (search-ms) handler precisely so the file's internet origin stops being visible to the shell and the protected-view warning never fires. For a Windows/Office estate, that means Mark-of-the-Web must be enforced on every file arriving by mail or download and must survive the handoff to a protocol handler, and execution of provenance-stripped shortcuts, installers and script hosts must be blocked outright rather than being allowed on a reputation-service verdict — the exploit's entire purpose is to remove the marking that any reputation or warning decision is keyed on. The binary fix for this CVE ships in the Windows/Office cumulative update and requires a reboot, with no live-patch path, so provenance enforcement is what has to hold the affected hosts through the interval before that reboot lands.
