new_control_requirements.description: Both patch-tracking gaps on this entry describe the same operational failure, and it is an inventory failure rather than an SLA failure: the vulnerable JMX/RMI stack is embedded inside many third-party Java products, operators cannot patch Java independently of each bundling vendor, and per-application patch tracking left hosts running 6u113, 7u99 and 8u77 long past the April 2016 Critical Patch Update, with CISA still listing the flaw as exploited when it added it to KEV on 2023-05-12. So the inventory has to record, for every Java application in the estate, the runtime it actually executes on: the private or bundled JRE shipped inside the product as well as the system-wide installation, plus Java SE Embedded and JRockit R28.3.9 deployments, which are routinely absent from an application-level software list altogether. A product-level inventory cannot answer whether an affected build is present, and that is the specific reason a patch programme scored as compliant kept running affected runtimes for years. Each recorded runtime then carries its own remediation state and its own owner: where the runtime is the operator's, upgrading it and restarting the JVM or application closes it; where the runtime is bundled by a vendor, the operator upgrading the system JRE does not remediate that product, and the entry stays open against the vendor's build. Precondition: this control makes the exposure countable, it does not reduce it. For every runtime the inventory finds that has no vendor build carrying the fix, the reachability restriction on the JMX/RMI port is what bounds the window, and the packet gives a public proof-of-concept and confirmed exploitation, so an entry left open with no dated vendor commitment is an accepted exposure rather than a pending patch.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Packet NIS2-Art21-patch-management gap: 'the vulnerable JMX/RMI stack is embedded inside many third-party Java products; operators cannot patch Java independently of each bundling vendor, so the April 2016 fix reached fielded systems slowly and CISA still listed it as exploited in 2023.' AU-Essential-8-Patch gap: 'because the vulnerable JMX component ships inside diverse Java applications, patch tracking per application meant many hosts ran the affected 6u113/7u99/8u77 builds long past the April 2016 CPU.' active_exploitation_notes: 'because JMX is embedded in many Java middleware products, the same primitive was reused across numerous downstream products' RCE chains'; CISA added it to KEV on 2023-05-12. affected_versions: Oracle Java SE 6u113, 7u99, 8u77; Java SE Embedded 8u77; JRockit R28.3.9. patch_available true, live_patch_available false, poc_available true, active_exploitation confirmed, cvss 9.8, rwep_score 70.

CVE-2016-8735.name: Apache Tomcat Remote Code Execution Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: With JmxRemoteLifecycleListener configured and JMX/RMI ports reachable, an attacker sends a serialized Java gadget-chain object over JMX; the listener's failure to adopt the CVE-2016-3427 credential-type fix causes unsafe deserialization and remote code execution in the Tomcat JVM.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none for the JMX RCE path once the ports are reachable, but exploitation depends on the non-default listener being enabled
attack_vector.complexity: high — requires the specific JMX listener configuration and reachable RMI ports; where those hold, public deserialization tooling makes execution straightforward
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered — identified by the Apache Tomcat project. No AI involvement documented.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Upgrading to a fixed Tomcat release or removing JmxRemoteLifecycleListener; if remote JMX is needed, binding it to localhost and tunneling, and firewalling the RMI ports.
prevention.adequacy: Patch or listener removal is sufficient; disabling the unused feature is the strongest control since it eliminates the surface entirely.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Network monitoring for serialized-object magic bytes on JMX/RMI ports and alerting on Tomcat JVM spawning shell processes.
detection.adequacy: Detection can catch the gadget delivery but is best paired with removing the exposed listener.

response.what_would_have_worked: Rebuilding compromised Tomcat hosts and rotating any credentials or keys the JVM could access.
response.adequacy: Response addresses compromise; it does not prevent the deserialization RCE.

NIST-800-53-CM-7.gap: CM-7 least-functionality would forbid exposing the optional JmxRemoteLifecycleListener and its JMX/RMI ports, but many Tomcat builds enable remote JMX for monitoring; where that non-default surface is left reachable, the deserialization RCE persisted long enough for a 2016 bug to warrant KEV listing in 2023.

NIS2-Art21-network-security.gap: NIS2 network-security expects management interfaces to be segmented, yet JMX/RMI ports are frequently exposed beyond the management VLAN; an attacker reaching them delivers a serialized gadget chain unauthenticated, so boundary controls that overlook JMX leave the RCE open.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: CAF B4 system-security hardening should disable unused listeners, but JmxRemoteLifecycleListener is opt-in for JVM monitoring and easily forgotten; leaving it plus reachable RMI ports means the CVE-2016-3427-derived deserialization flaw executes code despite otherwise-patched Tomcat.

AU-Essential-8-App-Hardening.gap: Essential Eight application-hardening targets removing unneeded features, and remote JMX is exactly such a feature; environments that enabled it for monitoring without restricting the RMI ports remained exploitable, which is why a 2016 flaw returned to KEV in 2023.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.9.gap: A.8.9 configuration management should baseline Tomcat without remote JMX or with tightly scoped access, but drift toward enabling JmxRemoteLifecycleListener for observability reopened the deserialization RCE on servers assumed to be patched.

attack_vector.description: A local attacker with any user context exploits a use-after-free (CWE-416) in the Win32k kernel driver, reclaiming freed window/menu objects to corrupt kernel memory and manipulate a process token, escalating to NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM.
attack_vector.privileges_required: local user (any authenticated account able to run code)
attack_vector.complexity: low — AV:L/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N; public analysis details the UAF reclaim and token-swap steps
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered — reported by Avast from in-the-wild detection. No AI involvement documented.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Installing the May 2023 Windows cumulative update that fixes the Win32k use-after-free.
prevention.adequacy: The patch removes the freed-object reuse; because win32k is reachable from every interactive process, hardening cannot substitute for the fix.

detection.what_would_have_worked: EDR heuristics for token manipulation and unexpected user-to-SYSTEM privilege transitions, plus win32k crash telemetry.
detection.adequacy: Detection can flag the escalation but only after the kernel primitive fires; it does not close the vulnerable code path.

response.what_would_have_worked: Isolating affected hosts and hunting for the initial-access malware the escalation was chained with.
response.adequacy: Response contains follow-on activity but presupposes SYSTEM was already obtained.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: SI-2 flaw remediation on a monthly Patch Tuesday cadence left this Win32k UAF exploitable in the field: it was already under active exploitation when added to KEV on 2023-05-09, so any host not patched immediately hosted a working local-to-SYSTEM primitive.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: NIS2 patch-management timelines presume advance notice, but this zero-day was live at disclosure; an entity on a standard Windows servicing schedule ran an actively-exploited kernel escalation on every endpoint until the May 2023 update reached it.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: CAF B4 system-security hardening cannot mitigate a kernel use-after-free in a core graphics subsystem (win32k) that every interactive Windows process can reach; only the vendor patch removes the freed-object reuse.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Essential Eight 'Patch operating systems' gives 48 hours for actively-exploited critical flaws, but because this was weaponised before disclosure, slower OS-patch SLAs left standard-user machines with a ready SYSTEM-escalation exploit.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: A.8.8 vulnerability management may rank a 7.8 local LPE below network-facing CVEs, yet as a confirmed in-the-wild kernel escalation it warranted out-of-band patching that a CVSS-only prioritisation would defer.

CVE-2023-1389.name: TP-Link Archer AX-21 Command Injection Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: An unauthenticated attacker sends a POST to /cgi-bin/luci;stok=/locale (country write operation); the country parameter is passed to popen() unsanitized, executing injected commands as root.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none (unauthenticated)
attack_vector.complexity: low - single crafted POST; public PoC and botnet modules available
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered - demonstrated at Pwn2Own Toronto 2022. No AI involvement documented.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Applying firmware 1.1.4 Build 20230219+ and disabling remote/WAN management of the router web interface.
prevention.adequacy: Patch removes the popen() injection; restricting management-interface reachability is the compensating control given unauthenticated root access.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Monitoring for the /locale country injection pattern and for routers fetching ELF payloads or launching DDoS traffic.
detection.adequacy: Detects botnet recruitment but does not stop the initial single-request compromise.

response.what_would_have_worked: Factory-reset and reflash of affected routers plus blocking outbound botnet C2.
response.adequacy: Per-device effective but does not scale across a dispersed SOHO fleet.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: SI-2 flaw remediation relies on owners applying firmware 1.1.4 Build 20230219, but consumer routers rarely auto-update, so the root-level popen() injection stayed exploitable across the fleet during the botnet surge that followed the 2023-05-01 KEV listing.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: NIS2 patch-management does not typically inventory employee/home Archer AX21 routers used for remote work, so the unauthenticated command-injection sink escapes the entity's patch cycle while botnets recruit the devices as root.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: CAF B4 hardening assumes the router web-management interface is not exposed and firmware is current, but the vulnerable country parameter is reachable and the popen() call runs as root, so the baseline leaves a preauth root-RCE path open.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Essential 8's internet-facing patch SLA cannot be met on unmanaged home routers, so despite the 8.8 rating and near-1.0 EPSS the popen() injection remains live and continuously exploited.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: A.8.8 technical vulnerability management cannot enumerate SOHO routers outside the asset inventory, so the CWE-77 root command injection on the Archer AX21 is an untracked, actively-exploited exposure.

new_control_requirements.name: PERIMETER-DEVICE-ZERODAY-SLA-TIER
new_control_requirements.description: The TP-Link Archer AX21 (AX1800) is the edge gateway for whatever network sits behind it, and the packet's defect is a pre-auth root remote code execution on that gateway: the country parameter of the write operation on /cgi-bin/luci;stok=/locale is passed to popen() without sanitization, so one unauthenticated POST executes commands as root on the device that is the trust boundary. A remediation tier measured in the weeks a general patch SLA allows does not fit that shape, and the packet says why in its own numbers — confirmed mass exploitation by Mirai variants, Condi and AndroxGh0st recruiting the router as root, a public proof of concept, and EPSS around 0.99999. For this device the control means a distinct tier: firmware 1.1.4 Build 20230219 or later deployed on the clock that opened with the 2023-05-01 KEV listing and its 2023-05-22 due date, or the vulnerable interface isolated until it is. Completion is measured per unit on the firmware version the router reports after it comes back up — live_patch_available is false and the packet records that installing 1.1.4 Build 20230219 reboots the device, so a unit that has taken the image but not restarted onto it is still executing the popen() sink and counts as exposed. Scope from what the packet's affected and affected_versions name: Archer AX21 (AX1800) below firmware 1.1.4 Build 20230219; widen only where a verified source identifies another model carrying the same vulnerable handler. Precondition on the isolation alternative, which is where this control is most often over-claimed: the vulnerable parameter sits on the router's web administration surface, so disabling WAN-side administration bounds who can reach it from the internet — but the packet records exploitation over the adjacent network as well as through an exposed web interface, and every client on the network this router exists to serve reaches that surface from the inside. For a unit serving a general user or household network there is no segment that removes the path, only isolation of that network from anything that matters, so isolation is a holding measure for the window before the firmware lands and not a closure. That is also why the enterprise-side expression of this tier is a reachability and firmware-version question asked of remote-work gateways, not a ticket that closes when a central console reports the push.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Packet: CWE-77, vector states the country parameter of the write operation on the /cgi-bin/luci;stok=/locale endpoint 'was not sanitized before being used in a call to popen(), allowing an unauthenticated attacker to inject commands, which would be run as root, with a simple POST request'. affected_versions: TP-Link Archer AX21 (AX1800) firmware < 1.1.4 Build 20230219. cisa_kev true, kev_date 2023-05-01 with due 2023-05-22; active_exploitation confirmed, active_exploitation_notes record 'mass exploitation by multiple botnets (Mirai variants, Condi, AndroxGh0st) that recruit the router as root; EPSS ~0.99999' and that 'Exploitation over the adjacent/management network or an exposed web interface begins within days of PoC availability'. poc_available true, CVSS 8.8, RWEP 76. patch_available true, patch_required_reboot true, live_patch_available false, live_patch_notes 'No live-patch mechanism for the router firmware; remediation requires installing firmware 1.1.4 Build 20230219 or later, which reboots the device.' The AU-Essential-8-Patch gap records that the internet-facing patch SLA 'cannot be met on unmanaged home routers'; the UK-CAF-B4 gap records that the hardening baseline 'leaves a preauth root-RCE path open'.

new_control_requirements.name: PERIMETER-COMPROMISE-REBUILD-NOT-PATCH
new_control_requirements.description: The outcome the packet records for the Archer AX21 is command execution as root, and confirmed recruitment of the device into botnets — Mirai variants, Condi and AndroxGh0st — at an EPSS of roughly 0.99999. That combination is what makes patch-in-place the wrong default here. Installing firmware 1.1.4 Build 20230219 closes the popen() injection and reboots the unit, but the update is applied on top of a device an attacker held as root: the stored configuration and the administrative credential are carried across the upgrade, and root command execution was sufficient to alter either. For this router the control means a unit whose administration surface was reachable by an untrusted client or from the internet during the exposure window is handled as an incident case rather than a patch ticket — after the firmware update, reset it to factory defaults and rebuild the configuration from a known-good baseline instead of restoring the saved configuration file, set a new administrative credential, and rotate credentials and keys belonging to the network behind it. Preconditions and limits, stated because this control is the half that is easy to overstate: it does not close the injection — the firmware level and the reboot do that, and a rebuilt unit still running a pre-1.1.4 image is fully exploitable again on the next request. It applies to units that were exposed; a unit whose administration surface was never reachable by an untrusted party during the window is an ordinary patch item, and the packet gives no basis for treating every Archer AX21 as compromised. And a factory reset recovers nothing already exfiltrated and closes no session already intercepted, which is why the credential rotation rather than the reset is the load-bearing step. Scope to the model the packet names, Archer AX21 (AX1800) below firmware 1.1.4 Build 20230219, and widen only where a verified source identifies another model carrying the same handler.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Packet: attack_vector 'An unauthenticated attacker sends a POST to /cgi-bin/luci;stok=/locale (country write operation); the country parameter is passed to popen() unsanitized, executing injected commands as root.' active_exploitation confirmed; active_exploitation_notes record 'Confirmed mass exploitation by multiple botnets (Mirai variants, Condi, AndroxGh0st) that recruit the router as root; EPSS ~0.99999 reflects near-certain ongoing exploitation.' poc_available true. patch_available true with live_patch_available false and live_patch_notes 'remediation requires installing firmware 1.1.4 Build 20230219 or later, which reboots the device'. The NIST-800-53-SI-2 gap records that the injection 'stayed exploitable across the fleet during the botnet surge that followed the 2023-05-01 KEV listing' — the population this control addresses. RWEP 76, CVSS 8.8, kev_date 2023-05-01.

CVE-2021-45046.name: Apache Log4j2 Deserialization of Untrusted Data Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: With a non-default PatternLayout using a Context Lookup or Thread Context Map pattern, attacker-controlled data placed in the MDC is evaluated as a ${jndi:...} lookup, triggering an outbound JNDI request and remote class load for code execution.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none (attacker controls a logged input that reaches the Thread Context Map)
attack_vector.complexity: high per CVSS (requires a non-default logging configuration) but trivially weaponized where that configuration exists
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered — found by the Apache Logging community/researchers. No AI involvement documented.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Upgrading to Log4j 2.16.0/2.12.2 (which removes message lookups and disables JNDI by default); interim removal of the JndiLookup class and egress filtering of LDAP/RMI.
prevention.adequacy: The 2.16.0/2.12.2 upgrade is definitive; the 2.15.0 patch was insufficient, so only the second upgrade closes it.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alerting on ${jndi:} strings in inputs and on outbound LDAP/RMI/DNS from application servers.
detection.adequacy: Useful but noisy amid mass internet-wide scanning; catches attempts more than confirms success.

response.what_would_have_worked: Hunt for post-exploitation web shells, miners, or ransomware staging; rotate secrets reachable from any compromised host.
response.adequacy: Necessary given the ransomware association; patching alone does not evict an established foothold.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: SI-2 flaw remediation could not act on CVE-2021-45046 quickly because operators first had to locate every application bundling a vulnerable Log4j 2.x; the fix (2.16.0/2.12.2) also superseded an already-shipped 2.15.0 patch, forcing a second remediation pass a routine SLA does not anticipate.

NIS2-Art21-supply-chain.gap: NIS2 Art.21 supply-chain security assumes visibility into third-party components, but Log4j is a deeply transitive dependency most operators did not know they ran, so the vulnerable code sat inside packaged products long after the 2021 disclosure and the 2023-05-01 KEV listing.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: CAF B4 secure-configuration expects logging to be inert, yet under a non-default PatternLayout with a Context/Thread Context lookup, log data itself became an RCE sink; B4 baselines rarely audit logging-pattern configuration for this exposure.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Essential Eight patch-applications assumes a discrete application to patch, but Log4j 2.15.0 was an incomplete fix requiring re-patching to 2.16.0/2.12.2 across every embedding product, so a single patch pass left many systems exploitable.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: A.8.8 technical-vulnerability management relies on an accurate component inventory (SBOM); without one, organizations could not enumerate where the vulnerable Log4j library ran, leaving a ransomware-associated RCE unremediated well past the KEV due date.

new_control_requirements.name: INCOMPLETE-PATCH-SEQUENCE-SEVERITY-MULTIPLIER
new_control_requirements.description: This CVE exists because a prior remediation was incomplete: the packet's vector states the fix that addressed CVE-2021-44228 in Log4j 2.15.0 was incomplete in certain non-default configurations, leaving the same JNDI-lookup primitive reachable through attacker-controlled Thread Context Map data. That makes the operator's problem a records problem as much as a code problem — the version move to 2.15.0 is already closed on the flaw-remediation ledger, so the follow-on step reads as a routine minor bump rather than as an unremediated actively-exploited flaw. Applied to this CVE, an application on 2.15.0 must be scored as unremediated for this primitive and driven to 2.16.0 (Java 8) or 2.12.2 (Java 7) with the affected Java application restarted, on the clock that opened with the 2023-05-01 KEV listing. The sequence position also sets the standard for what counts as a fix: the packet credits the fixed releases with removing support for message lookup patterns and disabling JNDI functionality by default — a capability removal — so a narrower fix on this same primitive should be treated as provisionally incomplete until the capability-removing version is in service. Distinguishing test: pull the remediation evidence for this CVE and check what it points at; if it points at the December 2021 Log4Shell response rather than at a per-application version reading of 2.16.0 or 2.12.2 on the runtime classpath, the attestation is recording the first CVE's closure as this one's.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Packet vector: the fix to address CVE-2021-44228 in Apache Log4j 2.15.0 was incomplete in certain non-default configurations, allowing attackers with control over Thread Context Map (MDC) input data to craft a JNDI Lookup pattern; the packet states Log4j 2.16.0 (Java 8) and 2.12.2 (Java 7) fix the issue by removing support for message lookup patterns and disabling JNDI functionality by default. live_patch_notes: remediation requires upgrading Log4j to 2.16.0 (Java 8) or 2.12.2 (Java 7) and restarting the affected Java application. CISA KEV-listed 2023-05-01, active_exploitation confirmed, PoC available, CVSS 9.0, RWEP 74, patch_available true, live_patch_available false.

new_control_requirements.name: MITIGATION-ACTIVE-PATCH-PENDING-VERDICT-CLASS
new_control_requirements.description: The packet itself separates the two states this control requires an audit to distinguish: removing the JndiLookup class from the classpath is recorded as a stopgap mitigation, not a vendor live-patch, while remediation is upgrading to 2.16.0 (Java 8) or 2.12.2 (Java 7) and restarting the affected Java application. Applied to this estate, every Java application carrying Log4j needs an explicit verdict of (a) fixed version resolved on the runtime classpath and the application restarted, (b) still on an affected version with the JndiLookup class stripped, or (c) neither — and (b) has to appear as a time-bound compensating-control state with a dated action item, never as a patched-per-SLA outcome. Preconditions on (b), which are the reason it cannot be recorded as closure: the stopgap holds only while that class stays absent from the artifact, so a redeploy, a dependency re-resolution, a rollback to an earlier build, or a restore that reinstates the original library returns the application to full exposure silently, and the removal is applied per artifact rather than centrally, so it has to be re-verified on every build rather than once. It also leaves the affected version in place, so the capability changes the packet credits the fixed releases with — removal of message lookup patterns and JNDI disabled by default — are not in effect for anything else that reaches the same code. And because the fix takes effect only on restart, an application whose dependency was upgraded but whose process has not been restarted is still state (c) dressed as state (a). Distinguishing test: for each application recorded in state (b), rebuild it from its own pipeline and inspect the produced artifact for the JndiLookup class; if it comes back, the mitigation was a one-off edit to a deployed artifact and the next deployment reopens the flaw.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Packet live_patch_notes: 'No live-patch mechanism; remediation requires upgrading Log4j to 2.16.0 (Java 8) or 2.12.2 (Java 7) and restarting the affected Java application. The stopgap of removing the JndiLookup class from the classpath is a mitigation, not a vendor live-patch.' patch_available true, live_patch_available false. Packet vector states the fixed releases remove support for message lookup patterns and disable JNDI functionality by default. CISA KEV-listed 2023-05-01, active_exploitation confirmed, PoC available, CVSS 9.0, RWEP 74.

new_control_requirements.name: TIER-3-DEPENDENCY-INVENTORY
new_control_requirements.description: Log4j is not an installed product on this estate but a library reached through Java applications — the packet's remediation is expressed per application (upgrade Log4j and restart the affected Java application), so how much of the estate is remediated is exactly how much of it the dependency inventory can see. Applied to this CVE, the inventory has to record per application: the Log4j version actually resolved onto the runtime classpath rather than only the version named as a direct dependency; the Java track, because the packet gives different fixed releases for Java 8 (2.16.0) and Java 7 (2.12.2), so a single target version applied estate-wide leaves one track wrong; and whether the logging configuration uses a non-default PatternLayout with a Context Lookup or a Thread Context Map pattern (%X, %mdc, %MDC), which the packet gives as the condition under which attacker-controlled MDC data reaches the JNDI lookup. That last item is a configuration property rather than a code property, so an application marked not-exploitable on configuration grounds is re-exposed the moment someone adds a correlation-id pattern to a log format, with no dependency change to trigger a re-scan — it has to be re-checked on logging-configuration change, not only on dependency change. Distinguishing test: take applications whose declared direct dependencies name no Log4j at all and enumerate their resolved runtime classpath; an inventory built from declared direct dependencies reports full coverage while transitively-included copies sit on an affected version.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Packet live_patch_notes: remediation requires upgrading Log4j to 2.16.0 (Java 8) or 2.12.2 (Java 7) and restarting the affected Java application — two fixed releases on two Java tracks, applied per application. Packet vector conditions exploitation on a non-default Pattern Layout with either a Context Lookup (for example, $${ctx:loginId}) or a Thread Context Map pattern (%X, %mdc, or %MDC) plus attacker control over MDC input data. The entry cites NIS2 Art. 21 supply-chain security measures as a framework gap. CISA KEV-listed 2023-05-01, active_exploitation confirmed, PoC available, CVSS 9.0, RWEP 74.

attack_vector.description: Over T3/IIOP an unauthenticated attacker binds a JNDI reference so a subsequent lookup makes WebLogic fetch and execute a remote class from an attacker LDAP/RMI server, achieving RCE.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none (unauthenticated) with network access to the T3/IIOP ports
attack_vector.complexity: low — public PoCs automate the JNDI bind/lookup against exposed WebLogic
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered — reported through Oracle's security program. No AI involvement documented.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Applying the January 2023 CPU and firewalling the T3/IIOP ports so they are never reachable from untrusted networks.
prevention.adequacy: Patch closes the flaw; restricting T3/IIOP is essential defense-in-depth because those protocols are the exposed attack channel.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Egress monitoring for WebLogic making outbound LDAP/RMI class-load fetches and IDS signatures for JNDI references in T3/IIOP traffic.
detection.adequacy: Effective as a tripwire but reactive; the class-load fetch already indicates active exploitation.

response.what_would_have_worked: Isolate the server, hunt for dropped miners/web shells, and rebuild if code execution is confirmed.
response.adequacy: Necessary because RCE on an app server invites persistence that patching afterward does not remove.

NIST-800-53-SC-7.gap: SC-7 boundary protection should have blocked the T3/IIOP naming ports from the internet, but WebLogic frequently exposes them by default; leaving IIOP/T3 reachable is exactly what makes CVE-2023-21839's remote class-load possible pre-auth, and a perimeter that only guards HTTP misses it.

NIS2-Art21-network-security.gap: NIS2 Art.21 network-security measures rarely restrict the proprietary T3/IIOP channels, so the JNDI-injection vector stays exposed even where HTTP is fronted by a WAF; the mass-exploitation after the 2023-05-01 KEV listing rode those unfiltered management protocols.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: CAF B4 secure-configuration assurance assumes application-server management protocols are internal, but internet-exposed T3/IIOP let an unauthenticated attacker drive a remote class-load; B4 baselines that harden HTTP endpoints do not close the IIOP naming service this CVE abuses.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Essential Eight patch-applications targets a 48-hour window for exploited internet-facing services, yet the January 2023 CPU shipped and public PoCs followed quickly; WebLogic estates that missed that window were mass-exploited around the KEV 2023-05-01 date.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.22.gap: A.8.22 network segregation would have isolated the WebLogic T3/IIOP ports from untrusted networks, but many deployments expose them flat; without segregation the unauthenticated JNDI class-load reaches the server, which A.8.8 patching alone would not prevent for unpatched hosts.

attack_vector.description: An unauthenticated attacker sends a POST to /minio/bootstrap/v1/verify on a distributed MinIO node; the endpoint returns all process environment variables including MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD and MINIO_SECRET_KEY, which the attacker uses to authenticate as admin and (via mc admin update) push a malicious binary for code execution.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none (unauthenticated network request to a distributed MinIO node)
attack_vector.complexity: low — a single unauthenticated POST; public PoC and a Metasploit module exist
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered — disclosed through a vendor GitHub Security Advisory. No AI involvement documented.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Upgrading to the fixed MinIO release and rotating the exposed root/secret keys.
prevention.adequacy: The upgrade fixes the endpoint, but any credentials already harvested remain valid until rotated, so patch alone is insufficient.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alerting on requests to /minio/bootstrap/v1/verify and on admin logins from new source IPs.
detection.adequacy: Detection can catch the disclosure request, but the follow-on admin action is indistinguishable from legitimate use once credentials leak.

response.what_would_have_worked: Rotate the root/secret keys and audit for maliciously pushed binaries after any bootstrap-verify hit.
response.adequacy: Response contains the incident but the Evil_MinIO backdoor may already have executed on the nodes.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: SI-2 patch cadence assumes days-to-weeks, but MinIO was mass-exploited within days of the 2023-03-20 fix and the KEV due date (2023-05-12) fell after the credential-harvesting wave; flaw remediation on this timeline could not outrun the scanning.

NIS2-Art21-vulnerability-management.gap: Vulnerability management must catch the unauthenticated bootstrap endpoint, yet internet-facing MinIO clusters returning environment secrets pre-auth were not flagged until KEV listing, and the days-long exploitation window outpaced typical scan cycles.

UK-CAF-B2.gap: B2 identity and access control assumes secrets are not recoverable pre-auth; once /minio/bootstrap/v1/verify discloses MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD, the credential-based access model collapses and the attacker holds full admin.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: The Essential Eight patch window did not close before the mass-exploitation wave; unpatched MinIO in dev/test clusters leaked root credentials that were then reused against production storage.

ISO-27001-2022-A.5.15.gap: A.5.15 access-control policy is defeated at the root: MinIO discloses the root credential itself pre-auth, so any access-control matrix built on that secret is bypassed the moment the bootstrap endpoint is queried.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: MinIO's remediation has three parts and only one of them is a patch, which is why a version-only SLA closes this ticket while the cluster stays owned. The packet's fixed release stops /minio/bootstrap/v1/verify returning process environment variables, but MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD and MINIO_SECRET_KEY left the process before the upgrade and remain valid after it -- an attacker who read them authenticates as admin against the patched build exactly as they did against the vulnerable one. For this deployment the mitigation the SLA measures is all three of the packet's steps: the upgrade to RELEASE.2023-03-20T20-16-18Z or later, rotation of the exposed MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD and MINIO_SECRET_KEY, and the service restart that puts the rotated values into the running process. The packet records no live-patch path, so that restart is unavoidable and every node takes it. Scope is the whole cluster rather than a representative node: the packet states the flaw affects cluster deployments and that all users of distributed deployment are impacted, and the disclosure endpoint answers per node, so a rolling upgrade that leaves one node on an affected release leaves the disclosure reachable and the rotation pointless. Distinguishing test: after the upgrade, POST to /minio/bootstrap/v1/verify on each node and confirm no environment content is returned, and separately confirm the pre-incident root credential no longer authenticates -- a flaw-remediation attestation that records the release string and stops there marks the cluster compliant while the leaked credential still works.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Packet: cisa_kev true, kev_date 2023-04-21, active_exploitation 'confirmed', poc_available true, rwep_score 66, cvss 7.5. patch_available true, live_patch_available false, live_patch_notes: 'No vendor live-patch; remediation requires upgrading to MinIO RELEASE.2023-03-20T20-16-18Z or later, rotating the exposed MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD / MINIO_SECRET_KEY, and restarting the service.' vector: 'In a cluster deployment starting with RELEASE.2019-12-17T23-16-33Z and prior to RELEASE.2023-03-20T20-16-18Z, MinIO returns all environment variables, including MINIO_SECRET_KEY and MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD... All users of distributed deployment are impacted.' attack_vector places the disclosure at an unauthenticated POST to /minio/bootstrap/v1/verify on a distributed MinIO node.

new_control_requirements.name: ENDPOINT-MGMT-DEPLOYMENT-CHANNEL-INTEGRITY
new_control_requirements.description: The packet's chain does not end at disclosure. With MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD in hand the attacker authenticates as admin and uses mc admin update to push a malicious binary, so MinIO's administrative API is a code-distribution channel for the server binary itself and a single disclosed credential is the whole gate on it. Treat it as that rather than as storage administration: file-integrity-monitor the MinIO binary and the service configuration on every node of the distributed deployment, alert on any replacement that does not correspond to a sanctioned operator action or a vendor upgrade, and restrict which identities may invoke the administrative update path at all. This is the half that still has value after the fixed release lands, because the upgrade closes the environment-variable disclosure but removes nothing that was pushed through the update path while the credential was exposed -- a node reachable during the exposure window has to be compared against a known-good binary rather than closed on its version string. It is also precisely what the access-control gaps recorded against this entry miss: an attestation that MinIO's admin accounts are controlled examines who is issued the root credential, not that holding it confers replacement of the running server, and rotating the credential afterwards does not evict a binary already installed. Precondition: integrity monitoring detects the substitution, it does not prevent it, and it is worth nothing on a node whose baseline was taken after the deployment was already exposed -- there the attacker's binary is what gets recorded as normal, and the comparison has to be against vendor-published artifacts rather than against the node's own history.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Packet attack_vector: the disclosed MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD and MINIO_SECRET_KEY are what 'the attacker uses to authenticate as admin and (via mc admin update) push a malicious binary for code execution.' live_patch_notes records remediation as the upgrade plus rotation of MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD / MINIO_SECRET_KEY plus a service restart -- none of which reverses a binary already pushed. active_exploitation 'confirmed' with poc_available true and kev_date 2023-04-21. Citing gaps include UK-CAF-B2 (Identity and access control) and ISO-27001-2022-A.5.15 (Access control).

CVE-2023-27350.name: PaperCut MF/NG Improper Access Control Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: An unauthenticated attacker reaches the SetupCompleted setup-wizard page due to improper access control, obtaining an authenticated admin session, then uses PaperCut's built-in print/device scripting to execute arbitrary OS commands as SYSTEM.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none (unauthenticated)
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L, reachable over the network with a public PoC/Metasploit module
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered — reported via Trend Micro ZDI and fixed by PaperCut. No AI involvement documented.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Upgrade to PaperCut 20.1.7 / 21.2.11 / 22.0.9, and (interim) restrict the admin interface to trusted networks and remove the server from direct internet exposure.
prevention.adequacy: Patching closes the auth bypass; because exploitation was near-immediate, network isolation was the critical stopgap for un-patched servers.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alerting on requests to SetupCompleted and on the PaperCut service process spawning cmd.exe/powershell.exe.
detection.adequacy: Process-lineage detection reliably catches the SYSTEM command execution stage.

response.what_would_have_worked: Assume compromise for internet-exposed instances, isolate the host, hunt for ransomware staging and secondary tooling, and rebuild.
response.adequacy: Response is essential given confirmed ransomware use following the RCE.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: SI-2's remediation window was outpaced by mass exploitation: PaperCut servers were compromised within days of the 2023-03 fix, so organisations that patched on a normal monthly SI-2 cadence were breached before they applied 20.1.7/21.2.11/22.0.9.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: NIS2 patch-management does not treat an internet-facing print server as critical infrastructure, yet CVE-2023-27350 gave SYSTEM-level RCE on exactly those overlooked boxes, so its risk-based patch prioritisation deprioritised the very asset ransomware crews targeted.

UK-CAF-B2.gap: CAF B2 identity-and-access-control presumes the admin console enforces authentication, but the SetupCompleted access-control flaw lets an unauthenticated user reach admin functions, so B2's privileged-account controls never engage before code execution.

AU-Essential-8-App-Hardening.gap: Essential 8 application-hardening does not contemplate disabling PaperCut's legitimate print/device-scripting feature, which is the exact primitive the exploit abuses to run commands as SYSTEM after the auth bypass — a built-in capability, not malware, so allow-listing/hardening leaves it enabled.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: A.8.8 technical-vulnerability management would rank this critical, but print-management servers are frequently absent from the asset register and internet-exposed on 9191/9192, so the control never scheduled the urgent patch that mass ransomware exploitation demanded.

new_control_requirements.name: ENTERPRISE-ERP-MANAGEMENT-FUNCTION-AUTHENTICATION
new_control_requirements.description: The SetupCompleted class is where PaperCut MF/NG makes its access-control decision on this CVE, and the packet is that decision failing open: a remote unauthenticated attacker reaches the setup-wizard page through it and comes out holding an authenticated administrative session. Bound to this product, the control means each administrative function on the PaperCut application server authorizes its own caller rather than inheriting a verdict from a setup-state check that fronts it, and the administrative surface — the packet records these servers internet-exposed on 9191/9192 — answers only from a segment with an operational need to administer printing. The identity-and-access control cited as insufficient on this entry is never consulted: the attacker authenticates as no PaperCut operator, so per-account privilege scoping is bypassed rather than abused, and an attestation that every PaperCut administrator authenticates at login passes cleanly while this path stays open. Distinguishing test: from a segment with no print-administration role, issue unauthenticated requests to each administrative endpoint on a staging PaperCut instance and confirm each is refused before the function runs. Precondition: the endpoint-side authorization is a property the vendor upgrade to 20.1.7, 21.2.11 or 22.0.9 (or later) establishes — this control states what to verify, it does not implement it. Restricting admin-interface network access is the packet's documented interim mitigation and it bounds who can present the request, but it leaves the bypass fully exploitable to anything inside the permitted segment and is unavailable where the console must stay broadly reachable. patch_required_reboot is false, which means no host reboot is needed, not that the fix takes effect on an already-running service: the packet describes a service upgrade, so measure completion by the version the running PaperCut service reports, not by the installer having been run.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Packet fields for this entry: vector — 'The specific flaw exists within the SetupCompleted class. The issue results from improper access control. An attacker can leverage this vulnerability to bypass authentication and execute arbitrary code in the context of SYSTEM. Was ZDI-CAN-18987'; attack_vector describing the unauthenticated attacker reaching the SetupCompleted setup-wizard page and obtaining an authenticated admin session; affected_versions '< 20.1.7', '21.x < 21.2.11', '22.x < 22.0.9'; patch_required_reboot false; live_patch_notes 'remediation is upgrading PaperCut MF/NG to 20.1.7, 21.2.11, or 22.0.9 (or later), a service upgrade rather than a host reboot; restricting admin-interface network access is a documented interim mitigation'. The UK-CAF-B2 gap records that the control 'presumes the admin console enforces authentication... so B2's privileged-account controls never engage before code execution'; the ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8 gap records these servers 'internet-exposed on 9191/9192'.

new_control_requirements.name: CONTROL-PANEL-PLUGIN-USER-SURFACE-MUST-NOT-REACH-ROOT-OPERATIONS
new_control_requirements.description: PaperCut's built-in print/device scripting is the constrained user surface this control governs, and on this CVE it is the second half of the chain: the packet does not stop at the authentication bypass — having obtained an administrative session, the attacker uses the product's own scripting capability to execute arbitrary OS commands as SYSTEM. That is an administrative console feature wired directly to a SYSTEM-level operation, which is the pattern the control forbids. Applied to this product it means the command-executing operations sit behind their own authorization boundary that the console can only reach through a constrained, validated interface, so that obtaining an admin session is not the same as obtaining SYSTEM; and operationally, that the scripting capability is enabled only on servers whose printing workflow genuinely requires it. The application-hardening control cited on this entry cannot reach this: the primitive is a legitimate shipped product feature rather than malware, a macro or a browser plugin, so allow-listing and hardening leave it enabled by design. Precondition, and it is a severe one here: by the time the scripting feature is invoked the attacker already holds an administrative session, so a configuration toggle is within their reach to reverse — disabling the feature raises the cost of the SYSTEM step but does not close it, and it gives nothing at all on a server already compromised, which for this CVE is a live possibility rather than a hypothetical given the packet's record of mass exploitation within weeks by Cl0p and LockBit ransomware affiliates and the Bl00dy gang. The closure is the vendor upgrade plus restricting which networks can reach the console; this control names the architectural property the product was missing and the interim reduction, not a substitute for either.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Packet fields for this entry: attack_vector — the attacker 'obtain[s] an authenticated admin session, then uses PaperCut's built-in print/device scripting to execute arbitrary OS commands as SYSTEM'; vector recording code execution 'in the context of SYSTEM'; active_exploitation_notes 'Mass-exploited within weeks of disclosure; used by Cl0p and LockBit ransomware affiliates and the Bl00dy gang, plus nation-state activity'. The AU-Essential-8-App-Hardening gap records that hardening 'does not contemplate disabling PaperCut's legitimate print/device-scripting feature, which is the exact primitive the exploit abuses to run commands as SYSTEM after the auth bypass — a built-in capability, not malware, so allow-listing/hardening leaves it enabled'.

new_control_requirements.name: PERIMETER-COMPROMISE-REBUILD-NOT-PATCH
new_control_requirements.description: This is the internet-facing pre-auth-RCE-under-active-exploitation case the control exists for, arriving on a print server rather than a firewall: the packet has PaperCut MF/NG servers exposed on 9191/9192 taking unauthenticated code execution as SYSTEM, mass-exploited within weeks of disclosure by Cl0p and LockBit ransomware affiliates, the Bl00dy gang and nation-state activity, KEV-listed 2023-04-21 with ransomware use recorded as Known. The requirement for this product is that the default incident response for any PaperCut server that was reachable during that window is configuration capture, rebuild and credential rotation — the print-system service account, the administrative credentials the bypass hands over, and any credential the server held or that transited it — rather than upgrading in place to 20.1.7/21.2.11/22.0.9 and closing the remediation ticket. This is precisely the shape of the flaw-remediation gap recorded on this entry: the packet states that organisations patching on a normal monthly cadence were breached before they applied the fix, so for those servers 'patched' and 'not compromised' are two different findings, and because the primitive is code execution as SYSTEM, nothing the upgrade performs removes what was installed beforehand. Precondition: the upgrade here is a service upgrade rather than a host reboot, which makes patch-in-place cheap and fast — that low cost is exactly what makes it the reflexive default that skips the compromise assessment, so the rebuild decision has to be taken deliberately and written into the runbook in advance rather than weighed per incident.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Packet fields for this entry: cisa_kev true with kev_date 2023-04-21; active_exploitation 'confirmed'; active_exploitation_notes 'Mass-exploited within weeks of disclosure; used by Cl0p and LockBit ransomware affiliates and the Bl00dy gang, plus nation-state activity. KEV-listed 2023-04-21 with ransomware use recorded (Known). Preauth RCE as SYSTEM on internet-exposed print servers'; poc_available true; patch_required_reboot false with live_patch_notes describing 'a service upgrade rather than a host reboot'. The NIST-800-53-SI-2 gap records 'PaperCut servers were compromised within days of the 2023-03 fix, so organisations that patched on a normal monthly SI-2 cadence were breached before they applied 20.1.7/21.2.11/22.0.9'; the ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8 gap records these servers internet-exposed on 9191/9192.

CVE-2023-2136.name: Google Chrome Skia Integer Overflow Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: From a renderer process the attacker already controls, a crafted HTML page drives an integer overflow in Skia that corrupts memory to break out of the Chrome sandbox and execute in the higher-privileged browser process.
attack_vector.privileges_required: requires prior control of the renderer process (chained); no user authentication
attack_vector.complexity: the overflow itself is low-complexity, but exploitation requires an initial renderer compromise first, making the overall chain high-complexity
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered — reported by Google's Threat Analysis Group. No AI involvement documented.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Updating Chrome to 112.0.5615.137 and ensuring the paired renderer bugs are also patched
prevention.adequacy: The patch removes the overflow; because it is a chain stage, defenders must also close the renderer-compromise bug it is paired with.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Endpoint telemetry for Chrome child-process anomalies and sandbox-escape indicators
detection.adequacy: Sandbox-escape behavior is hard to distinguish from normal browser activity without dedicated browser-exploit telemetry.

response.what_would_have_worked: Investigating for targeted-implant delivery on endpoints that ran vulnerable Chrome
response.adequacy: Because the escape typically delivers an implant, response should assume host-level compromise on exploited endpoints.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: SI-2 could not pre-empt a zero-day; the Skia overflow was exploited before the 2023-04-18 fix, and endpoint browser patch-rollout speed determined how long the sandbox-escape stage stayed usable after the 2023-04-21 KEV listing.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: Browser fleets under NIS2 patch-management must auto-update to close a zero-day sandbox escape; any lag in Chrome update deployment left the renderer-to-host escape available to the targeted chains that used it.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: CAF B4 leans on the browser sandbox as a containment boundary; this integer overflow in Skia breaks out of that sandbox from a compromised renderer, so the containment control system-security guidance assumes failed.

AU-Essential-8-App-Hardening.gap: Essential Eight application hardening relies on the browser sandbox to contain web-content exploits; a Skia sandbox escape defeats that containment, and hardening options do not disable the vulnerable 2D-rendering path.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: A.8.8 technical vulnerability management could only react — the sandbox escape was a zero-day, so remediation depended on rapidly deploying Chrome 112.0.5615.137 across all managed endpoints.

new_control_requirements.name: BROWSER-MANAGED-UPDATE-NO-DEFERRAL
new_control_requirements.description: The packet gives a fixed build — Chrome/Chromium 112.0.5615.137 — and a KEV-listed sandbox escape under confirmed exploitation, which is the case a staged enterprise update ring is worst at: the ring exists to soak a release across a validation window, and the window is the exposure. For this CVE the control means the security-channel update to 112.0.5615.137 or later is pushed to every managed Chrome/Chromium install on the clock that opened with the 2023-04-21 KEV listing, with user deferral disabled, and completion measured by the build each browser instance is actually running rather than by the version approved or staged in the management console; the packet records no live-patch mechanism, so an instance still executing a pre-112.0.5615.137 build carries the vulnerable Skia even once the newer build is on disk. This is also the control that carries the exposure the user-application-hardening gap cited on this entry cannot: hardening settings govern what content the renderer is allowed to process, whereas the packet places this defect at the step after that — reached from a renderer the attacker already controls — so no hardening setting narrows the Skia integer overflow, and a hardening attestation passes cleanly while the escape stays available. Priority follows the packet rather than the absence of a public exploit: no PoC is recorded, but exploitation is confirmed, so waiting for a public PoC to raise the priority inverts the evidence. Precondition: this reaches only installs the browser update channel manages; a Chromium build shipped inside another product does not take the Chrome update and is not covered here — it belongs to the embedded-component inventory and parity requirement instead.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Packet vector: 'Integer overflow in Skia in Google Chrome prior to 112.0.5615.137 allowed a remote attacker who had compromised the renderer process to potentially perform a sandbox escape via a crafted HTML page.' attack_vector: from a renderer process the attacker already controls, the crafted page drives the overflow to break out of the sandbox and execute in the higher-privileged browser process. live_patch_notes: no live-patch mechanism; remediation requires updating Chrome/Chromium to 112.0.5615.137 or later. CISA KEV-listed 2023-04-21, active_exploitation confirmed, poc_available false, patch_available true, live_patch_available false, CVSS 9.6, RWEP 45. The entry cites ASD Essential Eight user application hardening as a framework gap.

new_control_requirements.name: EMBEDDED-MEDIA-PARSER-LIBRARY-INVENTORY-AND-PATCH-PARITY
new_control_requirements.description: The packet puts the defect in Skia — an embedded rendering component, not a separately installed product — and states remediation as two distinct actions: update Chrome/Chromium to 112.0.5615.137 or later, and rebuild the downstream products that embed the affected Skia, which it names as ChromeOS, Android and Flutter. Those are separate update tracks, so an attestation built on the browser fleet closes only the first action while shipped copies of the same vulnerable code stay in service. Applied here, the control means enumerating, alongside managed Chrome installs, the packet-named downstream products actually in service — ChromeOS devices, Android builds, and applications built with Flutter — and confirming each is on a build produced after the Skia fix, since each carries its own copy that the Chrome update never touches. Scope it to those products: the packet ties the affected Skia to Chrome/Chromium and to ChromeOS, Android and Flutter and provides no mapping into other software embedding Skia, so instructing operators to treat every graphics-rendering binary in the estate as an instance of this CVE manufactures rebuild and removal work against products no evidence here implicates; widen only where a verified source names another product carrying the affected component. Distinguishing test: after the Chrome fleet reports 112.0.5615.137, take one in-service Flutter-built application and one Android or ChromeOS image and show each was produced after the Skia fix — an estate whose flaw-remediation evidence is the browser inventory alone reads clean while shipped software still embeds the vulnerable code. Precondition: rebuilding is available only for products the operator builds, or for which a fixed build can be obtained; a downstream product whose supplier ships no rebuilt version is not remediated by this control and stays on the exposure register rather than being closed by it.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Packet live_patch_notes: 'No live-patch mechanism; remediation requires updating Chrome/Chromium to 112.0.5615.137 or later and rebuilding downstream products (ChromeOS, Android, Flutter) that embed the affected Skia.' Packet vector places the integer overflow in Skia in Google Chrome prior to 112.0.5615.137, reachable via a crafted HTML page from a compromised renderer process to escape the sandbox. CISA KEV-listed 2023-04-21, active_exploitation confirmed, poc_available false, patch_available true, live_patch_available false, CVSS 9.6, RWEP 45.

CVE-2017-6742.name: Cisco IOS and IOS XE Software SNMP Remote Code Execution Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: An attacker who holds a valid SNMP read-only community string (v1/v2c) or SNMPv3 credentials sends a crafted SNMP packet to a vulnerable OID, triggering a buffer overflow in the IOS/IOS XE SNMP subsystem to execute code or reload the router; APT28 used it to inject the in-memory Jaguar Tooth implant.
attack_vector.privileges_required: authenticated to SNMP — but community strings are frequently weak defaults ('public'), effectively lowering the bar for internet-facing routers
attack_vector.complexity: low — once a valid community string is known or guessed, a single crafted SNMP packet triggers the overflow
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered — disclosed by Cisco and later weaponized by APT28 per CISA AA23-108. No AI involvement documented.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Upgrading to the Cisco fixed release, restricting SNMP to a trusted management plane, disabling affected MIBs/OIDs, and replacing default/weak community strings with SNMPv3 and strong credentials.
prevention.adequacy: The patch is required; SNMP access restriction and SNMPv3 hardening are strong compensating controls that also remove the credential-guessing entry point.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Monitoring for SNMP scanning with default community strings, crafted SNMP packets to sensitive OIDs, and router memory/behavior anomalies consistent with an in-memory implant.
detection.adequacy: Detection is difficult because Jaguar Tooth is memory-resident; NetFlow and SNMP-access logging help but do not prevent exploitation.

response.what_would_have_worked: Rebooting to clear the in-memory implant only after patching, rotating SNMP and device credentials, and forensically validating router firmware integrity.
response.adequacy: Response can remove the memory-resident implant but must be paired with the patch, or the router is immediately re-exploitable.

NIST-800-53-CM-7.gap: CM-7 least functionality should disable or tightly restrict SNMP, but routers commonly leave SNMP v1/v2c enabled with default community strings; that exposed, low-privilege-gated service is exactly what APT28 abused to reach the vulnerable OID, so failing to minimize SNMP exposure left the overflow reachable long after the June 2017 fix.

NIS2-Art21-network-security.gap: NIS2 Art.21 network-security requires protecting management protocols, yet SNMP was reachable from untrusted networks with guessable community strings; restricting SNMP to a management plane and enforcing SNMPv3 with strong credentials was the missing control that would have blocked the crafted-packet path used to plant Jaguar Tooth.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: CAF B4 system-security hardening of network devices is undermined because the SNMP subsystem overflow gives code execution on the router itself; without the Cisco fixed release and hardened SNMP configuration, device hardening does not stop an attacker holding a weak community string.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Essential Eight patching applies to network infrastructure firmware that is often left on multi-year-old IOS images; the 2023 APT28 campaign exploited routers still unpatched six years after the 2017 fix, showing the patch control fails where network-device firmware is treated as set-and-forget.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: A.8.8 technical-vulnerability management frequently omits network-device firmware from the vulnerability program; organizations without an inventory of IOS/IOS XE SNMP exposure could not identify or remediate the vulnerable routers before state-sponsored exploitation.

new_control_requirements.name: PERIMETER-COMPROMISE-REBUILD-NOT-PATCH
new_control_requirements.description: Bound to a Cisco IOS / IOS XE device that was SNMP-reachable from untrusted space while this flaw was unpatched, this control needs re-scoping rather than restating, because its usual premise does not hold here: the packet's implant is in-memory (Jaguar Tooth) and the packet's remediation is a fixed Cisco software release that reboots the device, so the upgrade itself clears memory-resident code. What the upgrade does not touch is the exploit's own precondition. The packet requires the attacker to already know the device's SNMP read-only community string (v1/v2c) or its SNMPv3 user credentials, and an image upgrade rotates neither — so the same access that produced the first implant works against the rebooted device, and the second run costs the attacker nothing. It also does not surface anything the attacker changed while resident. Applied to this device, remediation is three steps, not one: before the reload discards volatile state, capture and diff the running and startup configuration against a known-good baseline (SNMP community and user definitions, ACLs, any added local accounts, any configuration that would restore attacker access after reboot); rotate every SNMP community string and SNMPv3 credential the device carries and every device that shares them, since a community string is a per-device shared secret rather than a per-operator one; then bring the device up on the fixed release from the baseline configuration rather than from the configuration the compromised device saved for itself. Distinguishing test: after the upgrade, show that the device's SNMP credentials differ from the pre-incident values and that its running configuration matches the baseline — an estate that records the fixed IOS release against the asset and closes the ticket has remediated the overflow and preserved the credential. Preconditions and limits: the configuration diff assumes a known-good baseline exists to diff against; where none does, the step degrades to an engineer reviewing the configuration line by line and is weaker for it. And rebuilding the device does not tell you what the resident implant read or reached from that position, so a device confirmed compromised still owes downstream credential rotation for anything it held or could authenticate to.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Packet: CWE-119 buffer overflow in the SNMP implementation of Cisco IOS and IOS XE; the attacker 'must know the SNMP read only community string (SNMP version 2c or earlier) or the user credentials (SNMPv3)'; attack vector records that APT28 used it to inject the in-memory Jaguar Tooth implant; CISA KEV-listed 2023-04-19 with active_exploitation confirmed and poc_available true; RWEP 73 / CVSS 8.8; patch_available true and live_patch_available false, with the live-patch note stating remediation requires upgrading to a Cisco fixed software release per advisory cisco-sa-20170629-snmp, which reboots the device. AU-Essential-8-Patch and ISO 27001:2022 A.8.8 are recorded as insufficient for this entry — both are satisfied the moment the fixed release is installed.

new_control_requirements.name: APPSERVER-REMOTING-PROTOCOL-RESTRICTION
new_control_requirements.description: The SNMP agent on IOS / IOS XE is the listener class this control governs, on a router rather than an application server: a non-HTTP management protocol that answers on the device itself, whose parser is the vulnerable code, and which the packet says is exploitable only by traffic directed at the affected system. The requirement for these devices is that the SNMP agent answers only the management hosts that legitimately poll it — enforced with an SNMP access list and view on the device plus infrastructure ACLs on the paths that reach it, rather than assumed from 'the management VLAN is internal' — and that the affected MIBs and OIDs the packet's mitigation names are removed from the served view wherever the estate does not poll them, which is the least-functionality step the CM-7 gap is about. Distinguishing test: from a general user VLAN and from external transit, send SNMP requests at a staging device and confirm they are dropped before the agent parses them; a device that passes a configuration audit for 'SNMPv3 with authentication enabled' while its agent still answers packets sourced from anywhere has satisfied the audit and left the overflow reachable. Preconditions, and this is where the control is easy to over-claim: restricting reachability bounds who can send the crafted packet, it does not repair the parser, and the packet states the flaw affects all versions of SNMP (1, 2c and 3) — so moving the estate to SNMPv3 with strong credentials raises the cost of obtaining a valid credential but leaves the overflow fully reachable by anyone holding one, and a leaked v1/v2c community string is a single shared secret rather than a per-operator account. The monitoring platform that must poll the device is by definition inside the permitted set, so its compromise satisfies the exploit's stated access precondition in full. This is the holding measure for the window before the fixed software release lands, and taking that release reboots the device.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Packet: 'The vulnerability is due to a buffer overflow in the affected code area. The vulnerability affects all versions of SNMP (versions 1, 2c, and 3)'; 'Only traffic directed to the affected system can be used to exploit this vulnerability'; the live-patch note records Cisco's recommended mitigations as restricting SNMP access to trusted management hosts, disabling affected MIBs/OIDs, and enforcing SNMPv3 with strong credentials, with the fixed software release (which reboots the device) as the remediation; live_patch_available false; KEV 2023-04-19, active_exploitation confirmed, poc_available true. NIST 800-53 CM-7 (Least Functionality), NIS2 Art.21 security of network and information systems, and UK CAF B4 (System security) are the framework controls recorded as insufficient for this entry.

attack_vector.description: A local application triggers a use-after-free in macOS; reusing the freed object corrupts memory in a way that grants the app elevated privileges beyond its user context.
attack_vector.privileges_required: local user (a running application on the host)
attack_vector.complexity: low — a local use-after-free with a reliable trigger once conditions are met (CVSS AC:L)
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered — reported to Apple by an external researcher. No AI involvement documented.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Upgrade all Macs to macOS Mojave 10.14.4 or later where the memory-management fix ships.
prevention.adequacy: The OS update is the only fix; there is no configuration mitigation for the underlying UAF.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Endpoint telemetry flagging anomalous privilege gains or exploitation-chain behavior from unprivileged apps.
detection.adequacy: EDR may catch the surrounding chain but not the in-process memory corruption itself.

response.what_would_have_worked: Investigate the app that gained privileges, remove associated malware, and rotate credentials handled on the host.
response.adequacy: Response addresses the follow-on activity; the escalation itself is only prevented by patching.

NIST-800-53-AC-6.gap: AC-6 least privilege cannot contain a use-after-free that yields elevated privileges within macOS itself: once a local app triggers the freed-memory reuse, it gains rights above its assigned user context, defeating the privilege boundary AC-6 relies on.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: NIS2 Art.21 patch management on a macOS fleet depends on 10.14.4 being deployed, but the fix requires moving to a specific Mojave point release; endpoints held back on older macOS for app-compatibility reasons stayed exploitable well past KEV listing (2023-04-17).

UK-CAF-B4.gap: CAF B4 system security for endpoints cannot remediate an OS memory-management flaw through configuration; MDM hardening does not remove the vulnerable code path fixed only in macOS 10.14.4.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Essential Eight patch-operating-systems sets a one-month SLA, but macOS point-release upgrades are commonly deferred for compatibility testing, so the fixed 10.14.4 build routinely lands after the SLA window on managed Macs.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: A.8.8 technical-vulnerability management may treat a local-only macOS escalation as low priority, but as a KEV-listed in-the-wild bug it warranted expedited handling, exposing a gap between CVSS-driven triage and real exploitation.

CVE-2023-2033.name: Google Chromium V8 Type Confusion Vulnerability (CVE-2023-2033)

attack_vector.description: A crafted JavaScript page passes a JSGlobalProxy to Error.captureStackTrace, confusing V8's object typing and corrupting the heap into read/write primitives usable for renderer code execution.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none (unauthenticated) but requires the victim to load an attacker-controlled page
attack_vector.complexity: high - reliable V8 heap grooming, though a public PoC lowers the barrier for reuse
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered - reported by Clement Lecigne of Google TAG. No AI involvement documented.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Keep Chromium on auto-update so 112.0.5615.121 lands immediately; enterprise-force the emergency update.
prevention.adequacy: The patch closes the type confusion, but as a zero-day with a later public PoC, only rapid deployment limited the widened exposure.

detection.what_would_have_worked: EDR watching for browser renderer anomalies or unexpected child processes after page loads.
detection.adequacy: The in-renderer confusion is largely invisible to host telemetry until a sandbox escape spawns activity.

response.what_would_have_worked: Force-update all Chromium browsers and investigate targeted users for follow-on implant delivery.
response.adequacy: Contains further use but cannot reverse a successful renderer compromise.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: SI-2 flaw remediation cannot help before disclosure: CVE-2023-2033 was already exploited when Google patched it, and once a public PoC landed the exposure window for any Chrome below 112.0.5615.121 widened to all opportunistic attackers, not just the original TAG-tracked operator.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: NIS2 patch-management on a periodic browser cadence left the type confusion live between the April 2023 emergency release and the next scheduled update; with a PoC public, that gap was directly exploitable via a crafted page.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: CAF B4 endpoint hardening does not constrain V8's JIT object handling, so the JSGlobalProxy/Error.captureStackTrace confusion could corrupt the renderer heap on any unpatched Chromium; sandboxing limits but does not eliminate impact.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Essential Eight's 48-hour actively-exploited-app patch bar is regularly missed for browsers; endpoints off Chrome auto-update stayed exploitable to the public CVE-2023-2033 PoC during and after the 2023-05-08 KEV due date.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: A.8.8 technical-vulnerability management ranking by CVSS treats 8.8 as High-not-Critical, understating a zero-day with a public exploit; deprioritising it left the type confusion open while it was actively used.

new_control_requirements.name: BROWSER-MANAGED-UPDATE-NO-DEFERRAL
new_control_requirements.description: The packet records no live-patch mechanism for this flaw and states the remediation exactly: Chrome/Chromium auto-update to 112.0.5615.121 or later, followed by a browser restart to load the patched build. That places the whole residual exposure in the gap between the update arriving on disk and the user relaunching the browser, which is why this control has to bind both halves for this CVE. On a managed estate it means the security update channel is not deferred by the update ring at all for a KEV-listed renderer defect, and the relaunch is forced by policy rather than left to the user's convenience — the delivery path here is an ordinary page visit (the packet's path is a crafted JavaScript page passing a JSGlobalProxy to Error.captureStackTrace, confusing V8's object typing and corrupting the heap into read/write primitives usable for renderer code execution), and the browser session least likely to be restarted, an instance left open for weeks, is exactly the one most likely to meet such a page. Completion must be measured on the version V8 is actually executing, not the version deployed: a host whose management record shows 112.0.5615.121 while the running browser has never been relaunched is still executing the pre-fix renderer, and every framework control citing this CVE closes on the deployed version. Distinguishing test: collect the running browser's version from managed hosts and confirm it is at or above 112.0.5615.121 — an estate reporting package-level compliance while long-lived sessions keep the old build resident is exposed to a defect the packet records as KEV-listed since 2023-04-17, with a public exploit and confirmed in-the-wild use. Precondition: forcing the relaunch bounds the window, it does not undo a visit that already happened; a host that rendered untrusted web content while below the fixed build belongs on the incident path rather than being closed on the update record.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Packet: type confusion in V8 in Google Chrome prior to 112.0.5615.121 allowed a remote attacker to potentially exploit heap corruption via a crafted HTML page; a crafted JavaScript page passes a JSGlobalProxy to Error.captureStackTrace, confusing V8's object typing and corrupting the heap into read/write primitives usable for renderer code execution. cisa_kev true, kev_date 2023-04-17, active_exploitation confirmed, poc_available true, CVSS 8.8, RWEP 66. patch_available true; live_patch_available false with live_patch_notes: no live-patch mechanism, remediation is Chrome/Chromium auto-update to 112.0.5615.121 or later followed by a browser restart to load the patched build.

attack_vector.description: A malicious app already on the device triggers a Parcel serialization mismatch in WorkSource within the Android Framework, causing the system to misinterpret data and grant the app elevated privileges without extra permissions or user interaction.
attack_vector.privileges_required: local (a low-privilege app installed on the device)
attack_vector.complexity: low — no user interaction and no additional execution privileges are needed once the app runs.
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered — surfaced from in-the-wild Android abuse and fixed in the March 2023 bulletin. No AI involvement documented.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Applying the 2023-03-01 Android security patch level and restricting app installs to vetted sources (Play Protect / no sideloading).
prevention.adequacy: The framework patch closes the escalation; source restriction reduces the chance a malicious app reaches the device but does not fix the underlying flaw.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Mobile threat defense / Play Protect flagging apps that request escalation or exhibit parcel-abuse behavior.
detection.adequacy: Behavioral detection of a framework-level escalation is unreliable and post-hoc.

response.what_would_have_worked: Removing the offending app, updating the security patch level, and reviewing the device for further compromise.
response.adequacy: Reactive and dependent on an available OEM patch.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: SI-2 flaw remediation depends on the Android March-2023 patch level reaching devices, but OEM/carrier fragmentation means many handsets received the fix late or never; a malicious app on an unpatched device could still exploit the WorkSource parcel mismatch to escalate, as reflected in the 2023-04-13 KEV listing.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: NIS2 patch-management over a BYOD/mobile estate cannot compel Android OEM firmware updates, so the March-2023 fix for this parcel-mismatch LPE was undeployable on schedule across diverse devices, leaving a local escalation path open to sideloaded or abusive apps.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: CAF B4 system security assumes app sandboxing contains a rogue app, but this Android Framework parcel mismatch lets an already-installed app escalate privileges without additional permissions or user interaction, so sandbox trust alone does not stop it — the framework patch is required.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Essential Eight patching cannot enforce a timeline on Android security-patch-level uptake, so between the 2023-04-13 KEV date and fragmented OEM rollout, unpatched devices remained escalatable by a malicious app with no special privileges.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: A.8.8 technical vulnerability management presumes remediation can be scheduled, but the availability of the fix for this Framework LPE is gated by Android security-patch-level delivery per OEM, so vulnerability-management SLAs cannot guarantee closure of the privilege-escalation path on affected fleets.

new_control_requirements.name: MOBILE-OS-MINIMUM-PATCH-LEVEL-ENFORCEMENT
new_control_requirements.description: The packet's precondition is an app already on the device, and the outcome is local privilege escalation with no additional execution privileges needed and no user interaction — so on a handset below the 2023-03-01 Android security patch level there is no prompt to decline, no permission grant to review and no user decision in the path, and the only lever left is what organizational data that handset is permitted to hold. Applied to this CVE, the 2023-03-01 or later patch level must operate as an access condition across the affected Android 11, 12, 12L and 13 population — mail, VPN and document access denied to a device below it — rather than as a reported field on a patch-compliance dashboard.
