NIS2-Art21-vulnerability-management.gap: The gap is scope rather than speed: Cacti is catalogued as a support utility rather than an in-scope service, even though its database holds the SNMP community strings and device credentials for the very network and information systems Art.21 exists to protect.

UK-CAF-C1.gap: C1 assumes the monitoring infrastructure is a trusted observer, and this CVE hands the attacker the collector itself. Nothing in the principle requires monitoring of the monitoring host, so the bots run on the one server least likely to be watched by the capability C1 assesses.

AU-ISM-1546.gap: The fix arrived through entirely ordinary channels, but Cacti is characteristically installed from a distribution package by a NOC team and never enters the application register the control is measured against — so patch-compliance reporting stays green on a host it cannot see.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.9.gap: A.8.9 derives secure baselines from the vendor default, and here the vendor default is the exploit primitive — the pre-existing poller row naming the Cacti server's own hostname is what makes a spoofed header resolve to an authorised client, so the baseline encodes the bypass rather than removing it.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2022-46169 was fixed on 2022-12-05, MooBot and ShellBot were mass-exploiting it from January 2023, and the KEV due date of 2023-03-09 sat two months behind the fix — a cadence that catalogues Cacti as a support utility rather than an in-scope service never reaches it inside that window. A KEV-triggered clock takes the internal asset rating out of the decision on a pre-auth RCE with EPSS 0.99826.

new_control_requirements.name: SECURITY-TOOL-INTEGRITY-VERIFICATION
new_control_requirements.description: Security tools (AV/AM, EDR, vulnerability scanners) must be treated as in-scope of vulnerability management with the same SLAs as other privileged software. Definition-update channels must use TLS with certificate pinning. Compliance audits must include a trust-anchor-inversion test: deliver a crafted input to the security tool in a sandbox and confirm rejection.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2022-46169 makes the monitoring platform itself the attack vector: remote_agent.php derives caller identity from an attacker-supplied X-Forwarded-For header, and the stock poller row naming the Cacti server's own hostname means the shipped vendor baseline encodes the bypass — while the compromised collector holds the SNMP community strings for every device it watches. Only treating the monitoring tool as privileged in-scope software and adversarially feeding it a spoofed-header request surfaces that; nothing requires the monitor to be monitored.

CVE-2023-21715.name: Microsoft Office Publisher Security Feature Bypass Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: A user is socially engineered into downloading and opening a specially crafted Publisher (.pub) file. Publisher's own handling of that file bypasses the Office macro policies that block macros in files from untrusted locations, so the document's VBA executes without the trust-bar block or security warning that would normally fire on a Mark-of-the-Web-tagged download — turning an otherwise-blocked macro payload into working code execution on the endpoint.
attack_vector.privileges_required: low — PR:L, an authenticated local user session on the target machine, plus UI:R because the victim must fetch and open the file; there is no remote path (AV:L)
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; the real cost is phishing delivery rather than exploitation, and Microsoft rated exploit-code maturity Unproven (E:U) while simultaneously recording Exploited: Yes
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered — Microsoft credits Hidetake Jo, Rick Cole, Charlie Hurel and Matthew Mesa, plus Haifei Li with EXPMON, an automated exploit-detection and sandbox-emulation platform. Sample-driven detection of live attacks, with no AI system named in any primary source.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Install the February 2023 Office security release through the Click-to-Run channel and, more durably, remove Publisher from the Microsoft 365 Apps deployment configuration on endpoints with no business need for it.
prevention.adequacy: Patching closes it, but Microsoft's own record shows Exploited: Yes with Publicly Disclosed: No at release, so exploitation preceded the fix and no patch cadence covered the exposure window. Removing Publisher is the stronger control precisely because it does not depend on a patch clock — the component has no business use in most organisations.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alerting when MSPUB.EXE spawns wscript.exe, cscript.exe, powershell.exe, mshta.exe or rundll32.exe, or initiates outbound connections, and on macro telemetry showing VBA execution against a file carrying a Zone.Identifier stream.
detection.adequacy: The macro-on-a-MOTW-tagged-file signal is the one that specifically catches this bypass, because it detects the policy failing to fire rather than the payload itself — which is the only observable difference between this CVE and a normal blocked document.

response.what_would_have_worked: Block .pub attachments at the mail gateway as an interim control, then investigate the endpoint for the second-stage payload the macro fetched and rotate any credentials handled on that host.
response.adequacy: Gateway blocking is the compensating control that held during the pre-patch window; endpoint response is otherwise identical to any macro-borne intrusion, since what this CVE bought the attacker was delivery, not a novel post-exploitation capability.

NIST-800-53-SI-3.gap: For document-borne code the SI-3 enforcement point most organisations depend on is the Office macro policy, and this flaw lets a crafted .pub run its macros without that policy firing — so a fully implemented, fully attested control produces no signal because it silently does not apply to this file type.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: Exploitation preceded the fix, so the Art.21 measure that was supposed to hold during that window was the macro policy — and this vulnerability is the bypass of it. Answering document-borne execution risk with patch management alone leaves no control standing, and Art.21 does not name the compensating one.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: UK organisations evidence B4 endpoint hardening with the NCSC-recommended Office macro configuration, which here was present, correctly applied and ineffective — and B4's evidence model cannot distinguish an enforced macro policy from one that is enforced but bypassable for a specific file type.

AU-Essential-8-App-Hardening.gap: The maturity questions are whether macros are blocked for users without a business need and whether users can change the setting; neither can detect a bypass inside Publisher's file handling, and the highest-value action available — uninstalling Publisher — is not something the model asks about at any maturity level.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.7.gap: Malware protection was evidenced with endpoint anti-malware plus the macro block at the very sites where this was exploited before a patch existed; the delivered .pub is unremarkable to signature detection because the malicious behaviour lives in the macro the policy should have stopped.

new_control_requirements.name: PROTECTION-MECHANISM-FAILURE-CLASS-REGRESSION
new_control_requirements.description: Detonation chambers, EDR rules, and AppLocker/WDAC policies covering protection-mechanism classes (MOTW, SmartScreen, AMSI, ASR, WDAC, Driver Block Rules) must include class-level regression testing executed on every patch deployment, not just one-off bypass-CVE remediation. The test battery for class-X must include all historic class-X bypass primitives — incomplete patches re-introduce risk that one-off testing does not detect.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2023-21715 is a bypass of the Office macro policy itself: a crafted .pub file runs its VBA with no trust-bar block even though the download carries Mark-of-the-Web, so a fully deployed and fully attested enforcement point produced no signal because it silently did not apply to that file type. Only a MOTW/macro-policy regression battery executed on each patch deployment can tell an enforced policy from one that is enforced and bypassable.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2023-21715 shipped with Microsoft recording Exploited: Yes and Publicly Disclosed: No, so attacks preceded the February 2023 Office release and no patch cadence covered the exposure window at all. KEV listing on 2023-02-14 is the trigger that forces the documented compensating control the lesson names — blocking .pub at the mail gateway — instead of leaving patch management as the only measure against a bypass of the control patch management was relying on.

CVE-2023-23376.name: Microsoft Windows Common Log File System (CLFS) Driver Privilege Escalation Vulnerability (CVE-2023-23376)

attack_vector.description: An unprivileged process writes a CLFS Base Log File in which CLFS_CONTROL_RECORD has been relocated to offset 0x1FF and CLFS_LOG_BLOCK_HEADER->SignaturesOffset patched from 0x3F8 to 0x28, so the sector-signature array overlaps DumpCount. clfs.sys's own metadata-extension path then parses an out-of-range block index and does the corrupting, yielding an arbitrary kernel write built by incrementing DumpCount at a controlled address — aimed at pipe-attribute fields on newer Windows 11 builds or PreviousMode on earlier ones — and ending in a SYSTEM token.
attack_vector.privileges_required: low — PR:L, any ordinary authenticated account can create a Base Log File; in the observed intrusions that foothold came from phishing or credential abuse well before this CVE was reached
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L, UI:N, a deterministic file-format attack with no race window; what raises the practical bar is portability, since the write target's layout shifts per Windows build and working code needs per-build offsets
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered — Microsoft's own MSTIC and MSRC surfaced it as an already-in-the-wild zero-day, and Kaspersky's later root-cause work was manual reverse engineering of a captured sample. This predates the AI-assisted-discovery wave entirely.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Install the February 2023 cumulative updates reaching builds 10.0.10240.19747 through 10.0.22621.1265, plus the Server 2008 SP2 / 2008 R2 SP1 / 2012 / 2012 R2 monthly rollups, and reboot so the updated boot-loaded clfs.sys takes effect.
prevention.adequacy: The update is the only fix — CLFS cannot be disabled, removed or configured away, and Windows offers no live-patching path for the general fleet. But Microsoft published the fix and the exploited flag on the same day, so the entire pre-disclosure window had no covering control beyond restricting who can execute code on the host at all.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alerting on .blf Base Log Files written to user-writable directories with CLFS_CONTROL_RECORD moved to 0x1FF and a second crafted record at 0x2FF, and on a SYSTEM-token process appearing immediately after CLFS log-file activity from an unprivileged parent.
detection.adequacy: The structural .blf signature is specific enough to be actionable, but it requires file-content inspection of a log format most EDR treats as noise — the parent-to-SYSTEM transition is the signal more products actually carry.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treat SYSTEM escalation on the host as a pre-encryption stage: isolate immediately, hunt for defense-impairment activity and staged encryptor binaries, and reset every credential cached on the machine.
response.adequacy: Speed is the whole response value here — KEV records ransomware use as Known, and this CVE's operational role is the step immediately before the encryptor, so hours matter more than completeness.

NIST-800-53-AC-6.gap: Least privilege is the exploit's entry condition, not a barrier: stripping local-administrator rights and running users as standard leaves the vulnerable driver just as reachable from a standard user token, and MSRC confirms successful exploitation returns SYSTEM.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: The Art.21 patch clock starts at vendor disclosure, but MSTIC and MSRC found this in the wild and Microsoft shipped the fix and the exploitation flag on the same day — so an entity fully compliant with its declared SLA had zero coverage for the entire pre-disclosure window on a driver present in every Windows install it operates.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: B4 expects a hardened, minimised build with unnecessary functionality removed, but CLFS is a boot-loaded kernel driver with no disable switch, no service to stop and no configuration surface — there is no attack-surface-reduction decision available that takes this path off a Windows host.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: The 48-hour target for vulnerabilities with working exploits is measured from vendor release, which against a bug already flagged as exploited at publication starts a clock on a window that had closed — and the model offers no compensating mitigation for a kernel driver reachable from any authenticated session.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: Risk-based prioritisation reliably ranks a CVSS 7.8 local elevation below the network-facing 9.8s of the same month, which is the wrong ordering for a bug whose role is converting a phished foothold into SYSTEM immediately before encryptor deployment.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2023-23376 carries KEV ransomware status Known and its operational role is the step immediately before encryptor deployment, yet at CVSS 7.8 a risk-based schedule reliably ranks this CLFS local elevation below the network-facing 9.8s of the same Patch Tuesday. Keying the clock to the KEV listing rather than the base score is what reorders a bug whose whole value is converting a phished foothold into SYSTEM.

new_control_requirements.name: LIVE-PATCH-CAPABILITY
new_control_requirements.description: For any system that processes production workloads and cannot tolerate unplanned reboots: live kernel patching capability (kpatch, livepatch, kGraft, or equivalent) must be deployed and tested quarterly.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2023-23376 is fixed only by the February 2023 cumulative update plus a reboot, because clfs.sys is a boot-loaded kernel driver that cannot be disabled, stopped or configured away and offers no attack-surface reduction in the interim. Uptime-constrained servers therefore stay exposed to an actively-exploited SYSTEM escalation until the next maintenance window — the exact interval a 48-hour target measured from vendor release cannot bridge without a live-patch path.

CVE-2023-23529.name: Apple Multiple Products WebKit Type Confusion Vulnerability (CVE-2023-23529)

attack_vector.description: A targeted user loads attacker-controlled web content — a link, a malicious ad, a watering hole, a page rendered from a message — and a JavaScriptCore/WebKit type confusion yields arbitrary code execution inside the sandboxed WebContent process. That is the renderer half of a chain: the same iOS 16.3.1 release also fixed a kernel use-after-free (CVE-2023-23514) of exactly the shape needed to escape the sandbox. Because Apple's platform rules force every iOS browser and in-app WebView onto WebKit, avoiding Safari does not avoid the surface.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N, no credentials or prior access, but UI:R because the victim must load the malicious content
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L with no race condition; delivery is the gating step rather than exploit reliability, and no public PoC has emerged in three years because the vendor kept WebKit Bugzilla 251944 restricted
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered — Apple credits an anonymous researcher in all four advisories carrying this CVE, with additional recognition to The Citizen Lab. The anonymity means no tooling attribution exists either way; recorded as human research on the strength of the vendor credit line.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Update to iOS/iPadOS 16.3.1, macOS Ventura 13.2.1 or Safari 16.3 (all 2023-02-13); pre-A9 hardware needed iOS/iPadOS 15.7.4, which did not ship until 2023-03-27. Lockdown Mode, which disables just-in-time JavaScript compilation, materially shrinks the WebKit surface for high-risk users in the interim.
prevention.adequacy: Patching is the only fix and there is no live-patch path — Apple's Rapid Security Response mechanism did not ship its first release until 2023-05-01, after this fix. The 42-day gap before iPhone 6s, iPhone 7, iPhone SE 1st generation, iPad Air 2, iPad mini 4 and iPod touch 7 received 15.7.4 means the oldest devices in the estate ran exposed past the 2023-03-07 KEV due date through no failure of the operator.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Collecting WebContent crash reports and JetsamEvent logs referencing JavaScriptCore, which are the only host-side artifact available on iOS.
detection.adequacy: Barely a detection at all in practice — third-party EDR cannot observe process execution or memory on iOS, so an unreliable heap-grooming attempt leaves a crash log the operator usually has no pipeline to ingest, and a successful exploit leaves nothing.

response.what_would_have_worked: Force an OS update across the mobile estate including BYOD, enable Lockdown Mode for high-risk users, and treat suspected targeting as a case for Apple's threat-notification process rather than local forensics.
response.adequacy: Response options are structurally thin on the platform: with no on-device forensic access, updating and hardening are close to the whole response, which is why the exposure window is where the risk actually lives.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: SI-2 is scoped to organisation-managed systems while much of the exposed population is personally owned BYOD, and its remediation clock keys to first vendor release — systematically under-counting the 42 extra days pre-A9 devices waited for iOS 15.7.4.

NIS2-Art21-network-security.gap: The declared network-security measures — segmentation, secure gateways, monitored perimeters — are all bypassed by a renderer compromise on a phone that never traverses them, executing off content fetched over TLS the entity does not terminate.

UK-CAF-C1.gap: C1 presumes host telemetry can be collected, and on iOS and iPadOS it architecturally cannot — so a C1 'achieved' rating carries no information about whether this bug was used against the estate.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: ASD scopes the patching mitigations to workstations, servers and network devices, placing mobile devices outside the model entirely — an organisation at Maturity Level 3 across all eight mitigations can be fully compliant with its whole iPhone and iPad estate on the vulnerable WebKit build.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.7.gap: Apple's security model forbids on-device anti-malware scanning outright, so the control cannot be implemented on the affected devices and an ISMS records it as not applicable rather than as an uncovered risk — while Lockdown Mode, the one measure that genuinely shrinks the surface, is nowhere in the control text.

new_control_requirements.name: MOBILE-ENDPOINT-MDM-ENFORCED-KEV-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: iOS / iPadOS / macOS estates must enforce KEV-class updates within 24h via DDM; user-deferral disallowed.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2023-23529 was exploited in the wild and KEV-listed 2023-02-14, and the only remediation is the iOS/iPadOS 16.3.1, macOS Ventura 13.2.1 or Safari 16.3 update — Apple's Rapid Security Response mechanism did not exist until 2023-05-01, so there was no live-patch path. Because Apple's platform rules force every iOS browser and in-app WebView onto WebKit, an update the user can defer leaves the whole rendering surface of the device exposed; enforcement, not reporting, is what closes it.

new_control_requirements.name: MOBILE-ZERO-CLICK-HARDENING
new_control_requirements.description: High-risk mobile users must operate in a reduced-attack-surface mode (e.g. Lockdown Mode) that disables automatic processing of untrusted message attachments, fonts, and link previews, closing the zero-click delivery path patch SLAs cannot outrun.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2023-23529 fires the moment a targeted user loads attacker-controlled content — a link, a malicious ad, a page rendered from a message — as the renderer half of a chain with the kernel use-after-free fixed alongside it, and pre-A9 hardware (iPhone 6s, iPhone 7, iPhone SE 1st generation, iPad Air 2, iPad mini 4, iPod touch 7) waited until 2023-03-27 for iOS 15.7.4, past the KEV due date, through no operator failure. Lockdown Mode disables the just-in-time JavaScript compilation this type confusion needs and is the only measure that shrinks the surface across a 42-day window no patch SLA could have closed.

CVE-2023-21823.name: Microsoft Windows Graphic Component Privilege Escalation Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: Code already running on the machine — a document that was opened, a script that was executed, or an existing low-privilege process — drives the Microsoft Graphics Component through a crafted graphics object whose size calculation wraps (CWE-190). The undersized allocation that results gives controlled memory corruption and elevation to SYSTEM. The MSRC title says Remote Code Execution, but Microsoft's own FAQ resolves the contradiction with the AV:L vector: 'remote' describes where the attacker sits, while the attack itself is carried out locally.
attack_vector.privileges_required: low — PR:L, an existing low-privilege foothold with code execution on the host; UI:N once that foothold exists
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L, deterministic once the wrapping size value is reachable, with no race window; Microsoft rates exploit-code maturity High (E:H), meaning functional in-the-wild code exists even though nothing usable is public
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered — Microsoft credits Genwei Jiang and Dhanesh Kizhakkinan of Mandiant, whose work centres on analysing exploits caught in the wild. No AI tooling is credited in the acknowledgement, the MSRC advisory, or any subsequent writeup.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Install the February 2023 Windows cumulative updates for the applicable SKU (KB5022834, KB5022836, KB5022838, KB5022840, KB5022842/KB5022921, KB5022845, KB5022858 and the legacy Server rollups) AND separately update Microsoft Office for Universal to 16.0.14326.21330, Office for Android to 16.0.16130.20156 and Office for iOS to 2.70.23021003.
prevention.adequacy: Shipping only the Windows KBs — which is what a WSUS, SCCM or Intune programme naturally does — leaves the CVE open on three other products in the same advisory. Worse, MSRC states the Microsoft Store will not install the fix at all for customers who disabled Store automatic updates, so a hardened baseline actively blocks half the remediation.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Inventory-driven detection rather than behavioural: reporting hosts below the fixed Windows build numbers, hosts running Store-delivered Office components below the fixed versions, and hosts where Store automatic updates are disabled by policy.
detection.adequacy: The exploit itself produces little distinctive telemetry — it is graphics-object parsing inside a normal process — so the reliable detection is finding the half-remediated hosts, not catching the attempt.

response.what_would_have_worked: Reconcile the affected-product list against the estate across all three delivery channels, pull the Store update manually where policy blocks it, and treat a SYSTEM escalation on any unpatched host as a full compromise of that machine.
response.adequacy: The reconciliation is the load-bearing step: without it the organisation closes the vulnerability record on OS-patch evidence while functional in-the-wild code still has reachable targets.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: SI-2 is operationalised through a single enterprise update channel, and this one CVE needs three — Windows KBs, Microsoft Store, and Google Play plus the App Store — so a programme reporting 100% KB compliance is genuinely unremediated and the evidence diverges from the exposure silently.

NIS2-Art21-vulnerability-handling.gap: Vulnerability handling is asserted against an asset register that rarely lists Store-delivered Office variants or Office for Android and iOS as separately patchable assets with their own version floors, so the entity's evidence records the OS remediation and omits three affected products from the same advisory.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: Blocking the Microsoft Store is standard secure-baseline advice a B4 assessment scores favourably, and it is precisely what prevents this fix from arriving — the control and the remediation are in direct conflict, so a stronger B4 posture leaves the CVE open longer.

AU-ISM-1546.gap: The patch timeframe is measurable and enforceable for the Windows KBs but unenforceable for the app-store-delivered Office builds, where the organisation controls neither release cadence nor install trigger — so ISM-1546 evidence for this CVE cannot be made complete across the published product set.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: The technical-vulnerability process inherits the blind spots of the A.5.9 inventory, and a Windows-only inventory never lists the Office for Universal, Android and iOS components — so the record closes on OS evidence while Microsoft's own E:H rating says functional exploit code still has targets.

new_control_requirements.name: EDR-PLATFORM-UPDATE-DISTINCT-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: EDR / AV platform-update channels must be tracked as distinct patch surfaces with their own SLA, separate from OS-update SLA. Defender platform updates, CrowdStrike Falcon-sensor updates, SentinelOne agent updates, etc. ship outside the OS-patching cadence and require dedicated monitoring and SLA tracking.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2023-21823 needs three delivery channels to be remediated — the February 2023 Windows cumulative updates, Microsoft Store-delivered Office for Universal 16.0.14326.21330, and Office for Android 16.0.16130.20156 plus Office for iOS 2.70.23021003 — and MSRC states the Store will not install the fix where Store automatic updates are disabled by policy, so the hardened baseline blocks half the remediation. Tracking each non-OS update channel as its own patch surface with its own SLA is what stops a programme reporting 100% KB compliance from being genuinely unremediated.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2023-21823 is KEV-listed 2023-02-14 with Microsoft rating exploit-code maturity High, meaning functional in-the-wild code still has targets on every host left on the unpatched Store or mobile Office builds. A KEV clock that demands verified mitigation forces the record to close against the whole published affected-product set rather than against OS-patch evidence alone.

CVE-2015-2291.name: Intel Ethernet Diagnostics Driver for Windows Denial-of-Service Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: The adversary brings their own copy of the validly-Intel-signed pre-1.3.1.0 iqvw64e.sys, drops it into a user-writable path and registers it as a kernel service with sc.exe. They then issue DeviceIoControl with IOCTL 0x80862007, whose input buffer selects jump-table case 0x33 — a raw kernel memmove taking attacker-supplied source, destination and length. That arbitrary kernel read/write is used to swap the calling process's token for the SYSTEM process token and to patch csagent.sys and peer EDR drivers with trampolines at hard-coded offsets, so the security product keeps reporting healthy while it has stopped inspecting.
attack_vector.privileges_required: low per the CVSS vector (PR:L) for the IOCTL itself, but the bring-your-own-vulnerable-driver path that put this CVE in KEV requires local administrator rights to register a kernel-mode service
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L, and the vector understates it: case 0x33 is a memmove handed out by design, so there is no memory-corruption craft, no heap grooming and no race, and KDMapper productises the primitive against builds from Windows 10 1607 through Windows 11 25H2
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered — published by Glafkos Charalambous in March 2015 (Exploit-DB 36392), roughly a decade before practical AI-assisted vulnerability discovery. The technique is manual IOCTL enumeration and driver reverse engineering, and every subsequent public writeup reproduces it by hand in IDA.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Enable HVCI / Memory Integrity, or deploy WDAC / App Control carrying the Microsoft Vulnerable Driver Blocklist whose rule ID_FILEATTRIB_IQVW64 denies iQVW64.SYS from 0.0.0.0 through 1.4.0.21, and remove local-administrator rights so registering a kernel-mode service is not available in the first place.
prevention.adequacy: No framework required the control that actually works. The KEV-listed action for this entry is the vendor driver update to 1.3.1.0, which does not remove the attack path at all — the adversary supplies the vulnerable binary themselves, and Microsoft's blocklist ceiling of 1.4.0.21 sits above Intel's own fixed version, meaning even post-fix builds are treated as unsafe to load. Image blocking, not patching, is the remediation.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alerting on new kernel-mode service entries under HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services whose ImagePath points at a temp or user-writable directory, on iqvw64e.sys appearing outside a legitimate Intel PROSet installation path, and on hosts reporting Memory Integrity disabled.
detection.adequacy: The service-registration event is the last reliable observation point, because once the driver loads the attacker's next move is blinding the very agent that would report anything further — detection has to fire before the load completes or not at all.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treat the host as fully compromised at kernel level: rebuild rather than clean, verify EDR driver integrity across the fleet rather than trusting console health, and enable Memory Integrity estate-wide as the durable fix.
response.adequacy: Console health is worthless as a response input here — the documented technique leaves the agent reporting green while inert — so fleet-wide driver integrity verification is the only trustworthy scoping method after a confirmed load.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: Flaw remediation is the wrong control class and produces active false assurance: an attestation showing every host on a current Intel network driver is entirely compatible with every one of those hosts being exploitable, because the driver that loads is the one the attacker carried in.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: Vulnerability handling is evidenced against a register of installed software versions, and this CVE is exploited by a driver that is not installed — dropped at execution time from attacker-controlled storage — so a flawless register coexists with total exposure, and Art.21 never names the code-integrity deny-list that would help.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: B4 states the right outcome at the wrong default: HVCI / Memory Integrity is off on Windows installations upgraded in place rather than clean-installed, and B4's outcome text does not name it — so 'systems hardened, drivers signed' can be assessed as achieved on a host that will still load a 2015 driver exposing a kernel memmove.

AU-Essential-8-App-Hardening.gap: User application hardening addresses browsers, Office macros, PDF readers, Java and web advertisements — the user-mode surface only. The Essential Eight contains no driver-blocklist or code-integrity mitigation anywhere in the model, so Maturity Level 3 across all eight still permits the kernel-driver load.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.7.gap: Malware protection presumes the anti-malware control is doing the protecting; here it is the target. Agents deployed everywhere, signatures current, console green — the exact evidence an auditor accepts — is satisfied precisely while the EDR has been patched inert at hard-coded offsets.

new_control_requirements.name: VULNERABLE-DRIVER-BLOCKLIST-ENFORCEMENT
new_control_requirements.description: Enforce a kernel vulnerable/malicious-driver blocklist (HVCI plus the vendor recommended-driver blocklist) so a signed-but-vulnerable driver cannot be loaded for bring-your-own-vulnerable-driver privilege escalation.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2015-2291 is exploited by an adversary who carries in their own validly-Intel-signed pre-1.3.1.0 iqvw64e.sys, registers it as a kernel service and calls IOCTL 0x80862007 case 0x33 — a raw kernel memmove — so the KEV-listed action of updating to 1.3.1.0 removes nothing, and Microsoft's blocklist rule ID_FILEATTRIB_IQVW64 deliberately denies the image through 1.4.0.21, above Intel's own fixed version. Image blocking through HVCI plus the vendor driver blocklist is the remediation; flaw remediation against the installed-driver register produces active false assurance.

new_control_requirements.name: EDR-AS-VULNERABILITY-SECONDARY-OVERLAY
new_control_requirements.description: Organizations whose primary EDR is also a high-value attack target (Defender, CrowdStrike, SentinelOne) must deploy an independent secondary overlay capable of detecting anomalous behavior by the primary EDR's own processes. The overlay can be a second-vendor behavioral EDR, network-side EDR-bypass telemetry, or out-of-band SYSTEM-process spawn monitoring — but must NOT share trust roots with the primary EDR.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2015-2291's arbitrary kernel write is used in the wild to patch csagent.sys and peer EDR drivers with trampolines at hard-coded offsets, so the agent keeps reporting healthy on the console while it has stopped inspecting — agents deployed, signatures current, console green is exactly the evidence an auditor accepts, and it is satisfied precisely while the product is inert. Detection and post-incident scoping therefore require an overlay that does not share trust roots with the blinded primary agent.

CVE-2022-24990.name: TerraMaster OS Remote Command Execution Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: One unauthenticated GET to /module/api.php?mobile/webNasIPS carrying the literal header 'User-Agent: TNAS' returns JSON whose PWD field is the administrator password hash, alongside firmware version, MAC, network configuration and running services. The attacker recomputes the AUTHORIZATION, TIMESTAMP and SIGNATURE headers from that hash and POSTs to mobile/createRaid with shell metacharacters in the raidtype parameter, which flows through volume_make_from_disks() into _backexec() and reaches popen() unsanitised as root. Metasploit ships the whole chain, joined with CVE-2022-24989, as unauthenticated root RCE.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; the disclosure step needs nothing but TCP reachability and a fixed User-Agent string, and the credential it returns supplies the authentication for the command-injection step
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L, UI:N, no encoding, brute force, race or session to establish; EPSS 0.83546 (99.657th percentile) against a base score of only 7.5, and both steps are automated end-to-end in the shipped Metasploit module
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered — Octagon Networks published it on 2022-03-07 after manually reverse-engineering TOS's api.php dynamic class instantiation and the $notCheck / $notHeader allowlists in mobile.class.php. Classic PHP source review of extracted firmware, with no AI tooling credited in the writeup, the Metasploit module, or the nuclei template.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Upgrade to TerraMaster TOS 4.2.30 or later, rotate the administrator password because the pre-upgrade hash was disclosed to anyone who could reach the appliance, and remove the NAS from the internet including any UPnP-created port forward on the upstream router.
prevention.adequacy: The firmware upgrade closes the endpoint but cannot undo the leak — a box that was reachable before 4.2.30 must be assumed to have surrendered its administrator hash, so upgrading without rotating the credential preserves the attacker's access. Removing inbound exposure is the step that survives the next TOS vulnerability.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alerting on HTTP requests to /module/api.php carrying the exact User-Agent string 'TNAS', on responses containing a PWD field, on createRaid POSTs whose raidtype value holds shell metacharacters, and on probe artifacts such as /tmp/a.txt plus unexpected outbound connections from the NAS.
detection.adequacy: The signals are unambiguous — a fixed User-Agent literal has no false-positive population — but they only exist where NAS traffic crosses an inspected path, and the deployment shape that makes this CVE dangerous is exactly the one where it does not: a branch or home-office appliance port-forwarded straight to the internet.

response.what_would_have_worked: Assume root compromise: rebuild the appliance, rotate every credential it stored, restore from an offline copy rather than from the NAS itself, and verify no Deadbolt-class encryption has reached the shares.
response.adequacy: The restore source is the decisive detail — where the NAS is simultaneously the primary store and the backup target, the response plan's first step reads from the system the attacker owned first, which is why an offline copy has to exist before the incident.

NIST-800-53-SC-7.gap: Boundary protection is assessed at the organisation's managed perimeter, while these appliances acquire their own exposure outside it through UPnP mappings and manual port forwards on branch routers — and with no authentication step to reinforce, a boundary control that never sees the traffic has nothing to enforce.

NIS2-Art21-business-continuity.gap: Continuity measures assume the recovery tier survives the incident, but here the NAS is both primary store and backup target, and root on that device precedes ransomware on the recovery data itself — so the tested restore plan is a single point of failure the measure never modelled.

UK-CAF-D1.gap: Response and recovery planning is exercised against scenarios where recovery data is intact and reachable, and D1 plans name these appliances as the recovery source rather than treating them as internet-facing web applications carrying their own pre-authentication RCE chain.

AU-Essential-8-Backup.gap: The mitigation measures backup frequency, retention and restore testing and says nothing about the security posture of the device holding the backups — so Maturity Level 3 is fully demonstrable on a NAS that hands its administrator hash to any unauthenticated request.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.13.gap: A.8.13 expresses protection as access control and encryption applied to the backup copies, but the failure happens a layer earlier at the appliance's own management plane, where api.php dispatches allowlisted methods with no authentication at all — the backup data's controls are never reached.

new_control_requirements.name: BACKUP-TIER-NETWORK-ISOLATION
new_control_requirements.description: Backup-orchestration appliances and backup-data destinations must be network-isolated from the data-plane networks they protect. Management surfaces must be reachable only from operator subnets; backup-data paths must use unidirectional or pull-only patterns from the backup tier to the protected systems where possible.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2022-24990 returns the administrator password hash to any unauthenticated GET to /module/api.php carrying 'User-Agent: TNAS', then reaches popen() as root through the createRaid raidtype parameter — a chain Metasploit ships end to end — and the appliance it roots is simultaneously the primary store and the backup target, acquiring its own internet exposure through UPnP mappings and branch-router port forwards outside the managed perimeter. Isolating the backup tier's management surface to operator subnets removes the TCP reachability the whole chain depends on.

new_control_requirements.name: PERIMETER-COMPROMISE-REBUILD-NOT-PATCH
new_control_requirements.description: Pre-rehearsed IR runbook for any perimeter device that suffers a pre-auth RCE CVE in active exploitation MUST default to config-exfil + rebuild + credential rotation, not patch-in-place. Patch-in-place leaves attacker-installed implants intact.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2022-24990 discloses the administrator hash before the command-injection step, so any TerraMaster NAS reachable before TOS 4.2.30 must be assumed to have surrendered that credential — upgrading in place preserves the attacker's access and leaves any Deadbolt-class staging on the shares. Recovery planning that names this appliance as the restore source is reading from the system the attacker rooted first, which is why the runbook has to default to rebuild, credential rotation and an offline restore copy.

CVE-2026-18556.name: N-able N-central Authentication Bypass Using an Alternate Path or Channel Vulnerability (CVE-2026-18556)

attack_vector.description: An unauthenticated caller reaches an alternate authentication path on an internet-facing N-central console and receives a privileged administrative session without any credential exchange taking place. The operator then drives N-central's own Take Control remote access and job automation — surfacing under the built-in "MSP Support" operator identity — to reach every endpoint the MSP manages, pushing tooling downstream and enumerating domain controllers. N-able has published neither the vulnerable endpoint nor the alternate channel, so the working request exists only inside the intrusion set.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N in both the CNA CVSS 4.0 vector and NVD's CVSS 3.1; the request is unauthenticated and needs no prior foothold
attack_vector.complexity: high — AC:H in both vectors, but the rating prices in N-able's deliberate withholding of root cause rather than any operational difficulty; CISA recorded exploitation as active on 2026-08-04 and set a three-day remediation window
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered. N-able is the CNA, the CVE Program record carries an empty credits array, and the disclosure came out of Adlumin MDR incident response on a customer environment on 2026-07-31. The observed tradecraft is hands-on-keyboard; no AI-assisted weaponization is reported for this chain.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Apply N-central 2026.3.1 Hotfix 1 (2026.3.1.7, released 2026-08-02) — not the intermediate 2026.2 build, which closed only the originally-reported path — and remove the console from public internet exposure so the bypass has no reachable listener.
prevention.adequacy: Insufficient on its own. Exploitation preceded the hotfix, so any console that was internet-reachable before 2026-08-02 has to be treated as potentially compromised; and the fix an operator would reasonably have applied in April 2026 left the alternate channel open as CVE-2026-18577.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alert when an administrative N-central session appears with no matching credential-validation or MFA event, and correlate Take Control sessions on managed endpoints (Windows event IDs 8192/8193 with 4102 for the account login) against the ticketing system so technician-less sessions surface. Hunt the ten source addresses N-able published on 2026-08-02 and the BASupSrvc_*.log.gz agent logs.
detection.adequacy: Detection is the only operator-side instrument available, because with no public exploit defenders cannot test their own exposure — but N-able's own detection service template states explicitly that a clean result is not evidence the environment was unaffected.

response.what_would_have_worked: Apply the hotfix, pull the console off the internet, enable MFA, audit administrative users, roles and policies for attacker-created entries, sweep managed endpoints for the campaign's persistence artifacts (a Windows service named Cloudflared, an svchost.exe binary in a user's Documents folder), and notify downstream managed customers directly.
response.adequacy: Downstream notification is the load-bearing part: the managed entities whose endpoints were reached have no independent trigger of their own and learn about it only if the provider tells them.

NIST-800-53-IA-2.gap: Every privileged N-central account could be shown to enforce multi-factor authentication and the outcome would be identical, because the CWE-288 alternate path issues an administrative session without the login exchange ever executing — the authenticator is never consulted, so IA-2 produces neither a denial nor a failed-authentication record for anyone to alert on.

NIS2-Art21-supply-chain.gap: Art.21(2)(d) obliges the MSP to manage its own supplier risk, but here the MSP is the supply chain: console takeover propagates Take Control and job automation into every managed customer, and the 24-hour early-warning clock runs at the provider — the entities whose endpoints were reached get no mechanism of their own to detect that their provider's RMM was taken over.

UK-CAF-B2.gap: B2 is scored on how well identities are verified and privileges constrained, and both read green: the bypass emits a fully privileged session under the legitimate built-in "MSP Support" operator, so a self-assessment records tightly controlled and monitored privileged access while an anonymous internet caller holds RMM administration of the whole estate.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: The maturity model measures whether the vendor's current release is deployed inside the target window, and MSPs on 2026.2 or 2026.3.1 satisfied exactly that while staying exploitable through the alternate path; Essential Eight has no concept of a shipped fix that fails to close the defect, so an ML3 score bought nothing between 2026-04-28 and the 2026-08-02 hotfix.

ISO-27001-2022-A.5.15.gap: An access-control policy can only govern the logical access surface the organisation is able to enumerate, and N-able has still not described the alternate authentication channel publicly — so no role definition, access rule, segregation matrix or periodic review in the ISMS could have been written to deny a path nobody outside the vendor can name.

new_control_requirements.name: FLEET-CONTROL-PLANE-ADMIN-PRIVILEGE-TIER
new_control_requirements.description: Administrators of fleet-control-plane systems (MDM/UEM, EDR consoles, identity providers, container orchestrators, configuration management) must be classified as a distinct privilege tier above application admins, with: PAM-jumphost-only access, FIDO2 step-up per session, just-in-time elevation with approval workflow, separate identity from any other admin role, and dedicated PAW (privileged access workstation) hardware. Compliance frameworks must enumerate this tier explicitly rather than collapsing it into 'admin'.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2026-18556 issues a fully privileged N-central session under the built-in "MSP Support" operator without the credential exchange ever executing, so MFA on every privileged account produced neither a denial nor a failed-authentication record, and no access-control rule could be written against a channel N-able still has not described. N-central is a fleet control plane, and jumphost-only reachability for its administrators is the control that removes the anonymous internet path the bypass depends on.

new_control_requirements.name: FLEET-COMPROMISE-IR-PLAYBOOK
new_control_requirements.description: Pre-rehearsed IR playbook for fleet-control-plane compromise including: MDM-pushed certificate revocation, device-trust-state invalidation, configuration-profile audit since the suspected compromise window, downstream device-quarantine criteria, and credential rotation for any account that authenticated through a compromised fleet device during the exposure period.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2026-18556 console takeover inherits Take Control and job automation into every managed customer estate — the operators pushed tooling downstream and enumerated domain controllers — while the managed entities have no independent trigger of their own and learn of it only if the provider tells them. Downstream quarantine criteria, administrative role/policy audit since the compromise window, and rotation of every credential used through a reached endpoint have to be rehearsed at the provider before the event.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2026-18556 was KEV-listed 2026-08-04 with a three-day BOD 26-04 due date against confirmed compromise of customer consoles, and the only build that definitively remediates is N-central 2026.3.1 Hotfix 1 (2026.3.1.7, 2026-08-02) — an MSP running the 2026.2 fix from 2026-04-28 satisfied its patch-maturity target and stayed exploitable. The KEV clock's "documented compensating controls" limb (remove the console from the public internet, enable MFA) is what covers the interval a version-currency measure treats as compliant.

CVE-2026-34486.name: Apache Tomcat Missing Encryption of Sensitive Data Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: An attacker who can reach the Tomcat Tribes cluster receiver (default TCP 4000) sends a framed membership packet that fails EncryptInterceptor decryption. The fix for CVE-2026-29146 moved super.messageReceived(msg) outside the try block, so the interceptor logs the GeneralSecurityException and then forwards the message anyway; the attacker's unencrypted bytes reach ObjectInputStream.readObject() with no ObjectInputFilter, and a Commons Collections gadget chain executes as the Tomcat user. Public exploits deliver this as a one-command Docker reproduction and as a verified Nuclei template.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; no authentication and no cluster membership are required, only network reach to the Tribes receiver
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L with no user interaction; the only real gate is reachability (clustering enabled, EncryptInterceptor configured, receiver port routable), and CISA moved its SSVC technicalImpact from "partial" to "total" within a day of the KEV listing
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered — Bartlomiej Dmitruk of striga.ai found it by reading the CVE-2026-29146 patch and spotting the moved call, reported 2026-03-26 and disclosed 2026-04-09. AI appears only downstream and post-disclosure: one public reproduction repository states its reproduction was completed with the GLM-5.1 model, and Unit 42 places this CVE in the manual toolset of an operator who ran Hermes Agent over DeepSeek autonomously against other targets — so it should not be recorded as AI-autonomously exploited.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Replace the Tomcat JARs with 11.0.21, 10.1.54 or 9.0.117 (commit 1fab40cc) — or the corresponding distribution rebuild — and restart the JVM on every cluster node; for operators pinned to end-of-life 8.5.x, HeroDevs NES 8.5.105 carries the fix. Where a restart cannot be scheduled, restrict TCP 4000 to cluster members or disable clustering.
prevention.adequacy: The upgrade closes the defect cleanly, but the operational trap is what it replaces: on affected builds the configured EncryptInterceptor is not a mitigating control at all, so an operator reasoning from "our cluster traffic is encrypted" will defer the restart on a node that is fully exploitable.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alert on Catalina logs that record an EncryptInterceptor decryption failure immediately followed by normal message processing rather than a drop — that fail-open sequence is the exploitation signature — and on inbound frames beginning with the ASCII membership magic TRIBES-B followed by a Java serialization header ac ed 00 05 from a source that never completed legitimate membership.
detection.adequacy: The log sequence distinguishes a patched node from an unpatched one precisely, but it lives in application logs that are rarely shipped to a SIEM; network-side detection of non-member connections to TCP 4000 is the more practical control.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treat any node that logged the fail-open sequence as executing attacker code: rebuild rather than restart, rotate the credentials and keystores the Tomcat process could read, and hunt for the SNOWLIGHT Linux dropper staged in the China-nexus campaign SoCRadar tracked across 100+ countries.
response.adequacy: Response has to cover the whole cluster: Tribes replicates session state between nodes, so an implant that establishes itself on one member sits inside the trust boundary of all of them.

NIST-800-53-SC-8.gap: SC-8 is evidenced by showing the cryptographic mechanism is configured, and EncryptInterceptor was configured on every exploited host, so the evidence was truthful. The control carries no fail-closed requirement, which means the very configuration that satisfied the assessor is what forwarded attacker plaintext into ObjectInputStream.readObject().

EU-CRA-Art13.gap: Apache met the manufacturer obligations — CVE-2026-29146 was received, fixed and disclosed on schedule — but conformity evidence attests that a security fix shipped, not that the fix fails safe; nothing in an Art.13 technical-documentation review exercises the decryption-failure branch that the remediation itself converted into an unauthenticated RCE path.

UK-CAF-B5.gap: Tribes clustering exists to deliver exactly the resilience outcome B5 rewards, so an organisation that scored well by replicating sessions across nodes is the organisation that gave itself an extra unauthenticated deserialization sink on TCP 4000; B5 has no counterweight obliging the availability mechanism's own trust boundary to be assessed.

AU-Essential-8-App-Hardening.gap: The control is enumerated against user-facing execution surfaces — Office macros, browsers, PDF readers, Java content in browsers, PowerShell — and a server-side cluster receiver appears nowhere on that list, so an ML3 application-hardening assessment leaves a fail-open interceptor listening on a routable port entirely untouched.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.24.gap: This deployment satisfied the cryptographic-use rules twice over: CBC had been replaced per the earlier remediation and interceptor keys were managed. A.8.24 audits algorithm selection, key lifecycle and policy conformance and contains no clause about behaviour when decryption fails, which is the entire vulnerability — correct cryptographic policy, and the cluster still accepted unencrypted attacker input.

new_control_requirements.name: APPSERVER-REMOTING-PROTOCOL-RESTRICTION
new_control_requirements.description: Application servers that expose binary remoting protocols (Oracle WebLogic T3/IIOP, and equivalents) must restrict those protocols to trusted hosts and apply vendor critical patch updates on an accelerated schedule when a remoting flaw is KEV-listed. Place T3/IIOP behind a connection filter (weblogic.security.net.ConnectionFilterImpl) or network ACLs so only known hosts can reach them, never expose the ports to untrusted networks, and apply the Oracle CPU bundle (with server restart) rather than deferring to the next quarterly window. The distinguishing test: from an untrusted network segment, attempt an unauthenticated T3/IIOP connection to a staging WebLogic instance and confirm it is refused at the connection filter before any data is served - a perimeter-firewall + quarterly-patch policy that still leaves T3/IIOP reachable from an internal untrusted segment leaves the unauthenticated data-access path open.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2026-34486 needs only network reach to the Tomcat Tribes cluster receiver (default TCP 4000), where a framed membership packet lands in ObjectInputStream.readObject() with no ObjectInputFilter and a Commons Collections chain runs as the Tomcat user. The remediation is exactly this control's shape: restrict TCP 4000 to cluster members or disable clustering now, then replace the JARs with 11.0.21 / 10.1.54 / 9.0.117 and restart the JVM on every node rather than waiting for a routine window.

new_control_requirements.name: CRYPTO-SUBSYSTEM-CVE-DISCLOSURE
new_control_requirements.description: When a CVE affects a kernel cryptographic subsystem (IPsec, RxRPC, etc.), any compliance controls that rely on that subsystem must be documented as 'not a compensating control' until the CVE is patched. Risk assessments must note this explicitly.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2026-34486 makes EncryptInterceptor fail open — the interceptor logs the GeneralSecurityException and then forwards the attacker's unencrypted bytes anyway — so on affected builds the configured cryptographic mechanism provides no protection at all, and its presence is precisely what satisfied the assessor. Until the fixed release is on every node, an encrypted-cluster configuration must be recorded in the risk assessment as not a compensating control.

new_control_requirements.name: BUG-FAMILY-MITIGATION-PERSISTENCE
new_control_requirements.description: When a CVE patch lands, retain the pre-patch compensating controls (module blacklists, sysctl restrictions) until the patched code has soaked for a stated review period. Patches for one bug in a primitive class can introduce sibling bugs in the same class; the original compensating control may still apply to the sibling.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2026-34486 was created by the fix for CVE-2026-29146, which moved super.messageReceived(msg) outside the try block — the remediation itself converted the decryption-failure branch into an unauthenticated deserialization sink. An operator who dropped the network-level restriction on TCP 4000 once the earlier patch shipped discarded the one control that still worked against the sibling defect, which is why the pre-patch mitigation has to survive a stated soak period.

attack_vector.description: Two HTTP requests against a default install. An unauthenticated GET to /api/v1/auto_login returns a JSON body containing access_token and refresh_token minted at SUPERUSER level to any network caller; the attacker then POSTs Python source to /api/v1/validate/code with an Authorization: Bearer header, and the endpoint hands it to exec(). Because the code runs at function-definition time via decorators, default arguments and annotations, nothing needs to invoke the defined function — the payload executes during parsing, so there is no subsequent flow-run event to correlate against.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; the first request mints the credential the second request uses, so the chain is unauthenticated end to end
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L with no user interaction and no fingerprinting, heap grooming or race; CISA recorded exploitation active, automatable "yes" and technicalImpact "total" on the publication date itself
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered. IBM is both CNA and product owner, the credits array is empty, and no primary source names an external reporter or any AI tooling. The AI dimension is contextual rather than attributional: Langflow is itself an agent-orchestration platform, and Unit 42 documented an operator running Hermes Agent over DeepSeek to autonomously hunt exposed Langflow instances while exploiting a different CVE. PoC development for this chain in late July 2026 was conventional human work.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Upgrade Langflow OSS to 1.10.1 from PyPI and restart the service. Where an upgrade cannot happen immediately, set LANGFLOW_AUTO_LOGIN=false with explicit LANGFLOW_SUPERUSER credentials, bind the listener to 127.0.0.1 behind an authenticating reverse proxy, and remove internet exposure.
prevention.adequacy: The upgrade closes the chain, but the interim mitigation only breaks the unauthenticated half: /api/v1/validate/code still executes submitted Python for any caller holding a valid token, converting an unauthenticated RCE into an authenticated one. Remediation verification also has to test the chain rather than a component, since the CVE composes CVE-2026-9103 and CVE-2026-8481.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alert on any HTTP 200 from /api/v1/auto_login to a source outside the expected client range, and on a POST to /api/v1/validate/code from that same source within seconds carrying Python source rather than a flow-component definition. Back it with process telemetry: the uvicorn worker spawning shell or python children, or opening outbound connections, with no user-initiated flow execution logged.
detection.adequacy: The two-request pattern is unmistakable, but definition-time execution means the application produces no flow-run record to correlate against, so anything relying on Langflow's own execution logging will see nothing at all.

response.what_would_have_worked: Rotate every secret the Langflow host held — model API keys, data-connector credentials, downstream service tokens — before rebuilding, and treat the endpoint as structurally hostile going forward rather than as a patched surface.
response.adequacy: Secret rotation is the whole response: the Langflow host is the credential concentrator for the organisation's AI pipelines, so evicting the code without rotating leaves the attacker everything worth taking. The same /api/v1/validate/code sink was already KEV-listed as CVE-2025-3248, so plan for recurrence.

NIST-800-53-CM-7.gap: Least functionality closes what the organisation does not need, and /api/v1/validate/code is documented, intended Langflow behaviour that exists specifically to run user-supplied Python for flow components — a fully baselined host still exposes an interpreter over HTTP, because CM-7 has no way to distinguish a product's core feature from a surplus service.

EU-AI-Act-Art-15.gap: Art.15 is the EU instrument that explicitly names AI accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity, but it binds only systems classified as high-risk under the Act; an internally deployed low-code orchestration platform generally falls outside that classification, so the AI-security regulation does not reach the host holding the API keys, model endpoints and data connectors for every downstream AI workload.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: B4 assesses secure configuration against operator-controllable hardening, and the exploitable state here is the vendor default — LANGFLOW_AUTO_LOGIN issuing SUPERUSER tokens to anonymous callers is shipped behaviour, not drift from a baseline — so a B4-conformant deployment of an unmodified supported release was fully exploitable on day one.

AU-Essential-8-App-Hardening.gap: The enumerated hardening targets are Office macros, browsers, PDF readers, .NET and PowerShell; a Python AI-orchestration server whose default configuration publishes an exec() endpoint is not among them, so an ML3 maturity score says nothing whatever about the most dangerous execution surface in the organisation's AI stack.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.28.gap: Secure coding governs the organisation's own development lifecycle, and Langflow arrives as a third-party OSS package pulled from PyPI and dropped into a pipeline — nothing in A.8.28 obliges anyone to review an imported dependency's server-side execution endpoints or its anonymous token-minting route before exposing them to a network.

new_control_requirements.name: AI-APP-BUILDER-EXECUTION-ENDPOINT-AUTH-AND-SANDBOX
new_control_requirements.description: A visual LLM app/agent builder (Langflow, Flowise, and similar) must authenticate every endpoint that can reach a code-execution path - validate-code, flow-build, flow-run, public-flow endpoints - and must never run flow-supplied or request-supplied code through a compile-and-run / dynamic-evaluation path with host privileges. Place the builder behind authenticated access control, never expose it to untrusted networks, and sandbox any code the platform executes on a user's behalf (no filesystem/network/process access beyond the flow's intent). The distinguishing test: send an unauthenticated request to each flow validate/build/run endpoint on a staging instance with a payload that attempts a non-flow action (a shell or network call) and confirm it is refused before any code runs - paper 'AI platform' policies that leave a public endpoint wired to a code-execution sink still permit unauthenticated RCE.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2026-9198 chains an unauthenticated GET /api/v1/auto_login that mints SUPERUSER tokens to any network caller with a POST to /api/v1/validate/code that hands submitted Python straight to exec() at definition time. The vendor-recommended interim fix only breaks the token half — the exec() sink still runs for any token holder — and the same validate/code endpoint was already KEV-listed as CVE-2025-3248, so authenticating every code-reaching endpoint and sandboxing the executor is the structural remediation the 1.10.1 upgrade does not deliver.

new_control_requirements.name: AI-ML-DEVELOPER-TOOLING-INVENTORY
new_control_requirements.description: Organizations using AI/ML systems must maintain a separate inventory of developer-tooling control planes (notebook servers, experiment trackers, model registries, vector-DB admin UIs, agent frameworks) with: exposed network endpoints (HTTP, WebSocket, gRPC), authentication mechanism per endpoint, blast-radius mapping (which model artifacts/training data/production deployments are reachable from each tool), and patch SLA tier separate from generic application patching.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2026-9198 is exploitable in the shipped default state of a Langflow OSS package pulled from PyPI and dropped into a pipeline, and the required response is rotating every model API key, data-connector credential and downstream token the host held — it is the credential concentrator for the organisation's AI workloads. Nothing enumerated its anonymous token-minting route, its authentication mechanism per endpoint, or what a compromise reaches, which is the inventory and blast-radius mapping this control requires.

CVE-2026-18577.name: N-able N-central Authentication Bypass Using an Alternate Path or Channel Vulnerability (CVE-2026-18577)

attack_vector.description: The same authentication-bypass class as CVE-2026-18556, reached through the alternate channel that N-central 2026.2's fix left open. An unauthenticated request yields an administrative console session and account takeover on any build through 2026.3.1; the operator then opens Take Control sessions to managed endpoints under the default "MSP Support" identity, registers a Cloudflare tunnel as a Windows service for outbound-only persistence that survives revoking N-central access, and moves laterally toward domain controllers. N-able has published no root cause, so no defender-side reproduction exists.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; the request is unauthenticated, and the CVSS 4.0 vector adds SC:L/SI:L/SA:L to record that impact propagates past the console into managed estates
attack_vector.complexity: high — AC:H in both the CNA CVSS 4.0 (8.2) and NVD CVSS 3.1 (8.1) vectors, but the same record carries E:A (exploit maturity ATTACKED): the complexity is knowledge-gated and the knowledge is already in attacker hands
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered. N-able's Adlumin MDR detected the activity on 2026-07-31 after customers reported a spike in N-central licensing errors; the credits array is empty, consistent with vendor-side incident response. Huntress documented interactive hands-on-keyboard tradecraft — the opposite profile from the agentic exploitation Unit 42 recorded against other 2026 KEV entries.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Apply N-central 2026.3.1 Hotfix 1 (2026.3.1.7, released 2026-08-02), the only build the CNA declares unaffected, and remove the console from public internet exposure. No workaround blocks the bypass itself.
prevention.adequacy: Necessary and provably insufficient: exploitation of fully-patched 2026.3.1 consoles was underway from 2026-08-01, a day before the hotfix existed. Any console internet-reachable before 2026-08-02 needs a compromise assessment, not a patch.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alert on administrative console access with no corresponding authentication or MFA event followed immediately by user, role or policy modification; on Take Control sessions under "MSP Support" with no ticket behind them (endpoint events 8192/8193 plus 4102); and on registration of a new Windows service for a Cloudflare tunnel on managed endpoints.
detection.adequacy: The cloudflared persistence is the detection problem: it makes outbound-only encrypted connections that generate no inbound firewall event and blend with legitimate Cloudflare traffic, and by N-able's own statement it outlives revoking N-central access.

response.what_would_have_worked: Hotfix, then hunt: pull the console off the internet, enable MFA, audit administrative users, roles and policies for attacker-created entries, sweep managed endpoints for the Cloudflared service and the svchost.exe binary in Documents, check BASupSrvc_*.log.gz for technician-less sessions, and check the attacker domains and ten IP addresses N-able published.
response.adequacy: The vendor's own CVE-2026-18577-detection service template automates part of the endpoint sweep but carries an explicit caveat that a clean result does not guarantee the environment was unaffected — so a negative sweep cannot close the incident.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: SI-2 is evidenced by "the vendor's fix is installed", which organisations deploying N-central 2026.2 on 2026-04-28 legitimately held while remaining fully exploitable; nothing in the control obliges an operator to verify that a supplier's patch actually eliminated the defect class, and with no published root cause there was no operator-side test capable of showing the difference.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: Patch management assumes the vendor fix ends the exposure, but here the fix defined the exposure window: attackers were working against fully-patched 2026.3.1 consoles from 2026-08-01 and 2026.3.1.7 only shipped on 2026-08-02, so an essential or important entity sat inside the 24-hour early-warning obligation while its patch-compliance KPI read 100 percent.

UK-CAF-C1.gap: Monitoring is the one objective that produced anything here — N-able's own MDR raised the detection that started the investigation — and it still barely held; the operators' cloudflared persistence is outbound-only, encrypted and registered as a service, so a C1 posture resting on perimeter and inbound-connection telemetry would have generated nothing, and the tunnel survives revoking console access.

AU-Essential-8-MFA.gap: ML3 requires MFA for privileged users and N-able's post-incident guidance repeats the advice, but an alternate-channel bypass delivers an already-authenticated administrative session, so the second factor is never requested; MSPs that had enforced MFA on every technician account were compromised regardless, and their assessed maturity had no bearing on the outcome.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: Technical vulnerability management runs on vendor advisories, and the advisory the ISMS would have consumed — the CVE-2026-18556 fix shipped in 2026.2 — was itself the source of the residual exposure; no asset inventory, CVSS triage, patch SLA or periodic review distinguishes a complete fix from an incomplete one when the vendor has published no root cause to evaluate against.

new_control_requirements.name: INCOMPLETE-PATCH-SEQUENCE-SEVERITY-MULTIPLIER
new_control_requirements.description: Vulnerability-management programs must apply a severity multiplier when a CVE is the Nth in an incomplete-patch sequence on the same primitive (third MOTW bypass, second AMSI bypass, etc.). Framework controls treating each CVE as discrete obscure the structural defect; the Nth CVE in a sequence implies that future bypasses on the same primitive are likely.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2026-18577 is by definition the second CVE on the same N-central authentication primitive — an incomplete patch for CVE-2026-18556 that left the alternate channel open through 2026.3.1 — and attackers were working fully-patched 2026.3.1 consoles from 2026-08-01, a day before 2026.3.1.7 existed. Scoring it as a discrete item is what let "the vendor's fix is installed" and a 100-percent patch KPI stay true throughout the exposure window.

new_control_requirements.name: FLEET-CONTROL-PLANE-ADMIN-PRIVILEGE-TIER
new_control_requirements.description: Administrators of fleet-control-plane systems (MDM/UEM, EDR consoles, identity providers, container orchestrators, configuration management) must be classified as a distinct privilege tier above application admins, with: PAM-jumphost-only access, FIDO2 step-up per session, just-in-time elevation with approval workflow, separate identity from any other admin role, and dedicated PAW (privileged access workstation) hardware. Compliance frameworks must enumerate this tier explicitly rather than collapsing it into 'admin'.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2026-18577's alternate channel hands the caller an already-authenticated administrative session, so the second factor is never requested and MSPs that had enforced MFA on every technician account were compromised regardless of their assessed maturity. Only treating the RMM console as its own privilege tier — jumphost-only reachability and per-session step-up rather than login-time MFA — takes the anonymous internet caller off the path.

new_control_requirements.name: FLEET-COMPROMISE-IR-PLAYBOOK
new_control_requirements.description: Pre-rehearsed IR playbook for fleet-control-plane compromise including: MDM-pushed certificate revocation, device-trust-state invalidation, configuration-profile audit since the suspected compromise window, downstream device-quarantine criteria, and credential rotation for any account that authenticated through a compromised fleet device during the exposure period.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2026-18577 operators registered a Cloudflare tunnel as a Windows service on managed endpoints — outbound-only, encrypted, generating no inbound event, and by N-able's own statement surviving revocation of N-central access — so console remediation and inbound monitoring both end nothing. Downstream device-quarantine criteria and rotation of every credential used through a reached endpoint during the exposure window are the steps that actually close the residual access.

CVE-2026-20316.name: Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center Use of Hard-coded Password Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: A static username and password compiled into the Cisco Secure FMC appliance image authenticate a low-privileged account through the ordinary web interface, so an unauthenticated remote attacker simply logs in and reads device inventory, firewall policy and management-plane configuration. There is no exploit to write — possession of the credential is the exploit. Cisco raised its own Security Impact Rating to High because the account can be chained with other FMC vulnerabilities to escalate privileges; the follow-on privileged path invokes package_info.pl as root against a temporary file, leaving /var/tmp/license.tmp behind.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; the credential is vendor-embedded rather than operator-held, so from the attacker's side no privilege is required at all
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L with no user interaction; authenticating with a known static password requires no technique, and Cisco PSIRT confirmed in July 2026 that at least one party already holds it
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered — Cisco's advisory cisco-sa-fmc-static-cred-BET3Cjh credits Jimi Sebree of Horizon3.ai, and Horizon3 built a NodeZero Rapid Response test instead of publishing a PoC. A second, independent discovery track exists: a threat actor located the same credential before or concurrently with the coordinated report, which is the expected outcome for embedded credentials extractable offline from an appliance image. No AI tooling is credited on any track.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Apply the per-train hotfix package from Cisco's advisory (7.0 → GB-7.0.9.1-3, 7.2 → HL-7.2.11.1-4, 7.4 → HG-7.4.7.1-3, 7.6 → CY-7.6.5.1-2, 7.7 → AM-7.7.12.1-2, 10.0 → P-10.0.1.1-2) and keep the FMC management interface off the public internet on a dedicated management network.
prevention.adequacy: Incomplete by construction. Cisco states plainly there are no workarounds — the credential cannot be disabled, rotated or removed by the operator — and no hotfix is published for the 7.3 train even though 7.3.0 through 7.3.1.2 appear on Cisco's own affected list, so those deployments cannot reach a fixed state inside the three-day KEV window without a version migration.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Run Cisco's own compromise check from expert mode — zgrep "package_info.*license" /var/log/messages* — and look for /var/tmp/license.tmp on the appliance. Alongside that, alert on successful web-interface logins by a local account with no operational history in the deployment, sourced from outside the management network.
detection.adequacy: The zgrep hit and the license.tmp artifact are reliable after the fact, but the login itself succeeds normally and produces a legitimate-looking session rather than a failed-authentication pattern, so nothing in ordinary authentication monitoring flags it.

response.what_would_have_worked: Run the compromise check before declaring a patched FMC clean, assume the read access already occurred and treat device inventory and policy as disclosed reconnaissance for the whole perimeter, and review the FMC for the follow-on privilege-escalation chain Cisco warns the account enables.
response.adequacy: Because exploitation preceded the advisory, patch-then-verify is the only defensible order; and the disclosed data — the management plane of the firewall estate — cannot be rotated the way a credential can.

NIST-800-53-AC-2.gap: Account management operates over accounts the operator can enumerate, assign owners to, review and remove; this one lives inside the vendor's appliance image, never appears in an FMC user review, and cannot be disabled or rotated — a flawless AC-2 recertification of the firewall management platform enumerates none of the accounts that mattered.
