An organisation perfectly compliant on the timeframe still had a root-level pre-authentication RCE reachable — and hosting control panels are routinely scoped out of Essential Eight application inventories entirely.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.28.gap: Attacker-controlled input concatenated into a shell invocation inside a logging routine is the textbook A.8.28 defect, but the control binds the certified organisation's own development. For an operator running CWP it produces no assurance about login/index.php, and the certification scope typically excludes the vendor code where the CVSS 9.8 injection actually lives.

new_control_requirements.name: CONTROL-PANEL-PLUGIN-USER-SURFACE-MUST-NOT-REACH-ROOT-OPERATIONS
new_control_requirements.description: On a multi-tenant hosting control panel (cPanel/WHM and similar), no function reachable from the unprivileged user-end plugin surface may execute as root or run tenant-supplied scripts with host privileges. Privileged operations must live behind an administrative trust boundary with their own authorization, and the user-facing surface must only request them through a constrained, validated interface. The distinguishing test: from an ordinary tenant account on a staging panel, invoke each user-end plugin function (including enable/disable and configuration calls) with a payload that attempts a root-level action, and confirm the action is refused before any privileged code runs - a panel that passes an OS-hardening audit but wires a tenant-callable function to a root operation still grants user-to-root escalation.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2022-44877 injects shell metacharacters through the login parameter of CWP's /login/index.php and the command runs as root, because the multi-tenant hosting panel's whole request-handling surface — including the pre-authentication login page — executes in a root context. UK CAF B4 offers no secure-configuration lever here since that login page must stay internet-reachable for the shared-hosting customers it serves; separating the panel's caller-reachable functions from root operations is the only structural answer.

new_control_requirements.name: DEVICE-MANAGEMENT-GATEWAY-CONFIG-ENDPOINT-AUTH-INPUT-NEUTRALIZATION
new_control_requirements.description: A device-management / MDM gateway (Ivanti Sentry, MobileIron, and similar) is a privileged root-execution surface at the network perimeter; every config/message endpoint must authenticate the caller and must neutralize OS-command input before any shell or process invocation, and the appliance must never be left unmanaged with externally reachable endpoints. Require: inventory all gateway HTTP endpoints, ensure they are managed (mTLS with the management server or restricted HTTPS) so config interfaces are not externally reachable, neutralize OS-command metacharacters at every message handler, and remediate any confirmed-exploited unauthenticated root RCE on a KEV-tied expedited clock with mandatory forensic triage of exposed instances. The distinguishing test: send an unauthenticated request carrying an OS-command metacharacter payload to each gateway config endpoint on a staging instance and confirm it is refused before any command runs — paper 'appliance hardened' policies that leave an unmanaged instance's config endpoint wired to a root command sink still permit unauthenticated root RCE.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2022-44877 is the same primitive this control governs on a different management surface: an unauthenticated request to a network-exposed management panel's own endpoint, whose failed-login value is written into a shell context unescaped so bash performs command substitution as root. SI-10 names the missing neutralization exactly but binds the operator's own system, and a deploying organisation running third-party CWP has no input-validation hook to insert ahead of the 0.9.8.1147 vendor fix.

CVE-2022-41080.name: Microsoft Exchange Server Privilege Escalation Vulnerability (CVE-2022-41080)

attack_vector.description: With any valid mailbox credential the attacker authenticates at POST /owa/auth.owa, then POSTs application/soap+xml WSMan traffic to /owa/<mailbox>%40outlook.com/powershell carrying the X-OWA-ExplicitLogonUser header, with the public poc.py proxying pypsrp requests through a local listener on 127.0.0.1:13337. The OWA-side server-side request forgery reaches the backend Remote PowerShell endpoint — routing around the September 2022 ProxyNotShell URL-rewrite rule, which only matched (?=.*autodiscover)(?=.*powershell) — and CVE-2022-41082 then converts that reachable endpoint into code execution as SYSTEM.
attack_vector.privileges_required: low — PR:L; one valid mailbox account obtained by password spray, phishing or a prior breach, with no privileged account and no user interaction required
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L: the public poc.py automates login, proxy setup and cmdlet execution end to end, and the chain lands on any server missing the November 2022 SU, including servers that applied the September URL-rewrite mitigation
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered — MSRC credits coordinated human research (rskvp93, Q5Ca and nxhoang99 with VcsLab of Viettel Cyber Security, and zcgonvh with 360 noah lab). Weaponization was human too: the exploit script was a threat-actor artifact recovered by a researcher, and CrowdStrike attributed the OWASSRF intrusions to Play ransomware.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Install the November 8, 2022 security update KB5019758 (builds 15.00.1497.044, 15.01.2375.037, 15.01.2507.016, 15.02.0986.036, 15.02.1118.020) and restart, and enforce MFA on every mailbox rather than only on privileged accounts, since the chain begins with an ordinary user's credential. Where the SU cannot be applied immediately, disable OWA outright.
prevention.adequacy: The SU was available two months before the KEV listing, but MSRC shipped the CVE with a temporal vector of E:U/RL:O/RC:C — exploit unproven — which is precisely what deprioritises an Important-rated Exchange elevation in a patch queue. Applying Microsoft's own September mitigation instead of the SU left the server exploitable, so 'mitigated' was never a safe proxy for 'not vulnerable'.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Collect the Remote PowerShell proxy logs under V15\Logging\CmdletInfra\Powershell-Proxy\Http and flag Rps_Http rows whose ClientInfo is neither empty, 'Microsoft WinRM Client' nor 'Exchange BackEnd Probes' — CrowdStrike's Rps_Http-IOC.ps1 does exactly that and recovers the original external source IP and the proxied hop chain. Alongside it: frontend IIS rows showing POST to /owa/*/powershell answered 200, and PowerShell running as a child of w3wp.exe.
detection.adequacy: Nominally required and practically absent: the only high-fidelity source is a non-default, non-forwarded Exchange log that standard collection does not ingest, while the mainstream telemetry that is collected was cleared by the actor as part of Play's anti-forensics.

response.what_would_have_worked: Hunt the Rps_Http logs for anomalous ClientInfo rows, look for renamed Plink binaries, AnyDesk installations and cleared Windows event logs, reset mailbox credentials across the tenant because the entry point is an ordinary user account, and rebuild hosts where post-exploitation tooling is found.
response.adequacy: Play used this chain for initial access rather than as the objective, so the response scope is the whole environment downstream of the Exchange server, not the mail server alone — and the anti-forensic log clearing means the eviction decision has to be made on partial evidence.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: SI-2 explicitly permits a documented mitigation while a patch is scheduled, and Microsoft's September 2022 URL-rewrite rule was the sanctioned one. This chain was built to route around that exact rule by reaching Remote PowerShell through /owa/ instead of /autodiscover/, so an organisation following SI-2 correctly — mitigation applied, patch queued — was still fully exploitable; the mitigation escape hatch is what held the window open.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: Art.21 accepts compensating controls as interim risk treatment, and the compensating control here was the very rewrite rule the exploit defeats by design. The risk register would have shown a treated risk while the same servers were Play's initial-access route — a patch-management regime that reasons about mitigations rather than about the specific bypassed request path cannot detect that state.

UK-CAF-B2.gap: B2 is the control that actually gates this CVE and the one that fails: the chain needs a single valid mailbox credential at /owa/auth.owa, and OWA accepting single-factor logins from the internet supplies it. B2 requires authorised-user access control but does not force step-up authentication on internet-facing webmail, so a sprayed password converts a post-authentication Exchange flaw into an unauthenticated-equivalent path to SYSTEM.

AU-Essential-8-MFA.gap: MFA would have broken the precondition, but at lower maturity levels it is required only for privileged users and selected internet-facing services rather than for every mailbox. Because this CVE escalates from ANY unprivileged mailbox account to SYSTEM, partial coverage that exempts ordinary users leaves the exploit chain entirely intact.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.16.gap: The only high-fidelity detection lives in Exchange's Rps_Http Remote PowerShell proxy logs — a non-default, non-forwarded source that standard A.8.16 monitoring programmes do not collect — while the actor cleared the Windows event logs that those programmes do cover.

new_control_requirements.name: MITIGATION-ACTIVE-PATCH-PENDING-VERDICT-CLASS
new_control_requirements.description: Compliance verdicts must distinguish three states: (a) binary patch deployed (vulnerability eliminated), (b) vendor-mitigation rule active, no binary patch (residual risk: any defect in the mitigation rule reopens the vulnerability), (c) no mitigation, no patch (full exposure). Audit reports must surface (b) as a distinct compensating-control state with an associated time-bound action item, not as a 'patched per SLA' outcome.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2022-41080 was built to route around Microsoft's own September 2022 ProxyNotShell URL-rewrite mitigation, which matched only (?=.*autodiscover)(?=.*powershell), by reaching Remote PowerShell through /owa/ instead — so servers carrying the sanctioned mitigation with KB5019758 queued recorded a treated risk under SI-2 while Play used them for initial access. This is the residual-risk state the control names: mitigation-rule active with no binary patch is not a 'patched per SLA' outcome.

new_control_requirements.name: OWA-PER-REQUEST-SIEM-INGESTION
new_control_requirements.description: Exchange OWA per-request access logs (not just authentication events) must be forwarded to an external SIEM with at least 90-day retention. Authentication-only logging misses XSS-stage telemetry — the malicious request flows over an already-authenticated session.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2022-41080's exploitation flows over an already-authenticated OWA session, so the only high-fidelity evidence is per-request Exchange telemetry — the Rps_Http rows under V15\Logging\CmdletInfra\Powershell-Proxy\Http whose anomalous ClientInfo values recover the original external source IP — a non-default, non-forwarded log that standard monitoring never ingests. The Windows event logs a conformant A.8.16 programme does collect were cleared by the actor as part of Play's anti-forensics, leaving authentication-only ingestion blind to the whole intrusion.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2022-41080 was KEV-listed on 2023-01-10 with confirmed Play ransomware use, two months after KB5019758 shipped, and MSRC published it with a temporal vector of E:U/RL:O/RC:C — exploit unproven — which is precisely what deprioritises an Important-rated Exchange elevation in an SI-2 patch queue. Only a KEV-triggered deadline overrides the vendor's own exploitability rating once in-wild use is confirmed.

CVE-2023-21674.name: Microsoft Windows Advanced Local Procedure Call (ALPC) Privilege Escalation Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: From a sandboxed or medium-integrity process the attacker creates a private namespace via NtCreatePrivateNamespace, opens an ALPC port, calls NtWaitForWorkViaWorkerFactory with a WORKER_FACTORY_DEFERRED_WORK whose AlpcSendMessageFlags is 0x20000 (ALPC_MSGFLG_SYNC_REQUEST), lets the sending thread terminate, then closes the port so cleanup dereferences the stale WaitingThread pointer in the freed _KALPC_MESSAGE. Reclaiming that allocation with a fresh _ETHREAD — Theori sprays threads via repeated showOpenFilePicker() calls inside Chrome's file-picker process — turns the dangling pointer into arbitrary kernel read/write through LpcpCopyRequestData, escaping the browser sandbox into kernel scope.
attack_vector.privileges_required: low — PR:L with AV:L; the attacker must already be executing code on the host, which in the observed campaign came from a browser exploit, so this is the second stage of a chain rather than an entry point
attack_vector.complexity: low per the vector (AC:L), but in practice a use-after-free race requiring heap grooming — unreliable attempts bugcheck the machine with 0x50 rather than failing quietly, and only a trigger reproducer is public; the weaponized escalation stayed inside a commercial intelligence feed
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered — Avast's anti-exploit engine flagged the behaviour of a live attack using the bug to escape a Chromium sandbox, and MSRC credits Jan Vojtěšek, Milánek and Przemek Gmerek. Defensive telemetry rather than proactive research or AI tooling; Avast stated it never recovered the full infection chain.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Install the January 10, 2023 cumulative update for the affected train (KB5022297, KB5022289, KB5022286, KB5022282, KB5022287, KB5022303, KB5022291, KB5022352 / KB5022346) and reboot. For Windows 8.1, Windows RT 8.1 and Server 2012 R2 this update landed on their end-of-support date — it is the last servicing those hosts receive, so migration to a supported train is the only forward-looking control there.
prevention.adequacy: The fix and the KEV listing arrived on the same day, and no live-patch or hotpatch path applies, so remediation costs a reboot on every endpoint. On the 8.1 and Server 2012 R2 estate prevention has no achievable end state at all: this update closes this CVE and no future kernel defect will ever be fixed on those hosts.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Watch for a sandboxed or medium-integrity process creating a private namespace and ALPC port then issuing NtWaitForWorkViaWorkerFactory with AlpcSendMessageFlags=0x20000, for showOpenFilePicker used as a thread spray, and — the cheapest signal available — for unexplained 0x50 PAGE_FAULT_IN_NONPAGED_AREA bugchecks faulting in nt!SeCreateClientSecurity on endpoints below the January 2023 patch level.
detection.adequacy: Detection was required and is close to unattainable: the exploit runs entirely in memory as a sandbox escape, Avast found it only through anti-exploit behavioural telemetry, and the defender's most reliable artefact is the crash left behind by attempts that fail rather than by ones that succeed.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treat a confirmed escape as full host compromise — the scope change to kernel puts every credential and secret on the endpoint in play — reimage rather than clean, and hunt for the browser-side first stage that supplied code execution in the first place.
response.adequacy: Response is the only phase that addresses the chain rather than the link: fixing the ALPC use-after-free leaves the renderer-level exploit that delivered it entirely untouched.

NIST-800-53-SC-39.gap: SC-39 assumes the operating system supplies a correct separate-execution-domain primitive and the security posture inherits that correctness. The defect is inside the primitive — a use-after-free in the kernel's own ALPC message handling — so the browser sandbox boundary that the CVSS S:C flag records collapses into kernel scope, and no amount of SC-39 implementation effort by the operator addresses a bug in the isolation mechanism itself.

NIS2-Art21-incident-handling.gap: The 24-hour early-warning clock starts when the entity becomes aware of a significant incident, but this exploit runs in memory as a sandbox escape and leaves almost no operator-visible artefact — Avast found it through anti-exploit telemetry, not a customer-detectable event, and never recovered the full chain. An entity compromised this way most likely never generates the awareness that starts the clock.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: B4 rests on running vendor-supported, currently-patched platforms, and this fix landed on Windows 8.1's end-of-support date and in Server 2012 R2's final year. For estates that include those trains, B4's vulnerability-management outcome has no achievable end state — the update that fixes the ALPC use-after-free is also the last one those hosts will ever receive, so the residual risk is architectural rather than a patching backlog.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Essential Eight patches applications on one clock (48 hours for internet-facing services, a tight cadence for browsers) and operating systems on a considerably slower one. This bug is reached through the browser but fixed only by an OS cumulative update, so an organisation fully compliant with both clocks still leaves the sandbox-escape half of the chain unpatched for the whole OS window — the seam between the two is exactly what a browser-to-kernel chain exploits.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: A.8.8 schedules remediation from a risk classification, and this presents as a local low-privilege escalation that Microsoft rated Important, with an AV:L vector that pushes it down any score-ordered queue. It was nevertheless the first in-the-wild Windows kernel vulnerability of 2023 and reached KEV on the day it was patched — the risk-rating step actively deprioritises the item exploitation telemetry says to patch first, because it has no exploitation-aware category.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2023-21674 reached CISA KEV on 2023-01-10 — the same day it was patched and while already in use as a Chromium sandbox escape into kernel scope — yet it presents as an AV:L 'Important' local elevation that an A.8.8 risk-classification queue schedules behind remote criticals. The KEV listing is the only exploitation-aware signal that inverts that ordering, and no live-patch or hotpatch path exists to shorten the reboot-bearing cumulative-update rollout.

new_control_requirements.name: EOL-ASSET-DECOMMISSION
new_control_requirements.description: Network-reachable end-of-life devices with no vendor patch path must be isolated and decommissioned within a bounded window; mandatory compensating segmentation applies until removal since no remediation exists.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2023-21674's fix for Windows 8.1, Windows RT 8.1 and Server 2012 R2 (KB5022352 / KB5022346) landed on their end-of-support date, so those hosts took their last kernel servicing with this CVE and no future ALPC-class defect will ever be fixed on them. UK CAF B4's vulnerability-management outcome has no achievable end state on that estate — the residual risk is architectural, and only a bounded isolate-and-retire window with compensating segmentation closes it.

CVE-2018-5430.name: TIBCO JasperReports Server Information Disclosure Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: Any authenticated user, regardless of role, requests /jasperserver-pro/flow.html?_flowId=sampleFlow&page=../../../js.jdbc.properties; — the Spring web flow passes the page parameter unvalidated into resource resolution (traced from HttpServletRequestParameterMap.getAttribute() to DirResourceSet.getResource()), so the traversal escapes the JSP directory, and the trailing semicolon suppresses the automatic .jsp suffixing so the raw datasource credential file is returned. The same primitive loads administrator-only JSPs such as jsp/modules/administer/adminImport and awsConfiguration from a low-privileged account and, where a file can be uploaded, includes it for code execution.
attack_vector.privileges_required: low — PR:L; any authenticated session, including a read-only report consumer with no data entitlements. The published exploit stresses that it works regardless of user permissions
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L: a single GET, no race and no chaining. Note the scoring divergence in the record: the researcher rated the file read 7.7 with confidentiality impact only, while NVD's 8.8 carries I:H/A:H because the same primitive reaches JSP local file inclusion
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered — Hector Monsegur of Rhino Security Labs found it through manual source-and-sink analysis of a Spring web flow and disclosed it to TIBCO on 2017-12-22. No AI tooling in discovery or exploit development, and none credited by researcher or vendor.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Upgrade to JasperReports Server 6.2.5, 6.3.4 or 6.4.3 per TIBCO's 2018-04-17 advisory — and plan past that point, because 6.4.3 is still listed as affected by CVE-2018-18809 — then rotate the reporting datasource credentials, since an upgrade does not invalidate what an attacker already read.
prevention.adequacy: The fix has existed since April 2018 and the CVE still reached KEV four and a half years later, so patch availability was never the constraint. Prevention fails on inventory: embedded BI middleware rarely appears on the register that drives patching, and CISA published no campaign detail that would have prompted a search.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alert on authenticated GETs to flow.html carrying _flowId=sampleFlow with ../ in the page parameter, on page values terminated with a semicolon, and on any low-privileged account reaching resources under jsp/modules/administer/; downstream, on reuse of the js.jdbc.properties credentials against the reporting database from an unexpected host.
detection.adequacy: The request signature is distinctive, but the payoff is a read that leaves no server-side change — without web access-log review the compromise is invisible, and the credential reuse that follows looks like ordinary database activity.

response.what_would_have_worked: Rotate the datasource credentials and every other secret stored under the web application, review the reporting database for connections from unexpected sources, and check the web root for uploaded files paired with a page=../../../<name>; inclusion request.
response.adequacy: Credential rotation is effectively the whole of remediation: the vulnerability's real product is the contents of js.jdbc.properties, and upgrading leaves those credentials exactly as valid as before.

NIST-800-53-AC-3.gap: AC-3 presumes the mediator is invoked on every protected operation, and JasperReports Server's role model is such a mediator — but the sampleFlow page parameter routes a low-privileged report consumer straight into administrator JSPs without ever consulting it. The authorisation decision AC-3 audits is correct and simply never reached.

NIS2-Art21-vulnerability-handling.gap: Art.21 vulnerability handling assumes a forward-only flow of disclose, patch, close, yet this defect was fixed in April 2018 and was still being exploited well enough for a December 2022 KEV listing. The failure mode is inventory rather than cadence: JasperReports Server is embedded BI middleware that rarely appears on the asset register an Art.21 programme runs from.

UK-CAF-B2.gap: B2 assumes least-privilege accounts bound the damage of a compromised login, but here ANY authenticated account — including a read-only report viewer with no data entitlements — reads the datasource credential file. The privilege actually obtained is unrelated to the privilege granted, so the access model B2 assesses gives no signal about the exposure.

AU-Essential-8-App-Hardening.gap: User application hardening is scoped to user-agent software on endpoints — browsers, Office macros, PDF readers — and has nothing to say about server-side Java reporting middleware. A Spring web flow concatenating an unvalidated page parameter into a filesystem path sits entirely outside that control's surface, so high maturity here reduces the attack surface not at all.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.28.gap: The defect — attacker input flowing into path resolution, plus a suffix-appending 'defence' that a trailing semicolon defeats — is precisely what A.8.28 exists to prevent, but the control binds the certified organisation's own development rather than TIBCO's, and the scope statement typically excludes the vendor code where the traversal lives.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2018-5430 was fixed by TIBCO in April 2018 (JasperReports Server 6.2.5 / 6.3.4 / 6.4.3) and still earned a CISA KEV listing on 2022-12-29, four and a half years later, so patch availability was never the constraint. NIS2 Art.21 vulnerability handling assumes a forward-only disclose-patch-close flow with no event that re-opens a closed item, and a KEV-tied mitigation deadline is exactly that missing trigger for embedded BI middleware that never reached the asset register.

CVE-2018-18809.name: TIBCO JasperReports Library Directory Traversal Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: A single GET to /jasperserver-pro/reportresource/reportresource/?resource=net/sf/jasperreports/../../../../js.jdbc.properties. The reportresource service requires the resource value to begin with net/sf/jasperreports/ and runs that prefix check before any canonicalisation, so ../../../../ appended after the approved prefix escapes the intended directory. Two primitives are published: the bare traversal returns a directory listing of the application root, and appending a filename returns its contents — with the datasource credential file as the demonstrated target, confirmed by metadata.jdbc.driverClassName and metadata.hibernate.dialect in the response.
attack_vector.privileges_required: low per NVD's PR:L scoring, but the discovering researcher reports no authentication or authorisation precondition at all — treat unauthenticated traversal traffic against this endpoint as in scope
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L: one deterministic GET, no race and no chaining, and because the payload retains the expected net/sf/jasperreports/ prefix it still looks well-formed to filters keyed on a disallowed prefix
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered — Elar Lang found it by manually testing the reportresource service's prefix check and disclosed it to TIBCO on 2018-10-15, publishing after the vendor advisory. No AI tooling in discovery or exploit development, and none credited by researcher or vendor.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Upgrade the JasperReports Library by branch per TIBCO's 2019-03-06 advisory (6.3.4 and below to 6.3.5, 6.4.1 / 6.4.2 / 6.4.21 to 6.4.22, 7.1.0 to 7.1.1, 7.2.0 to 7.2.1), reaching the embedded copies inside JasperReports Server, the Community Editions, the ActiveMatrix BPM build and the Jaspersoft AWS offerings — then rotate the credentials in js.jdbc.properties.
prevention.adequacy: Patching is straightforward and has been available since March 2019; what makes prevention fail is scope. The vulnerable code is a jar bundled inside other vendors' products, so remediation requires an inventory sweep for embedded jasperreports jars rather than an upgrade of the products the organisation knowingly installed.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alert on GETs to reportresource/reportresource/ whose resource parameter contains ../ after the allowed prefix, on 200 responses whose bodies contain metadata.jdbc.driverClassName or metadata.hibernate.dialect (the matcher pair the public Nuclei template uses), and on any such request arriving with no authenticated session.
detection.adequacy: The response-body matcher is reliable, but WAF rules written against a disallowed prefix never fire — the payload opens with the permitted net/sf/jasperreports/ string — so detection has to inspect the whole parameter or the response body rather than the prefix.

response.what_would_have_worked: Rotate the reporting datasource credentials and anything else readable under the application root, review the database for connections from unexpected hosts, and inventory third-party products for bundled jasperreports jars that may still carry the vulnerable code.
response.adequacy: The exploit is confidentiality-only (C:H/I:N/A:N), so response is entirely about what was read: credentials that survive the upgrade untouched, and a directory listing that maps the application root for whatever comes next.

NIST-800-53-SI-10.gap: Input validation was implemented here and still failed: the service does check that resource begins with net/sf/jasperreports/. The defect is ordering — the allowlist runs before path canonicalisation, so traversal appended after the approved prefix passes validation and then escapes. SI-10 requires validity checking but never requires canonicalise-then-check, which is the entire vulnerability.

NIS2-Art21-supply-chain.gap: Art.21(2)(d) governs the relationship between an entity and its direct suppliers, but the vulnerable code is the JasperReports Library — a reporting component embedded inside other vendors' products and inside TIBCO's own server, BPM and AWS offerings. The operator's exposure lives in a transitive dependency they never selected or contracted for, which a supplier-relationship control has no mechanism to surface.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: B4 works through secure configuration and hardening of deployed systems, but this endpoint is enabled in the library's DEFAULT server implementation — there is no non-default feature to disable, no misconfiguration to correct, and the researcher reached it with no authentication precondition. Short of replacing the jar, B4 offers no lever, which is why the exposure persisted on systems otherwise configured to guidance.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: The patch-applications control measures the patch level of products in the inventory, and a JasperReports-embedding product can sit at its own latest release while still shipping a vulnerable jasperreports jar. The maturity model has no construct for component-level currency inside an application, so full compliance on the patch clock coexists with an unpatched CVE-2018-18809 on the same host.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: At CVSS 6.5 with C:H/I:N/A:N this rates Medium — commonly a 90-day window, routinely deferred behind Criticals — while being KEV-listed with EPSS 0.791 and paying out the datasource credential file that unlocks the database behind the reporting tier. The severity-ordered queue is the mechanism that keeps this specific vulnerability perpetually unscheduled.

new_control_requirements.name: TIER-3-DEPENDENCY-INVENTORY
new_control_requirements.description: Supply chain inventory must extend to tier-3 dependencies (dependencies of dependencies of direct dependencies). SBOM coverage for libsystemd-class transitive dependencies cannot be omitted under SR-3.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2018-18809 sits in the JasperReports Library jar bundled inside TIBCO's own server, ActiveMatrix BPM and Jaspersoft AWS offerings and inside other vendors' products, so the operator's exposure is a transitive component they never selected or contracted for and a NIS2 Art.21(2)(d) supplier-relationship control has no mechanism to surface. Remediation is an inventory sweep for embedded jasperreports jars, not an upgrade of the products the organisation knowingly installed.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2018-18809 scores CVSS 6.5 with C:H/I:N/A:N — a Medium that an A.8.8 severity-ordered queue parks in a 90-day window behind criticals — while being KEV-listed on 2022-12-29 with EPSS 0.791 and paying out the js.jdbc.properties datasource credentials that unlock the database behind the reporting tier. A KEV-triggered clock is what removes this specific vulnerability from the perpetually-deferred band the severity rating puts it in.

CVE-2020-3153.name: Cisco AnyConnect Secure Mobility Client for Windows Uncontrolled Search Path Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: A logged-in unprivileged Windows user opens a TCP connection to 127.0.0.1:62522 — the unauthenticated 'OCSC' TLV IPC port that Cisco's SYSTEM-privileged vpnagent.exe keeps listening whenever the AnyConnect service runs — and sends a CAC-nc-install message whose tab-separated path argument mixes backslash and forward-slash separators. vpndownloader derives the destination filename from the last backslash only while honouring the forward slashes as directory separators, so the SYSTEM-level copy escapes the AnyConnect Temp\Installer directory and lands vpndownloader.exe in C:\ProgramData\Cisco\, beside an attacker-written dbghelp.dll. When the agent relaunches the relocated binary as NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM it side-loads that DLL, converting a standard-user session into SYSTEM.
attack_vector.privileges_required: low — PR:L; valid credentials for any local Windows account, with no administrative rights and no user interaction (UI:N)
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L and fully deterministic: one loopback TCP connection and one IPC message, no race window and no memory-corruption primitive to groom, which is why the Metasploit module carries ExcellentRanking; the only practical constraints are an x86 payload and an appended '-ipc=<port>' argument on clients at 4.7 and above
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered — Yorick Koster reported it through the SSD Secure Disclosure programme after manually reverse-engineering the vpnagent IPC protocol and vpndownloader's filename parsing. No AI tooling is credited by the researcher, by SSD or by Cisco PSIRT, and the 2020 disclosure predates practical AI-assisted vulnerability discovery.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Upgrade every Windows endpoint to Cisco AnyConnect Secure Mobility Client 4.8.02042 or later, or migrate to Cisco Secure Client 5.x, and restart the Cisco AnyConnect Secure Mobility Agent service (an in-place upgrade does this). Cisco states explicitly that no workaround addresses the vulnerability.
prevention.adequacy: The fix replaces vpndownloader.exe on disk, so it is complete — but the delivery problem is circular: the off-network laptops most at risk reach the patch infrastructure through the very VPN client that needs upgrading, so an endpoint that never completes a tunnel never receives 4.8.02042. Disabling the VPN profile is not a substitute, because vpnagent.exe holds the loopback IPC listener open whenever the service runs.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alert on any non-Cisco process opening 127.0.0.1:62522, on vpndownloader.exe executing as SYSTEM from a directory other than the AnyConnect Temp\Downloader path, and on an unsigned dbghelp.dll appearing in C:\ProgramData\Cisco\ or beside a copied vpndownloader.exe in a %TEMP%\<6-random-chars> directory.
detection.adequacy: These signals are precise but late — the DLL write and the loopback connection happen seconds apart, so detection realistically catches the escalation as it succeeds rather than preventing it. A simple inventory check for vpndownloader.exe below file version 4.8.02042 (the same probe the Metasploit module's check() performs) is the higher-yield control.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treat the endpoint as compromised at SYSTEM: remove the relocated vpndownloader.exe and the side-loaded dbghelp.dll, upgrade the client, rotate every credential cached or typed on that host, and hunt for the follow-on ransomware staging that CISA records against this CVE.
response.adequacy: Post-SYSTEM cleanup on a Windows endpoint is unreliable by nature; because KEV records ransomware-campaign use, reimaging is the only defensible eviction path once the side-load is confirmed.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: Thirty-two months separated Cisco's 2020-02-19 fix from the 2022-10-24 KEV listing and fleets were still exposed, because SI-2's remediation channel runs over the VPN client it is trying to patch — an endpoint that cannot establish a tunnel never receives 4.8.02042, so the control's coverage metric silently excludes exactly the roaming hosts most likely to be attacked.

NIS2-Art21-vulnerability-management.gap: A CVSS 6.5 'local, medium' finding sits in a routine remediation band under Art.21 triage, yet a first-try Metasploit module with no race window turns any phished or contractor-held standard-user session on an essential entity's endpoint into SYSTEM. Severity-band scheduling systematically under-ranks reliable local escalations sitting on remote-access clients.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: B4 assumes the OS privilege boundary holds on a managed build, but the crossing here is performed by a trusted signed vendor service on the attacker's behalf — vpnagent.exe exposes an unauthenticated loopback IPC listener any logged-in user can drive, so a hardened SOE running standard-user accounts leaves no attacker-owned privileged code for B4's measures to constrain.

AU-Essential-8-App-Hardening.gap: User application hardening scopes browsers, Office macros, PDF readers and Java; a VPN client is filed as security tooling rather than attack surface, so nothing in the maturity model asks an organisation to restrict or monitor vpnagent.exe's IPC port. Application control fails for the same reason — the process that executes is Cisco's own signed vpndownloader.exe and the attacker's code arrives as a side-loaded DLL.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: A.8.8 schedules remediation off the published rating, and the vendor's 6.5 plus 'requires local credentials' framing kept this in ordinary patch cycles for two and a half years. Only CISA's 2022-10-24 KEV listing, with ransomware-campaign use recorded, reclassified it — a re-ranking that score-driven scheduling under A.8.8 never generates on its own.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2020-3153 sat in ordinary patch cycles for the 32 months between Cisco's 2020-02-19 fix and the 2022-10-24 KEV listing because a 6.5 'local, medium' score with 'requires local credentials' framing kept it in a routine severity band; only a KEV-triggered clock re-ranks a deterministic ExcellentRanking Metasploit SYSTEM escalation with recorded ransomware-campaign use ahead of the internet-facing queue.

new_control_requirements.name: PEN-TEST-SCOPE-INCLUDES-SECURITY-PRODUCTS
new_control_requirements.description: Penetration test and red-team scopes must explicitly include security-defense products (EDR, AV, DLP, identity-providers, secret-managers) as in-scope attack surface, not as defenses to evade. Scope language must call out that these products' admin interfaces, agent processes, and update channels are testable surfaces.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2020-3153 lives in the agent process of a security product: Cisco's SYSTEM-privileged vpnagent.exe holds an unauthenticated OCSC IPC listener on 127.0.0.1:62522 that any logged-in standard user can drive into a SYSTEM-level file copy. The VPN client was filed as security tooling rather than testable attack surface, so nothing scoped its agent IPC channel or its installer helper as something to attack.

CVE-2018-19323.name: GIGABYTE Multiple Products Privilege Escalation Vulnerability (CVE-2018-19323)

attack_vector.description: A user-mode process opens \\.\GIO with CreateFile and issues a single DeviceIoControl with IOCTL 0xC3502580 against a GIO_MSRIO_STRUCT {rw, reg, value}, giving it read and write access to Machine Specific Registers from ring 3. The published PoC first reads IA32_LSTAR (MSR 0xC0000082) to leak nt!KiSystemCall64 and defeat KASLR, then writes the same MSR to redirect the syscall entry point — SecureAuth notes this 'could be leveraged to execute arbitrary ring-0 code'. Because gdrv.sys is validly signed, attackers also carry it onto hosts that never ran GIGABYTE software and register it as a kernel service, using the flaw as a bring-your-own-vulnerable-driver ladder from local administrator to ring 0.
attack_vector.privileges_required: NVD scores this PR:N, but that vector is anomalous — CORE-2018-0007 records the flaw as 'Remotely Exploitable: No / Locally Exploitable: Yes' and the three sibling CVEs from the same advisory all carry PR:L. In practice: any local user, including LOW INTEGRITY processes, on a host with the vendor utility installed; local administrator in the BYOVD pattern where the attacker supplies the driver
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L and fully deterministic; one CreateFile plus one DeviceIoControl, roughly 70 lines of C in the advisory's PoC, with no race window and no memory-corruption grooming
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered — Diego Juarez of SecureAuth Labs found it by manually reverse-engineering the GIGABYTE GDrv driver, published as CORE-2018-0007 on 2018-12-18 in 'user release' mode after GIGABYTE denied the report on 2018-07-12. No tooling beyond the researcher is credited and the 2018 timeline predates practical AI-assisted discovery.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Deny the signed driver by hash rather than relying on an application update: the Microsoft vulnerable-driver blocklist (on by default with HVCI and on Windows 11 22H2 and later) or an App Control for Business policy covering gdrv.sys SHA-256 31f4cfb4c71da44120752721103a16512444c13c2ac2d857a7e6f13cb679b427 and ff6729518a380bf57f1bc6f1ec0aa7f3012e1618b8d9b0f31a61d299ee2b4339. Where the utility is installed, upgrade AORUS GRAPHICS ENGINE to 1.57 and XTREME GAMING ENGINE to 1.26, delete the driver and remove its kernel service with a reboot.
prevention.adequacy: Patching alone is insufficient and in two cases impossible: NVD names no fixed APP Center build for this CVE, and OC GURU II 2.08 is a retired product line with no vendor fix at all — those hosts must uninstall the software outright. More importantly, no application update revokes the code-signing certificate, so a fully patched fleet with zero GIGABYTE software is still exploitable by an attacker who brings the driver. Only the hash-based deny rule actually closes the exposure.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Sysmon Event ID 6 driver-load monitoring matching gdrv.sys by hash, alerting on kernel service creation from writable staging directories ('sc.exe create gdrv.sys binPath=C:\Windows\Temp\gdrv.sys type=kernel'), and flagging any process opening \\.\GIO or issuing IOCTL 0xC3502580 — the pattern Cisco Talos recommends for this driver class.
detection.adequacy: Driver-load time is the last point at which telemetry is trustworthy: once the MSR write lands, the attacker owns the syscall entry path and can suppress whatever the EDR would have reported. Detection must therefore fire before the IOCTL, not after.

response.what_would_have_worked: Remove the driver binary and its service entry, reboot to unload, add the hash to the blocklist fleet-wide, and treat the host as fully compromised — a ring-0 syscall redirect leaves no reliable in-band evidence.
response.adequacy: Rebuild is the only defensible outcome. KEV records ransomware-campaign use for this driver set and Talos observed gdrv.sys still being dropped by BlackByte as recently as July 2024, so an incident here is a foothold in an active intrusion, not a stray tool.

NIST-800-53-AC-6.gap: Least privilege is defined at the OS access-control layer and this primitive operates beneath it — an MSR write to IA32_LSTAR redirects the syscall entry point itself, so no account scoping, UAC split token or privileged-access workstation boundary survives. The advisory records \\.\GIO as openable by LOW INTEGRITY processes, meaning the least-privileged principal on the box reaches the same ring-0 outcome as an administrator.

DORA-Art-9.gap: Art.9 protection measures are scoped by the ICT asset inventory, and the vulnerable component is not on it: a financial entity that has never approved GIGABYTE consumer hardware still inherits the exposure because the signed gdrv.sys travels with the attacker. Nothing in the article requires inventorying or denying third-party signed kernel drivers that were never installed.

UK-CAF-B2.gap: B2 evidences who may hold privileged access through PAM and MFA on administrative accounts, but this crossing happens at the CPU register level with no privileged principal ever authenticating. An unprivileged session redirects nt!KiSystemCall64 while every identity-plane control B2 measures stays green.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Patching removes the local copy of gdrv.sys but does not revoke its signature, so a fully patched Windows fleet with no GIGABYTE software remains exploitable by an attacker who supplies the driver. The maturity model contains no control for blocking a validly-signed third-party kernel driver by hash, which is the only measure that works here.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: A.8.8 prioritises off the published score and that score is actively misleading: NVD's 9.8 with AV:N/PR:N contradicts CORE-2018-0007's own 'Remotely Exploitable: No' finding and the 7.8 AV:L its three siblings carry. An organisation triaging on the number chases a phantom network-facing critical and never arrives at the real requirement, a driver blocklist entry.

new_control_requirements.name: VULNERABLE-DRIVER-BLOCKLIST-ENFORCEMENT
new_control_requirements.description: Enforce a kernel vulnerable/malicious-driver blocklist (HVCI plus the vendor recommended-driver blocklist) so a signed-but-vulnerable driver cannot be loaded for bring-your-own-vulnerable-driver privilege escalation.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2018-19323 exposes ring-3 MSR read/write through \\.\GIO on a validly-signed gdrv.sys, so upgrading AORUS GRAPHICS ENGINE to 1.57 deletes the local copy without revoking the signature and an attacker carries the same driver onto a fully patched host with no GIGABYTE software. Only a hash-based deny rule covering the two published gdrv.sys SHA-256 values stops the IA32_LSTAR write that redirects nt!KiSystemCall64 beneath every OS access-control boundary.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2018-19323 carries an anomalous NVD 9.8 AV:N/PR:N score that contradicts CORE-2018-0007's own 'Remotely Exploitable: No' finding, so score-driven triage chases a phantom network-facing critical and never arrives at the real requirement. The 2022-10-24 KEV listing, with ransomware-campaign use and a 2022-11-14 due date, is the trigger that reorders it — and its acceptance of documented compensating controls is what lets the driver blocklist count as remediation where no patch closes the exposure.

CVE-2018-19322.name: GIGABYTE Multiple Products Code Execution Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: A user-mode process opens whichever GIGABYTE device object is present — the advisory PoC probes \\.\GPCIDrv64 first and falls back to \\.\GIO — and performs raw x86 port-mapped I/O through IOCTL 0x9C402588/0x9C40258C (GPCIDrv64 read/write) or 0x0C3506404/0x0C350A440 (GIO read/write). Unrestricted IN/OUT access from ring 3 reaches PCI configuration space, the SMBus and other platform controllers, which is how the driver's exposed function is 'leveraged in a number of ways to ultimately run code with elevated privileges'; the shipped PoC only forces a reboot, with the advisory noting that 'much more sinister stuff would also be possible'. Both drivers are validly signed, so attackers also stage them onto clean hosts as a BYOVD ladder.
attack_vector.privileges_required: low — PR:L; on a host that ran the vendor utility the advisory records both device objects as openable by non-privileged and even LOW INTEGRITY processes, while the BYOVD variant requires local administrator to register the kernel service
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; a CreateFile against one of two device names plus DeviceIoControl calls, no race window and no grooming. Turning IO-port access into reliable code execution is the least direct of the four advisory primitives, which matches this CVE's markedly lower EPSS than its siblings
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered — Diego Juarez of SecureAuth Labs reverse-engineered the GPCIDrv and GDrv drivers by hand; CORE-2018-0007 shipped 2018-12-18 as a user release after GIGABYTE replied on 2018-07-12 that its products were not affected. No AI tooling is credited and the timeline predates practical AI-assisted discovery.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Block both signed drivers by hash through the Microsoft vulnerable-driver blocklist or an App Control for Business policy, covering gdrv.sys SHA-256 31f4cfb4c71da44120752721103a16512444c13c2ac2d857a7e6f13cb679b427 and ff6729518a380bf57f1bc6f1ec0aa7f3012e1618b8d9b0f31a61d299ee2b4339 as well as GPCIDrv64.sys; where a utility is installed, move AORUS GRAPHICS ENGINE to 1.57 and XTREME GAMING ENGINE to 1.26, then delete the driver files, remove their kernel services and reboot to unload.
prevention.adequacy: Incomplete as a patch story: NVD names no fixed APP Center build for this CVE and OC GURU II 2.08 is retired with no fixed version, so those hosts have no vendor upgrade path and the software must simply be removed. Because this CVE is exposed by two distinct drivers, an update that removes one leaves the other reachable if any GIGABYTE utility remains — and neither update revokes either signature, so the deny rule is the load-bearing control.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Sysmon Event ID 6 driver-load alerting on gdrv.sys and GPCIDrv64.sys by hash, plus flagging any single process that probes both device names in sequence — that fallback pattern is exploit tooling behaviour, not vendor-utility behaviour.
detection.adequacy: Useful and cheap, but only at driver-load time; once port-mapped I/O is available the attacker is manipulating platform controllers below anything the OS can report. Unexplained hard reboots on a host carrying these device objects are a weak trailing signal — the advisory PoC demonstrates its write primitive by rebooting the machine.

response.what_would_have_worked: Remove both driver binaries and their service entries, reboot, push the hashes into the fleet-wide blocklist, and investigate how a kernel driver came to be staged in a writable directory such as C:\Windows\Temp on a host with no GIGABYTE hardware.
response.adequacy: Cleanup is straightforward; the intrusion that staged the driver is not. Talos still recorded gdrv.sys being dropped by BlackByte ransomware in July 2024, so the driver's presence should be treated as evidence of an active operator rather than as residue.

NIST-800-53-CM-7.gap: Least functionality tells an organisation to disable unnecessary functions, but the unnecessary function lives inside a signed third-party kernel driver as an IOCTL with no access check. CM-7 baselines enumerate installed applications and listening ports, never the IOCTL surface a loaded driver publishes, so the capability the control exists to remove is invisible to every CM-7 review.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: Art.21 patch management presumes an advisory-to-fix pipeline, and there was none: GIGABYTE had no security contact and denied the report outright, so between the 2018-12-18 user release and a later quiet vendor update an essential entity had no advisory, no severity rating and no fixed build to schedule. NVD still names no fixed APP Center version, so 'apply the vendor patch' remains an incomplete instruction.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: B4 expects protective measures at the platform layer, but port-mapped I/O reaches PCI configuration space, the SMBus and platform controllers where no OS-level hardening, privilege boundary or file-integrity control applies. B4 cannot mediate a hardware bus that a user-mode process reaches through a legitimate signed driver.

AU-ISM-1546.gap: ISM 1546 requires operating systems and applications to be patched, yet the exposure survives patching in both directions — a host with no GIGABYTE software is exploitable once the attacker copies the driver in, and a host patched to AORUS 1.57 still has no listed fixed APP Center build. The control's patch-centric framing never produces the instruction that matters, a signed-driver deny rule.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.9.gap: A.8.9 baselines record installed products and settings, not which kernel device objects exist or what DACL they carry. The insecure state here is that a default GIGABYTE install leaves \\.\GPCIDrv64 and \\.\GIO openable by LOW INTEGRITY processes — a configuration no A.8.9 baseline definition captures and therefore no drift check can flag.

new_control_requirements.name: VULNERABLE-DRIVER-BLOCKLIST-ENFORCEMENT
new_control_requirements.description: Enforce a kernel vulnerable/malicious-driver blocklist (HVCI plus the vendor recommended-driver blocklist) so a signed-but-vulnerable driver cannot be loaded for bring-your-own-vulnerable-driver privilege escalation.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2018-19322 is reachable through two distinct signed drivers — gdrv.sys and GPCIDrv64.sys — while GIGABYTE denied the report on 2018-07-12, NVD still names no fixed APP Center build, and OC GURU II 2.08 is a retired line with no fixed version, so there is no advisory-to-fix pipeline to schedule against. A hash deny rule covering both binaries is the only remediation that does not depend on the vendor shipping something.

new_control_requirements.name: KERNEL-MODULE-INVENTORY-AND-DISABLE
new_control_requirements.description: Maintain an inventory of loaded kernel modules. For modules not required for business function (RxRPC, unused crypto modules), disable via modprobe blacklist as a least-functionality control. Review quarterly.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2018-19322 publishes raw x86 IN/OUT port access through an IOCTL with no access check, and a default GIGABYTE install leaves \\.\GPCIDrv64 and \\.\GIO openable by LOW INTEGRITY processes — a state no installed-application or listening-port baseline records. A standing inventory of loaded kernel modules with a periodic business-need review is what surfaces a consumer overclocking driver still resident on a managed host and gets it unloaded and denied.

CVE-2018-19321.name: GIGABYTE Multiple Products Privilege Escalation Vulnerability (CVE-2018-19321)

attack_vector.description: A user-mode process opens \\.\GPCIDrv64 or \\.\GIO and maps arbitrary physical pages into its own address space through IOCTL 0xC3502004/0xC3502008 (GIO map/unmap, GIO_PHMAP request) or 0x9C402580/0x9C402584 (GPCIDrv64 map/unmap, GPCI_PHMAP request); the advisory PoC walks physical memory in 0x1000 strides writing 0xCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCC to prove unrestricted read/write. Arbitrary physical-memory access is the canonical route to locating and rewriting kernel structures — process tokens, code-integrity globals, PPL protection flags — with no memory-corruption bug involved, and public tooling weaponises exactly that for privilege escalation and PPL bypass. The signed driver is equally usable as a BYOVD ladder on hosts that never ran GIGABYTE software.
attack_vector.privileges_required: low — PR:L; on a host that ran the vendor utility a default install leaves both device objects openable by non-privileged processes 'even running at LOW INTEGRITY', while the BYOVD variant needs local administrator to register the kernel service
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; CreateFile plus a pair of map/unmap IOCTLs, no race window and no grooming. Physical-memory access is the most flexible of the four advisory primitives because it needs no KASLR leak and still supports data-only attacks on HVCI-enabled hosts where kernel code injection is blocked
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered — manual reverse engineering of the GPCIDrv and GDrv drivers by Diego Juarez of SecureAuth Labs, released as CORE-2018-0007 on 2018-12-18 after GIGABYTE stated its products were not affected. No tooling beyond the researcher is credited and the disclosure predates practical AI-assisted discovery.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: A hash-based deny rule for both signed drivers via the Microsoft vulnerable-driver blocklist or App Control for Business (gdrv.sys SHA-256 31f4cfb4c71da44120752721103a16512444c13c2ac2d857a7e6f13cb679b427 and ff6729518a380bf57f1bc6f1ec0aa7f3012e1618b8d9b0f31a61d299ee2b4339), plus HVCI/memory integrity to force attackers into data-only techniques. Where the utility is installed, move APP Center to 19.0422.1, AORUS GRAPHICS ENGINE to 1.57 and XTREME GAMING ENGINE to 1.26, delete the drivers, remove their services and reboot.
prevention.adequacy: OC GURU II 2.08 is a retired product line with no fixed version published, so affected hosts have no vendor upgrade path and the software must be uninstalled outright. For every other host the application update is beside the point: both binaries remain validly signed after it, so the deny rule is what actually removes the primitive. HVCI raises the cost of turning a physical-memory write into kernel code execution but does not stop token theft or protection-flag clearing.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alert on the map/unmap IOCTLs against either device, on bulk sequential physical-page mapping in 0x1000 strides from a single non-system process, and on Sysmon Event ID 6 driver loads matching either driver hash; watch for a protected process losing its PPL flag or terminating with no corresponding service-control or tamper-protection event.
detection.adequacy: The page-scanning stride is a strong signal but arrives only fractionally before the attacker rewrites the structures that decide what telemetry survives. The PPL-flag anomaly is a trailing indicator — by the time it fires the endpoint agent has already been neutered.

response.what_would_have_worked: Delete both drivers and their kernel services, reboot to unload, deploy the hashes fleet-wide, and rebuild the host — physical-memory writes leave no trustworthy in-band forensic record.
response.adequacy: Reimaging is the only reliable eviction. Because the primitive can clear code-integrity globals and PPL flags, any evidence collected from the running system after exploitation has to be treated as attacker-influenced.

NIST-800-53-SC-39.gap: SC-39 requires a separate execution domain per process, and arbitrary physical-page mapping dissolves that guarantee outright — once a user-mode process maps any physical page, every other process's memory including PPL endpoint agents and LSASS is directly readable and writable, with no API call left to intercept. There is no SC-39 implementation that survives a driver handing out physical memory by IOCTL.

EU-CRA-Art13.gap: Art.13's manufacturer duties to handle vulnerabilities and ship security updates are exactly what did not happen — GIGABYTE offered no security contact and formally denied the report in July 2018 — but the obligations attach to products placed on the market after the regulation applies. A driver signed and distributed in 2018 sits permanently outside the regulation's reach, and nothing in Art.13 can compel its revocation.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: B4 is built on the assumption that the platform enforces the kernel boundary. A physical-page write defeats that beneath every B4 measure: secure configuration, patching and privileged-account separation all operate on abstractions that a physical write can rewrite directly — including the code-integrity globals that decide whether the next unsigned driver loads.

AU-Essential-8-App-Hardening.gap: User application hardening and application control both operate on executables, and this attack presents none to block: the module that loads is a legitimate GIGABYTE-signed kernel driver that passes signature validation, and the attacker's effect is data-only writes into kernel structures. The maturity model has no notion of restricting which signed third-party kernel drivers may load.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: A.8.8 drives remediation from an asset-to-vulnerability mapping, and here the affected 'asset' arrives with the attacker. An organisation with no GIGABYTE product recorded anywhere can be fully conformant and still exploitable the moment a signed gdrv.sys or GPCIDrv64.sys is dropped on an endpoint, because the control never asks what third-party kernel drivers the platform will accept.

new_control_requirements.name: VULNERABLE-DRIVER-BLOCKLIST-ENFORCEMENT
new_control_requirements.description: Enforce a kernel vulnerable/malicious-driver blocklist (HVCI plus the vendor recommended-driver blocklist) so a signed-but-vulnerable driver cannot be loaded for bring-your-own-vulnerable-driver privilege escalation.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2018-19321 hands a user-mode process arbitrary physical-page map/unmap through signed gdrv.sys or GPCIDrv64.sys, so PPL endpoint agents and LSASS become directly readable and writable with no unsigned executable for application control to block and no API call left to intercept. Denying both drivers at load time — with HVCI forcing any residual attempt into data-only techniques — is the only measure that removes the primitive, since the vulnerable component arrives with the attacker rather than from the asset inventory.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2018-19321 is exploitable on organisations that have never approved GIGABYTE hardware, so an asset-to-vulnerability mapping shows nothing to remediate and score-driven scheduling never raises it. The 2022-10-24 KEV listing is the only trigger that puts a driver the organisation never installed onto a remediation clock, and its compensating-controls clause is what makes the blocklist entry the recorded mitigation.

attack_vector.description: A user-mode process opens \\.\GIO and calls DeviceIoControl with IOCTL 0xC3502808 — the driver's ring0 memcpy-like handler — passing a GIO_MemCpyStruct {dest, src, size}, which grants arbitrary kernel virtual-memory read and write in a single call with no memory-corruption bug required. Sophos documented the exact real-world use: RobbinHood ransomware dropped the signed GDRV.SYS with ROBNR.EXE, used the kernel write to patch nt!g_CiEnabled (Windows 7) or ci!g_CiOptions (Windows 8/10) in memory to disable Driver Signature Enforcement, then loaded its own unsigned RBNL.SYS to terminate protected endpoint-security processes and delete in-use files from kernel mode — on machines that had never had GIGABYTE software installed.
attack_vector.privileges_required: low — PR:L; on a host that ran the vendor utility a default install leaves \\.\GIO openable by non-privileged processes 'even running at LOW INTEGRITY', while the BYOVD pattern that RobbinHood used needs local administrator to register the kernel service
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L and fully deterministic; one CreateFile plus one DeviceIoControl, under 60 lines of C in the advisory PoC, and the primitive is a straight kernel memcpy with attacker-chosen source, destination and length
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered — Diego Juarez of SecureAuth Labs reverse-engineered the GDrv driver manually; SecureAuth was told GIGABYTE was 'a hardware company' and received a formal denial on 2018-07-12, so CORE-2018-0007 shipped as a user release. No AI tooling is credited and the timeline predates practical AI-assisted discovery.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: A hash-based deny rule for gdrv.sys through the Microsoft vulnerable-driver blocklist (on by default with HVCI and on Windows 11 22H2 and later) or an App Control for Business policy covering SHA-256 31f4cfb4c71da44120752721103a16512444c13c2ac2d857a7e6f13cb679b427 and ff6729518a380bf57f1bc6f1ec0aa7f3012e1618b8d9b0f31a61d299ee2b4339; on hosts that carry the utility, move APP Center to 19.0422.1, AORUS GRAPHICS ENGINE to 1.57 and XTREME GAMING ENGINE to 1.26, then delete the driver, remove its service and reboot.
prevention.adequacy: OC GURU II 2.08 is retired with no fixed version, so those hosts have no vendor upgrade path and the software must be uninstalled. For everyone else the update is nearly irrelevant to the real risk: RobbinHood attacked machines with no GIGABYTE software at all, because the update does not revoke the signature. Only the blocklist entry prevents the attack that actually happened.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Detection has to sit at driver-load time — Sysmon Event ID 6 matching gdrv.sys by hash, and alerting on 'sc.exe create gdrv.sys binPath=C:\Windows\Temp\gdrv.sys type=kernel' on a host with no GIGABYTE hardware. The trailing signals are the RobbinHood staging set in C:\Windows\Temp (STEEL.EXE, ROBNR.EXE, the unsigned RBNL.SYS and PLIST.TXT) and in-memory modification of nt!g_CiEnabled / ci!g_CiOptions.
detection.adequacy: Everything after driver load is unreliable by construction: disabling DSE and killing the EDR agent is this chain's first move, not its last, so the telemetry a SOC would normally hunt in stops being produced at the moment of compromise.

response.what_would_have_worked: Isolate the host, assume kernel-level compromise and total loss of endpoint telemetry, rebuild from known-good media, push the driver hashes into the fleet-wide blocklist, and treat the event as a ransomware pre-encryption stage with credential rotation and lateral-movement hunting.
response.adequacy: There is no in-place recovery. Both RobbinHood in 2020 and BlackByte as recently as July 2024 used this driver specifically to remove security software before encryption, so the correct posture is incident response on a live ransomware intrusion, not malware cleanup.

NIST-800-53-SI-3.gap: SI-3 is the control this CVE deletes rather than evades: the ring0 memcpy patches the code-integrity globals, loads an unsigned driver and terminates protected anti-malware processes from kernel mode with tamper protection bypassed. The endpoint agent SI-3 depends on is killed before it can alert, so the control generates no evidence of its own failure.

NIS2-Art21-vulnerability-management.gap: Art.21 vulnerability handling presumes a vendor pipeline exists. GIGABYTE gave SecureAuth no security contact and formally denied the report, so between the 2018-12-18 user release and a later quiet vendor update an essential entity running the directive's process correctly had no advisory, no severity rating and no fixed build to act on — the process executed and produced nothing.

UK-CAF-C1.gap: C1 monitoring is structurally blind here because disabling Driver Signature Enforcement and killing the EDR agent happens first. Detection has to move earlier, to driver-load time with hash matching — every post-compromise signal C1 would normally collect is produced by an agent the attacker has already terminated.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Patching cannot close this. gdrv.sys is a validly-signed standalone file, so an attacker copies it onto a fully patched host that never ran GIGABYTE software — exactly what RobbinHood did. Uninstalling the utility removes the local copy without revoking the certificate, and the maturity model contains no hash-based driver blocklist control.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.7.gap: A.8.7 is written around detecting and removing malicious code, but the component granting kernel access is a legitimate vendor-signed driver that passes every signature check and allowlist. The control has no category for 'signed, legitimate, and exposing an unauthenticated ring0 memcpy to LOW INTEGRITY processes' — and the malware that follows is loaded only after A.8.7's own enforcement mechanism has been switched off in kernel memory.

new_control_requirements.name: VULNERABLE-DRIVER-BLOCKLIST-ENFORCEMENT
new_control_requirements.description: Enforce a kernel vulnerable/malicious-driver blocklist (HVCI plus the vendor recommended-driver blocklist) so a signed-but-vulnerable driver cannot be loaded for bring-your-own-vulnerable-driver privilege escalation.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2018-19320's ring0 memcpy handler (IOCTL 0xC3502808) is what RobbinHood used to patch nt!g_CiEnabled / ci!g_CiOptions in memory, disable Driver Signature Enforcement and load its own unsigned RBNL.SYS — on machines that never had GIGABYTE software installed, and Talos still recorded BlackByte dropping gdrv.sys in July 2024. Uninstalling the utility removes the local copy without revoking the certificate, so only the hash-based blocklist entry prevents the attack that actually happened.

new_control_requirements.name: AV-EDR-AVAILABILITY-MONITORING
new_control_requirements.description: Treat loss of AV/EDR availability as a first-class security event: alarm when an endpoint stops reporting Defender/EDR telemetry or its protection service crashes/restarts abnormally, correlate with inbound network activity, and patch the Defender antimalware platform to the fixed build (4.18.26040.7) as a KEV-priority item. A remotely-disable-able defender must not fail silent.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2018-19320 is used to terminate protected anti-malware processes from kernel mode with tamper protection bypassed, so the endpoint agent is killed as the chain's first move and produces no evidence of its own failure. Once the ring0 write lands, the agent going silent is the only remaining signal — which means silence has to be alarmed on rather than read as a healthy host.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2018-19320's vendor gave SecureAuth no security contact, said it was 'a hardware company' and formally denied the report on 2018-07-12, so a directive-driven vulnerability-handling process executed correctly and produced no advisory, no severity rating and no fixed build to act on. The 2022-10-24 KEV listing is the vendor-independent trigger, and its compensating-controls clause makes the driver blocklist the recordable mitigation.

CVE-2022-41352.name: Synacor Zimbra Collaboration Suite (ZCS) Arbitrary File Upload Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: The attacker emails a .tar (or .cpio/.rpm) archive to any address the Zimbra server accepts. amavis automatically submits the attachment for malware inspection and shells out to GNU cpio, which honours the archive's symlink and absolute-path entries because of the unfixed 2015 cpio flaw CVE-2015-1197, writing outside the extraction directory. Public tooling plants a JSP web shell under the Jetty-served Zimbra web directories — the Metasploit module drops a randomly named 4-10 character .jsp under /opt/zimbra/jetty_base/webapps/zimbra/ and polls the URL until it answers — yielding command execution as the zimbra service account and access to every mailbox on the host.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N and UI:N; sending mail to any address the server accepts is the entire trigger, because amavis extracts the attachment without operator involvement
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L, but distribution-dependent as well as version-dependent: Ubuntu carries pax as a Zimbra prerequisite and amavis prefers it, while RHEL/CentOS 7 and later dropped pax from the default install, leaving the vulnerable GNU cpio path in place. The Metasploit module landed 2022-10-07, three days before the vendor patch, collapsing the skill floor to point-and-shoot; EPSS sits around 0.955
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered — this surfaced through in-the-wild compromise rather than research: Zimbra forum operators reported compromised servers in September 2022, Rapid7 published its analysis on 2022-10-06 while the flaw was still unpatched, and Kaspersky counted roughly 876 servers already compromised before a CVE identifier existed. No AI tooling is credited by Zimbra, Rapid7 or Kaspersky.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Apply Zimbra Collaboration 9.0.0 Patch 27 or 8.8.15 Patch 34 (published 2022-10-10), which drops the cpio dependency and makes pax a Zimbra prerequisite. Before the patch existed, the effective control was Zimbra's own workaround — install the distribution's pax package and restart Zimbra, after which amavis prefers pax over cpio.
prevention.adequacy: The patch closes the extraction path but does not evict an existing shell, so remediation on any exposed host is incomplete without hunting and removing JSP files under /opt/zimbra/jetty/webapps/zimbra/public and /opt/zimbra/jetty_base/webapps/zimbra/. The pax workaround was the only control available during the September 2022 mass-exploitation window and remains worth applying wherever patch state is uncertain.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alert on amavis producing writes outside its extraction directory, on any .jsp appearing in a Jetty-served Zimbra directory, and on those URLs being fetched over HTTPS shortly after an inbound archive attachment. The named shells Kaspersky recovered — .error.jsp, ResourcesVerificaton.jsp, ResourceVerificaton.jsp, ZimletCore.jsp, searchx.jsp, seachx.jsp — are direct file-integrity indicators.
detection.adequacy: File-integrity monitoring on the web-served directories is high-fidelity here because those paths should never receive new files from the mail pipeline. It arrives after the write, though — the attacker has code execution as the zimbra account by the time the shell is fetched.

response.what_would_have_worked: Patch or install pax, remove every JSP web shell from the Zimbra web directories, rotate mailbox and service credentials, and treat all mail data on the host as exfiltrated given the zimbra account's access to every mailbox.
response.adequacy: Kaspersky recorded a blanket wave against effectively every vulnerable server in Central Asia from 2022-09-30, so an unpatched internet-facing ZCS host from that period should be treated as compromised rather than merely vulnerable, with the full mailbox corpus in scope for breach assessment.

NIST-800-53-SI-3.gap: SI-3 requires malicious-code protection at system entry points, and here that protection was the entry point — amavis invoked GNU cpio to unpack inbound attachments for antivirus scanning, so a traversing archive gave the sender an arbitrary write as the zimbra user out of the scanner itself. Nothing in SI-3 asks whether the scanning pipeline's own extractors are sandboxed or safe on untrusted input.

NIS2-Art21-supply-chain.gap: Art.21 supply-chain measures scope direct suppliers and service providers, but exploitability was decided by a transitive OS component — GNU cpio still carrying CVE-2015-1197 — reached through amavis. Both Zimbra's supplier assurance and the operator's would show conformant while a RHEL/CentOS 7+ host with cpio and no pax stayed one email away from remote code execution.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: B4 secure configuration assumes platform components run with least function, yet ZCS extracted untrusted archives as the zimbra user, which also owns /opt/zimbra/jetty/webapps/zimbra/public — writable by the extractor and served by Jetty at the same moment. One traversal therefore produced a live executable endpoint with no second exploitation stage required.

AU-Essential-8-App-Hardening.gap: User application hardening targets browsers, Office macros and PDF readers on workstations and says nothing about a server-side Jetty instance executing attacker-written JSP out of a public/ directory, which is the entire exploitation path. The shells simply ran because their URLs were requested.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: A.8.8 schedules technical-vulnerability work by rated severity, but roughly 876 servers were compromised before this had a CVE identifier and the KEV due date of 2022-11-10 falls a month after the 2022-10-10 patch. An entity on a risk-rated cadence had no artefact to prioritise during the September waves; only the non-version-based workaround changed the outcome in that window.

new_control_requirements.name: SECURITY-TOOL-INTEGRITY-VERIFICATION
new_control_requirements.description: Security tools (AV/AM, EDR, vulnerability scanners) must be treated as in-scope of vulnerability management with the same SLAs as other privileged software. Definition-update channels must use TLS with certificate pinning. Compliance audits must include a trust-anchor-inversion test: deliver a crafted input to the security tool in a sandbox and confirm rejection.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2022-41352 makes the malicious-code protection the entry point: amavis invoked GNU cpio to unpack inbound mail attachments for antivirus scanning, so an archive with a traversing entry gave any sender an arbitrary write as the zimbra user out of the scanner itself. The trust-anchor-inversion test — deliver a crafted archive to the scanning pipeline in a sandbox and confirm rejection — is the only audit step that treats the scanner's own extractor as attack surface.

new_control_requirements.name: TIER-3-DEPENDENCY-INVENTORY
new_control_requirements.description: Supply chain inventory must extend to tier-3 dependencies (dependencies of dependencies of direct dependencies). SBOM coverage for libsystemd-class transitive dependencies cannot be omitted under SR-3.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2022-41352's exploitability was decided by a transitive OS-level component — GNU cpio still carrying the 2015 symlink flaw CVE-2015-1197 — reached through amavis, not by Zimbra code. A RHEL/CentOS 7+ host with cpio and no pax was one email from remote code execution while both Zimbra's supplier assurance and the operator's own showed conformant, because neither inventory reached the extractor binary.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
