new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2021-25369 was fixed silently by Samsung in March 2021 as a Moderate-rated SVE-2021-19897 with no exploitation notice, and its use by a commercial surveillance vendor only became public when Project Zero published in November 2022 — the same week CISA listed it. The KEV listing, not the vendor advisory, was the first actionable signal a defender could have acted on, so the remediation clock has to key off it.

new_control_requirements.name: EOL-ASSET-DECOMMISSION
new_control_requirements.description: Network-reachable end-of-life devices with no vendor patch path must be isolated and decommissioned within a bounded window; mandatory compensating segmentation applies until removal since no remediation exists.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2021-25369's affected population — Galaxy S10, A50 SM-A505F and A51 SM-A515F on kernel 4.14.113 — is past Samsung's security-update window, so a handset that never took an SMR Mar-2021-or-later build has no fixed version available at all and continues leaking live task_struct and sys_call_table addresses to system_app context. Such devices belong in a decommissioning queue, not a patch backlog.

CVE-2021-25370.name: Samsung Mobile Devices Memory Corruption Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: decon_set_win_config() in the Exynos DPU driver calls fd_install() on the retire fence and then keeps using the struct file pointer, so a plain close() from userspace frees an object the driver still dereferences. The in-the-wild sample grooms the heap with 30,000+ memfd_create open/close cycles, sprays 25 fake 0x140-byte struct file objects through the Mali MEM_PROFILE_ADD ioctl with f_op pointed at signalfd_op and private_data pointed at addr_limit (task_struct + 8, leaked via CVE-2021-25369), then calls signalfd() on the dangling fence fd to land a single 8-byte write over addr_limit — after which USER_DS/KERNEL_DS toggling gives arbitrary kernel read/write and sys_call_table patching.
attack_vector.privileges_required: high — PR:H; the driver path is driven from a system_app-context process that the chain obtains through CVE-2021-25337 first, so this link is not independently reachable by an untrusted app
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; the defect is a deterministic lifetime error rather than a race and the grooming and spray sequence is reliable, but it additionally requires the KASLR leak from CVE-2021-25369 and is bounded to Exynos hardware on kernel 4.14.113 with the Mali r19p0 driver
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered — recovered by Google TAG as part of the late-2020 in-the-wild chain and root-caused by Project Zero; Samsung records SVE-2021-19925, privately disclosed 2020-12-12, with no automated or AI tooling credited by Google, Samsung or ARM.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Move handsets to Samsung SMR Mar-2021 Release 1 or later (SVE-2021-19925), which moves the fd_install() call to the latest possible point in decon_set_win_config so the struct file stays valid for the remainder of the function.
prevention.adequacy: There is no configuration workaround — the vulnerable path is the ordinary DECON window-config ioctl the display stack uses in normal operation — and the affected Exynos generation on kernel 4.14.113 is now past Samsung's update window, so unpatched handsets have no upgrade path and must be retired or network-isolated.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alert on kernel panic or oops traces naming decon_set_win_config or decon_create_release_fences on Exynos devices, and on a JNI library that opens both /dev/mali0 and the DECON device in the same session.
detection.adequacy: Panic traces are the only realistic signal and they are retrospective and inverted — a failed spray panics while a successful exploit produces nothing, and once addr_limit is overwritten the attacker sits above every logging facility the device has.

response.what_would_have_worked: Scope the incident to the whole chain (CVE-2021-25337 and CVE-2021-25369 on the same device timeline), image the handset, and replace hardware that cannot take SMR Mar-2021 or later.
response.adequacy: Arbitrary kernel read/write with sys_call_table patching means nothing on the device can be trusted afterwards, so only replacement is a defensible eviction.

NIST-800-53-SC-39.gap: SC-39 requires a separate execution domain per process and this defect corrupts the component that enforces it — once addr_limit is attacker-controlled, USER_DS/KERNEL_DS toggling gives read/write over all kernel memory, so no SC-39 implementation choice on the handset changes the outcome.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: A risk-ranked patch queue read Samsung's 'Moderate' rating and NVD's 4.4 availability-only score as a local denial of service on a phone; the reality — the kernel read/write stage of a commercial surveillance chain — was not public until November 2022, twenty months after the fix shipped and the same week CISA listed it.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: There is no operator-side hardening for a use-after-free in an OEM display driver: the vulnerable path is the ordinary DECON window-configuration ioctl and the fix was Samsung moving fd_install() later inside its own code, so B4 offers no setting to disable, no interface to restrict and no compensating control on the device.

AU-ISM-1546.gap: 1546 keys its timeframes to vendor advisory severity, and Samsung published this as a Moderate memory-corruption-leading-to-kernel-panic issue, so a conformant programme applied it on the routine monthly schedule while the same defect was already serving as the escalation stage of an in-the-wild chain TAG had captured in late 2020.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.28.gap: Installing a file descriptor into the userspace table before the driver has finished using the struct file is exactly the lifetime error secure-coding review exists to catch, but the code belongs to Samsung's Exynos display driver rather than the certified organisation — an ISMS scoped to its own development lifecycle gives zero assurance about the handsets on its network and has no mechanism to require it of the OEM.

new_control_requirements.description: Managed mobile fleets must enforce a minimum OS security-patch level as a condition of access to organizational data, not merely report it. For Android, the MDM/EMM must read the device security-patch level and block or quarantine devices below the patch level that fixes a KEV-listed Framework flaw (here, 2026-06-01), and constrain installation of untrusted/side-loaded apps on devices that cannot yet update - since the privilege escalation is driven by locally running code. The distinguishing test: enroll a device pinned below 2026-06-01 and confirm the MDM policy denies it access to protected resources (rather than only recording the stale patch level on a dashboard) - paper 'mobile patching' policies that surface patch level without enforcing it leave exploitable devices in production.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2021-25370 has no configuration workaround — the vulnerable path is the ordinary DECON window-config ioctl the Exynos display stack uses in normal operation — and the fix exists only in SMR Mar-2021 Release 1 (SVE-2021-19925), which moves fd_install() to the end of decon_set_win_config. The escalation runs from a locally installed app that first obtains system_app context, so enforcing the minimum SMR level as an access condition and constraining side-loaded installs are the only levers an operator holds on the device.

new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2021-25370 was published by Samsung as a Moderate 'memory corruption in dpu driver' and scored 4.4 availability-only by NVD, so severity-keyed patch queues ranked it as a local denial of service on a phone while it was in fact the arbitrary-kernel-read/write stage of an in-the-wild surveillance chain, overwriting addr_limit and patching sys_call_table. A clock keyed to the 2022-11-08 KEV listing overrides the vendor's under-rating; one keyed to advisory severity does not.

Network isolation followed by replacement within a bounded window is the only remaining remediation for that fleet segment.

CVE-2022-3723.name: Google Chromium V8 Type Confusion Vulnerability (CVE-2022-3723)

attack_vector.description: A crafted HTML page drives V8 through a type-confused object and corrupts the renderer heap, giving code execution inside the Chrome renderer with no user action beyond loading the page — delivered from an arbitrary site or a compromised advertising slot. Avast reported it on 2022-10-25 with an exploit already in use and Google shipped 107.0.5304.87 two days later, but neither party published the chain and Chromium bug 1378239 remains restricted, so whether the observed attacks carried a sandbox-escape stage is not publicly established and should not be assumed.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; the attacker needs no account or foothold, only that the target loads attacker-controlled web content (UI:R is satisfied by clicking a link or rendering a malicious ad)
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L for delivery; the exploitation ceiling is what bounds it, since renderer code execution is site-isolated and sandboxed (S:U) and reaching the host requires a second, chained escape bug
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered — Chrome's release note credits Jan Vojtesek, Milanek and Przemek Gmerek of Avast on 2022-10-25, a two-day turnaround consistent with surfacing the bug from live attack telemetry. The sanitiser and fuzzer stack listed in the same note is release boilerplate and is not credited with this finding.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Push Chrome 107.0.5304.87 (Mac/Linux) or 107.0.5304.87/.88 (Windows), Edge Stable 107.0.1418.26 or Edge Extended Stable 106.0.1370.61, and force a browser relaunch fleet-wide via the RelaunchNotification / RelaunchNotificationPeriod policies. Chromium derivatives such as Opera required their own rebuild on the 107 branch.
prevention.adequacy: There is no hot-patch path for a V8 defect and, critically, installing the fix is not applying it — Chrome's updater stages the new build silently while the vulnerable V8 keeps running in every live renderer until relaunch, so an inventory report showing the fixed version can coexist with days of continued exposure.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Correlate renderer-process crashes and unexpected renderer restarts across a small set of URLs on builds below 107.0.5304.87, and treat any child process parented to a Chrome renderer as evidence that a chained sandbox escape completed.
detection.adequacy: The exploit was never published and no JavaScript signature or hash exists, so detection is limited to crash-state and process-lineage heuristics; the renderer-parented child is the highest-value signal precisely because it indicates the chain went past this bug and reached the host.

response.what_would_have_worked: Verify running-version compliance rather than installed-version compliance, force relaunch on stragglers, and investigate any host that produced renderer-parented child processes as a suspected host compromise.
response.adequacy: With no published indicators, response has to be posture-driven — closing the relaunch gap is the only action that reliably changes exposure across a fleet.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: SI-2 measures time from patch availability and the exploit predated the patch; it also misses the browser-specific failure mode that governs real exposure, since a fleet report showing 107.0.5304.87 installed can coexist with users still executing the vulnerable engine until every renderer is torn down.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: Art.21 frames patching around the entity's own systems and maintenance windows, but this component updates on Google's cadence and the exposure window opened before disclosure — on 2022-10-28 the correct action was not a scheduled window at all but a same-day forced relaunch across every managed endpoint.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: No browser hardening baseline blocks this path: the trigger is ordinary JavaScript on a crafted page served over HTTPS from any site or ad slot. Site isolation and the renderer sandbox constrain the follow-on escape rather than this bug, so B4 conformance measurably reduced blast radius while leaving the vulnerability fully reachable.

AU-Essential-8-App-Hardening.gap: The control is defined by disabling the features attackers abuse — Flash, Java, web advertisements, untrusted macros — and none of those levers touches plain JavaScript executed by V8; a Maturity Level 3 organisation was exactly as exposed as a Level 0 one until Chrome was updated and relaunched.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: The 8.8 rating misleads in both directions — UI:R reads as 'requires user interaction' when the interaction is merely visiting a page, while the score ignores that renderer execution lands inside the sandbox and needs a second bug to reach the host — and risk-rated scheduling is the wrong instrument for an actively exploited browser zero-day whose only effective answer is update-and-relaunch within hours.

new_control_requirements.name: BROWSER-MANAGED-UPDATE-NO-DEFERRAL
new_control_requirements.description: Enterprise update rings must not defer security-channel browser updates beyond 24h.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2022-3723 was fixed in Chrome 107.0.5304.87 two days after Avast reported it with an exploit already in use, but Chrome's updater stages the build silently while the vulnerable V8 keeps running in every live renderer until the browser is relaunched — so a deferring update ring, or one that measures installed rather than running version, leaves users executing the vulnerable engine for days after the fleet reports compliant. Remediation requires the update plus a forced relaunch via RelaunchNotification / RelaunchNotificationPeriod.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2022-3723 was in active exploitation on 2022-10-25 before any patch existed and CISA listed it on 2022-10-28, and there is no hot-patch path for a V8 defect and no browser-hardening lever that touches plain JavaScript on a crafted page. A KEV-keyed same-day push-and-forced-relaunch across every managed endpoint is the entire remediation, not a scheduling decision.

CVE-2022-42827.name: Apple iOS and iPadOS Out-of-Bounds Write Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: An application already running on the device performs an out-of-bounds write in the iOS/iPadOS kernel and obtains arbitrary code execution with kernel privileges — Apple's own stated impact. Apple named no subsystem, published nothing beyond 'an out-of-bounds write issue was addressed with improved bounds checking', and credited an anonymous researcher, so neither the corrupted structure nor the mitigations the exploit had to defeat (PAC, KTRR/CTRR, PPL) are in the public record. What is established is that Apple treated it as urgent enough to ship in iOS 16.1 on 2022-10-24 as an actively-exploited fix and backport it to the 15.x line three days later.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; no elevated entitlement is needed, only local code execution inside an app, and the CVSS UI:R is satisfied by the user installing or launching that app
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L per NVD, but the practical barrier cannot be assessed from primary sources: Apple published no subsystem, no bug-class detail and no chain, and contemporary iOS kernel exploitation must contend with PAC, KTRR/CTRR and PPL, so a reliable chain is expensive to build and is normally paired with a remote or sandbox-entry bug Apple did not disclose
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered — Apple credits 'an anonymous researcher' in both HT213489 and HT213490 and names no organisation, tool or methodology. No party has claimed AI-assisted discovery, and the October 2022 timeframe predates AI-assisted vulnerability discovery being operationally material.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Move devices to iOS/iPadOS 15.7.1 (HT213490) or iOS 16.1 / iPadOS 16 (HT213489) and enforce it with an MDM software-update policy or Declarative Device Management update enforcement rather than relying on user-deferrable notifications.
prevention.adequacy: Apple's Rapid Security Response mechanism did not begin delivering fixes until 2023, so remediation is a full OS update plus restart with no out-of-band channel — and devices older than iPhone 6s fall outside both fixed advisories, never received a fix, and can only be retired.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Watch for unexplained kernel panics or spontaneous reboots clustered around the launch or backgrounding of one specific app on builds below the fixed ones, and pull panic-full-*.ips logs from Analytics Data or a sysdiagnose bundle for data-abort and memory-corruption signatures.
detection.adequacy: A failed out-of-bounds write panics far more often than it succeeds, so panic frequency is the most reliable on-device signal — but a successful exploit produces no host telemetry at all, because iOS exposes no EDR hook at kernel level.

response.what_would_have_worked: Corroborate from off-device signals — unexpected network destinations, new configuration profiles, MDM enrolment changes — then wipe and restore affected handsets and rotate credentials and tokens held on them.
response.adequacy: With kernel-privilege execution the attacker sits above every on-device integrity check, so wipe-and-restore plus credential rotation is the only defensible eviction — and devices below iPhone 6s cannot be brought to a fixed state at all.

NIST-800-53-SC-39.gap: SC-39 process isolation is what the iOS app sandbox implements and what Apple's stated impact voids — an application executing arbitrary code with kernel privileges corrupts the component enforcing every process boundary, and iOS exposes no hooks for an operator to strengthen, monitor or compensate for it.

DORA-Art-9.gap: Employee iPhones and iPads carry payment authorisation, trading approvals and MFA push, so they sit squarely in scope — yet an entity's protective options on iOS reduce to version enforcement alone, with no EDR agent, no kernel-level monitoring and no third-party exploit mitigation permitted, so Art.9 delivered no detection or containment capability during the pre-patch window.

UK-CAF-C1.gap: C1 assumes the operator can collect and analyse security-relevant telemetry from in-scope systems; with kernel-privilege execution the attacker sits above every logging facility iOS exposes, and the only obtainable artefacts are panic logs and sysdiagnose bundles pulled by hand from an individual device.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: The control assumes the organisation can push updates to the OS families in scope, but iOS updates stay user-deferrable unless a DDM or MDM software-update policy forces them — so high maturity across workstations and servers is fully compatible with an iPhone fleet weeks behind 15.7.1 / 16.1, which is the entire exploitable population.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: The only input available to the register is 'below 15.7.1 / 16.1' because Apple named no subsystem, and NVD's CPE set additionally spans macOS, tvOS and watchOS ranges that Apple's own advisories for those platforms do not list — so a scanner-fed process over-reports on Macs and Apple TVs while under-reporting on the unenrolled handsets that actually matter.

new_control_requirements.name: MOBILE-ENDPOINT-MDM-ENFORCED-KEV-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: iOS / iPadOS / macOS estates must enforce KEV-class updates within 24h via DDM; user-deferral disallowed.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2022-42827 was fixed only in iOS 16.1 / iPadOS 16 and the 15.7.1 backport, and Apple's Rapid Security Response channel did not begin delivering fixes until 2023, so remediation is a full OS update plus restart that remains user-deferrable unless an MDM software-update policy or Declarative Device Management enforcement forces it. The lagging, unenrolled handset population is the entire exploitable population for this kernel write.

new_control_requirements.name: MOBILE-ZERO-CLICK-HARDENING
new_control_requirements.description: High-risk mobile users must operate in a reduced-attack-surface mode (e.g. Lockdown Mode) that disables automatic processing of untrusted message attachments, fonts, and link previews, closing the zero-click delivery path patch SLAs cannot outrun.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2022-42827 gives an application arbitrary code execution with kernel privileges, and a reliable chain of that kind is normally paired with a remote or sandbox-entry bug Apple never disclosed. Because iOS permits no EDR agent, no kernel-level monitoring and no third-party exploit mitigation, a reduced-attack-surface mode is the only prevention lever that operates for high-risk users during the pre-patch window this actively-exploited zero-day occupied.

new_control_requirements.name: EOL-ASSET-DECOMMISSION
new_control_requirements.description: Network-reachable end-of-life devices with no vendor patch path must be isolated and decommissioned within a bounded window; mandatory compensating segmentation applies until removal since no remediation exists.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2022-42827's two fixed advisories reach back only to iPhone 6s, iPad Air 2, iPad 5th generation, iPad mini 4 and iPod touch 7th generation; anything older never received the fix and cannot be brought to a remediated state by any action. Those handsets must be withdrawn from organizational access and retired within a bounded window rather than carried as permanent patch backlog.

CVE-2020-3433.name: Cisco AnyConnect Secure Mobility Client for Windows DLL Hijacking Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: Any user with valid local credentials connects to the Cisco AnyConnect Secure Mobility Agent's IPC listener on 127.0.0.1 TCP/62522 and sends a single crafted 'CAC-nc-install' message naming vpndownloader.exe together with an attacker-supplied dbghelp.dll. The SYSTEM-privileged service copies both into a temp installer directory under C:\ProgramData\Cisco\Cisco AnyConnect Secure Mobility Client\Temp\ and executes the copy; because vpndownloader.exe resolves dbghelp.dll from its own directory, the attacker's DLL loads inside the SYSTEM process and an NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM shell appears.
attack_vector.privileges_required: low — PR:L; the sole precondition Cisco states is valid credentials on the Windows host, with no administrative rights required
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; the sequence is deterministic and race-free, the original PoC ships as a single executable that returns a SYSTEM prompt, and Metasploit carries it as an ExcellentRanking local exploit, so weaponisation cost is effectively zero — no memory-corruption craft, no ASLR bypass, no chained prerequisite
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered — Antoine Goichot of PwC Luxembourg found the AnyConnect IPC flaws through manual analysis of the agent's localhost IPC channel in May 2020 and published both the write-up and the proof of concept himself; no fuzzing, static-analysis tooling or AI assistance is credited by Cisco, the researcher or Rapid7.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Upgrade Cisco AnyConnect Secure Mobility Client for Windows to 4.9.00086 or later — which added a 'Cisco Systems, Inc' code-signature check on every binary the installer component loads — or move to Cisco Secure Client 5.x, which supersedes the AnyConnect 4.x line.
prevention.adequacy: Cisco states there are no workarounds, so upgrading is the whole of prevention. The upgrade restarts the Secure Mobility Agent service and drops any active VPN session, which is exactly why remote-worker fleets defer it — and that deferral is what kept the CVE exploitable long enough for CISA to list it in October 2022, more than two years after the fixed release shipped.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alert on any process other than the AnyConnect UI connecting to 127.0.0.1 TCP/62522, on vpndownloader.exe executing from a ProgramData temp path rather than its install directory, and on a DLL such as dbghelp.dll appearing under ...\Temp\Downloader\ or ...\Temp\Installer\<random>.tmp\.
detection.adequacy: These are high-fidelity and cheap to collect, and the AnyConnect 'Code-signing verification succeeded' event immediately preceding a SYSTEM process creation is a clean corroborator — the pre-4.9.00086 check validated the downloader executable but not the DLLs it went on to load.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treat any host below 4.9.00086 showing the temp-path vpndownloader execution as SYSTEM-compromised — rebuild, rotate local and cached domain credentials, and review VPN session logs for lateral movement.
response.adequacy: Because CISA records this CVE with ransomware campaign use Known, an observed exploitation on a remote-access endpoint should be scoped as a pre-ransomware privilege-escalation step rather than an isolated local escalation.

NIST-800-53-AC-6.gap: AC-6 governs the privileges assigned to accounts and roles, not the privilege a SYSTEM service is willing to lend to a local caller it never authenticates — a rigorously least-privileged workstation still handed SYSTEM to any logged-on user through an unauthenticated loopback IPC listener for as long as AnyConnect below 4.9.00086 was installed.

NIS2-Art21-network-security.gap: The VPN client belongs to the Art.21 secure-remote-access control set, and here that control was itself the escalation path: every remote worker required to run AnyConnect carried a local-to-SYSTEM primitive with public exploit code, so hardening the perimeter increased endpoint attack surface on the very hosts the control was protecting.

UK-CAF-B2.gap: B2 rests on distinguishing standard users from privileged ones and governing privileged access through approvals and separate admin accounts, but on any host below 4.9.00086 standard-user credentials plus one crafted localhost IPC message produced NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM — privileged-access management controlled nothing the attacker actually needed.

AU-ISM-1546.gap: This is the control that would have closed it and it failed on dwell time rather than design: the fixed release and advisory landed 2020-08-05, public PoC availability was recorded in revision 1.1 on 2020-08-13, and CISA still had to add the CVE in October 2022 — because patch programmes routinely exempt the VPN client on the grounds that upgrading disconnects users.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.9.gap: A.8.9 assumes a hardened baseline can reduce exposure while a patch is scheduled, but the IPC listener is how the agent performs privileged installs and cannot be disabled or firewalled without breaking the client — Cisco's advisory states plainly there are no workarounds, so a conformant baseline delivered exactly zero risk reduction until each organisation actually upgraded.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2020-3433 had a fixed release — AnyConnect 4.9.00086 — and an advisory on 2020-08-05, with public proof-of-concept code recorded in advisory revision 1.1 on 2020-08-13, yet CISA still had to add it to KEV on 2022-10-24 with knownRansomwareCampaignUse=Known. That is more than two years of dwell on a remote-access estate, caused by patch programmes exempting the VPN client because the upgrade restarts the Secure Mobility Agent and drops the session.

new_control_requirements.name: SECURITY-TOOL-INTEGRITY-VERIFICATION
new_control_requirements.description: Security tools (AV/AM, EDR, vulnerability scanners) must be treated as in-scope of vulnerability management with the same SLAs as other privileged software. Definition-update channels must use TLS with certificate pinning. Compliance audits must include a trust-anchor-inversion test: deliver a crafted input to the security tool in a sandbox and confirm rejection.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2020-3433 makes the security product itself the escalation path: the SYSTEM-privileged Cisco AnyConnect Secure Mobility Agent accepts an unauthenticated 'CAC-nc-install' message on 127.0.0.1:62522 and loads an attacker-supplied dbghelp.dll alongside vpndownloader.exe. Cisco states there are no workarounds, so a hardened baseline delivers zero reduction and the client must instead carry the same vulnerability-management SLA as any other privileged software, audited by delivering that crafted IPC message in a sandbox and confirming rejection.

new_control_requirements.name: PEN-TEST-SCOPE-INCLUDES-SECURITY-PRODUCTS
new_control_requirements.description: Penetration test and red-team scopes must explicitly include security-defense products (EDR, AV, DLP, identity-providers, secret-managers) as in-scope attack surface, not as defenses to evade. Scope language must call out that these products' admin interfaces, agent processes, and update channels are testable surfaces.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2020-3433 was found by manual analysis of AnyConnect's localhost IPC channel and returns NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM from ordinary standard-user credentials via a single-executable PoC carried in Metasploit at ExcellentRanking. A scope that treats the remote-access client as a defense to be relied on rather than an agent process to be tested never examines the loopback listener that voids the standard-user-versus-privileged distinction on every host it is installed on.

attack_vector.description: A target taps a bit.ly link delivered by SMS, which routes through an exploit-hosting page before redirecting to a legitimate destination; the page drives a type confusion in WebKit's FTL JIT compiler to gain code execution in the renderer. The in-the-wild chain paired it with a PAC bypass Apple had already removed from WebKit and the n-day AGXAccelerator escape CVE-2021-30900, landing a stager that beaconed GPS position and could sideload an .IPA.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; the attacker needs no account or prior access, but UI:R means the target must open the attacker's link in WebKit
attack_vector.complexity: low to trigger — AC:L, one tap on an SMS link — but commercial-spyware-grade to build: an FTL JIT type confusion, a PAC bypass and a chained sandbox escape, which is why no public PoC exists more than three years on
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered — Apple credits Clément Lecigne of Google's Threat Analysis Group, who found it by reverse-engineering an active commercial-surveillance chain. No AI-assisted tooling appears in Apple's advisories or TAG's write-up.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Update to iOS 16.1.2, iOS/iPadOS 15.7.2, macOS Ventura 13.1, tvOS 16.2 or Safari 16.2 (iOS 12.5.7 for legacy hardware), retire handsets past their final supported release, and enable Lockdown Mode for individuals plausibly in a surveillance vendor's target set.
prevention.adequacy: Insufficient on its own. No live-patch channel existed — Apple's Rapid Security Response did not ship until iOS 16.4.1 — so remediation meant a full OS update and restart, and the iOS 12.5.7 backport for iPhone 5s/6, iPad Air and iPad mini 2/3 arrived 2023-01-23, six weeks past the KEV due date. BOD 22-01 also has no reach over the personal, unmanaged handsets that were actually exploited.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Watch for WebKit renderer crashes or JIT aborts immediately after a link opens on a device below iOS 15.1, and for applications appearing outside App Store or MDM provenance on targeted handsets.
detection.adequacy: Detection is post-hoc and misses the population that mattered: the sandbox escape ran in the same session as the renderer bug, and unmanaged personal devices produce no telemetry an operator can query.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treat a suspected hit as full device compromise — restore from a clean iOS image, rotate every account credential reachable from the handset, and replace hardware that is past its final supported OS release.
response.adequacy: Reimaging is the only reliable eviction given the second-stage implant, but devices past end of OS support cannot be remediated at all; for those the response is replacement, not recovery.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: Flaw remediation only reaches assets the organization enrolls, and Apple scoped exploitation to iOS releases older than 15.1 — personal, unmanaged handsets that had already missed the CVE-2021-30900 fix 14 months earlier. SI-2's remediation clock governed devices that were never the target.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: The exploited asset was a personal iPhone reached by an SMS link, not a system in the entity's network, so Art.21 gives no mechanism to force iOS 16.1.2 onto it — and the payload's objective, GPS beaconing and .IPA sideload against an individual, sits outside what entity-scoped patch obligations measure.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: Nothing in a stock iPhone configuration blocks the FTL JIT path; the only setting that removes the JIT surface is Lockdown Mode, which is off by default and postdates the exploited releases, so a device can satisfy every B4 hardening item and still be one tap from arbitrary code execution in WebKit.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: The 48-hour OS-patching window cannot start before the vendor ships: the iOS 12.5.7 backport for iPhone 5s/6, iPad Air, iPad mini 2/3 and iPod touch 6 landed 2023-01-23, six weeks after the KEV due date, and the maturity model carries no requirement covering hardware past its final supported release.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: A risk-ordered queue built on EPSS ~0.085 and a UI:R-discounted CVSS 8.8 ranks this beneath dozens of unauthenticated server-side bugs, while the signal that actually mattered — a live commercial-spyware zero-day on the KEV list — is not an input A.8.8 requires anyone to weight.

new_control_requirements.name: MOBILE-ENDPOINT-MDM-ENFORCED-KEV-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: iOS / iPadOS / macOS estates must enforce KEV-class updates within 24h via DDM; user-deferral disallowed.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2022-42856 was KEV-listed 2022-12-14 with a 2023-01-04 due date, and Apple shipped no live-patch channel for it — Rapid Security Response did not exist until iOS 16.4.1 — so the only remediation was a full OS update and restart of iOS 16.1.2 / 15.7.2 / iPadOS 15.7.2, macOS Ventura 13.1, tvOS 16.2 or Safari 16.2. SI-2 and A.8.8 require the update be scheduled and risk-scored (and A.8.8's inputs, EPSS ~0.085 and a UI:R-discounted CVSS 8.8, rank it low), but neither forces the KEV deadline onto the handset against user deferral.

new_control_requirements.name: MOBILE-ZERO-CLICK-HARDENING
new_control_requirements.description: High-risk mobile users must operate in a reduced-attack-surface mode (e.g. Lockdown Mode) that disables automatic processing of untrusted message attachments, fonts, and link previews, closing the zero-click delivery path patch SLAs cannot outrun.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2022-42856 was reached by rendering attacker-supplied JavaScript through the stock Safari FTL JIT after a single SMS bit.ly tap against individuals in Italy, and no default iPhone setting removes that surface — Lockdown Mode is the only configuration that takes the JIT path away, and it is off by default and postdates the exploited releases. That is why a device can satisfy every B4 hardening item and why the 48-hour E8 patch clock could not help: it cannot start before Apple ships.

new_control_requirements.name: EOL-ASSET-DECOMMISSION
new_control_requirements.description: Network-reachable end-of-life devices with no vendor patch path must be isolated and decommissioned within a bounded window; mandatory compensating segmentation applies until removal since no remediation exists.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2022-42856's backport for iPhone 5s/6, iPad Air, iPad mini 2/3 and iPod touch 6 (iOS 12.5.7, Apple HT213597) landed only on 2023-01-23, six weeks past the KEV due date, and any handset past its final supported iOS release received no fix at all. The E8 patch maturity model carries no requirement covering hardware past end of OS support, so a bounded replacement window — not a patch clock — is the only remediation available for that population.

CVE-2022-42475.name: Fortinet FortiOS Heap-Based Buffer Overflow Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: A single crafted HTTP(S) request to the internet-facing SSL-VPN web listener overflows a heap buffer inside the sslvpnd daemon, and the corrupted allocation is steered into control-flow hijack for command execution as root on the appliance. In-the-wild operators followed with a purpose-built implant rather than a shell: a trojanized IPS library staged as libips.bak and renamed over libips.so, plus code injected into /bin/miglogd and /bin/syslogd to delete operator-named strings from the device's own logs.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N/UI:N; the SSL-VPN listener answers the crafted request before any authentication step
attack_vector.complexity: low by the vector (AC:L) and discoverable at internet scale via the /remote/login body string and favicon hash, but reliable memory-corruption exploitation is version-specific — the public PoCs hardcode per-build offsets and warn they will probably not work unmodified
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered — Fortinet PSIRT published FG-IR-22-398 after learning of in-the-wild exploitation and characterised the operator as an advanced actor with deep FortiOS reverse-engineering capability. Neither Fortinet, Mandiant nor the Dutch services claim AI-assisted discovery.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Upgrade to FortiOS 7.2.3 / 7.0.9 / 6.4.11 / 6.2.12 / 6.0.16, FortiOS-6K7K 7.0.8 / 6.4.10 / 6.2.12 / 6.0.15 or FortiProxy 7.2.2 / 7.0.8 / 2.0.12 and reboot; migrate FortiOS 5.0-5.6 and FortiProxy 1.0-1.2, which receive no fix. Where the window cannot be met, disable the SSL-VPN service entirely.
prevention.adequacy: Necessary but not sufficient. The Dutch MIVD/AIVD established the actor held the bug at least two months before Fortinet's advisory and infected as many as 14,000 devices during that window, and COATHANGER survived firmware upgrades — so a unit matching Fortinet's IoC list needs a rebuild, not a version bump.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Hunt the sslvpnd 'Signal 11 received' crash entries that mark failed attempts, the implant file set (/data/lib/libips.bak, /data/etc/wxd.conf, /var/.sslvpnconfigbk), and outbound appliance connections to the published C2 addresses on 444, 8443, 8033, 20443 and 30080/30081/30443.
detection.adequacy: On-box evidence is untrustworthy by design: the implant patches miglogd and syslogd across 27 model/version pairs, deletes matching entries from decompressed elog files and rebuilds them. Usable detection has to come from network-side flow records and off-box collection.

response.what_would_have_worked: Rebuild the appliance from known-good firmware, rotate every VPN credential and certificate it terminated, and treat the device as the intrusion origin when scoping the internal hunt.
response.adequacy: The only reliable eviction path — implant persistence across firmware upgrade means a patched-looking device can still be under attacker control, and the appliance fronts every remote-access tunnel, so response scope is the networks behind it.

NIST-800-53-SC-7.gap: The boundary device is the vulnerable component: one unauthenticated request to sslvpnd yields root on the appliance terminating every remote-access tunnel, and the implant then neuters the IPS engine that SC-7 enhancements normally count as defense in depth.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: The measured interval runs from Fortinet's 2022-12-12 advisory, but MIVD/AIVD put the actor in possession of the bug at least two months earlier with as many as 14,000 devices infected — including a NIS2-class ministry — so a perfectly compliant clock started after the breach it exists to prevent.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: FortiOS is a sealed appliance with no EDR and no binary inspection, so 'well-maintained' reduces to a version banner. The trojanized libips.so and COATHANGER's survival across firmware upgrades mean that banner can read fixed on a device the attacker still controls.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Meeting the 48-hour window exactly on 2022-12-12 was already too late given the months-long zero-day period, and the maturity model discharges the control at 'update applied' — it never requires the post-patch hunt for /data/lib/libips.bak, /data/etc/wxd.conf or /var/.sslvpnconfigbk.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.16.gap: Monitoring is defeated at the source rather than the SIEM: the implant injects into /bin/miglogd and /bin/syslogd, strips operator-specified strings from decompressed elog files and rebuilds them, so complete, well-retained, alert-tuned FortiGate logs can hold no record of the compromise.

new_control_requirements.name: PERIMETER-DEVICE-ZERODAY-SLA-TIER
new_control_requirements.description: Compliance frameworks must define a distinct patch SLA tier for pre-auth RCE on perimeter-trust-boundary devices (firewalls, VPN concentrators, WAFs, edge load-balancers). Tier requirement: vendor-mitigation deployed within 4 hours of KEV listing OR isolation of the vulnerable interface; standard 14/30-day SLAs do not apply because the device IS the trust boundary.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2022-42475 is unauthenticated heap-overflow RCE in sslvpnd on the FortiGate that terminates every remote-access tunnel, so the boundary device is the vulnerable component and the implant then disables the IPS engine SC-7 enhancements normally credit. MIVD/AIVD put the actor in possession of the bug at least two months before Fortinet's 2022-12-12 advisory with as many as 14,000 devices infected, and the only interim option was disabling SSL-VPN entirely — an isolate-the-interface decision that no routine appliance-patch window contemplates.

new_control_requirements.name: PERIMETER-COMPROMISE-REBUILD-NOT-PATCH
new_control_requirements.description: Pre-rehearsed IR runbook for any perimeter device that suffers a pre-auth RCE CVE in active exploitation MUST default to config-exfil + rebuild + credential rotation, not patch-in-place. Patch-in-place leaves attacker-installed implants intact.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2022-42475's COATHANGER implant renames a trojanized libips.bak over libips.so so FortiOS auto-executes it, and MIVD/AIVD found it survived firmware upgrades — a FortiGate upgraded to 7.2.3 presents a fixed version banner while still under attacker control. The E8 patch control is discharged at 'update applied' and CAF B4 evidence reduces to that same banner, so nothing triggers the rebuild from known-good firmware plus VPN credential and certificate rotation the intrusion actually requires.

new_control_requirements.name: FIREWALL-EGRESS-TELEMETRY-SEPARATE-TRUST-ZONE
new_control_requirements.description: Firewall and other perimeter-trust-boundary devices must forward syslog, threat logs, and authentication logs to a SIEM hosted in a separate trust zone (different management plane, different credentials, different authentication path). Telemetry stored on the compromised device is destroyed by the attacker; telemetry on a separate-trust-zone collector survives.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2022-42475's implant injects into /bin/miglogd and /bin/syslogd with offsets for 27 FortiGate model/version pairs, searches decompressed elog files for operator-specified strings, deletes them and rebuilds the log, and can stop logging outright. Complete, well-retained, alert-tuned FortiGate logs therefore hold no record of the compromise, because the device authoring them is the compromised component — only records already streamed to a collector in a different trust zone survive.

CVE-2022-44698.name: Microsoft Defender SmartScreen Security Feature Bypass Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: The attacker signs the payload with a deliberately malformed Authenticode blob — Magniber used a signer certificate serial number absent from the embedded signature certificates — so Windows cannot parse it. SmartScreen throws while validating and returns an error instead of a verdict, and shdocvw.dll's DoSafeOpenPromptForShellExec leaves EDI at its initialised 0, which means Run. The Mark-of-the-Web warning is never shown, so a downloaded .JS/.JSE or MSI executes on the first double-click.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; the victim only has to double-click the downloaded file (UI:R), which the absent warning makes routine
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L, no memory corruption, no offsets and no version dependence across the affected Windows range; once the malformation is described, constructing the corrupt signature is trivial
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered — Will Dormann (ANALYGENCE) spotted the malformed-signature bypass in in-the-wild Magniber samples in October 2022, with campaign analysis from HP Wolf Security and the root-cause write-up from 0patch. No AI tooling is credited by any of them.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Install the 2022-12-13 cumulative updates — KB5021233, KB5021234, KB5021235, KB5021237, KB5021249 — or apply 0patch's in-memory micropatches, which shipped in October ahead of the vendor fix and redirect the SmartScreen-error path to the legacy security-warning dialog. Independently, block .js/.jse execution through the script host so the payload class dies whether or not the prompt renders.
prevention.adequacy: Partial. The December fix closed one throw site in smartscreen.exe rather than the fail-open default, and Google TAG observed the same class re-weaponized by Magniber as CVE-2023-24880 with over 100,000 malicious MSI downloads from January 2023, more than 80% against European users, until the March 2023 update.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alert on MOTW-tagged files that shell-execute with no prompt, on smartscreen.exe returning an error rather than a verdict, and on files whose Authenticode signer serial is absent from the embedded certificates; hunt the published TAG sample hashes.
detection.adequacy: The failure is silent by construction — SmartScreen emits no verdict to log — so any detection built on SmartScreen telemetry reads green. Only signature-parse anomaly checks or raw endpoint execution telemetry surface it.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treat the unprompted double-click as ransomware execution: isolate the host, hunt Magniber and Qakbot staging, and restore from offline backups.
response.adequacy: Purely reactive, and the margin is thin — CISA records ransomware use as Known, so the interval between the missing prompt and encryption is measured in minutes rather than days.

NIST-800-53-SI-3.gap: The malicious-code control was enabled and MOTW was correctly applied to the download; the defect converts a validation exception into an allow decision because shdocvw.dll reads SmartScreen's error through an uninitialised register that means Run. SI-3 evidence tests that the control is on, never that it fails closed.

EU-CRA-Art13.gap: Effective vulnerability handling was not delivered for a product placed on the EU market: the December 2022 update closed a single throw site rather than the fail-open default, and the same class returned as CVE-2023-24880 with over 100,000 malicious MSI downloads from January 2023 — 80%+ against European users — before the March 2023 fix landed.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: Every configuration element was correct — Zone.Identifier applied, SmartScreen enabled, the file flagged as internet-sourced — and the user still saw no prompt, so B4's evidence trail and any monitoring keyed to SmartScreen verdicts both stay green while Magniber runs.

AU-Essential-8-App-Hardening.gap: Blocking .js/.jse execution through the script host is the layer that would have survived the missing prompt, but organizations treating the warning itself as their download gate had no fallback the moment it stopped rendering, and the maturity levels never require testing what a security warning does when it fails.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.7.gap: Certification rests on deployed endpoint protection plus enabled download warnings, both true here while a ransomware family CISA flags as Known executed on first double-click. The distinguishing test — shell-execute a MOTW-tagged file carrying a corrupt signature and confirm the host fails closed — is nowhere in the control text.

new_control_requirements.name: PROTECTION-MECHANISM-FAILURE-CLASS-REGRESSION
new_control_requirements.description: Detonation chambers, EDR rules, and AppLocker/WDAC policies covering protection-mechanism classes (MOTW, SmartScreen, AMSI, ASR, WDAC, Driver Block Rules) must include class-level regression testing executed on every patch deployment, not just one-off bypass-CVE remediation. The test battery for class-X must include all historic class-X bypass primitives — incomplete patches re-introduce risk that one-off testing does not detect.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2022-44698 makes SmartScreen fail open — an unparseable Authenticode signature returns an error that shdocvw.dll's uninitialised decision register reads as Run — and Microsoft's 2022-12-13 cumulative updates closed one THROW_HR site rather than the fail-open default, so Google TAG saw the same primitive re-weaponized by Magniber as CVE-2023-24880 with over 100,000 malicious MSI downloads from January 2023 until the March 2023 fix. Only a battery that re-runs every historic MOTW/SmartScreen bypass on each patch deployment distinguishes 'control enabled' from 'control fails closed'.

new_control_requirements.name: DOWNLOAD-PROVENANCE-ENFORCEMENT
new_control_requirements.description: Enforce Mark-of-the-Web / content-provenance on all internet-sourced files and block execution of provenance-stripped shortcuts, installers, and script hosts regardless of a reputation service verdict, which attackers bypass by design.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2022-44698 removed the verdict, not the provenance: the browser applied the Zone.Identifier stream, SmartScreen was enabled and the file was flagged internet-sourced, yet the user got no prompt and Magniber ran on first double-click. Blocking execution of internet-origin script hosts and installers on the provenance marker itself — .js/.jse through the script host in particular — is the layer that survives a reputation service that returns an error instead of a decision.

new_control_requirements.name: INCOMPLETE-PATCH-SEQUENCE-SEVERITY-MULTIPLIER
new_control_requirements.description: Vulnerability-management programs must apply a severity multiplier when a CVE is the Nth in an incomplete-patch sequence on the same primitive (third MOTW bypass, second AMSI bypass, etc.). Framework controls treating each CVE as discrete obscure the structural defect; the Nth CVE in a sequence implies that future bypasses on the same primitive are likely.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2022-44698 is not a discrete defect: the December 2022 update closed a single throw site and the same MOTW/SmartScreen fail-open class returned as CVE-2023-24880, with over 100,000 malicious MSI downloads from January 2023 and more than 80% of them against European users, before March 2023. Scoring each entry separately let operators book the December patch as a clean close-out — the remediation-adequacy failure CRA Art.13 places on the manufacturer, invisible to any per-CVE severity queue.

CVE-2022-27518.name: Citrix Application Delivery Controller (ADC) and Gateway Authentication Bypass Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: On an appliance whose ns.conf configures it as a SAML service provider or identity provider ('add authentication samlAction' / 'add authentication samlIdPProfile'), an unauthenticated request reaches the SAML processing path and triggers an improper-resource-lifetime flaw, yielding code execution with administrator rights before any login is evaluated. APT5 then modified legitimate on-box binaries to persist across reboots and upgrades.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N/UI:N, though exploitation is gated on a configuration precondition the CVSS vector does not express: the appliance must have SAML SP or IdP configured, and 13.1 is not affected at all
attack_vector.complexity: low by the vector (AC:L), but the practical barrier is capability rather than access — Citrix withheld the technical detail, the target is a closed FreeBSD appliance, and more than three years on there is still no public PoC, Metasploit module or Nuclei template; observed use stayed confined to APT5
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered — Citrix credits no external researcher and stated it had observed targeted exploitation; NSA published APT5 hunting guidance the same day. Discovery traces to incident data, and neither Citrix nor NSA claims AI-assisted analysis.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Upgrade to Citrix ADC / Gateway 13.0-58.32 or 12.1-65.25, or ADC 12.1-FIPS / 12.1-NDcPP 12.1-55.291, or move to 13.1 which is unaffected; where the upgrade cannot land immediately, remove the samlAction / samlIdPProfile lines from ns.conf to disable the vulnerable path at the cost of SAML SSO.
prevention.adequacy: Incomplete for two populations. Builds prior to 12.1 are end of life and received no fix at all, so for those the only remediation is replacing or migrating off the appliance rather than patching it; and upgrading does not clear an existing intrusion, because NSA reports APT5 persists by modifying legitimate on-box binaries.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Run the NSA hunting pass: compare on-box binaries against vendor-shipped media for the installed build, look for administrator-level activity with no preceding successful authentication event, and use Citrix's own exposure test on ns.conf.
detection.adequacy: The appliance takes no EDR agent and offers limited operator visibility, which is why bespoke guidance had to be published instead of pointing at ordinary telemetry — and the tampered binaries include the ones that generate the device's logs.

response.what_would_have_worked: Rebuild the appliance from vendor media, rotate every credential and certificate the gateway terminated, and re-federate the applications sitting behind it.
response.adequacy: The only reliable eviction path, and the scope is wider than the box: because the ADC adjudicates authentication for every federated application, response has to cover the downstream estate, not just the appliance.

NIST-800-53-IA-2.gap: The vulnerable SAML handler processes attacker input before any authentication decision is reached, so MFA strength, session policy and account controls all sit behind the exploited code — and the attacker ends up executing as administrator on the appliance that adjudicates IA-2 for every downstream application.

NIS2-Art21-identity-management.gap: Only appliances with samlAction or samlIdPProfile configured are exploitable, so maturing toward gateway-terminated federated SSO is precisely what created the exposure; nothing in Art.21 requires the SSO terminator to be governed as a crown-jewel asset with its own integrity assurance.

UK-CAF-B2.gap: B2 evidence is account-centric — who authenticated, what privilege was granted, when access was reviewed — and APT5 never authenticated. With persistence living in modified on-box binaries, the access-review record stays clean while the attacker holds administrator-level execution.

AU-Essential-8-MFA.gap: A Citrix Gateway doing SAML is how many entities satisfy the internet-facing MFA requirement, yet the flaw is reached before the challenge, so Maturity Level 3 contributes nothing — and the Essential Eight has no control at all for firmware or binary integrity on a network appliance, which is where the persistence lived.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.16.gap: The ADC is closed FreeBSD with no agent and limited operator visibility, which is why NSA had to publish bespoke hunting guidance rather than point at ordinary telemetry; since the tampered binaries include those generating the appliance's logs, fully compliant monitoring can still hold no record of a months-long intrusion.

new_control_requirements.name: PERIMETER-VPN-GATEWAY-AUTH-BYPASS-EXPEDITED-REMEDIATION
new_control_requirements.description: A remote-access VPN gateway (GlobalProtect, IKEv1/IKEv2 concentrators, SSL-VPN portals) is itself the authentication enforcement point for the network perimeter; an authentication-bypass flaw on that device must be remediated on a KEV-tied expedited clock, not the routine appliance-patch window. Require: enumerate every internet-facing VPN/portal authentication surface, subscribe to the vendor's advisory feed, apply vendor interim mitigations within hours of a confirmed-exploited auth bypass, and restrict gateway exposure to known client networks where feasible. The distinguishing test: on a staging gateway running the vulnerable release, send an unauthenticated request to the portal/gateway and confirm no VPN session or interior reachability is granted before authentication completes — paper 'VPN authentication enforced' policies do not detect a pre-credential bypass that grants an interior foothold.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2022-27518 is processed by the Citrix ADC / Gateway SAML SP/IdP handler before any authentication decision, so APT5 executes as administrator on the appliance that adjudicates MFA and session policy for every application federated behind it — Maturity Level 3 phishing-resistant MFA is reached only after the exploited code. Citrix's interim mitigation is deleting the samlAction / samlIdPProfile lines from ns.conf, an hours-scale gateway action that only exists if the internet-facing portal authentication surface has been enumerated and is governed on a KEV-tied clock rather than the routine appliance-patch window.

new_control_requirements.name: PERIMETER-COMPROMISE-REBUILD-NOT-PATCH
new_control_requirements.description: Pre-rehearsed IR runbook for any perimeter device that suffers a pre-auth RCE CVE in active exploitation MUST default to config-exfil + rebuild + credential rotation, not patch-in-place. Patch-in-place leaves attacker-installed implants intact.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2022-27518 post-exploitation by APT5 persists by modifying legitimate on-box binaries, so upgrading to 13.0-58.32 or 12.1-65.25 leaves an implanted appliance implanted — NSA had to publish a binary-comparison hunt against vendor media rather than point at telemetry. Because the attacker never authenticated, B2's account-centric evidence (who logged in, what privilege was granted, when access was reviewed) stays clean throughout, so nothing but a default-to-rebuild runbook plus rotation of every credential and certificate the gateway terminated evicts them.

new_control_requirements.name: FIREWALL-EGRESS-TELEMETRY-SEPARATE-TRUST-ZONE
new_control_requirements.description: Firewall and other perimeter-trust-boundary devices must forward syslog, threat logs, and authentication logs to a SIEM hosted in a separate trust zone (different management plane, different credentials, different authentication path). Telemetry stored on the compromised device is destroyed by the attacker; telemetry on a separate-trust-zone collector survives.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2022-27518 is exploited on a closed FreeBSD appliance that takes no EDR agent, and the legitimate binaries APT5 replaces for persistence include the ones that generate the device's own logs — so an organisation with fully compliant, well-retained monitoring can hold no evidence of a months-long intrusion. Only ADC syslog and authentication records already forwarded to a SIEM on a separate management plane and credential path survive that tampering.

CVE-2022-26500.name: Veeam Backup & Replication Remote Code Execution Vulnerability (CVE-2022-26500)

attack_vector.description: Reaching the Veeam Distribution Service on TCP/9380, the attacker completes an NTLMSSP handshake with an empty username and password and then drives the internal API's file primitives — the public LeakIX client's veeamcp and veeamdl copy and download arbitrary absolute paths on v10 and v11 servers. Writing into a location the product or the OS later executes converts the path-traversal read/write into code execution; in the wild the weaponized form was Veeamp.exe, which read the VeeamBackup SQL database and printed the decrypted Credentials table.
attack_vector.privileges_required: contested and it matters: NVD scores PR:L and describes 'remote authenticated users', while CISA and Veeam KB4288 both describe unauthenticated internal-API access and the public client authenticates with empty NTLMSSP credentials — treat the effective requirement as none wherever TCP/9380 is reachable
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L, no user interaction, a single TCP service and no per-build offsets; the only friction is network reachability, not attacker skill
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered — Veeam KB4288 credits Nikita Petrov of Positive Technologies through coordinated disclosure. Weaponization was human as well: Kaspersky attributes in-the-wild use to a hand-written C# credential dumper, not to generated exploit code.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Patch the backup server to build 11.0.1.1261 P20220302 (11a) or 10.0.1.4854 P20220304 (10a), after which managed servers update their Distribution Service automatically; upgrade 9.5U3 and 9.5U4, which receive no patch. Segment TCP/9380 away from user VLANs, and stop and disable the Distribution Service wherever the patch cannot land yet.
prevention.adequacy: The fix existed from March 2022 but KEV only flagged it in December, so entities driven by regulatory signals rather than vendor KBs carried nine months of exposure — and patching does nothing about credentials Veeamp already exfiltrated from the VeeamBackup database.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alert on NTLMSSP handshakes carrying an empty username and password to TCP/9380 followed by internal-API file copy or upload calls, on files written by the Veeam service account outside the Distribution Service's directory tree, and on the presence of Veeamp.exe or equivalent credential-extraction tooling on or near backup servers.
detection.adequacy: The signature is unambiguous but almost never collected — 9380 is an internal management port most estates do not monitor, so the detection exists in principle and not in the SIEM.

response.what_would_have_worked: Rotate every credential stored in the VeeamBackup database, rebuild the backup server, and validate restore points against a copy the compromised platform could not reach.
response.adequacy: Mandatory given Cuba, Conti and Yanluowang use: the stolen Credentials table is the lateral-movement inventory for everything the platform backs up, so credential rotation has to extend well beyond the backup fabric.

NIST-800-53-SC-7.gap: TCP/9380 is treated as an internal management port and rarely segmented, which puts an unauthenticated file read/write primitive against the backup control plane one hop from any compromised workstation. SC-7 as commonly implemented never asks whether the host holding credentials for every backed-up system is isolated from those systems.

DORA-Art-9.gap: The ICT protection obligation covers backup integrity, yet the platform exposed an unauthenticated internal API on TCP/9380 and the observed tooling harvested exactly the stored credentials the regulation expects protected. Veeam fixed it in March 2022 while CISA flagged it in December, so a financial entity tracking regulatory signals rather than vendor KBs left the gap open for nine months.

UK-CAF-D1.gap: Response and recovery planning assumes the recovery capability sits outside the incident. Reaching TCP/9380 gives file write plus, via Veeamp, the stored credentials for every managed server, so a documented and exercised D1 plan built on unpatched Veeam 11.x scores well while being the fastest route to total compromise.

AU-Essential-8-Backup.gap: Every requirement — retention, restoration testing, and at ML3 preventing unprivileged accounts from modifying or deleting backups — is account-scoped, but the attacker executes as the Veeam service holding its stored credentials, so each restriction is enforced against an identity that has already been superseded.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.13.gap: The control certifies copies, schedules and restoration tests and never touches the backup application's management plane, so an auditor can sign off a fully compliant regime running Veeam 11.x below build 11.0.1.1261 P20220302 with 9380 open to the user VLAN. The useful questions — which segments reach the Distribution Service, and at what build — are not in A.8.13.

new_control_requirements.name: BACKUP-TIER-NETWORK-ISOLATION
new_control_requirements.description: Backup-orchestration appliances and backup-data destinations must be network-isolated from the data-plane networks they protect. Management surfaces must be reachable only from operator subnets; backup-data paths must use unidirectional or pull-only patterns from the backup tier to the protected systems where possible.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2022-26500 is reached through the Veeam Distribution Service on TCP/9380, an internal management port most estates leave flat with the user VLAN, and yields file read/write plus — via Veeamp against the VeeamBackup Credentials table — the stored credentials for every managed server. SC-7 never nominates the backup fabric as a key internal boundary, A.8.13 certifies copies and restore tests without asking which segments reach 9380, and D1 assumes the recovery capability sits outside the incident when it is one hop from any compromised workstation.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2022-26500 was fixed by Veeam in March 2022 (11a build 11.0.1.1261 P20220302 / 10a build 10.0.1.4854 P20220304) but only KEV-listed on 2022-12-13, so financial entities driving remediation from regulatory signals rather than vendor KBs carried nine months of exposure on the host holding credentials for every backed-up system. DORA Art.9 states the ICT protection obligation without an interval; once the KEV signal finally arrived, a 4-hour clock against an already-available build is what converts that obligation into a deployment date.

CVE-2022-26501.name: Veeam Backup & Replication Remote Code Execution Vulnerability (CVE-2022-26501)

attack_vector.description: The attacker dials TCP 9380, wraps the .NET NNS framing and completes an NTLMSSP handshake with an empty username and password, then sends FIData/FISpec XML documents whose FISessionID is the all-zero GUID — no authenticated session at any point. A CacheRequest (FIScope=190, FIMethod=24) stages an arbitrary absolute path on the backup server for retrieval over an attacker-run SCP listener, and an UploadRequest carrying FileRemotePath, SshCredentials and SshTrustAll drives the agent-push path to write and execute on a host no operator job ever selected.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N/UI:N; the Distribution Service honours an NTLMSSP null session and an all-zero session identifier, so no account is involved
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L understates it: no memory corruption, no race window, no per-build offsets, and the same request works across the entire affected range. The only precondition is network reachability to TCP 9380, so exploitation is gated by segmentation rather than skill
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered — reported to Veeam by Nikita Petrov of Positive Technologies through manual protocol review and fixed in KB4288; Kaspersky attributes the in-the-wild weaponization to a hand-written C# utility rather than generated exploit code.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Apply the KB4288 fix — 11a build 11.0.1.1261 P20220302 or 10a build 10.0.1.4854 P20220304 — accepting the service restart; upgrade 9.5, which is affected, out of support and never patched. Where the patch cannot land immediately, stop and disable the Veeam Distribution Service on the backup server and every designated distribution server.
prevention.adequacy: Closes the API but does not close the incident. With CISA recording ransomware use as Known, the host needs a hunt for prior credential theft from the VeeamBackup database before it can be treated as clean — and on 9.5 there is no patch to apply at all.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alert on anonymous NTLMSSP handshakes to TCP 9380 followed by requests carrying the all-zero FISessionID, on Svc.VeeamBackup.log cache or upload entries with no matching operator-initiated job, on outbound SSH/SCP from the backup server to an unexpected listener, and on veeamp.exe or aswarpot.sys appearing on or near the backup fabric.
detection.adequacy: The log evidence is present on the host but no product ships a rule for it, and by the time Burntcigar is loading the signed Avast driver to terminate endpoint protection, detection is racing encryption.

response.what_would_have_worked: Rebuild the backup server, rotate every credential held in the VeeamBackup database, and validate restore points from immutable or genuinely offline copies before trusting any of them.
response.adequacy: Essential: with pre-authentication code execution the attacker owned the copies, the catalog and the stored credentials before any restore was attempted, so recovering from the compromised platform can reintroduce the attacker.

NIST-800-53-SC-7.gap: The backup fabric is almost never nominated as a key internal boundary, so the Distribution Service sits flat with the servers it protects. Because it accepts an NTLMSSP null session and then honours file staging and agent push, reachability of TCP 9380 is equivalent to code execution on the one host that can read every restore point in the estate.

NIS2-Art21-business-continuity.gap: Backup management and disaster recovery are named as the answer to a ransomware incident, which presumes the platform is a refuge. A pre-authentication 9.8 inside Veeam Backup & Replication with a Known ransomware flag makes the continuity control both the initial foothold and the source of the decrypted Credentials table used to reach the rest of the network.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: There is no misconfiguration to find: the service listens on TCP 9380 by default and pre-fix builds accept unauthenticated internal-API calls as a property of the defect, so a hardening-baseline assessment returns clean. On 9.5 — affected, out of support, unpatchable — the vulnerability-management outcome cannot be satisfied at all short of a product upgrade.

AU-Essential-8-Backup.gap: Frequency, off-network retention, restoration testing and the ML3 restriction on unprivileged accounts altering backups are all measured against accounts, and this exploit needs none. The audit evidence keeps passing unchanged while an unauthenticated network peer holds code execution on the backup server itself.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.13.gap: The control assumes the backup system is a trustworthy, operator-controlled component holding known-good state. Pre-authentication RCE inverts that — the attacker owns the copies, the catalog and the stored credentials before any restore — so 'restores succeeded last quarter' is false assurance for an organisation already staged for backup destruction.

new_control_requirements.name: BACKUP-TIER-NETWORK-ISOLATION
new_control_requirements.description: Backup-orchestration appliances and backup-data destinations must be network-isolated from the data-plane networks they protect. Management surfaces must be reachable only from operator subnets; backup-data paths must use unidirectional or pull-only patterns from the backup tier to the protected systems where possible.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2022-26501 needs no account at all — the Veeam Distribution Service on TCP 9380 accepts an NTLMSSP null session and then honours file-staging and agent-push API methods, and LeakIX's April 2022 scans found instances answering from the public internet while Cuba reached others laterally. Reachability alone is therefore code execution on the one host that can read every restore point, which makes the continuity platform NIS2 Art.21(2)(c) names as the ransomware answer into the entry vector unless the backup tier is isolated from the networks it protects.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2022-26501 is a CVSS 9.8 pre-auth RCE that CISA records with knownRansomwareCampaignUse=Known, and there is no misconfiguration for a CAF B4 hardening assessment to find: the service listens on 9380 by default and pre-fix builds accept unauthenticated internal-API calls as a property of the defect, so the only variable is the build. That makes the KEV listing (2022-12-13) the single actionable signal, and it has to carry an hours-scale deadline to reach 11.0.1.1261 P20220302 / 10.0.1.4854 P20220304 or stop the Distribution Service.

CVE-2022-4262.name: Google Chromium V8 Type Confusion Vulnerability (CVE-2022-4262)

attack_vector.description: A crafted HTML page exploits a V8 parser inconsistency: a function containing an eval() call inside an arrow function with a class-expression default argument compiles to different bytecode on first versus subsequent compilation. The page first forces bytecode flushing — the Project Zero reproducer allocates six 31 GB ArrayBuffers — so the function is re-parsed down the other path, then converts the resulting PropertyCell/FeedbackCell confusion into arbitrary read/write in the V8 heap. The observed campaign delivered it through one-time SMS links and chained CVE-2022-3038 to escape the renderer sandbox.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; the target only has to open the attacker's page (UI:R), which the Heliconia campaign achieved with a single SMS link
attack_vector.complexity: low to trigger — AC:L, one crafted HTML page — but originally high to build, requiring the bytecode-flush precondition plus turning a cell confusion into arbitrary read/write; mistymntncop's public exploit.js has since removed that development cost, which EPSS ~0.155 has not caught up with
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered — the Chrome stable-channel note credits Clément Lecigne of Google's Threat Analysis Group, who found it by analysing an exploit already deployed in the wild, and Samuel Groß of V8 Security wrote the root-cause analysis. No AI tooling appears in the release note, the Project Zero RCA or the TAG report.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Update to Chrome Stable 108.0.5359.94 (108.0.5359.94/.95 on Windows, Extended Stable 108.0.5359.94) and enforce a managed forced-relaunch policy so the fixed V8 binary actually replaces the running one; extend the same sweep to every Chromium-derived browser and embedded WebView on the estate.
prevention.adequacy: Incomplete on its own. Auto-update stages the fix on disk while a long-lived browser process keeps executing the old binary, so the relaunch policy is the control that actually ends exposure — and Chromium derivatives stay vulnerable until each rebases past the V8 fix commit. Samsung Internet, not Chrome, was the browser attacked in the wild.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Flag JavaScript that forces bytecode flushing through multi-gigabyte ArrayBuffer allocations, V8 crash telemetry immediately after a page executes an arrow function whose class-expression computed key contains eval(), and renderer code execution followed in the same session by a sandbox-escape attempt.
detection.adequacy: The detections that work exist only on managed desktops, which were not the target — the exploited surface was personal mobile browsers reached by one-time SMS links, where none of this telemetry is collected.

response.what_would_have_worked: On suspected targeting, assume the full chain ran — sandbox escape plus the Android kernel stages — and rebuild the device, then rotate credentials for the chat and browser data the implant was built to decrypt.
response.adequacy: Necessary, because renderer compromise was never the end state: the observed chain finished in a C++ spyware implant carrying libraries for decrypting chat and browser data.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: Remediation timelines presume disclosure precedes exploitation, but Google shipped 108.0.5359.94 only after TAG recovered a working exploit from Variston's Heliconia framework. SI-2 also stops at 'update installed', with no requirement for the forced relaunch that actually retires the vulnerable V8 binary from a Chrome process running for days.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: The asset register is keyed on the product you patch, and the browser exploited in the wild was Samsung Internet, not Chrome — so a record reading 'Google Chrome 108.0.5359.94, compliant' says nothing about the Chromium-derived browsers, embedded WebViews and mobile browsers on the same estate that had not yet rebased past the V8 fix.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: Delivery was a one-time SMS link opening a personal mobile browser in a targeted UAE campaign — a surface B4's outcome tests neither assess nor credit — so an operator can evidence full compliance across the corporate fleet while the individuals actually selected for Heliconia targeting are compromised through a channel the framework never inspects.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: The application-patching clock reads from vendor release, but here the exploit existed first and the fix second, so the window only opened on 2022-12-02 after the exploitation period had already run. Even at Maturity Level 3 the control is discharged by installing the update rather than by forcing the relaunch that ends exposure.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: Score-driven prioritisation reads CVSS 8.8 with UI:R and S:U as a routine renderer-sandboxed browser bug next to a queue of unauthenticated 9.8s. The signals that mattered — a surveillance vendor already chaining it with CVE-2022-3038, CVE-2022-22706 and CVE-2023-0266, and a public exploit.js that erased the development cost — are not inputs A.8.8 requires.

new_control_requirements.name: BROWSER-MANAGED-UPDATE-NO-DEFERRAL
new_control_requirements.description: Enterprise update rings must not defer security-channel browser updates beyond 24h.
