UK-CAF-B2.gap: B2 treats the ADB shell user and the video/graphics group as bounded local identities, but the integer overflow converts write access to /dev/graphics/fb0 into a read-write mapping of the entire kernel. Access-control assurance over that group is meaningless once membership in it is a route to ring 0.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Operating-system patch timeframes were met on the Linux server estate — RHSA-2015:0695, 0782 and 0803 backported the fix, years late but within a measurable process — while the Android handsets the CVE actually names never received it. The maturity model scores the patchable population and stays silent on the unpatchable one, which is exactly where the KEV listing points.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: A.8.8 requires timely vulnerability information for assets in use, but the authoritative exploit evidence here lives in an XDA-Developers thread and a droidrzr.com root-method post, both NVD exploit-tagged, rather than in any vendor or distro advisory. A programme that ingests only advisory feeds never sees the exploit that earned this CVE its KEV listing.

new_control_requirements.name: MOBILE-OS-MINIMUM-PATCH-LEVEL-ENFORCEMENT
new_control_requirements.description: Managed mobile fleets must enforce a minimum OS security-patch level as a condition of access to organizational data, not merely report it. For Android, the MDM/EMM must read the device security-patch level and block or quarantine devices below the patch level that fixes a KEV-listed Framework flaw (here, 2026-06-01), and constrain installation of untrusted/side-loaded apps on devices that cannot yet update - since the privilege escalation is driven by locally running code. The distinguishing test: enroll a device pinned below 2026-06-01 and confirm the MDM policy denies it access to protected resources (rather than only recording the stale patch level on a dashboard) - paper 'mobile patching' policies that surface patch level without enforcing it leave exploitable devices in production.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2013-2596 is reached by Motochopper through the ADB shell on Motorola Android 4.1.2 builds that never received the 3.8.9 fb_mmap fix, and developer options stayed enabled across enterprise-issued Atrix HD, RAZR HD and RAZR M fleets whose configuration baselines enumerated software, ports and services but not device-side debug transports. An MDM that reads the patch level, quarantines devices below the fixed build and constrains locally installed or side-loaded code governs exactly the precondition the exploit needs.

new_control_requirements.name: EOL-ASSET-DECOMMISSION
new_control_requirements.description: Network-reachable end-of-life devices with no vendor patch path must be isolated and decommissioned within a bounded window; mandatory compensating segmentation applies until removal since no remediation exists.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2013-2596 turns one crafted mmap2 call against /dev/graphics/fb0 into a read-write mapping of the entire kernel, and on the Motorola Android 4.1.2 builds the CVE explicitly names no fix was ever issued, so wiping and re-provisioning the handset restores exactly the same exposure. Isolation plus replacement inside a bounded window is what distinguishes an unpatchable asset from a merely unpatched one, which the patch-management process on its own cannot express.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2013-2596's authoritative exploit evidence is an XDA-Developers thread and a droidrzr.com root-method post that NVD tags as exploit references, not a vendor or distro advisory, so a programme fed only by advisory feeds never saw the Motochopper release that earned the 2022-09-15 KEV listing. Keying the remediation clock and its compensating-control option to KEV entry rather than to advisory publication is what puts this CVE in front of the operator at all.

attack_vector.description: perf_event_open() copies the 64-bit attr.config into a 32-bit int before its sanity check, so a value with the high word set survives validation and then indexes perf_swevent_enabled out of bounds; the sw_perf_event_destroy() teardown path decrements a location of the attacker's choosing. semtex.c turns that single decrement into an IDT-adjacent overwrite, executes shellcode in ring 0 and zeroes the uid and gid fields of its own credential structure.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; any unprivileged local account suffices, which makes shared shells, CI runners, hosting tenants and container workloads the natural targets, and on a container host the same write reaches the shared host kernel
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L and deterministic: no race, no information leak and no heap spray, with semtex.c running to a few hundred lines and completing in seconds
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered — Tommi Rantala found it with the Trinity system-call fuzzer in April 2013, a randomised fuzzer with no machine-learning component, and weaponisation was hand-written by 'sd' with retargeted variants from Andrea Bittau and 'sorbo'.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: The upstream fix in Linux 3.8.9 (commit 8176cced706b, which keeps attr.config as u64 in perf_swevent_init) or a vendor kernel — RHSA-2013:0830, 0832, 0840 and 0841, RHSA-2013:0829 for MRG 2, Ubuntu USN-1825-1 through USN-1838-1 — each requiring a reboot; where a reboot could not be scheduled, blocking perf_event_open() with seccomp or setting kernel.perf_event_paranoid to 3 on distros carrying that hardening patch.
prevention.adequacy: Patching worked, but the fix and the public exploit landed together, so any host carrying an unprivileged shell account was already reachable inside the remediation window. The upstream perf_event_paranoid maximum of 2 is not sufficient as a stopgap, because it still permits the unprivileged software-event creation this bug lives in.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Auditing perf_event_open() calls whose attr.config carries a high word, and alerting on unprivileged processes acquiring uid 0 without an execve of a setuid binary; on container hosts, any workload reaching host-kernel privilege.
detection.adequacy: Syscall auditing catches this only where perf_event_open was already in the audit rule set, which was uncommon, and the credential change is instantaneous and in-process — there is no exec event for conventional endpoint tooling to hang a detection on.

response.what_would_have_worked: Rebuild the host and rotate every credential, key and token present on it, scoping the incident to the node rather than the workload because the write lands in shared kernel memory.
response.adequacy: Container tenancy sets the response boundary: escalating from one workload to the host kernel puts every co-resident tenant in scope, so restarting the offending container is not containment.

NIST-800-53-CM-7.gap: Least functionality never treated perf_event_open() as optional, yet that syscall is reachable by any unprivileged local user by default and constitutes the entire attack surface. Gating it with seccomp, or raising perf_event_paranoid to 3 where the distro supported it, was the one configuration change that blocked exploitation, and no CM-7 baseline of the era enumerated it.

DORA-Art-9.gap: Art.9 is written around ICT systems supporting critical or important functions and assumes privilege boundaries hold inside a host. This flaw voids that assumption on every 2.6.37-3.8.8 Linux host: one unprivileged account on a shared batch, jump or web tier reaches root, and on a container host it reaches the shared kernel. The article's governance-level framing yields no test that would surface the condition on a financial entity's Linux estate.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: B4 is evidenced through hardening baselines and patch state, but the introducing commit sat unnoticed for three years and the bug was ultimately found by Trinity syscall fuzzing — an assurance activity B4 does not contemplate. A fully-evidenced B4 posture told the operator nothing about this exposure between 2011 and 2013.

AU-ISM-1546.gap: The patch clock starts at advisory publication, but semtex.c circulated at the same moment the fix landed in 3.8.9, so even the 48-hour Maturity Level 3 window is a window in which every unprivileged shell account on the host already held root. A timeframe-based control cannot express a clock that starts simultaneously with the exploit's.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: Every distro-managed host was in scope and was remediated through RHSA-2013:0830, USN-1825-1 and their siblings. What A.8.8 misses is the long tail the KEV listing targets — appliances and embedded Linux images that vendored a 2.6.37-3.8 kernel and never rebased, where no asset record names a kernel version to evaluate in the first place.

new_control_requirements.name: CONTAINER-HOST-NAMESPACE-ESCAPE-HARDENING
new_control_requirements.description: Container hosts must treat the kernel - not the namespace boundary - as the last line of defense against a confined workload. Patch host kernels to the fixed release for each maintained series (with reboot) or apply a vendor live-kernel-patch, and layer compensating controls that block cgroups/namespace escapes even on an unpatched kernel: confine every container with AppArmor or SELinux and a seccomp profile, drop CAP_SYS_ADMIN, and disable unprivileged user namespaces where workloads do not need them. The distinguishing test: from inside a representative container on a staging host, attempt the release_agent escape (create user+cgroup namespaces, mount cgroupfs, write a payload path to release_agent, trigger cgroup release) and confirm it is refused before any code runs as root - a fleet that passes image-scan and RBAC audits but permits this on an unpatched, unconfined host still allows container-to-host root.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2013-2094 is reachable by any unprivileged local account through perf_event_open(), and its out-of-bounds decrement lands in shared kernel memory, so a confined workload reaches the host kernel and every co-resident tenant with it — restarting the offending container is not containment. Seccomp confinement of the syscall, or kernel.perf_event_paranoid set to 3 where the distro carried that hardening patch, was the one compensating control that held on an unpatched host; the upstream maximum of 2 is not sufficient because it still permits the unprivileged software-event creation the bug lives in.

new_control_requirements.name: LIVE-PATCH-CAPABILITY
new_control_requirements.description: For any system that processes production workloads and cannot tolerate unplanned reboots: live kernel patching capability (kpatch, livepatch, kGraft, or equivalent) must be deployed and tested quarterly.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2013-2094's every vendor remediation — RHSA-2013:0830, 0832, 0840 and 0841, RHSA-2013:0829 for MRG 2, and USN-1825-1 through USN-1838-1 — is a kernel package upgrade requiring a reboot, in code compiled into vmlinux with no hot-swap path, while semtex.c circulated at the moment the fix landed in 3.8.9. A shared batch, jump or hosting tier that could not take an unplanned reboot was owned inside its own patch window, so the capability to apply the fix without restarting is what makes any patch timeframe achievable here.

new_control_requirements.name: KERNEL-EXPLOITATION-DETECTION
new_control_requirements.description: Deploy auditd or eBPF-based monitoring rules for kernel privilege escalation indicators. Alert within 60 seconds of detection.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2013-2094 zeroes the uid and gid fields of its own credential structure in-process and instantaneously, with no execve of a setuid binary for conventional endpoint tooling to hang a detection on, so the only observable signals are perf_event_open() calls whose attr.config carries a high word and an unprivileged process acquiring uid 0. Those are auditd or eBPF rules that no framework in scope required, which is why a governance-level protection obligation produced no test that would have surfaced the escalation on a Linux estate.

CVE-2010-2568.name: Microsoft Windows Remote Code Execution Vulnerability (CVE-2010-2568)

attack_vector.description: Windows Shell parses a crafted .LNK or .PIF shortcut's icon reference while Explorer renders the containing directory, resolves it to a DLL on removable media, an SMB share or a WebDAV mount, and loads that DLL into the shell process — no file is opened, no macro is enabled and no AutoRun entry is involved. Stuxnet used exactly this to execute from USB media before MS10-046 shipped, and Metasploit's ms10_046_shortcut_icon_dllloader automates the remote WebDAV form.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; the DLL loads at whatever privilege the user browsing the directory already holds, with no credential or prior foothold needed
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L with UI:R, where the 'interaction' is merely a directory being rendered; there is no memory corruption to get right, so the exploit is architecture-independent and behaves identically from Windows XP through Windows 7
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered — VirusBlokAda's Sergey Ulasen and Oleg Kupreev isolated it inside Stuxnet while investigating reboot loops on customer machines in June 2010, and weaponisation was nation-state exploit development delivered on binaries signed with stolen Realtek and JMicron certificates. The 2015 patch bypass was likewise found by a human researcher, Michael Heerklotz, reported through ZDI.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: MS10-046 (KB2286198, released out of band on 2010-08-02) AND MS15-020, since the whitelist check the first update added was bypassable as CVE-2015-0096. Every affected Windows release is now out of support, so on the OT/ICS and legacy embedded estates where this CVE stays current there is no patch to apply and the practical measures are removable-media control and host replacement.
prevention.adequacy: A host that installed MS10-046 and stopped there stayed exploitable through the same icon-loading path for four and a half years until MS15-020. The pre-patch workarounds Microsoft documented — disabling shortcut-icon display via the registry and stopping the WebClient service — blank most icons and cut only the WebDAV leg, so neither is a substitute for both updates, and on the out-of-support population neither update is available at all.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alerting on DLL loads into explorer.exe sourced from removable drives, UNC paths or WebDAV mounts, on .LNK files whose icon resource points outside the local system, and on WebClient service traffic to external hosts.
detection.adequacy: The load happens inside a trusted shell process during ordinary browsing, and Stuxnet's carrier was signed with stolen Realtek and JMicron certificates that satisfied the trust checks endpoint products relied on — which is why the zero-day was ultimately found by analysts chasing reboot loops rather than by any detection product.

response.what_would_have_worked: Isolate the host, image it for the loaded DLL and its shortcut, trace the removable media or share it arrived on and every other machine that mounted the same path, then rebuild rather than clean.
response.adequacy: Response has to follow the media rather than the host: one USB stick or share reaches every workstation that renders its directory, and in air-gapped OT cells that transfer path is the sanctioned one, so containment scoped to a single machine misses the propagation entirely.

NIST-800-53-MP-7.gap: Media-use restriction fails at its own premise: the DLL loads the moment Explorer renders the icon, with no file opened and no AutoRun involved, so 'disable AutoRun' and 'scan removable media on mount' — the two implementations most estates deployed after Conficker — never intercept it. MP-7 also assumes an approved-media allowlist is enforceable in OT areas where USB is the only sanctioned transfer path into an air-gapped cell.

NIS2-Art21-network-security.gap: Segmentation is assumed to bound exposure, but this vector crosses air gaps on removable media and, in its remote form, fires over a WebDAV or SMB share the instant a user browses the directory. An entity with textbook OT/IT separation still carries the full blast radius, which is why the LNK exploit remained among the most-detected exploits worldwide for years after MS10-046 shipped.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: Secure-configuration evidence cannot cover a parser that lives in operating systems long past end of support — XP SP3, Server 2003 SP2, Vista and Server 2008 persist in OT/ICS cells precisely because the essential function depends on them. B4 assurance for those systems degenerates into a compensating-control narrative wrapped around an icon parser that will never be fixed on that host.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: The OS-patching control was satisfied by installing MS10-046 out of band on 2010-08-02 — and that patch was incomplete. The bypass Michael Heerklotz reported through ZDI became CVE-2015-0096 and was closed only by MS15-020 in March 2015, so a Maturity Level 3 estate that had 'patched' stayed exploitable through the same path for four and a half years. A patch-application maturity score has no way to express a fix that does not fix.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.7.gap: A.8.7 presumes signature and behavioural malware protection is the defence, but this zero-day was isolated by VirusBlokAda analysts investigating reboot loops rather than by any product's detection logic, and the malware carrying it was signed with stolen Realtek and JMicron code-signing certificates that defeated the trust signals endpoint protection relied on. Assurance built on deployment coverage and signature currency gives no reading on a novel shell-parsing exploit delivered on a signed binary.

new_control_requirements.name: INCOMPLETE-PATCH-SEQUENCE-SEVERITY-MULTIPLIER
new_control_requirements.description: Vulnerability-management programs must apply a severity multiplier when a CVE is the Nth in an incomplete-patch sequence on the same primitive (third MOTW bypass, second AMSI bypass, etc.). Framework controls treating each CVE as discrete obscure the structural defect; the Nth CVE in a sequence implies that future bypasses on the same primitive are likely.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2010-2568 was closed by MS10-046 (KB2286198) out of band on 2010-08-02, but the whitelist check that update added was itself bypassable: Michael Heerklotz's ZDI-reported bypass became CVE-2015-0096 and was only fixed by MS15-020 in March 2015, so a host that installed the first update and stopped there stayed exploitable through the same icon-loading path for four and a half years. A patch-application maturity score cannot express a fix that does not fix; treating the shell shortcut-parsing primitive as an incomplete-patch sequence can.

new_control_requirements.name: EOL-ASSET-DECOMMISSION
new_control_requirements.description: Network-reachable end-of-life devices with no vendor patch path must be isolated and decommissioned within a bounded window; mandatory compensating segmentation applies until removal since no remediation exists.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2010-2568's vulnerable shell parser lives in Windows XP SP3, Server 2003 SP2, Vista and Server 2008 — all out of support, and all still resident in OT/ICS cells precisely because the essential function depends on them, which is why the CVE was still worth a KEV listing in 2022. With neither MS10-046 nor MS15-020 available to that population, isolation with mandatory compensating segmentation and replacement inside a bounded window is the remediation, rather than a secure-configuration narrative wrapped around an icon parser that will never be fixed on that host.

new_control_requirements.name: DOWNLOAD-PROVENANCE-ENFORCEMENT
new_control_requirements.description: Enforce Mark-of-the-Web / content-provenance on all internet-sourced files and block execution of provenance-stripped shortcuts, installers, and script hosts regardless of a reputation service verdict, which attackers bypass by design.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2010-2568 loads an attacker's DLL into the shell the instant Explorer renders a crafted .LNK from a WebDAV or SMB share — no file opened, no macro enabled — and the Stuxnet carrier was signed with stolen Realtek and JMicron certificates that satisfied the trust and reputation signals endpoint protection relied on. Blocking execution of provenance-stripped shortcuts regardless of the reputation verdict is the control that does not depend on the signature being trustworthy, which signature-currency-based malware-protection assurance did.

CVE-2021-31010.name: Apple iOS, macOS, watchOS Sandbox Bypass Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: Attacker code already executing inside an application sandbox on an iPhone, iPad, Mac or Apple Watch hands a crafted serialized object to the Core Telephony system service, whose deserialization path validates it inadequately; the resulting integrity failure lets the process act outside the restrictions its sandbox profile imposes. Apple names the component and the bug class but never the IPC transport, and the entry sits in the same advisory as FORCEDENTRY (CVE-2021-30860), which is the zero-click initial-access half of the pattern this escape completes.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none per the CVSS vector (PR:N), but the real precondition is code execution already held inside an application sandbox — this is the escape stage of a chain, not an entry point
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; a deserialization validation gap is deterministic, with no race window and none of the reliability tax that memory-corruption primitives carry, which is exactly why chains of this era reached for it
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered — Apple credits Citizen Lab and Google Project Zero, two named human research organisations working from in-the-wild mercenary-spyware samples. No AI tooling appears in any primary source, and 2021 predates the AI-assisted discovery wave.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Move devices to iOS 12.5.5, iOS/iPadOS 14.8, macOS Big Sur 11.6, macOS Catalina with Security Update 2021-005 or watchOS 7.6.2 (or any later train) — each requires a reboot, and no live-patch path exists because the fix ships inside the OS image. There is no configuration workaround: Core Telephony is a system service every sandboxed application is entitled to reach, so the deserialization path cannot be disabled, firewalled or entitlement-stripped. Hardware past its final supported OS train can never reach a fixed build and must be retired rather than patched.
prevention.adequacy: Updating is complete remediation where it can be applied, but for eight months there was nothing to apply it against by identifier: Apple shipped the Core Telephony fix in September 2021 with no CVE attached and only added the CVE-2021-31010 entry to its advisories on 25 May 2022, so an identifier-driven patch programme saw no vulnerability until the KEV listing a year after the code was already fixed.

detection.what_would_have_worked: MDM-reported build state below the fixed versions, plus Apple's own mercenary-spyware threat notifications to affected account holders; behaviourally, a sandboxed application passing serialized objects to Core Telephony and then performing file access, network egress or work outside its container.
detection.adequacy: Detection is structurally unavailable on stock Apple platforms — there is no on-device artifact an enterprise tool can read for this path, so triage collapses to version state and vendor notification, and absence of evidence is not evidence of absence.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treat a notified or suspect device as compromised end to end: update or retire the hardware, rotate every credential and token that touched it, and lift any MDM software-update deferral policy holding managed devices below the September 2021 security trains.
response.adequacy: Response is the only remaining lever once a sandbox escape has run, and it is a blunt one — a chained implant of this class leaves nothing the organisation can inspect to scope what was taken.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: Flaw remediation only moves when a flaw is identified, and Apple published the fixed builds in September 2021 without attaching a CVE to the Core Telephony entry. An SI-2 programme keyed on vulnerability identifiers had nothing to schedule until the May 2022 advisory revision, so the remediation clock effectively started at the August 2022 KEV listing rather than when the fix shipped.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: Art.21 vulnerability handling presumes the vendor names an identifier and the asset is on the ICT register. Neither held: disclosure was silent for eight months, and iOS 12.x handsets, iPadOS tablets and watchOS wearables commonly sit outside an essential entity's inventory entirely, so a fully conformant entity could carry this sandbox escape on every corporate iPhone and Apple Watch.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: B4 hardening is layered on top of the platform's isolation boundary, and here the boundary itself is what breaks. Profile restrictions, app allowlisting and network policy — the measures actually available to an operator of a managed Apple device — none of them sit between a sandboxed process and the Core Telephony service every sandboxed app is entitled to call.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: The 'patch operating systems' mitigation is scoped by the ACSC to workstations, servers and network devices; iOS, iPadOS and watchOS fall outside the assessment boundary. Even where mobile is pulled in scope voluntarily, the two-week and 48-hour targets trigger on a vendor advisory naming the flaw, and no such advisory named it until May 2022.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: A.8.8 depends on timely vulnerability information that the vendor deliberately withheld for eight months, and its risk-based prioritisation would then have ranked a 7.5 sandbox bypass with no confidentiality and no availability impact below the remote-code-execution entries in the same advisory — inverting the real priority, since this was the escape stage of a zero-click chain aimed at named individuals.

new_control_requirements.name: MOBILE-ENDPOINT-MDM-ENFORCED-KEV-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: iOS / iPadOS / macOS estates must enforce KEV-class updates within 24h via DDM; user-deferral disallowed.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2021-31010 has no configuration workaround — Core Telephony is a system service every sandboxed application is entitled to reach, so the only remediation is the iOS 12.5.5 / iOS 14.8 / Big Sur 11.6 / watchOS 7.6.2 image plus a user-accepted reboot, and MDM software-update deferral policy is precisely what held managed Apple fleets below those September 2021 trains. Only a DDM-enforced KEV deadline with deferral disallowed converts an update an entity can mandate but cannot install into one that actually lands.

new_control_requirements.name: MOBILE-ZERO-CLICK-HARDENING
new_control_requirements.description: High-risk mobile users must operate in a reduced-attack-surface mode (e.g. Lockdown Mode) that disables automatic processing of untrusted message attachments, fonts, and link previews, closing the zero-click delivery path patch SLAs cannot outrun.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2021-31010 is the sandbox-escape stage of the same mercenary-spyware chain as FORCEDENTRY (CVE-2021-30860) in the same Apple advisory, whose initial access is automatic processing of an untrusted message attachment; and iPhone, iPad and Apple Watch hardware past its final supported OS train can never reach a fixed build, so a reduced-attack-surface mode is the only remediation those devices will ever have.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2021-31010 was fixed silently in September 2021 with no CVE attached and only appeared in Apple's advisories on 25 May 2022, so an identifier-driven remediation programme had nothing to schedule and a CVSS 7.5 sandbox bypass with no confidentiality or availability impact would have ranked below the RCE entries in the same advisory anyway. A mitigation clock keyed to the 2022-08-25 KEV listing is the only trigger that fired at all for this flaw.

CVE-2020-36193.name: PEAR Archive_Tar Improper Link Resolution Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: An attacker uploads a tar-family archive to a PHP application that extracts it with Archive_Tar. The archive carries two members: a symlink entry whose link target resolves outside the extraction root, followed by a regular-file entry whose name routes through that planted symlink. Pre-fix Tar.php never canonicalises the symlink's resolved target against the extraction directory, so the write lands anywhere the PHP process user can reach — and the instant it lands in a web-served directory the arbitrary write becomes code execution, which is why Drupal rated it Critical 18/25 rather than scoring it on the integrity-only CVSS impact.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; only whatever access the application already grants for submitting an archive, which for Drupal means tar-family uploads are enabled and processed
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; two crafted tar members, no timing window, no memory grooming. The real gate is reachability rather than difficulty, and Drupal's own risk vector marks the upload precondition TD:Uncommon.
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered — Drupal credits four named individual reporters and the upstream change is a hand-written canonicalisation check. No fuzzer, static analyser or AI system appears in the upstream repository, the Drupal advisory or any distro advisory.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Pin pear/archive_tar to 1.4.13 or later — never 1.4.12, which closed the traversal but rejected legitimate relative symlinks and was widely rolled back to restore module installs — or take the downstream fix: Drupal core 7.78 / 8.9.13 / 9.0.11 / 9.1.3, Debian DSA-4894, Gentoo GLSA 202101-23, or RHEL 8.4 php:7.4 via RHSA-2022:6541. Drupal's interim mitigation, disabling .tar, .tar.gz, .bz2 and .tlz uploads, needs no code change at all.
prevention.adequacy: The mechanics of prevention are trivial — Archive_Tar is a single PHP file, so replacing Tar.php takes effect on the next request once opcache resets, with no daemon restart. The trap is version choice: bumping to the release the advisory named shipped the extraction regression, and reverting to restore functionality put the traversal straight back. Hosts on end-of-life PHP 7.2/7.3 streams receive no distro patch at all and must replace the library themselves.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Reject or alert on symlink members (tar typeflag '2') in user-supplied archives whose linkname escapes the extraction root — the exact condition the upstream canonicalisation check was added to catch — and watch for files appearing outside the application's extraction or temp tree immediately after an archive-processing request, or a first-ever HTTP request to a newly created .php path in the webroot.
detection.adequacy: These signals are precise but sit downstream of the write: by the time a new file in the webroot is observable the arbitrary-write primitive has already fired, and the archive-upload request that carried it looks identical to the legitimate module-install workflow.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treat any host that extracted an untrusted archive as potentially web-shelled: enumerate files written outside the extraction tree by the PHP process user, review webroot, configuration and cron paths for new content, and rebuild rather than clean where a shell is found.
response.adequacy: Response is reliable only if the write was noticed, and the primitive is quiet by design — a single file created by the same user that owns the webroot, in a directory the web server already serves.

NIST-800-53-SR-3.gap: Supply-chain process controls act on identified suppliers, and no organisation ever selected Archive_Tar: it arrives vendored inside Drupal core or bundled in a distro php-pear package. With no supplier relationship in scope, a fully conformant SR-3 programme has no line of sight to a 1.4.11 copy of Tar.php several levels down in composer.lock.

NIS2-Art21-supply-chain.gap: Art.21(2)(d) is drafted around direct suppliers and service providers and the security of their offerings. Nobody contracted for Archive_Tar and it appears on no supplier register, so an entity meeting every supply-chain obligation against that register still ships the vulnerable library and still extracts attacker-supplied archives through it.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: B4 expects unneeded functionality to be disabled, but the vulnerable function here is ordinary archive extraction — the mechanism the CMS uses to install modules and themes. That is why Drupal offered blocking tar-family uploads as an emergency mitigation rather than as a hardening default: the control's cost is the platform's core administrative workflow, and B4 gives an operator no framework for that trade.

AU-ISM-1546.gap: ISM-1546 drives patching of applications with known exploited vulnerabilities, but a PHP library inside a CMS tarball is not an application any inventory tool enumerates. Worse, the naive compliant action — bump to the version the advisory names — satisfies the control while shipping the release that broke relative-symlink extraction, so operators who then reverted reopened the traversal with a green control.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.28.gap: Secure coding is exactly what the upstream fix implements, and exactly what the affected organisations never had authority over. Virtually every victim consumed Archive_Tar as a dependency of Drupal or php-pear; A.8.28 binds an organisation's own development activity and has no purchase on source it did not write, did not review and in most cases did not know it shipped.

new_control_requirements.name: TIER-3-DEPENDENCY-INVENTORY
new_control_requirements.description: Supply chain inventory must extend to tier-3 dependencies (dependencies of dependencies of direct dependencies). SBOM coverage for libsystemd-class transitive dependencies cannot be omitted under SR-3.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2020-36193 lives in Archive_Tar 1.4.11, a library nobody selected: it reaches victims vendored inside Drupal core or bundled in a distro php-pear package, several levels down in composer.lock, so it appears on no supplier register and in no direct-dependency listing. Only an inventory that reaches transitive components surfaces the vulnerable Tar.php as something to patch.

new_control_requirements.name: SCANNER-PAPER-COMPLIANCE-TEST
new_control_requirements.description: A vulnerability scanner that reports 'patched' based on kernel package version alone is paper compliance. The operational test: does the scan account for the module-unload mitigation surface, AND does it verify the kernel is on a build that includes the specific Fragnesia patch (not just any version newer than the Dirty Frag patch that introduced Fragnesia)?
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2020-36193's advisory names Archive_Tar 1.4.12 as the fix, but 1.4.12 rejected legitimate relative symlinks (pear/Archive_Tar issue #35) and was widely rolled back to restore module and theme installs — so a version-string check records the host as remediated at 1.4.12 and stays green after the revert to 1.4.11, while only 1.4.13 is both fixed and functional.

CVE-2020-28949.name: PEAR Archive_Tar Deserialization of Untrusted Data Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: A tar whose member filename is prefixed with a PHP stream wrapper — file://, php://, or the uppercase PHAR:// variant — is handed to Archive_Tar::extract(). The pre-1.4.11 _maliciousFilename() check rejected only the literal string 'phar://', so every other scheme survives and the member is written to an absolute attacker-chosen path with the PHP process user's permissions; the Metasploit module defaults that path to /tmp/msf.php. Where the write lands in a web-served directory, requesting it yields code execution.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; but UI:R, so a human or scheduled job must feed the archive to the library, which in practice is a CMS module or theme upload-and-install workflow
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; one crafted member name, no race window and no memory corruption, weaponised in Metasploit from January 2021 — nineteen months before the KEV listing. The only genuine constraint is where the PHP process may write, since the payload must land somewhere the web server will execute.
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered — reported upstream by GitHub user @xorathustra with a hand-built reproducer after observing that the existing filename defence enumerated a single known-bad scheme. No AI system, fuzzing harness or automated analysis appears in the upstream issue, the Drupal advisory or the Metasploit module credits.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Upgrade Archive_Tar to 1.4.11 or later — standardise on 1.4.13, which also carries the sibling symlink fix without the relative-symlink regression — or take Drupal core 7.75 / 8.8.12 / 8.9.10 / 9.0.9, Debian DSA-4817, Gentoo GLSA 202101-23 or RHEL 8.4 php:7.4 via RHSA-2022:6541. Drupal's no-code-change interim measure is to block .tar, .tar.gz, .bz2 and .tlz uploads.
prevention.adequacy: Swapping the library is complete and cheap, taking effect on the next request after an opcache reset. Two things blunted it in practice: the KEV entry's title and short description for this identifier actually describe the sibling uppercase-PHAR bypass, so an operator triaging from KEV text alone was reading about the wrong bug, and hosts on deprecated PHP 7.2/7.3 streams were told no php-pear patch would ship and had to replace the library themselves.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alert on tar member names containing '://' — the exact pattern the fixed _maliciousFilename() generalised to reject — on a PHP worker writing outside its upload or temp tree during extraction, and on the appearance of /tmp/msf.php or another artefact matching the Metasploit module's configured output path.
detection.adequacy: The '://' member-name check is a strong, exploit-derived signal, but the delivery step is an administrator performing the platform's normal install action, so nothing upstream of extraction distinguishes malicious from routine.

response.what_would_have_worked: Scope the write: enumerate absolute paths the PHP user touched during archive processing, remove any planted file, rebuild the host if the write reached a web-served or scheduled-execution path, and rotate credentials readable by the web-server user.
response.adequacy: Response works only where the artefact is found, and the primitive lets the attacker choose the destination — so cleanup keyed on the extraction directory misses the whole point of the bug.

NIST-800-53-SI-10.gap: Input validation was implemented — as a denylist of exactly one string. SI-10 draws no distinction between a check that rejects one known-bad scheme and one that rejects every scheme, so an assessor could record the control as implemented while file://, php:// and PHAR:// all passed through to an absolute-path write.

DORA-Art-9.gap: Every Art.9 protection measure sits downstream of the trigger, which is an authorised content editor or administrator uploading an archive through a sanctioned business workflow. Segmentation, access control and encryption are all satisfiable and all irrelevant, because Art.9 offers nothing that distinguishes a legitimate module archive from a weaponised one at the moment the library extracts it.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: B4 leans on least privilege, and least privilege buys nothing here: the write happens as the ordinary web-server user, into directories that user already owns and the web server already serves. There is no privilege boundary for the attacker to cross, so the outcome can be fully met while a file:// tar member drops an executable PHP file into the webroot.

AU-Essential-8-App-Hardening.gap: User application hardening enumerates browsers, Office macros, PDF readers and similar workstation software. The attacker-controlled input here is a tar processed server-side by a CMS — outside every measure the maturity model names — and the delivery action is identical to the platform's normal install flow, so no maturity level distinguishes it.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.28.gap: The upstream fix is textbook secure coding: replace the scheme-specific denylist with a general 'any scheme://' rejection. But affected organisations consumed Archive_Tar inside Drupal core or a distro php-pear package, had no code-review relationship with the function that failed, and A.8.28 does not extend to auditing vendored third-party source shipped inside a platform release.

new_control_requirements.name: ECOMMERCE-PLATFORM-EXTENSION-UNTRUSTED-DESERIALIZATION-GUARD
new_control_requirements.description: An e-commerce platform (Magento / Adobe Commerce and similar) and every third-party extension it loads must never pass request-supplied data (cookies, headers, body, query parameters) to a native deserialization function (PHP unserialize(), and equivalents in other runtimes) on an unauthenticated storefront request path. Patch-management and secure-coding programs must enumerate every installed extension as part of the storefront's code-execution surface, not only the core platform. The distinguishing test: send an unauthenticated storefront request carrying a crafted serialized object in each cookie / header an extension reads, on a staging store, and confirm it is rejected before any deserialization runs - paper 'platform patched' attestations that ignore the installed extensions still permit unauthenticated RCE through an extension's object-injection sink.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2020-28949's pre-1.4.11 _maliciousFilename() was a denylist of exactly one string, 'phar://', so file://, php:// and the uppercase PHAR:// variant in an uploaded tar member name reached an absolute-path write as the web-server user and dropped an executable PHP file into the webroot. The failing sink is in a PHP library the CMS bundles rather than in the platform an operator audits, which is exactly the surface this control forces a programme to enumerate and test rather than attest.

new_control_requirements.name: CONFIGURATION-SIDE-LIVE-PATCH-INVENTORY
new_control_requirements.description: For any web-fabric vulnerability with a configuration-side mitigation path: that path must be inventoried, tested, and deployable independent of the vendor-patch path. Operators cannot wait for nginx 1.30.1+ if a named-capture refactor mitigates immediately.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2020-28949 has a no-code-change mitigation Drupal published with its own advisory — block .tar, .tar.gz, .bz2 and .tlz uploads — which removes the extraction path entirely at the point the trigger occurs, an authorised editor uploading an archive through a sanctioned workflow. Hosts on end-of-life PHP 7.2/7.3 streams were told no php-pear patch would ship at all, so the configuration-side path was their only available remediation.

CVE-2022-0028.name: Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS Reflected Amplification Denial-of-Service Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: An attacker sends spoofed-source TCP traffic to a PAN-OS firewall's external-facing interface, aimed at destinations a URL-filtering profile blocks. The appliance answers with amplified block-response and reset packets directed at the spoofed address, turning the firewall into a reflector that floods a third party of the attacker's choosing. Nothing on the firewall is read, altered or knocked over — Palo Alto states explicitly that exploitation does not affect the confidentiality, integrity or availability of its products — but the traffic implicates the operator's public address as the DDoS source and helps obscure the real attacker.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N and UI:N; unauthenticated spoofed-source TCP with no credentials and no exploit code anywhere in the path
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L on the mechanics, but the decisive precondition is configuration rather than software version: a URL-filtering profile with one or more blocked categories bound to a security rule whose source zone has an external-facing interface, which the vendor calls atypical and likely unintended. Version-only scanning therefore overcounts affected devices badly.
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered — responsibly reported by Excellium-Services S.A. CSIRT / CERT-XLM, and the vendor's own account traces it to a service provider identifying an attempted reflection attack in live traffic. No AI system or automated discovery method is credited.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Take the vendor's no-reboot workaround first — either remove the URL-filtering profile from any security rule whose source zone has an external-facing interface, or enable zone protection on every zone carrying such a profile (Packet Based Attack Protection with both 'TCP Drop > TCP SYN with Data' and 'Strip TCP Options > TCP Fast Open', or Flood Protection with a SYN activation threshold of 0 so SYN cookies engage) — then queue the upgrade to PAN-OS 8.1.23-h1, 9.0.16-h3, 9.1.14-h4, 10.0.11-h1, 10.1.6-h6 or 10.2.2-h2 behind it. Cloud NGFW and Prisma Access were resolved with no customer action; Panorama M-Series and virtual appliances are not affected.
prevention.adequacy: Prevention here is unusually cheap and unusually likely to be skipped. A configuration commit closes the reflection immediately with no maintenance window, yet because the operator's own confidentiality, integrity and availability are untouched there is no internal pressure to act — which is precisely why this persists on real fleets long past the 2022-09-12 due date.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Inbound TCP SYN bursts to the external interface carrying a spoofed source set to the intended victim and aimed at blocked URL categories; the appliance emitting amplified block-response and reset traffic to a host it holds no session with; and traffic-log entries showing an external source zone on URL-filtering-blocked sessions with no legitimate internal client behind them.
detection.adequacy: In practice the detection that actually fires is external — an abuse complaint or upstream provider notification naming the firewall's public address, which is exactly the path by which the vendor learned of the attempted attack. By then the harm has already been delivered to someone else's link.

response.what_would_have_worked: On any abuse notification, apply the zone-protection or policy-binding change immediately, upgrade behind it, and answer the reporting party with the remediation timeline; then audit every other perimeter appliance for the same profile-to-external-zone binding.
response.adequacy: Response is straightforward once the operator accepts that the incident is somebody else's outage. The organisational obstacle is ownership, not technique — an incident with no internal impact rarely reaches the queue that would fix it.

NIST-800-53-SC-5.gap: Denial-of-service protection is written to defend the organisation against DoS aimed at it. Here the organisation's firewall is the weapon rather than the target, so a control set sized entirely around inbound protection generates no finding, no alert and no remediation pressure while the appliance amplifies spoofed TCP at a third party.

NIS2-Art21-network-security.gap: Art.21 network-security measures are assessed against continuity of the entity's own essential service, and this defect costs the entity nothing measurable — no downtime, no data loss, no degradation. It therefore never surfaces in the risk assessment, and Art.21 has no mechanism holding an essential entity accountable for running an open reflector while its own function is demonstrably unaffected.

UK-CAF-B5.gap: B5 asks whether the essential function is resilient to disruption. The essential function stays up throughout — that is the substance of the vendor's own severity FAQ — so a B5 assessment framed as 'can we keep operating' returns green with the misconfiguration untouched, because the outcome B5 measures is not the outcome at risk.

AU-ISM-1546.gap: ISM-1546 drives patching of known-exploited vulnerabilities, and a PAN-OS upgrade on the device carrying all site traffic realistically takes weeks. The gap is that the vendor's no-reboot workarounds neutralise the reflection in a single commit, and the control's patch-centric framing gives an assessor neither credit for nor a prompt toward taking that immediate mitigation while the upgrade is scheduled.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.9.gap: Configuration management is the control that actually governs this and the one that would not have caught it: the trigger is a specific policy binding the vendor itself describes as atypical and likely unintended, and no baseline in general circulation flagged that combination as dangerous before August 2022. A fully conformant programme documented, enforced and monitored the misconfiguration as compliant.

new_control_requirements.name: PERIMETER-DEVICE-ZERODAY-SLA-TIER
new_control_requirements.description: Compliance frameworks must define a distinct patch SLA tier for pre-auth RCE on perimeter-trust-boundary devices (firewalls, VPN concentrators, WAFs, edge load-balancers). Tier requirement: vendor-mitigation deployed within 4 hours of KEV listing OR isolation of the vulnerable interface; standard 14/30-day SLAs do not apply because the device IS the trust boundary.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2022-0028 is a KEV-listed (2022-08-22) defect on PA-Series, VM-Series and CN-Series firewalls whose external-facing interface is the perimeter itself, and Palo Alto states outright that exploitation does not affect the confidentiality, integrity or availability of the appliance — so a routine appliance-patch window generates no internal pressure at all while the device amplifies spoofed TCP at a third party. Only an SLA tier keyed to KEV listing on a perimeter device, rather than to measured self-impact, starts the clock.

new_control_requirements.name: CONFIGURATION-SIDE-LIVE-PATCH-INVENTORY
new_control_requirements.description: For any web-fabric vulnerability with a configuration-side mitigation path: that path must be inventoried, tested, and deployable independent of the vendor-patch path. Operators cannot wait for nginx 1.30.1+ if a named-capture refactor mitigates immediately.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2022-0028's vendor workarounds — removing the URL-filtering profile from any security rule whose source zone has an external-facing interface, or enabling zone protection with 'TCP Drop > TCP SYN with Data' and 'Strip TCP Options > TCP Fast Open' or a SYN activation threshold of 0 — neutralise the reflection in a single configuration commit with no reboot, while the PAN-OS 10.2.2-h2-class upgrade is maintenance-window work on the device carrying all site traffic. The mitigation path has to be pre-inventoried and tested, because the patch-centric framing gives an assessor no prompt toward taking it.

CVE-2022-22536.name: SAP Multiple Products HTTP Request Smuggling Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: A single unauthenticated HTTP request carrying a manipulated Content-Length desynchronises the ICM's memory-pipe request buffer, so attacker-controlled bytes are prepended to the next victim request arriving over the same proxied connection. The attacker then executes functions as that already-authenticated victim, harvests the session, or poisons the intermediary web cache so later users are served the attacker's response. The published PoC pairs the desync with an injected 127.0.0.1 loopback Host header to defeat the ICM/Web Dispatcher ACL and reach internal-only paths such as /heapdump/ and /sap/public/bc/icf/info.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N and UI:N; one unauthenticated HTTP request, no credentials, and no participation from the victim beyond issuing the request the attacker prepends to
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L on the exploit itself, which is why a CVSS 10.0 with AC:L is not inflated here. What raises real-world difficulty is topology rather than technique: the desync is exploitable where an HTTP(S) proxy or Web Dispatcher sits between clients and the backend, so a scanner hit needs the intermediary confirmed before it is a finding rather than a probe artefact.
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered — Onapsis Research Labs found it by reading how the ICM buffers and re-associates request data across a proxied connection, and disclosed it with SAP as HotNews Note 3123396. No AI-assisted analysis, fuzzing harness or automated tooling is credited by Onapsis, SAP, Tenable or CISA.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Apply SAP HotNews Security Note 3123396 to every ICM and Web Dispatcher instance in the landscape — patched kernels for KERNEL 7.22, 7.49, 7.53, 7.77, 7.81, 7.85, 7.86, 7.87 and 8.04 plus the KRNL64NUC and KRNL64UC variants, patched Web Dispatcher 7.22EXT through 7.87, and patched Content Server 7.53 — with an ICM or Web Dispatcher restart, then confirm with the Onapsis ICMAD scanner rather than assuming the kernel level reached every host.
prevention.adequacy: Patching is the only fix and it must be landscape-wide: the desynchronisation occurs between the ICM and whatever intermediary fronts it, so hardening the reverse proxy, load balancer or WAF alone closes nothing. Two frictions delayed it in practice — the fix sits behind an SAP Support Portal login that CISA calls out in the KEV note, so no outside assessor or supply-chain questionnaire can verify it, and the restart lands on an ERP system usually under change freeze.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alert on requests whose Content-Length disagrees with the body actually sent, or an oversized Content-Length followed by padding bytes and a second concatenated request line; on external requests reaching internal-only ICF paths the ACL should answer 403 or 404; on 'HTTP/1.0 400 Bad Request' or 'HTTP/1.0 500 Dispatching Error' strings appearing inside a 200 response body; and on any user receiving content another user requested.
detection.adequacy: The request-shape signals are precise and are exactly what public detection tooling matches on, which cuts both ways: the same template that lets a defender find vulnerable instances makes opportunistic mass scanning for them routine, and the EPSS at the 99.9th percentile reflects that.

response.what_would_have_worked: Assume session hijack: invalidate SAP sessions, rotate credentials for accounts active during the exposure window, purge intermediary caches that may hold poisoned entries, and audit for function execution attributed to users who did not perform it.
response.adequacy: Response is achievable but scoping is hard, because the attacker's actions are recorded under a legitimate user's identity — the audit trail is accurate and useless at the same time.

NIST-800-53-SC-7.gap: Boundary protection is defeated on its own terms. The proxy or Web Dispatcher is the boundary device, and the flaw lives in that device's disagreement with the ICM about where one request ends and the next begins — so each additional layer adds another desync boundary rather than another barrier, and an assessment that counts perimeter devices scores the architecture higher exactly as it becomes more exploitable.

NIS2-Art21-network-security.gap: Art.21 network controls assume an unauthenticated attacker must first defeat authentication to reach business function. This one needs no credentials and defeats nothing: it inherits a session that was legitimately established, so for an entity running SAP as its system of record the integrity failure occurs entirely inside an already-permitted HTTP flow that the network measures are designed to allow.

UK-CAF-B2.gap: Every B2 outcome can be met in full — MFA, least privilege, session lifetime policy, privileged access management — and the attacker still executes as the victim, because smuggling attaches attacker-controlled bytes to a session that authenticated correctly. B2 has no outcome covering the case where the identity is genuine and only the request content is forged.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: The two-week internet-facing patch target assumes the patch is obtainable and applicable. This one ships as a kernel replacement behind a vendor Support Portal login and needs an ICM restart on a system typically under change freeze, so an organisation assessed at Maturity Level Three on paper can still be months out on a preauthentication 10.0 in the most business-critical platform it runs.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.22.gap: Network segregation is the control most SAP landscapes lean on — put the ICM behind a DMZ proxy and treat the backend as protected. That architecture is the precondition for this attack rather than the mitigation, since the desync is exploitable specifically where a proxy sits between clients and the backend. Conformance actively increased exposure.

new_control_requirements.name: ENTERPRISE-ERP-MANAGEMENT-FUNCTION-AUTHENTICATION
new_control_requirements.description: An enterprise ERP platform (Oracle PeopleSoft, Oracle E-Business Suite, SAP, and similar) must authenticate every management-plane and environment-management function before it can be invoked, and must not expose any takeover-capable function to an unauthenticated network caller. Segment the ERP management surface from untrusted networks and place it behind authenticated access control. The distinguishing test: send an unauthenticated network request to each environment-management / configuration endpoint on a staging instance and confirm it is refused before any privileged action runs - paper 'ERP access control' policies that attest user-login authentication while leaving a critical management function reachable without credentials still permit unauthenticated takeover.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2022-22536's published exploit pairs the ICM desynchronisation with an injected 127.0.0.1 loopback Host header to defeat the ICM and Web Dispatcher ACL and reach internal-only paths such as /heapdump/ and /sap/public/bc/icf/info from an unauthenticated caller. The management surface of NetWeaver ABAP/Java, Content Server and Web Dispatcher was reachable without credentials, and adding proxy layers in front of it made the desync worse rather than gating the function.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2022-22536 is a CVSS 10.0 unauthenticated flaw KEV-listed 2022-08-18 that lets one HTTP request execute functions as an already-authenticated victim in an organisation's system of record, yet SAP Note 3123396 ships as a kernel replacement behind a Support Portal login and needs an ICM restart on a platform normally under change freeze — a two-week internet-facing target left the crown-jewel system exposed for weeks that a KEV-triggered mitigation deadline does not.

new_control_requirements.name: SCANNER-PAPER-COMPLIANCE-TEST
new_control_requirements.description: A vulnerability scanner that reports 'patched' based on kernel package version alone is paper compliance. The operational test: does the scan account for the module-unload mitigation surface, AND does it verify the kernel is on a build that includes the specific Fragnesia patch (not just any version newer than the Dirty Frag patch that introduced Fragnesia)?
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2022-22536's desynchronisation occurs between the ICM and whatever intermediary fronts it, so patching only the reverse proxy, load balancer or WAF closes nothing and a landscape-level 'kernel patched' attestation hides every ICM and Web Dispatcher instance the rollout missed. Onapsis shipped a dedicated ICMAD scanner precisely because the kernel level recorded for the landscape is not evidence that each host actually took Note 3123396.

CVE-2022-32894.name: Apple iOS and macOS Out-of-Bounds Write Vulnerability (CVE-2022-32894)

attack_vector.description: Code already running in a sandboxed userland process triggers an out-of-bounds write in the XNU kernel and obtains arbitrary code execution with kernel privileges. Jamf Threat Labs reverse-engineered the in-the-wild path and found the attacker did not attack the kernel directly from the app sandbox but pivoted through the Display Co-Processor, using the under-protected DCP as a trampoline into the AP kernel. The natural first stage is CVE-2022-32893 in WebKit from the same 2022-08-17 advisory, making browse-then-escalate the expected sequence, and once kernel read/write is held every boundary — sandboxing, code-signing enforcement, per-app data separation — is administered by attacker-controlled code.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; the exploit runs as code already present on the device, which in a real chain is placed there remotely by the paired WebKit bug
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L, consistent with the 'improved bounds checking' fix language: a deterministic out-of-bounds write with no race condition. The AV:L should not be read as requiring physical or interactive access; scored as the second half of a browse-to-own chain the practical vector is network-reachable, and UI:R is satisfied by the victim visiting a page.
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered — Apple credits 'an anonymous researcher' in both August 2022 advisories and never described the vulnerable subsystem. No primary source attributes any part of the discovery or its weaponisation to AI tooling.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Update to iOS/iPadOS 15.6.1 or macOS Monterey 12.5.1 (2022-08-17), or macOS Big Sur 11.7 and watchOS 9 (2022-09-12). Apple ships no live-patch mechanism for XNU, so every fix is a full OS update plus reboot. Because iOS 15 and macOS Monterey have since passed Apple's support horizon, hardware that cannot move to a currently-serviced major release has no forward remediation path and must be handled with compensating controls — Lockdown Mode where available, device retirement otherwise.
prevention.adequacy: The update mitigates the escape method rather than the root cause: Jamf concluded the DCP-to-AP-kernel path stayed reachable on iPhone 12 and later until Apple closed ColdInvite (CVE-2023-27930) in iOS 16.5, so 'patched' and 'not exploitable via the co-processor' were different states for nine months. An operator who applied 15.6.1 and stopped was not clear of the class.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Panic logs or sysdiagnose bundles referencing the Display Co-Processor on iPhone 12 and later; otherwise the only durable operator check is the MDM-reported OS build number combined with Lockdown Mode status.
detection.adequacy: There is no endpoint agent to query on iOS or iPadOS and no kernel event feed to collect, so a kernel-privilege implant produces zero monitorable events across more than half the affected device population — the detection layer is structurally absent rather than merely weak.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treat a suspect device as unrecoverable in place: move it to a currently-serviced release or retire the hardware, rotate every credential and token it held, and enable Lockdown Mode for users in the targeting profile this class of exploit serves.
response.adequacy: Response has to proceed on suspicion because confirmation is unavailable, and the attacker's kernel privileges mean any on-device evidence could have been curated before the responder ever looked.

NIST-800-53-SC-39.gap: The requirement for a separate execution domain per process is satisfied entirely by the XNU kernel, and an out-of-bounds kernel write collapses the enforcing mechanism itself. An assessment recording 'the operating system enforces hardware-backed process isolation' was factually correct and bought nothing, because the control has no expression that survives compromise of the isolator.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: Vulnerability handling assumes the entity can push the fix to the vulnerable estate. This lives in iOS, iPadOS, watchOS and macOS on devices that are frequently personally owned or lightly enrolled, and the fix ships only as a full OS update requiring a user-accepted reboot — so between the vendor release and the KEV due date the compliant action and the effective action diverged for exactly the population most likely to be targeted.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: Every B4-shaped control on an Apple device — app sandboxing, code-signing enforcement, System Integrity Protection — is adjudicated by the kernel this write corrupts, and the exploited path arrived through a display co-processor no B4 assessment question contemplates. A self-assessment can be honestly green while an attacker holds kernel read/write via a peripheral processor outside the assessment scope.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: The ACSC scopes 'patch operating systems' to workstations, servers and network devices, leaving iOS, iPadOS and watchOS outside the mitigation entirely. No maturity level would have driven an iPhone fleet to 15.6.1 inside the 48-hour exploited-vulnerability window, and an entity could hold Maturity Level Three while its whole mobile estate sat unpatched.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.16.gap: Monitoring for anomalous behaviour presumes a telemetry surface exists. On iOS and iPadOS there is no EDR agent, no kernel event feed and no process-level audit log available to the organisation, so a kernel-privilege compromise on a managed iPhone generates no monitorable events at all — the control can be documented, resourced and audited as implemented while remaining structurally incapable of observing this.

new_control_requirements.name: MOBILE-ENDPOINT-MDM-ENFORCED-KEV-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: iOS / iPadOS / macOS estates must enforce KEV-class updates within 24h via DDM; user-deferral disallowed.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2022-32894 is fixed only inside iOS/iPadOS 15.6.1, macOS Monterey 12.5.1, macOS Big Sur 11.7 and watchOS 9 — Apple ships no live-patch mechanism for XNU — so every remediation is a full OS image plus a user-accepted reboot on devices that are frequently personally owned or lightly enrolled. Between the 2022-08-17 release and the 2022-09-08 KEV due date the compliant action and the effective action diverged for exactly the population a kernel-privilege implant targets, which a DDM-enforced 24h deadline with deferral disallowed is what closes.

new_control_requirements.name: SCANNER-PAPER-COMPLIANCE-TEST
new_control_requirements.description: A vulnerability scanner that reports 'patched' based on kernel package version alone is paper compliance. The operational test: does the scan account for the module-unload mitigation surface, AND does it verify the kernel is on a build that includes the specific Fragnesia patch (not just any version newer than the Dirty Frag patch that introduced Fragnesia)?
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2022-32894's iOS 15.6.1 update mitigated the escape method rather than the root cause: Jamf Threat Labs found the Display Co-Processor to AP-kernel path stayed reachable on iPhone 12 and later until Apple closed ColdInvite (CVE-2023-27930) in iOS 16.5. An MDM build-number verdict therefore reported the fleet patched for nine months while the same primitive remained exploitable.

new_control_requirements.name: MOBILE-ZERO-CLICK-HARDENING
new_control_requirements.description: High-risk mobile users must operate in a reduced-attack-surface mode (e.g. Lockdown Mode) that disables automatic processing of untrusted message attachments, fonts, and link previews, closing the zero-click delivery path patch SLAs cannot outrun.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2022-32894 is the kernel half of a browse-then-escalate chain whose first stage is CVE-2022-32893 in WebKit from the same 2022-08-17 advisory, and iOS 15 and macOS Monterey have since passed Apple's support horizon — hardware that cannot move to a currently-serviced release has no forward remediation path at all, leaving Lockdown Mode as the only operator-available control for that population.

CVE-2022-32893.name: Apple iOS and macOS Out-of-Bounds Write Vulnerability (CVE-2022-32893)

attack_vector.description: A maliciously crafted web page rendered by WebKit triggers an out-of-bounds write inside the content-rendering process, giving the attacker code execution in the renderer with no download, no install and no credential prompt — the user-visible event is a page load. On Apple platforms renderer execution is sandboxed, so the natural pairing is CVE-2022-32894 from the same 2022-08-17 advisory to escape to kernel privileges. The blast radius is wider than the Apple framing implies: the same defect ships inside WebKitGTK and WPE WebKit below 2.36.7, where the reachable process is often a mail client, help viewer or documentation reader nobody classified as internet-facing.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; UI:R is satisfied by the victim rendering attacker-supplied content, which for an embedded WebKitGTK view can be as little as opening a message that loads remote HTML
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; the 'improved bounds checking' fix language indicates a deterministic out-of-bounds write rather than a race, and the only precondition is that the target renders attacker-supplied web content.
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered — three Apple advisories credit 'an anonymous researcher' against WebKit Bugzilla 243557, and neither Apple nor the WebKitGTK project made any tooling claim. In 2022 the browser-security field's automated discovery was conventional coverage-guided fuzzing.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: On Apple platforms: iOS/iPadOS 15.6.1 and macOS Monterey 12.5.1 (2022-08-17), Safari 15.6.1 (2022-08-18) — which is the only remediation for Big Sur and Catalina Macs, since they received no OS update — and the 2022-08-31 iOS 12.5.6 backport for iPhone 5s, iPhone 6/6 Plus, iPad Air, iPad mini 2 and 3 and iPod touch 6th generation. On Linux: WebKitGTK and WPE WebKit 2.36.7 (WSA-2022-0008), shipped by Red Hat as RHSA-2022:6540, RHSA-2022:6634 and RHSA-2025:10364.
prevention.adequacy: The Apple side is complete if the update is accepted; Apple's willingness to backport to five-to-nine-year-old hardware two weeks later is the clearest available signal of real-world targeting. The Linux side is the residual gap: updating the WebKitGTK package is necessary but not sufficient until every long-running process holding the old library is restarted, and an asset register that lists applications by product name gives no way to know which of them embed the engine.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Repeated com.apple.WebKit.WebContent renderer crashes on affected Apple builds, or WebKitWebProcess crashes on WebKitGTK embedders — out-of-bounds writes fail noisily against device models and builds the exploit was not calibrated for, so crash volume is the one signal that survives on platforms with no endpoint agent. Correlate against WebKit Bugzilla 243557 and advisory WSA-2022-0008.
detection.adequacy: Crash volume is a weak proxy: it reports failed attempts, not successful ones, and on iOS and iPadOS there is no host telemetry channel to collect it from in the first place.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treat renderer compromise as a chain — assume the paired kernel escalation was attempted on the same device — update or retire affected hardware, rotate credentials entered in the browser during the exposure window, and enumerate Linux hosts by installed WebKitGTK/WPE library version rather than by browser name, restarting every embedder after the package update.
response.adequacy: Response depends on knowing the engine's footprint, which is exactly the inventory question most organisations cannot answer for a shared rendering library embedded in unrelated desktop software.

NIST-800-53-SI-3.gap: Malicious code protection has nothing to act on: the payload is a structurally legitimate HTML/JavaScript document and the corruption occurs inside WebKit's own memory during normal rendering. Signature engines, reputation feeds and file-based quarantine never get a decision point, so an assessment showing full endpoint AV coverage with current definitions describes a control that was never in the path.

EU-CRA-Art13.gap: The manufacturer obligations bind whoever ships the product with digital elements, and this exposes the transitive-engine problem: WebKitGTK and WPE WebKit below 2.36.7 carry the defect inside mail clients, help viewers and desktop applications whose makers do not think of themselves as shipping a browser. The operator's exposure is set by whichever downstream vendor rebuilds against 2.36.7 last, not by their own patching discipline.

UK-CAF-C1.gap: Security monitoring is assessed on whether collection is comprehensive enough to detect attacks. This one leaves no file on disk, no new process, no persistence key and no outbound connection until the attacker chooses to make one; on iOS and iPadOS there is no host telemetry channel at all, and on macOS the surviving signal is a renderer crash report. A C1 outcome rated achieved on log-collection breadth is describing coverage of a data source this attack never touches.

AU-Essential-8-App-Hardening.gap: User application hardening targets web browsers directly, but every measure in it is a configuration decision — block Flash, block web ads, block Java, disable unneeded features. None of those alter WebKit's bounds checking on the affected code path, so a fully hardened browser reaches the vulnerable routine exactly as a default one does and Maturity Level Three carried the same exposure as Maturity Level Zero.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: The exposure question cannot be answered from an asset register that records applications: the vulnerable unit is the shared WebKitGTK or WPE WebKit library, embedded in software listed by product name with no engine attribution, and on Apple platforms it is an OS component implied by the build number. A process that polls advisories by vendor and product registers the Apple advisory and misses the same CVE inside a Linux mail client.

new_control_requirements.name: TIER-3-DEPENDENCY-INVENTORY
new_control_requirements.description: Supply chain inventory must extend to tier-3 dependencies (dependencies of dependencies of direct dependencies). SBOM coverage for libsystemd-class transitive dependencies cannot be omitted under SR-3.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2022-32893's vulnerable unit is the shared WebKitGTK / WPE WebKit library below 2.36.7, embedded inside mail clients, help viewers and documentation readers whose vendors do not describe themselves as shipping a browser — an asset register keyed on product name registers the Apple advisory and misses the same CVE inside a Linux desktop application. The operator's exposure window is set by whichever downstream rebuild against 2.36.7 lands last, which only an engine-level component inventory can surface.

new_control_requirements.name: BROWSER-MANAGED-UPDATE-NO-DEFERRAL
new_control_requirements.description: Enterprise update rings must not defer security-channel browser updates beyond 24h.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2022-32893 has no configuration expression: blocking Flash, ads, Java or unneeded browser features does not alter WebKit's bounds checking on the affected code path, so a fully hardened browser reached the vulnerable routine exactly as a default one did. Only the version bump to iOS/iPadOS 15.6.1, macOS Monterey 12.5.1, Safari 15.6.1 or WebKitGTK 2.36.7 removes it, and Apple's 2022-08-31 backport to five-to-nine-year-old hardware shows how hot the window was.

CVE-2022-2856.name: Google Chromium Intents Insufficient Input Validation Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: A crafted HTML page passes unvalidated input into Chrome's Intent handling, and the browser navigates to an attacker-chosen destination without a click or a confirmation. Nothing is disclosed and nothing is disrupted — C:N and A:N — the integrity that falls is the browser's decision about where to go, which makes this a delivery primitive whose severity is inherited from whatever it lands on: a second-stage exploit page or a credential-harvest host. In telemetry it appears as the hop before the payload rather than as the payload.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; UI:R means only that the user opens a page the attacker controls or can inject into
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; nothing is groomed or raced, only a page served. The hard part is scoping rather than exploitation: NVD's description names Chrome on Android while its CPE set covers Windows, macOS, Linux and Android, and CISA notes the affected code reaches Edge, Opera and other Chromium browsers.
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered — Google Threat Analysis Group's Ashley Shen and Christian Resell reported it on 2022-07-19 from hunting live intrusions, and Google stated an exploit already existed in the wild. Chrome's coverage-guided fuzzing infrastructure is credited separately in the same release post; this CVE is not among those findings, and no source attributes the exploit's construction to AI tooling either.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Update to Chrome stable 104.0.5112.101 (Mac, Linux) or 104.0.5112.102/101 (Windows), released 2022-08-16, and update every Chromium downstream on its own release line — Microsoft Edge 104.0.1293.47, plus Opera and other Chromium-derived browsers per the CISA KEV note, and the Fedora 37 chromium rebuild. There is no configuration workaround: Intent handling cannot be disabled by enterprise policy, and the fix does not take effect until every browser window closes.
prevention.adequacy: Patching works; the inventory does not. An estate keyed on the Chrome version string alone under-reports the exposed population by every Edge, Opera and Chromium-derived install it runs, and the Android half of that population frequently sits on personally-owned handsets the organisation cannot force to update. Google had known of in-the-wild exploitation since 2022-07-19, so the exposure window opened well before any operator could act on it.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Browser history or proxy logs showing an intent:// or scheme-handler navigation from a page the user did open to a host the user never selected, with no intervening click event — the observable is a page transition nobody initiated, typically landing on a second-stage exploit or credential-harvest host.
detection.adequacy: The signal exists in proxy telemetry but is easy to lose in ordinary redirect noise, and on the Android population most likely to be affected there is usually no proxy or browser-history collection at all.
